Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-An'am (6), verse 1:

The Most High begins Surah al-An'am with His saying:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ (1)

When you hear the word "al-hamd" (praise), you must understand that it is the word for commendation, laudation and thanks. Praise is an innate matter that exists within us, and we direct it to Allah. He, the Most High, took us by the hand and made clear and explained to us that all praise is due to Allah, so that we would not differ over the direction in which it is to be aimed, because He is the One who supplied every human being with some of his means.

When you ask someone about anything, the chain of what he has supplied you with traces back to Allah. Therefore every praise must be directed to Allah.

Let me give this example: suppose a person's aircraft has crashed in some desolate place, where there is none of the means of life, and he wished to eat, drink and find shelter so that he could sleep, but he found nothing of this. Sleep overtook him, then he woke up suddenly and found a table on which were all the delicacies of food and drink, and beside that he found a tent containing a bed, a covering and a tap for washing. When he sees all of that, he does not begin to use anything before he asks about its source, because he wants to thank the One who bestowed upon him these abundant blessings. So it is as if you, O human being, when you confronted the universe and found things serving you, for which neither you nor those before you had any work, since no one had claimed them for himself—you found a sun that rises, air that blows, water that quenches, land that is cultivated, and other things that serve you, and the Truth informed you that He is the One who granted you all this. Would you not then thank Him?

When humanity benefited from the electric lamp, a clamour arose to honour Edison who invented it. How much more, then, should we honour the Creator of the sun that illuminates the whole universe? Human inventions perpetuate the names of their owners, and a clamour is raised to honour them. So what of us, regarding the Creator of the whole universe? Why do we honour the maker of a lamp that lights narrow spaces, however wide they may be compared with the earth, while some of us neglect to glorify the Creator of the sun that lights the earth by day and disappears for half the day so that man may rest? Yet it moves in a constant course; if it sets for you, it has risen for others, for it swims in its orbit.

So praise belongs to Allah when man encounters this existence and finds all the requisites of life, which no human power can subject, nor any human claim. Praise is a necessary reality even if people differ over whom it should be addressed to. We direct it to Allah, the Exalted, because He is the Giver of blessings.

The Surahs of the Qur'an that the Creator opened with "al-hamdu lillah" are five: al-Fatihah, al-An'am, al-Kahf, Saba' and Fatir. They revolve around two things: material upbringing, through establishing structures by means of sustenance, or the continuation of the species through marriage; or spiritual and moral upbringing, by supplying them with the method of the heavens. Sometimes the Truth says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ The word "Rabb" means that He has taken charge of the upbringing of creation toward an end and a mission, and upbringing requires material requisites and immaterial requisites, spiritual and methodological. Therefore the Truth brings it comprehensive of the whole universe, as in the Opening of the Book: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds (2)﴾ (Surah al-Fatihah).

He is the Lord of all the worlds, their Owner and their Nurturer, and it is He who brings them into being in the manner that makes them fit to perform their mission in life, through the strength of structures, through the continuation of the species by marriage, and through the strength of values. A second time the Truth brings the method alone, as in His saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who revealed the Book to His servant﴾ (part of verse 1, Surah al-Kahf).

And another time the Truth brings only visible things, saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light (1)﴾ (part of verse 1, Surah al-An'am).

Here He brings things that pertain to visible matter, such as the heavens and the earth, and the darknesses and the light, which are things you can see clearly. And at another time the Truth brings unseen things along with seen things, as in His saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two and three and four (1)﴾ (part of verse 1, Surah Fatir).

He brings the whole collection in the Opening of the Book; He brings the method alone as in Surah al-Kahf; He brings the material universe as in Surah al-An'am; and He brings the material and immaterial universe as in Surah Fatir.

So praise is due, and is due indeed, and it is directed to Allah even if its apparent causes are from other than Allah, because all the causes of the world and the universe ultimately lead back to Allah. Here, in Surah al-An'am, the Truth singled out praise for Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth with what is in them of creatures, and then mentioned the darknesses and the light. Creation, as we know, is bringing into existence from nothing. "Ja'l" (making) applies to a created thing and directs it toward a purpose from it. For this reason the Truth said: ﴿and made the darknesses and the light﴾. Darkness is a privative matter, while light is a positive matter, and light dispels darkness. So the basic state is the existence of darkness, which differs in its colours, as for example: the darkness of a cave, the darkness of the sea, the darkness of the land. For this reason the Most High said: ﴿darknesses, one above another; when he stretches out his hand, he can scarcely see it (40)﴾ (part of verse 40, Surah al-Nur).

It is his hand; he knows its direction, but he can scarcely see it. So the Truth here specifies the praise for the creation of the heavens and the earth, because they are the container of all creatures. The scholars said: do not take "darkness" as merely the material darkness in which things are not seen, nor take "light" as merely the sensory light by which things are seen; rather, let us take "the darknesses and the light" as referring to both the immaterial matter and the sensory matter. He, glory be to Him, made "darknesses" plural in this verse and "light" singular, because the causes of darkness are many, but light has only one cause.

The Most High says: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾ (part of verse 153, Surah al-An'am).

"Subul" (ways) is plural, and the way of Allah is singular, because it is one. As if the ways of Satan are many, and the ways of people likewise are many according to their desires, but the way of Allah is one; therefore He makes guidance a light and misguidance darknesses.

﴿and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾. We say—and to Allah belongs the highest similitude—that you, O human being, when Allah bestows upon you and places in your hands what you may pass on of goodness to others, you say: "I did such-and-such for so-and-so," and then he denies it afterwards. It is as if the particle "thumma" (then) here is for remoteness. Indeed, "thumma" comes for conjunction like the particle "fa" (then). But "fa" denotes joining two things between which there is no time gap; for example, the saying of the Most High: ﴿then He caused him to die and assigned him a grave (21)﴾ (Surah Abasa).

Whoever loves a person, and that person dies, hastens to bury him, so that he does not swell and rot before him. For this reason the Most High says, after the burial: ﴿then, when He wills, He will raise him again (22)﴾ (Surah Abasa).

As if a long time may pass until the Resurrection, when the Truth will raise His creation. Remoteness may also be remoteness of rank or station. For this reason the Truth uses "thumma" here as a separation between the creation of the heavens and the earth and the making of the darknesses and the light, and between those who disbelieve in their Lord: ﴿then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾. They are those who make equals of Allah with others. We may take "ya'diluna" (ascribe equals) as dependent on their disbelief… that is, because of their disbelief they make Allah equal to others. Or the meaning may be that they swerve (ya'diluna), i.e., turn away from the true God to other than God, or ascribe partners to Allah. This is a saying that applies to atheists or polytheists. Allah, glory be to Him, brought the heavens and the earth into being from nothing, and no one may dare to say to Allah: "How did You create the heavens and the earth?" For He, glory be to Him, says in another verse:

﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not take the misleaders as helpers (51)﴾ (Surah al-Kahf).

Allah, glory be to Him, brought the heavens and the earth into being from nothing. The heavens and the earth are the container of the universe, and they were created before man and before the rest of creation. None of His creatures witnessed their creation, so it is not proper for anyone to ask about the manner of creation; rather, he must take his knowledge of creation from its Creator, who is Allah. Some people have come and said that the earth separated from the sun and then cooled, but these are mere conjectures and not established fact, because none of them witnessed the creation of the heavens and the earth. These are the people of conjecture who fall under His saying, the Most High:

﴿and I would not take the misleaders as helpers﴾ (part of verse 51, Surah al-Kahf).

The Qur'an said this before these people came. It is as if He, glory be to Him, gives us a forewarning of the coming of these misleaders before they exist. They did not witness the matter of creation; rather, like all of us, they arrived upon the heavens and the earth later. It was incumbent upon them not to plunge into a matter they neither knew nor observed. Likewise is their saying about the creation of man as an ape, when they were not with Allah at the moment of the creation of the universe and of man, nor were they partners to Him. Therefore the Truth teaches us the courtesy due to Him, and He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge; indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart—all of those will be questioned about (36)﴾ (Surah al-Isra').

"And it is upon us to take the report of creation from Allah, who said:

﴿He it is who created you from clay, then decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him; then you still doubt.﴾ He, glory be to Him, comes to us with the matter of creation, clarifying that He created us from clay, after having spoken about the matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth. He, glory be to Him, had already informed us earlier that He created us from dust, from black mud fashioned into shape (ḥama' masnūn), and from clay like pottery (ṣalṣāl kālfakhkhār). These are complementary, not contradictory. Likewise, the Truth has clarified that He created every living thing from water. So the water mixed with the earth and became clay (ṭīn), then black mud fashioned into shape (ḥama' masnūn), then clay like pottery (ṣalṣāl kālfakhkhār), and all of these are complementary links. We did not witness the creation, but we receive the matter of creation from Him, glory be to Him, and we know that clay is the material of planting and fertility.

When the scholars analyzed clay, they found that it contains many elements. The largest quantity of these elements is oxygen, then carbon, then hydrogen, then fluorine, then chlorine, then sodium, then magnesium, then potassium, then iron, then silicon (transliterated here as al-sīlūz), then manganese, and others.

The elements in this universe are more than one hundred, but they do not all enter into the composition of the human being; rather they enter into the composition of what benefits man, such as construction, adornment, and other things. In confirmation of His saying, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ (part of verse 53, Surah Fussilat).

The scientists of disbelief undertook this analysis and reported those findings which the Noble Messenger (ﷺ) informed us of in the miraculous, preserved Book that Allah has safeguarded as a firm proof. The Truth has preserved for us this proof, so that a non-believing scientist comes and arrives at some of the realities present in the Qur'an.

None of us was present at the moment of creation, but we witness death, which is the undoing of life, and the undoing of a thing occurs in the reverse of its building. We see those who demolish a structure begin by dismantling the last thing that was built and assembled: they remove the glass first, which was the last thing installed, then the wood, then the stones. Likewise, the undoing of life is by death. The human soul departs first, then afterward the body dries and parches until it becomes like clay like pottery, then black mud fashioned into shape, that is, it is afflicted by foulness and decay, then the water evaporates from it and it becomes dust. Therefore we affirm the One who created us in the matter of our creation, and we affirm Him in the matter of the heavens and the earth. When any speaker says otherwise, we say to him as the Noble Qur'an has informed us:

﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not take the misguiding ones as helpers﴾ (51), Surah al-Kahf.

Here the Truth informs us of the matter of the man: ﴿then He decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him; then you still doubt.﴾ No one among us knows his term, however much he presents himself to the physicians. The first term is the term fixed for each one of us, and the specified term with Him is the time of the barzakh (the intermediate state), and after it we are resurrected from our graves. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Say: its knowledge is only with my Lord; none will reveal it at its time but He﴾ (187, part of verse 187, Surah al-A'raf).

A person may come to know the approach of the precursors of his end and the nearness of his death through what Allah has revealed of His secrets by means of the advance of scientists. This is not from the unseen. In some cases the patient recovers, is cured and healed, and they say: a miracle has occurred. As for the specified term, we cannot know it, and the Truth, glory be to Him, specified this in five matters:

﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ (34, part of verse 34, Surah Luqman).

The Truth has spoken of the place and has not spoken of the time: ﴿then He decreed a term﴾, meaning He decreed a term for each one, then He made a specified term for every thing. The terms of individuals follow one another until the term of all comes, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then you still doubt.﴾ The proofs the Truth has presented are sufficient to keep anyone from doubting, yet there are those who dispute this after all these premises."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 3:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And He is God in the heavens and in the earth; He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn.﴾

Allah (Allah) is the proper name (ʿalam) for the Necessary Existent (wājib al-wujūd), and it is the name that God chose for Himself, comprehensive of all the attributes of perfection. The other attributes, which we call the Most Beautiful Names (al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā), such as the All-Powerful (al-Qādir), the All-Hearing (al-Samīʿ), the All-Seeing (al-Baṣīr), the Living (al-Ḥayy), the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyūm), and the Subduer (al-Qahhār), are all attributes that became names because they are absolute with respect to God. When these attributes are taken in their absolute sense, they belong to God, while it is permissible for them to be ascribed, in their created (ḥādith) mode of relation, to other than God. As for the name (Allah), it is not applied except to the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted:

God challenges those who disbelieve in Him to name anything other than Him by (Allah).

﴿Do you know anyone who is called by His name?﴾ (part of verse 65, surah Maryam)

The disbelievers heard this and none of them dared to name anything by the name (Allah). This is a form of challenge that remains until the Hour is established, and no one dares to say the opposite or to accept it, so as to name a thing or a being other than God by (Allah).

We know of nothing that existed by itself from eternity, before the cosmos came into being, except God. As for the most trivial things in our lives, which we regard as non-essentials, they do not exist by themselves; there must be a maker for them. A drinking cup, for example, does not serve an absolutely vital purpose in life, because a person can drink water with his palm or directly with his mouth. This cup required from man knowledge, capabilities, power and wisdom. Knowledge came to man through what God bestowed upon him of the capacity to investigate the material in the cosmos. Man looked at sand and discovered a means of smelting sand; he discovered a means of purifying glass with chemical materials; and he discovered a mechanical method for producing these cups.

The journey of making a cup has taken humanity great scientific and industrial journeys, and although it is not an absolute necessity in life, it is a luxury. How much more so the necessities: the sun, the moon, air and water? These things, therefore, must have a maker. And if the maker of the most trivial thing in human life goes to an office to register his invention so that he may benefit from it, how much more so the One who made everything, and who did not make them in order to benefit from them, but so that His creatures might benefit from them.

Humanity knows who made the lamp and its history, where it was born, where it lived, and where it was taught. How much more so the One who made the sun, the stars, the earth and man? The Truth, in His mercy, pointed to Himself and informed us that He, glory be to Him, is the One who created. No one has come to oppose Him, glory be to Him, and claim the making of the cosmos. And since nothing has an effect except by an influencer, we must know that He, glory be to Him, since He has said that it is He who created and originated, and no opposition has arisen against Him, His word is the truth. If there were a maker of the cosmos who did not know that God has informed us that He, glory be to Him, is the One who created, that maker, asleep and heedless of what he made, is not fit to be a god. And if he knew that God has informed us that He, glory be to Him, created the cosmos for us, and this maker did not dare to convey the truth to us, then this maker, the claimant, does not have the right to divinity.

As for the Truth, glory be to Him, He has informed us and taught us by conclusive proof that He is the One who created the cosmos. Since this is so, we must listen to Him, and the practical translation of listening to the Truth is worshipping Him and obeying Him in what He commands and forbids. Indeed, the world of the unseen realm, which you do not see, worships Him, glory be to Him. Everything in existence is under His command and glorifies Him with His praise.

﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾ (surah al-Isra, 44)

The seven heavens and the earth, and all the creatures in them, point to the precision of the craftsmanship and to God's dominion, and they glorify His transcendence and holiness, that He has no partner. Everything has a means of glorifying and exalting Him, but we do not see that, nor understand it, nor comprehend it. Here the Truth informs us that He is the One worshipped who is present in all existence. ﴿And He is God in the heavens and in the earth; He knows your secret and your open﴾. Since He is the One worshipped, it is fitting that He be obeyed in commands and prohibitions. But some of us obey and some of us disobey. Therefore the Truth has ordained for obedience a recompense: either bliss or punishment. There is a difference between the existence of a thing and the perception of a thing; beware of confusing the perception of existence with existence itself. So the thing whose existence you do not perceive, beware of saying that it does not exist.

An example of this is what we see throughout human history. The Creator has left in His creation secrets in existence which people derive, and which become manifest to them in benefits; and before humanity knew them and came upon them, they were performing their function in existence. An example is terrestrial gravity: it existed before man discovered it, and performed its work before man knew it. Its mention came in the Qur'an in a way that does not cause confusion at the time the Qur'an was revealed:

﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they should cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾ (surah Fatir, 41)

The Truth established the laws of gravity so that the heavens and the earth might carry out their works, and He preserves them by His power from ceasing, and made gravity a wondrous system that preserves the cosmos from disorder. Therefore gravity existed, and man did not know it except recently. Thus we know that there is a difference between the existence of a thing and the perception of a thing.

If it is said to you:

﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision, and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.﴾ (surah al-An'am, 103)

then you, O believer, affirm that; the essence of the Truth is not seen by eyes, and He knows everything hidden from you, and your eyes do not perceive Him. In the cosmos there are things that we may not perceive, although He, glory be to Him and exalted, created them and they work in your service; and after you perceived them, they continued to work in your service. If the Truth informs you of something you do not perceive, do not say: since this thing is not perceived, it does not exist. For example, you do not perceive electricity, nor gravity, nor the essence of the secrets of life, which is the soul that gives you the secret of life, and by which all your limbs are moved; if the soul departs, you become a motionless corpse. No one knows the place of the soul or perceives it; no one has heard it, smelled it, tasted it, or touched it. The soul exists within your self and you do not perceive it. Here you are, then: you cannot perceive a creature of God, so how will you perceive your Creator, who is God? If you did perceive Him, He would not be God; for if you perceived something, your limbs would have power over it, and it would become subject to your eye and your hand; and the absolute Powerful never becomes something subject to power. From His greatness is that He is not perceived.

Another example: the dream that you see and move within. Is the dream present in your body, or what? And forbearance, which is patience with others, so that you bear with them, show them kindness and smile at them: this forbearance makes you move. Do you perceive this forbearance? It is a meaning among the meanings in yourself which moves your limbs, and you do not perceive it, just like the courage with which you charge and move about, and you do not see it as a body, nor know its shape, color or taste. The Most High who governs this cosmos is not perceived by sight. What wearies people is that they try to combine perception and existence, and therefore we say: O human, search in your cosmos and you will surely find a difference between perception and existence.

We know that the name of God Himself is a word we pronounce, and by which we infer that He is the Supreme Creator, and by it He is challenged. You, O human, have invented, for example, the television, which before was non-existent and had no name, and it acquired a name since man brought it into being, fit for a specific task. But the name of God is existent and eternal before you, and the Messenger informed you of it; and He, glory be to Him and exalted, has a name in every language, and the existence of this name in every language by pronunciation is evidence of the priority of the existence of the essence, which is God. After that came disbelief, and we came to know that disbelief was an attempt to conceal the primordial existence, and thus the word disbelief indicated belief. What wears out a person is his attempt to confine the Supreme Existent to a form according to human capacities and limits. No one can confine His existence in a specific form, because from His greatness is that we cannot conceive of Him, and belief in Him, glory be to Him, indicates Him, and He says of Himself what He wills. I would like you to memorize this example and give it to your children:

Suppose a person is sitting with his family in a room, and then a knock comes at the door, and everyone sitting in the room is certain that someone is knocking at the door, and none of them disagrees on this matter. One of the sons says: "The knocker is Muhammad." The second says: "It is Mahmud." The third says: "No, it is Ibrahim." The wife says: "The knocker is a woman." But one of the sons says: "No, it is a man." The father says: "Perhaps it is a policeman who has come to ask me about a matter." The wife replies: "Expect good; you do every good, and every knocker must bring you good." Here the family disagreed not about the rationality of the knocker, but about the conception of the knocker. The father says: "Instead of confusion, let us ask him: who are you?" The knocker answers: "I am so-and-so."

Thus is the cosmos: man arrived in it and asked who created it. For man was struck by heedlessness after Adam knew his Lord, and after the Truth made the descendants of Adam bear witness that He is their Lord. Then the Truth sent the Messengers to convey to creation His method, His name and His attributes. By this He, glory be to Him, desired not to burden His creatures, and He informed people through the Messengers that He is the Most Generous Creator.

The flaw of the philosophers is that they were not content with rationalizing God, but wanted to imagine Him, and this is not possible. Therefore we say: we must listen to the Truth as He says of Himself what He wills, and there is no need for dispute. He, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿And He is God in the heavens and in the earth﴾. Beware, O Muslim, of understanding that heaven and earth here denote a container, for a container is a vessel and a space; and if you do not know the place of your soul in your body, how will you know the place of God? God by this statement intended that He is worshipped in the heavens and worshipped in the earth.

Let us note that some verses of the Qur'an hold the mind so that minds are always occupied with the words of God; and if the Qur'an had come with words whose meanings were easily grasped by ordinary understanding, the meanings of this great Book would not be renewed in every age, whereas the Truth intended this so that people might remain firm in their faith in every era. Here are some of those who attempt to delve into the Qur'an who asked about the meaning of the Truth's words:

﴿And He is the One who is God in the heavens and God in the earth, and He is the Wise, the All-Knowing.﴾ (surah al-Zukhruf, 84)

They asked about the meaning of the repetition: that He is God in the heavens and God in the earth. Some superficial readers supposed that He intended to say that there is a god in the heavens and another god in the earth, and they did not perceive that the intended meaning is: He is a god worshipped in heaven and worshipped on earth, and He is the possessor of absolute wisdom in all His acts, and He encompasses all His cosmos. And the Truth only intends by this statement to occupy minds with it.

We also say to those who did not grasp the meaning: there is a rule in the language that defines the indefinite and the definite. When we say: "The man came to me," this man is known to the speaker and the listener. But when we say: "A man came to me," this is not known to the listener, though it may be known to the speaker. And if we say: "A man came to me and I honored a man," the meaning is that the speaker is speaking of two men: one came, and the other was the object of honor. But if the speaker says: "A man came to me and I honored the man," the discourse here is about one man. Thus, if an indefinite is repeated as indefinite, it becomes different, and if an indefinite is repeated as definite, it is the very same. And when the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And He is the One who is God in the heavens and God in the earth﴾ (part of verse 84, surah al-Zukhruf)

some imagined that "god" (ilah) is indefinite, and when it was repeated it became something else; and if that were so, the world would be corrupted. But the predominant rule among the scholars grasped the spirit of the text. The scholars of monotheism (tawhid) said: we must draw attention to the fact that He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And He is the One who (wa-huwa alladhī)﴾, and the word "alladhī" is a single relative pronoun which indicates to us that the Truth's connection with the s

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 4:

It is as if the signs that demonstrate the truthfulness of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in conveying the message from his Lord do not satisfy them, but rather they turn away from them. Yet what was obligatory would have required that they prick up their ears to what would solve for them the riddle of life. The turning away has continued until our own time, even though we have come to know the expected lifespan of some of the things of our own manufacture, such as the electric light bulb, which needs replacing after every period, and other devices. Yet we do not know the expected lifespan of the sun, which has never once needed maintenance, and no one has asked: ":(And how does all this marvel come about?)"?

The Messenger (ﷺ) came to make clear to us that the One who created all creation informs us of what He requires and explains the universe to us, but man turns away from this.

The first "pitfall" into which a person falls is that there come to him the signs that point to the riddle of this existence from the Creator of existence, and to the manner in which the universe was arranged before the existence of man, and to how He made in the universe the sustenance by which he sustains his life and preserves his species; yet despite all this, he turns away from hearing all of it.

Surely the disbelievers did not merely turn away; they moved on to the second stage, which is denial. They did not content themselves with leaving the message of faith alone and turning away from it, but they add to that what the Truth clarifies in His saying: ﴿So they have denied the truth when it came to them, but there will come to them the news of that at which they used to mock﴾ (6:5). This is a move from turning away to denial. Turning away is a negative attitude, while denial is an active standing in the position of opposition and obstruction from the way of God. Then they move on to the third stage, which is mockery. We are thus before three stages: turning away, denial, and mockery. All of this is so that they may divert the one who follows away from following. An example of this is what the Truth has set forth for us in the matter of Noah:

﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾ (37). ﴿And he was constructing the ship, and whenever a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said: If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock﴾ (38) (Surah Hud).

So God, glory be to Him, revealed to Noah the clear message and commanded him to build the ship under His care, and not to address Him concerning the disbelieving wrongdoers who did not respond to God's call. Noah begins building the ship, but the disbelievers mock him because of their ignorance and because they did not trust the purpose and the goal. Noah mocks whoever mocks him.

Another example is the victory of Islam after the people of disbelief had been a power. But the arrogant tyrant among them comes, after his arrogance and pride, in humiliation; and some of them were killed and captured and tasted the bitterness of psychological disgrace. They had previously mocked the Messenger of God (ﷺ). An example of this is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, the chief of his people, concerning whom the saying of the Truth came:

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says: Tales of the ancients (15). We will brand him upon the snout (16)﴾ (Surah al-Qalam).

Al-Walid was a man of wealth and of might, with many sons, and he turned away from the Qur'an and mocked it. So the Truth made him an example for people, and set upon his nose a lasting mark by which he was disgraced, and it was a shame and a disgrace that did not leave him whenever he was mentioned.

This statement was revealed in the Qur'an at a time of weakness for the Muslims; then came the report of striking him upon the nose, which is the seat of pride, haughtiness and arrogance; then came Badr, so that the Muslims might see the realization of that. It is a divine speech, challenged with, and worshipped through its recitation. Thus do we affirm every matter that God brings.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 6, verse 6:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established on the earth as We have not established you, and We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain, and made the rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them other generations.﴾

This is what Quraysh witnessed in their winter and summer journeys. They saw the traces of 'Ad, the people of Hud, and the remnants of Thamud, the people of Salih. The resources of 'Ad and Thamud were greater than the resources of Quraysh. Quraysh has no dominion except through the existence of the Ka'bah, and if the Truth had left Abraha to demolish the Ka'bah, He would not have established them on the earth. Behold, these are civilizations that came before and that Allah, glorified and exalted, annihilated, and the Qur'an clarifies this:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the land, and Thamud who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh of the stakes, who transgressed in the lands and caused much corruption therein? So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.﴾ (Surah al-Fajr)

These were great civilizations with renown and fame in the ears of the world, like the civilization of the Pharaohs. None of that power (al-saulajan, "the scepter") can protect anyone from the command of Allah. The civilizations passed away and became a trace after being a visible reality, and the saying of the Truth applied to them:

﴿So each one We seized for his sin: among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those who were seized by the Blast, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabut)

The Truth recompenses every disbeliever with full recompense. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informs his people of what happened to other peoples: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ A "qarn" (generation) is customarily the group governed by a limited time or a limited condition. If we look at time, a qarn is at most one hundred years, and the generation that lives this span sees its grandchild grown into a man. We know that Noah, peace be upon him, lived nine hundred and fifty years, and He, glorified, says:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years.﴾ (part of verse 14, Surah al-'Ankabut)

The life of Noah, with all its length, is called a qarn. Therefore the qarn is a generation bound by a criterion, either temporal or conceptual: the temporal qarn lasts one hundred years, while the conceptual qarn may be the lifespan of a message or of a kingdom.

He informs the people of disbelief that He has decreed over others and destroyed them after establishing them on the earth, and that is through various kinds of establishment: ﴿and We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain, and made the rivers flow beneath them, then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them other generations.﴾ This report comes from the heavens, concerning what happened to earlier peoples such as the people of Saba', about whom the Truth said elsewhere in the noble Qur'an:

﴿There was for Saba' in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and the left. "Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him; a good land and a Lord Forgiving."﴾ (Surah Saba')

The dwelling of Saba' in Yemen was a sign indicating the power of Allah: two flourishing gardens on the right and left. The people of Saba' were to eat from the provision of Allah and give thanks for the blessing of Allah. They had the Dam of Ma'rib, and Allah gave them the capacity to build it, so they cut from the mountains—over which they had no control—in order to hold back the rainwater falling from the sky. Everything they did, then, they did because Allah willed it, but they turned away from two matters: from the abundant provision Allah had granted them, and they wanted to depend on themselves, as Qarun did when he said: (I was given it only on knowledge that is with me). They thought they were able to provide for themselves, and likewise they did not give thanks to Allah. Therefore Allah sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim, meaning a punishment of the same kind as their deed; and thus is the outcome of turning away and disbelieving in the blessings of Allah. Allah set over them an animal of the weakest and most contemptible of creatures, namely the rat, which gnawed through the dam, drowning their wealth and burying their homes.

He informs His Messenger of all these reports in order to draw the attention and alert a people who saw the traces of the civilization of 'Ad and Thamud. Sight is the sovereign of proofs, and the Messenger was charged with it so that they would know the outcome of turning away, denial and mockery. The Truth did not require of His Messenger anything but delivery alone; as for the faith of the people, the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is not charged with it. These people feared the dominance of (There is no god but Allah), for they are the ones who made gods of themselves and some of them dominated others. The strong imagines himself a god over the weak, the rich imagines himself a god over the poor, the learned imagines himself a god over the ignorant. But (There is no god but Allah) makes all people equal, and they reject that because they want dominion. An example of that is their saying:

﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf)

They did not dare to attack the Qur'an; rather they asked that dominion be given to one of the wealthy men of the two cities, Makkah or Ta'if. And this statement contradicted their actions and conduct toward the Messenger: they only preserved every precious thing they were keen upon with Muhammad (ﷺ). Had any of them seen a flaw in the trustworthiness of the Messenger of Allah, they would not have done that. But even while denying Muhammad, each of them would entrust only the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); a person, when his interest is at stake against his denial, puts his interest above his denial.

The Truth, glorified, makes clear that the turning away of these people, their denial, and their mockery have no connection, in any way, to the reality of your matter, O Messenger of Allah, nor to the reality of the Qur'an; rather it is obstinacy, like the obstinacy of the family of Pharaoh who denied the signs of Allah although their inner selves had seen these signs with certainty free of any denial:

﴿And they denied them, though their souls acknowledged them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ (Surah al-Naml)

The people of Pharaoh denied the message of Moses, peace be upon him, although they were certain of its truth, but they denied it through disdain, arrogance and injustice, so their end was among the worst of ends. This is always the condition of those who deny the signs of Allah.

Now and here are those who deny the new messages of the Messenger of Allah. The Truthful and Exalted Lord says about them:

﴿And if We had sent down to you a Book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is nothing but obvious magic."﴾

This Book, the Qur'an, if it had descended to these deniers written on paper of tangible material, which they could see, and they had touched it with their hands, they would have said what every denier says: "It is clearly magic." The deniers asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to send down to them a book from the heavens, so that they might read it, as one of several conditions, which Allah described, portraying their obstinate denial:

﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or [until] you have a garden of palms and grapevines and cause rivers to gush forth within it in profusion, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Am I but a human messenger?"﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 90–93).

So after the inimitability of the Qur'an had become clear to them, they tried falsehood and proposed signs as conditions for their faith: that the Messenger (ﷺ) cause a spring to gush forth for them in the land of Makkah whose water never ends; or that the Messenger (ﷺ) have a garden of palms and grapevines in Makkah, with rivers flowing through it; or that he call down the sky upon them in pieces as a severe punishment; or that Allah and the angels appear to them in person so they could see them with their own eyes; or that the Messenger have a house of decorated gold; or that he ascend into the sky and bring them a book from Allah confirming the truth of his message. But Allah, in His mercy and the breadth of His compassion, sanctifies His essence from being controlled by anyone or sharing in His power, so He declared to them, through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), His words, Exalted is He:

﴿Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Am I but a human messenger?"﴾ (part of verse 93, Surah al-Isra').

This is because the One who sends signs is the Lord of the worlds, and no one dares to impose His signs upon Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the receiver of Allah's signs, not a proposer of signs. He (ﷺ) knows that whoever proposes a sign to Allah and then denies it when it comes is struck and destroyed; this is the sunnah of Allah. The Messenger knows that he is the Seal (of the prophets), therefore he will never request any sign from Allah, lest the punishment of Allah descend after it if they deny it. The Truth conveys to His Messenger the arrogance of the tyrannical deniers and their haughtiness.

﴿And if We had sent down to you a Book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is nothing but obvious magic."﴾ (Surah al-An'am).

Allah knows that the hearts of some deniers have become heedless, so faith cannot enter them and falsehood cannot leave them, as He willed for them. Even if a book on paper descended to them, within the range of their sight, and they touched it with their hands, they would not believe. The mention of touching with the hands comes because touch is the sense shared by all, even the blind among them; and despite this, they would deny, saying, "This is nothing but obvious magic." Such a response does not stem from reason, reflection, or wisdom, and it is not fitting for a people known for eloquence and fluency, and for fine speech and composition. Magic alters people's perception of reality; and since they accuse the Messenger (ﷺ) of sorcery, why did he not bewitch them, and why were they specifically immune to magic? The one who is bewitched has no action or will in relation to the magician; if Muhammad (ﷺ) were a sorcerer, he would have produced from magic what would make them believe.

It is strange, for they are the people most discerning of the art of speech, the people of outstanding skill in expression, who know decisive speech and sound opinion and distinguish among the forms of discourse: oratory, writing, prose, poetry, rhymed prose, and unrhymed speech. Strange indeed that before the miracle of the Qur'an they stand bewildered, not knowing their own right course: at one time they say it is magic, at another that it is the speech of soothsayers, and at a third that it is the speech of a madman.

The Qur'an is not magic, because it possesses the eloquence they possess, and more than what they possess and excel in; the Messenger (ﷺ) did not do with them anything that would make them believe against their will. Nor is the Qur'an the speech of soothsayers, because the Messenger (ﷺ) grew up among them, and they know him as the truthful and trustworthy one who had received no knowledge from anyone; moreover, the speech of soothsayers has a particular manner and a well-known rhymed cadence, and the Qur'an is not like that. They know it is the speech of a sane man, for the speech of a madman does not cohere. And behold, the Truth says concerning the Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿You are not, by the favor of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character.﴾ (Surah al-Qalam, 2–4).

Allah has prepared His Messenger to receive prophethood with the strength of reason, not with foolish opinion, and in conveying the message of his Lord he has a reward that is neither cut off nor withheld, and he is upon a tremendous character. The great character, as we know, is facing events with balanced faculties, not contradictory ones, and only a sane person possesses this. They themselves testified to the character of Muhammad (ﷺ); so how could this great character come from a madman? And how could conduct characterized by soundness, righteousness, and goodness proceed from a madman? All their accusations against the Messenger (ﷺ), therefore, stemmed from their insistence on disbelief, not from any reality they had touched; everything they said about the Messenger, they were the first to witness its opposite and to experience its contrary.

And they came, persisting in disbelief, demanding another sign:

﴿And they say, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not then be reprieved.﴾ What is the angel (malak)? The angel is a kind (jins) that Allah placed in the unseen (al-ghayb), and we do not believe in it except because Allah, in whom we believe, said that He has angels, just as He said that there are jinn. The angels belong to the unseen kind, and the jinn are hidden from us. These deniers and rejecters demand the descent of an angel so that they may believe. So they have indeed recognised that there is an unseen realm, and that their original nature carries a trace of the message of heaven, but they deny it. Their saying "an angel" is evidence that in their depths there are residues of the religion of Ibrahim and the religion of Isma'il, and those traces have remained in their souls because it is a matter that does not touch their sovereignty. Even if the Truth had sent down an angel to them, they would not have believed either; they are liars. The Truth does not wish to apply His sunnah to them by sending down the sign they demand, lest His punishment descend upon them if they disbelieve in it. For if the Truth had sent down an angel to them as they demanded, and then they disbelieved, the matter would have been decided and they would have been destroyed without respite, because if it (the angel) had manifested itself to them in its true nature, their human constitutions could not have borne it.

The angel did descend with its decisive signs, while being unseen, sent down by Allah, glory be to Him, with the revelation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it acted upon the Messenger of Allah as it acted, and nothing of its action with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appeared except its effect alone. Here is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explaining to us that at the moment the angel first came to him in the cave of Hira: The angel said: "Read!"

(The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: He seized me and pressed me until I reached my limit of exertion, then he released me and said: "Read!" I said: "I am not a reader." He seized me a second time and pressed me until I reached my limit, then released me and said: "Read!" I said: "I am not a reader." He seized me a third time and pressed me until I reached my limit, then released me and said: "Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know.") The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to his house with his heart trembling, and entered upon his wife, Lady Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, and said: "Wrap me up, wrap me up!" So they wrapped him until the fright left him. He told her the news and said: "I have feared for myself." Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, said, enumerating the great qualities and character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "No indeed! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. Verily, you join the ties of kinship, bear the burdens of others, earn what is lost, host the guest, and help in the calamities of time."(1)

Thus was Khadijah's first faith from the moment she learned of the revelation. Then the Truth reassures His Messenger, saying:

﴿Did We not expand your breast for you? (1) And We removed from you your burden (2) which had weighed down your back (3) and We raised high your remembrance (4).﴾ (Surah al-Sharh).

Allah expanded the breast of His Messenger, so this breast became the descent-place of secrets and knowledge, and He lifted from the back of the noble Messenger the loads and heavy burdens. The name of the Messenger (ﷺ) became linked to the root of faith and belief, until the name of the Messenger of Allah became paired with His name, glory be to Him, in the first testimony of Islam: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

So this was the state of the Messenger of Allah when the angel appeared to him, not in its true angelic reality, for there is a difference between the human structure and the angelic structure. The human structure receives material things that suit its composition; if a power higher than it comes, it cannot receive it unless Allah prepares the angel and forms it in a form that makes it capable of being sent, and prepares the Messenger to be capable of receiving. We all know the story of Musa when he came to the appointed time of his Lord, and Allah described that encounter:

﴿When Musa came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look at You." He said, "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell unconscious. And when he recovered, he said, "Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first of the believers." (143)﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

The barrier to seeing Allah is the human being's inability to encompass Allah visually. When Allah manifested Himself to the firm, solid mountain, the mountain became dust, that is, crushed to pieces, and Musa, peace be upon him, fell thunderstruck from the terror of what he saw. When he recovered, he repented to Allah and declared that he was the first of the believers in Him, glory be to Him. If a human being was struck unconscious by the Truth's manifestation to a mountain, how could he be able to bear the Truth's manifestation to him?

We know that every creation has a capacity to receive what suits it. Let us give an example from our practical world — and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, and He is exalted above every likeness — we find a person, when he brings electricity into his house wishing to benefit from the light and illumination for a longer period and from the many benefits of electricity, yet when he wants to sleep he seeks to benefit from the darkness, so he extinguishes the lamps and places a small lamp that cannot bear to take energy directly from electricity at its strong source; therefore a person brings a transformer for energy, so the transformer receives the high electricity from its source and lowers it in a manner suited to the small lamp. Thus we keep a weak light at night to benefit from the law of darkness and sleep.

The Truth has bestowed upon us the favour that He created light and created darkness, and each of them has a function. If the creation of light, illumination and electricity has enabled humans to build civilisation, darkness has enabled humans to rest, and their souls are calmed so that they rise full of activity and vitality. And if we keep at night a glimmer of light that does not disturb, we do so so that we do not break things or collide with them when we rise at night to attend to a need.

Likewise the human being... he cannot, in his weakness, take directly from Allah... It is from the mercy of the Truth toward creation that He placed between Himself and creation intermediaries: the angel receives from Allah, the angel is an intermediary, the angel conveys to the chosen Messenger, and the chosen Messenger is an intermediary. And it is among the folly of the people of disbelief that they demanded the sending down of an angel as a messenger. Allah answers them in another place in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?" (94) Say, "If there had been upon the earth angels walking calmly, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger." (95)﴾ [Surah al-Isra'].

They demanded, in ignorance, that an angel be sent down to them as a messenger with guidance, and the Truth commands His Messenger to reply to them that if there were angels among mankind... that is, if there were angels walking on the earth, an angel would have descended to them as a messenger. And since this was not the case, the Truth sent a messenger from among the humans; for the messenger is supposed to deliver and also to be a behavioural model for the method, by applying the method to himself. If an angel had descended as a messenger and applied the method to himself, humans would have said: "You are an angel who can do what we cannot, and you are not fit to be a model for us." Therefore it was necessary that the messenger be of the same kind as those to whom he is sent, so that he may be a model and exemplar for them.

This is what refutes the claim of the divinity of Jesus, peace be upon him, or that he is the son of God, because Jesus, peace be upon him, asked them to do as he did. The Truth intended through the humanity of the messengers to affirm capability and exemplarity in the messengers, and therefore He said: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾, because humans cannot bear receiving the emanations and radiances of the angel, since they are not prepared to receive those emanations and radiances. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they are confused (9).﴾

1. Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Therefore, if God had willed to send a messenger from among the angels, He would have made him in the form of a human, because they would be unable to witness the angel in his original form, and they might perish upon seeing him. ﴿And We would have confused them with what they confuse [themselves with]﴾ (6:9), meaning: We would have obscured for them, through the presentation of a man, what they obscure for themselves, for they would then say, "You are only a human, not an angel." God has indeed sent the angel in the form of a human, as happened with the friend of God, Ibrahim (peace be upon him). God says:

﴿And inform them about the guests of Ibrahim. When they entered upon him and said, "Peace," he said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you." They said, "Do not fear. We give you good tidings of a knowledgeable boy."﴾ (15:51–53), (Surah al-Hijr).

God sent the angelic guests to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and he became afraid of them after he brought forward the calf and saw that they did not eat, until they told him something to reassure him, namely good news from God that a son, Ishaq, would be born to him from his wife (Sarah), after God had previously granted him Isma'il from (Hajar). Likewise, the True One sent an angel to Maryam the virgin, and he appeared to her as a well-formed human, to inform her of her conception of Isa (peace be upon him). Therefore, the angel takes on a human form when God sends him on a mission to humans, because the angel does not come to humans in his true reality. Among God's favors upon His Messenger is that He gave him the opportunity to see Jibril in his true form once, at Sidrat al-Muntaha, and once when he appeared in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi, in the guise of a traveling man who came to ask the Messenger about Islam and faith. ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar narrated about him, saying:

(My father, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, narrated to me, saying: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, a man suddenly appeared to us, with exceedingly white clothing and exceedingly black hair, showing no sign of travel, and none of us recognized him, until he sat down before the Prophet ﷺ, leaned his knees against his knees, and placed his palms on his thighs. He said: 'O Muhammad, tell me about Islam.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Islam is that you testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish prayer, give zakat, fast in Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House if you are able to find a way to it.' He said: 'You have spoken truly.' He said: 'We were amazed at him, that he asks and then confirms.' He said: 'Tell me about faith.' He said: 'That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in destiny, its good and its evil.' He said: 'You have spoken truly.' He said: 'Tell me about excellence (ihsan).' He said: 'That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you.' He said: 'Tell me about the Hour.' He said: 'The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking.' He said: 'Tell me about its signs.' He said: 'That the slave-woman gives birth to her mistress, and that you see the barefoot, naked, destitute herdsmen of sheep competing in building tall buildings.' He said: 'Then he departed, and I remained a while. Then he said to me: "O ʿUmar, do you know who the questioner was?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It was Jibril; he came to you to teach you your religion."')(1).

Thus, in our human nature we cannot see the angel unless God makes him take on a human form. That is why the True One said: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and We would have confused them with what they confuse [themselves with]﴾ (6:9). So confusion (labs) exists, as is evident from the fact that God sent angels in human form to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), Maryam daughter of ʿImran, and Muhammad ﷺ while he was sitting among his people.

1 Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Faith. This hadith is one of those in which Muslim is alone against al-Bukhari. Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, and both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) took it out in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was one day sitting out in front of the people, when a man came to him and said: 'What is faith?' He said: 'Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, meeting Him, His messengers, and that you believe in the resurrection...' etc. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and in his version he began with the question about faith.

Al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi) on Surah 6, verse 10:

Allah, the Exalted, consoles His Messenger after this, saying:

﴿And messengers before you were certainly ridiculed, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to ridicule.﴾

Here Allah informs His Messenger that the people of disbelief often mocked the messengers before him, and Allah brought them to disgrace through the punishment with which He had warned those who denied the messengers. Those who mock the news from heaven, Allah, glorified is He, encompasses them with punishment as recompense for what they used to ridicule.

Almighty and Glorious Allah says:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and then observe how was the end of those who denied."﴾

We know that the Truth (al-Haqq) never said "sīrū ʿalā al-arḍ" (travel upon the earth), because the earth is a vessel (ẓarf) in which man travels, and man is a vessel within the earth. This message from Allah came before we reached, through knowledge, the understanding that the earth is spherical and suspended in the air, and that the air surrounds it, and that the air is the sustenance of man with its oxygen and with the carbon dioxide that nourishes plants. We know that man can endure without food for weeks and without water for days, but cannot endure the cutting off of air from him for even a few moments. Therefore Allah never grants the air to anyone as a possession, and thus we have come to know that the air is of the same kind as the earth. When man travels, the air surrounds him, and on this basis he travels within the earth. This is from the miraculous expressive eloquence (al-iʿjāz al-adāʾī) of the Qur'an. We read His saying, the Truth:

﴿So travel through the earth and then observe how was the end of those who denied﴾ (part of verse 36, Surah al-Nahl)

And here in Surah al-Anʿām Allah, Glorious is He, says:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and then observe how was the end of those who denied."﴾ (Surah al-Anʿām)

What is the difference between the two? Especially since we know that fa' (ف) is a conjunction particle, and likewise thumma (ثم) is also a conjunction particle, and both of them indicate sequence (tartīb). But the difference is that fa' means sequence with immediacy (taʿqīb), i.e., without delay or lapse of time, like our saying: "Zayd came, then ʿAmr" (jāʾa Zaydun fa-ʿAmrun), meaning that ʿAmr came immediately upon Zayd's arrival without any interval. But thumma means the length of the time-gap separating the conjoined word from the word it is conjoined to. So when the Truth says:

﴿So travel through the earth and then observe how was the end of those who denied﴾ (part of verse 36, Surah al-Nahl)

it is as if observation and reflection are what is intended by the travel, and thus it becomes travel for lesson-taking (sayr al-iʿtibār).

And the Truth says: ﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and then observe how was the end of those who denied."﴾ This means that a person may travel through the earth for trade, agriculture, or any other work, and he must reflect and contemplate during that. So there is travel for taking lessons (iʿtibār) and travel for worldly benefit (maṣlaḥah). Travel for lessons means that a person takes the lesson directly, whereas travel for benefit means that he takes the lesson within the pursuit of benefit. The journeys of the Quraysh with their caravans to Syria and Yemen made them able to see the traces of those who denied, whether from the people of Thamud, the people of ʿĀd, or others. It was incumbent upon them to take the lesson during their striving for trade.

Al-Sha'rawi, in his commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 6, verse 12:

The Truth (al-Haqq) says to His Messenger ﷺ after that:

﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: To Allah. He has prescribed for Himself mercy. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who have lost their souls are the ones who do not believe.﴾

It is as if the Truth were teaching His Messenger the question and the answer, so that people learn through this that all dominion belongs to Allah. For however much they search for the owner of the universe, they will find none but Allah. Even among the deniers, the Truth says about them:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾ (Surah al-Ankabut, 61).

Despite their associating partners with Allah, they cannot but acknowledge that Allah is the Creator of everything. This is because a person may be deceived by what he possesses of choice (ikhtiyar) for himself, but when he looks at what befalls his own self by compulsion (idtirar), he immediately recognizes faith. A person may choose things, yet there are events that befall him in which he has no choice, and this is so that the Truth may alert His creation that He does what He wills, that He governs this universe, and that choice exists only so that a person may test himself by following Allah's obligations.

Events are of three kinds: an event that happens to you (yaqa' 'alayka), an event that happens within you (yaqa' fika), and an event that happens from you (yaqa' minka). What happens to you is not something over which you have choice, and what happens within you is not something over which you have choice either. Only the third kind remains to you, which is what happens from you. And you are bound in this by two brackets in which you have no choice: the bracket of birth and the bracket of death. So the whole matter belongs to Allah.

The Truth reassures His creation, saying: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy.﴾ This is a statement by which the Truth reassures His servants, so that people do not think that Allah punishes them without reckoning, for He is the Forbearing, the Possessor of grace, and He is the One who said:

﴿Say: "In the grace of Allah and His mercy—in that let them rejoice."﴾ (part of verse 58, Surah Yunus).

He, glory be to Him, pardons much, the door of His mercy and grace is open, and He grants repentance to every sinner. Among the grace of Allah is that He made some of the disbelievers stand against the Muslims at the beginning of Islam, and then afterward they became swords for Islam. He, glory be to Him, is the Merciful who gathers us for reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt or uncertainty. We all proceed driven toward that day; the disbeliever comes against his will, while the believer is certain of Allah's mercy and grace and rejoices in meeting his Lord.

The disbeliever—may Allah protect us—has lost his soul through his own deeds, in confirmation of the Truth's saying: ﴿Those who have lost their souls are the ones who do not believe.﴾ The loss of the soul follows from not believing. For if we look at ends and at means, we find that the means comes before the end. But in practical preparation, the end becomes clear before the means. The one who studies keeps in his mind the end, which is success, and so he exerts effort to succeed, for we know that every condition lies between two matters: between a motivating answer (jawab dafi') and an actual answer (jawab waqi'). Success is the motive for study, and study makes success actual. Ibn al-Rumi says:

"Would that someone showed me my goal before my path—
but how, when goals come only after paths?"

This statement of his is not sound, for a person must pay attention to the goal and recognize the means that will lead him to the goal. If the goal is that a person go to Allah, and the means is the method (manhaj), then why this bewilderment? Thus we know that those who did not believe have lost their souls, because they did not distinguish the motivating goal, which is going to Allah and submitting to His judgment, from the actual goal, which is the means. He, glory be to Him, has made it easy for His servants, for He has brought them the method by which they walk:

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 6, verse 13:

The True One, glorified and exalted, says after that:

﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (13)

Among the greatness of the Supreme Existent, the Necessarily Existing, is that He speaks of Himself in the third-person pronoun, and He, glorified is He, is the One who said at the beginning of some verses: ﴿Say, "He is Allah."﴾

The word "Say" (qul) is an imperative, so when the Truth says "He" (huwa), the pronoun "He" cannot be applied except to Allah, and it does not refer to anyone else but Allah. ﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day.﴾ The word "rests" (sakana) comes from the root s-k-n, and it comes with multiple meanings: it may mean dwelling (al-sukna), i.e. settling in a place, and it may mean stillness (al-sukun), which is the opposite of movement. The example of dwelling is God's saying to Adam:

﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾ (part of verse 35, Surat al-Baqarah).

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day.﴾ So it is as if the night and the day are a container, and all existence is contained within them. The containment of the night and the day corresponds to the containment of place, which is the earth. Every place on earth is reached by the night and the day. If we intend dwelling in the sense of residence, it is present; and if we intend it in the sense of stillness, which is the opposite of movement, it is present too, for every moving thing returns to a state of rest, and man is the master of movement, then he dies or comes to rest in the earth. Thus we see that the more general category that encompasses both of them is "whatever rests" (ma sakana), and for this reason the Truth said:

﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (13)﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

When He says: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day,﴾ He is speaking of time, and of time's encompassing of things that are temporal, that is, the things that occur in this time. Man, as we know, is an event, and everything that arises from him is an event, and it was originated by the Truth, the Necessarily Existing.

Since the event has come into existence, it must have a time and must have a place. As for the place of the event, it is the heavens and the earth and what is between them. As for the time of the event, it is the night and the day.

Thus the Truth has spoken of the creation of time after He had declared to us that He is the Creator of place.

﴿Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?" Say, "To Allah."﴾ (part of verse 12, Surat al-An'am).

Thus we know that time and place came into being when Allah willed that this universe should come into existence. And never say, O man: "Where was Allah before He created the universe?" Because "where" (ayna) is a search for a place, and "when" (mata) is a search for a time. "Where" and "when" came into being only after the existence of the event in the universe. The universe is a fixed container, that is, something stable. Time is a non-fixed container, because it is sometimes past, and sometimes present or future.

When the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day,﴾ it means that for Him are both containers: the fixed and the non-fixed... That is, for Him, glorified is He, is what is still, and likewise for Him is what moves in the universe, because every moving thing ultimately returns to stillness. Or His true word: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day﴾ means whatever settles in the night and the day, that is, for Him, glorified is He, is whatever settles in the night and the day, whether moving or still.

The Truth concludes this verse with His saying: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ Hearing is related to what is heard, that is, what has movement, and knowledge is related to what is heard, seen, smelled, and everything perceived by instruments of perception. Therefore His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ came to encompass both the moving and the still, so He, glorified is He, neither loses nor is absent from anything.

We know that when the Truth informs us about Himself with an attribute that has a counterpart among humans, we understand it within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. You, O man, have hearing, so you are called "hearing"; you have knowledge, so you are called "knowing"; you have sight, so you are called "seeing"; you have power, so you are called "powerful"; you may have abundant wealth, so you are called "wealthy"; you have existence, so you are called "existent"; and you are alive, so you are called "living".

But are these attributes in you the very same attributes in Allah? No; because the attributes of Allah are understood within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. We observe this in ourselves: a man has a state of life and a state of death, and in the state of life he has two conditions: wakefulness and sleep. In wakefulness we see by the law of sight, and this sight has limits; it is governed by the law of light, and likewise hearing is governed by the law of sound, the wave, and the vibration.

Yet a person sleeps, closes his eyes, and sees a dream containing red, green, and other colors. By what did you perceive the colors while your eyes were closed? Thus, since among humans there is seeing without an eye, do not say about Allah's seeing us that He has eyes like our eyes; rather He sees within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. He, glorified and exalted, is the Self-Subsisting who governs His servants in time and place, in their wakefulness and in their sleep.

As an example from our daily lives: we find a man and his wife sleeping in one bed, and the man may dream that he is facing his enemies, while the wife sees herself surrounded by the happiness of her children and grandchildren; each of them wakes up to recount what he saw over more than an hour, although the human brain does not work during sleep except for seven seconds.

So, in sleep, togetherness is cancelled, and likewise time and place. If those are the laws that govern man, we must know that the Creator of all laws, who is the Truth, cannot have His attributes comprehended, and we must take them within the frame of: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾.

Thereafter, the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿Say: Shall I take other than Allah as a protector, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, while He feeds and is not fed? Say: Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit, and do not be among the polytheists.﴾ (14)

The hamza here, in (أغير) ("ghayr," "other than"), is what the scholars call *hamzat al-inkar* (the hamza of disavowal, a rhetorical interrogative of denial). It is like someone saying: "Do you insult your father?" It is not really a question so much as a reproach and a rebuke. Likewise, ﴿Shall I take other than Allah as a protector?﴾ means that the Truth is commanding His Messenger to disavow taking any protector other than Allah.

Taking Allah as one's protector is a necessity, because a human being encounters events that confirm to him that he is weak and subject to change (*aghyar*, changing circumstances). In the hour of human weakness, one must take refuge in the One who is stronger than him and does not change. The protector, who is Allah, His strength cannot become weakness, His wealth cannot turn into poverty, and His knowledge cannot revert to ignorance. He is the One who changes things, and He does not change. Therefore, among Allah's blessings upon His creatures is that He made Himself their protector. He is the Possessor of change (while being unchanging).

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, teaches His creatures to be people of wisdom, who place matters in their proper places and put their trust in Him. He is the Living who does not die. We observe that the Truth here commands His Messenger to convey (the message) on His behalf. Here the precision of the Qur'anic delivery becomes manifest: the message comes exactly as it was revealed from the Truth, word for word.

An example of this is the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿Say: He is Allah, [who is] One.﴾ (1) (Surah al-Ikhlas)

The Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) conveys to us the Qur'anic text as it was revealed to him, beginning with the word "Say" (*qul*), and he conveys it to us with the trustworthiness of one who delivers the message from his Lord. Here he says: ﴿Say: Shall I take other than Allah as a protector?﴾ This is the God whose perfections came in the preceding verses: the One who created the heavens and the earth, who made the darknesses and the light, and to whom belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day. This true God is the one worthy of worship.

The Truth wants His Messenger to draw out the answer from the people, rather than himself saying: "I do not take anyone as a protector other than Allah." Glorified is He, He commands His Messenger to ask them: ﴿Say: Shall I take other than Allah as a protector?﴾ Let the question be put forth by you, O Messenger of Allah, as a conveyance from Allah, and give them freedom in answering, and the answer will be as you wish.

When a person hears such a question, he must ask himself and turn his mind over in order to find an answer.
