A person will find no answer other than to say: "I have no protector other than Allah," for the close protector is the one who supports a person in his weakness, and if he calls out for help, comes to rescue him.

A person does not cry out for help to anyone unless a great calamity has befallen him. When the strong one comes to relieve the one who cries out, he is reassured that the one who came to him will help him and free him. Taking a protector is a natural matter in the universe, and the abhorrent thing is that a person makes for himself a protector other than Allah. We, the believers, take one another as protectors within the framework of the protection of Allah, in fulfillment of the saying of the Truth:

﴿The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾ (71) (Surah al-Tawbah)

The believing men and believing women exchange love and support according to the covenant of faith between them and the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. Some of them command others with the commands of the (divine) method, and forbid others from the prohibitions which Allah has forbidden. They draw near to the Truth by establishing prayer. They fulfill Allah's right in their wealth through zakah, obey Allah, and comply with the commands of His Messenger. By this they attain the true promise of Allah, which is mercy. He, glorified is He, is able to care for them, He is Wise in protecting them, and Mighty, none can overcome Him.

Thus, you seek a protector in a moment of weakness and in a moment of hardship. No person has all the corners of life arranged so that he becomes strong and never weakens, or becomes wealthy and never becomes poor. We know that man is subject to change. We have never seen a strong man whose strength remained established, nor a wealthy man whose riches remained established. Man is the son of change, and his states come upon him beyond his capacity. Therefore he asks who will help him and assist him. The believer also loves to be strong in order to help others, because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has distributed talents among His creatures in the universe in order to ensure the continuation and permanence of mutual protection. You are in need of the work of another person, because you are weak in one respect while others are strong in it. The doctor needs the engineer, the engineer needs the doctor, and the doctor and engineer need the farmer, the farmer needs the work of the engineer and doctor, and the doctor, engineer and farmer need the work of the lawyer.

Thus Allah distributed talents in the universe, and He did not make any one person a collection of all talents. This is so that society may support itself, not through favor and generosity, but through the mutual support of need. Every person is a master in one corner of life, and the other corners are governed by other human beings. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is We who have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and raised some of them above others in degrees [of rank] that some of them may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ (32) (From verse 32 of Surah al-Zukhruf)

This is the proclamation from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, that He distributed talents among human beings so that they may support one another, and so that some of them may employ others in meeting one another's needs, in order for the affairs of life to be organized. In this distribution there is mercy from the Truth to the creation. For if people were equal in intelligence, and all became geniuses, who would then take charge of organizing the streets? Who would carry out the work of maintaining buildings, caring for and feeding animals, and attending to their affairs, and the other matters without which life cannot be ordered?

Each of us sees the man who empties the sewage pits and goes out in the morning saying: "O Opener, O All-Knowing; O Provider, O Generous." He seeks a new sewage pit to empty, so that he may earn the sustenance of himself and his dependents. Each of us is compelled and needs others. This is the meaning of:

﴿that they may take one another in service﴾ (from verse 32 of Surah al-Zukhruf)

Therefore, taking a protector is a natural matter, and faith in Allah grants us the wisdom to choose the protector. The believing person must choose as protector the one whom he finds when he needs him, so he must choose the protection of Allah and not the protection of changing things, and Allah subjects even his enemy to serve the believer. Therefore the Truth conveys to us through the tongue of His Messenger: (Say: Shall I take other than Allah as a protector?) Those who object to us taking Allah as a protector, and want us to take other than Him, see themselves as the example... for their hope may be disappointed. A person among them may take a human like himself as a protector, and when he needs him he finds him sick, or absent, or his heart has changed toward him. But the believer chooses Allah as his protector, because He does not vanish, does not change, and does not weaken. The Qur'an does not deny that a person may take a protector from among mankind, but the Truth guides us that He is the true Protector, and that the believer must take his believing brothers as protectors, because that is a protection from Allah and for the sake of Allah.

As for you, O Muslims, when you choose the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, as your protector, He is the One who brings to you all the corners of talents, prepares them and readies them to be in your service. For He, glorified and exalted is He, is ﴿the Originator of the heavens and the earth, while He feeds and is not fed﴾, and He created the heavens and the earth, the Truth, glorified is He, without precedent. He originated this universe without any prior model. When our master Jesus, peace be upon him, wanted to prove his miracle to his people, he took clay and shaped it like a bird. So there was a model that preceded him, found it, and followed it. Jesus is a human among the creation, but the Creator of all creation created the heavens and the earth without a model. As for you, O human, you may not pay attention to the matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth, because you see them every moment in a monotonous form, and you may think it is an easy matter. But the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of the people do not know.﴾ (57) (Surah Ghafir)

He, glorified is He, affirms that the creation of the heavens and the earth is a greater and more precise matter than the creation of people, but most people do not know this.

Glorified and exalted is He, who says:

﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are expanding it.﴾ (47) (Surah al-Dhariyat)

In His saying ﴿and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ there is an indication of the creation of this visible and invisible universe, because there are many celestial bodies and solar systems, and beyond that the vastness of that universe which the mind cannot grasp nor is able to define. This astonishing vastness is from the power of Allah, glorified and exalted is He. ﴿And indeed, We are expanding it.﴾

We find the Truth using the word *Fatir* (Originator) once for a beneficial thing and once for a corrupting thing. The example of the beneficial is what the Truth says here: ﴿the Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth without a prior model and with firm power.

The Truth, glorified is He, says in another place:

﴿When the sky splits asunder.﴾ (1) (Surah al-Infitar)

That is, the Truth describes here the Day of the Greatest Terror, when the sky will split apart and the stars will fall, so that none of them will perform its function, because Allah, glorified is He, has stripped them of what made them fit.

He also says:

﴿He who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return your vision; do you see any breaks?﴾ (3) (Surah al-Mulk)

The Truth is not incapable of anything. He is the Creator of seven heavens, perfected, some above others, so the observer does not see any defect in this creation. Let the human being return his gaze to the sky and he will find no defect, whether cracks or differences.

And *futur* (فطور) here means cracks. So the Truth, with His complete power, gives each thing the attributes that make it fit to perform what it was created for, so that no one supposes it has gone beyond the power of its Creator, glorified is He. He created the heavens and the earth with complete originality and precision, and He is able to split them apart and make them unfit at any time He wills. Similarly, the sun will be folded up, the stars will be extinguished, and the mountains will be blown away.

A scholar among the learned said: "I did not understand the word *Fatir* until a Bedouin came and said: 'So-and-so disputes with me over a well that I originated (*fatartuhu*).'" That is, the Bedouin was the one who began digging the well. Thus, *Fatir al-samawat wal-ard* (Originator of the heavens and the earth) means the One who created them without a model. And glorified is He, who says:

﴿Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them, and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?﴾ (30) (Surah al-Anbiya)

This wise statement was not understood by those who came before us, but the people of this age in which we live understood it after the scholars arrived at the conclusion that the heavens and the earth were one mass, and the Truth separated them by His will, and made water the life of every living creature.

Thus He, glorified is He, is capable of all things, and nothing falls outside the scope of His power. Before He bestows upon us the favor of the creation of life, He warns us not to let this worldly life deceive us. Therefore He said:

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. [He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed; and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.﴾ (1-2) (Surah al-Mulk)

It is as if He is alerting a person to receive life, so that he knows that He, glorified is He, brought into existence the breaker of life, which is death. So beware that you take life as something that gives you strength, movement, perception, and will in a routine and everlasting way, because there is a breaker of life, which is death.

Behold, He, glorified is He, says in another place in the noble Qur'an:

﴿Have you considered that which you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator? We have decreed death among you, and We are not outdone. [That] We may replace your likenesses and produce you in [forms] you do not know.﴾ (58-61) (Surah al-Waqi'ah)

A person does not see the sperm cells ejected from him into his spouse's womb, and no one can do that, nor care for them until they become a fetus and then a human. But the Truth is the One who decrees and creates. He is the Capable who gave us life and decreed death upon us, and none can overcome Him. He changes our forms when He wills, creates others and produces us in forms we do not know. He is the Giver of life, and He is the One who takes it away by death.

He says to us:

﴿Have you considered that which you plant? Is it you who makes it grow, or are We the Grower?﴾ (63-64) (Surah al-Waqi'ah)

Here, He, may He be exalted, alerts us that the crops we eat, and the fruits we gather from the earth, we have no part in them

He is the Messenger, the chosen and the selected, the protected from sin (ma'sum), who declares that he fears God, because the decree of God is possessed by no one, and none changes the decree of God except God, glorified and exalted. He has tied the fear to a condition, which is disobedience to God. But as long as he has not disobeyed his Lord, he does not fear. The presence of (in) indicates a conditional attachment, and such a thing cannot apply to the infallible Messenger, because he does not disobey God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 16:

Allah wished to show us that the infallible (ma'sum) cannot possibly disobey Allah. Yet this statement comes on the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that we may know that there is a great punishment with which Allah threatened whoever disobeys Him. It is a punishment that presses upon the disobedient until it reaches him. This punishment has the property that between it and the disobedient there is an attraction like the attraction of a magnet to other materials. Man's deliverance from punishment requires one who turns away from him this harsh kind of punishment. Allah the Exalted says concerning it:

﴿Whoever is spared it on that Day, He has indeed shown him mercy, and that is the clear triumph.﴾ (16)

It is as if the one from whom this punishment is not turned away is one who is drawn toward the force of the punishment, because the Fire of Hell has a shahiq (inhaling roar) that draws in and pulls toward itself those upon whom punishment has been decreed. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿For those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination. When they are thrown into it, they will hear from it a roaring (shahiq) while it boils up.﴾ (Surah al-Mulk, 6-7)

Those who disbelieve in Allah have a punishment that begins with hearing Hell in the midst of its boiling. The shahiq, as you know, is a force that draws and pulls air into the nose and chest, so what then of the force of the shahiq of Hell, as it pulls and draws in those upon whom the command of punishment has fallen?

This Fire itself responds to the Truth's question to it when it hears His saying:

﴿The Day We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Are there any more?"﴾ (Surah Qaf, 30)

Thus the force of punishment which Allah made the task of Hell is what presses and surges forward seeking more punishment for the disbelievers. He, glory be to Him, created everything to perform a function, and the Fire's function is to comply with the command of the Truth, blessed and exalted, when He orders it to carry out its task. Therefore it presses eagerly for those who are to receive the punishment, and the Fire never departs from the command and decree of Allah. If the Truth turns punishment away from a servant of His servants, the Fire complies with that command. ﴿Whoever is spared it on that Day, He has indeed shown him mercy.﴾ He, glory be to Him, does whatever He wills. If He were to call us to account with justice, then each one of us would be touched by something of the punishment of Hell; but it is the mercy of Allah that keeps the Fire from touching the believers, because He, glory be to Him and exalted, pardons much. And because the Fire has a shahiq, it inhales those decreed to be punished, and we know that the shahiq takes place more quickly than the zafir (exhalation). In life, the shahiq is of air.

The reason the shahiq is faster than the zafir is that the shahiq serves the first function of sustaining life, which is supplying the body with air, and man, as we know, cannot endure without air except for the shortest possible period. And it is part of Allah's mercy that He does not own the air for anyone. This shahiq that gives life on earth also exists in the Hereafter, and it is attributed to the Fire: it inhales in order to swallow the disobedient, and in this way it performs the task entrusted to it. We also know that the Fire performs its task with rage, in accordance with the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿It almost bursts with rage.﴾ (part of verse 8, Surah al-Mulk)

Does the Fire perform its task while not content with it? Does the Fire differ from all of Allah's creatures, which perform their task with happiness and harmony? Indeed the Fire almost bursts with rage because the disbeliever among them is one who knows the value of faith, and the Fire has feelings like the rest of creation. The whole universe has feelings. The universe, for example, rejoiced at the birth of Muhammad (ﷺ); the earth, the heavens, the stars, the trees and the whole universe rejoiced at the arrival of the Noble Messenger, because all these creatures are subjected to man, glorify Allah, and are obedient by their nature, just as the bringer of good news comes to guide man to the straight path so that he becomes obedient; so they rejoice at the coming of this bearer of good news.

We know that the place in which a person dwells rejoices if the person in it is obedient, and that same place grieves if the person is disobedient, and any place is distressed by the presence of any disobedient person in it. We see this clearly in the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, concerning the people of Pharaoh:

﴿How many gardens and springs did they leave behind? And crops and noble dwellings, and comfort in which they took delight. Thus did We cause others to inherit them. So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they reprieved.﴾ (Surah al-Dukhan, 25-29)

The earth on which the people of Pharaoh lived had feelings; the gardens, rivers, springs and all the blessings with which man is blessed have feeling and sensation, and they become angry, incensed and distressed by the presence of those who disbelieve in Allah's blessing in them. For this reason, the heaven and the earth do not weep over the sinking and destruction of these disobedient, polytheist disbelievers, whereas the heaven and the earth do weep when a believer departs from them. For us, in the saying of Imam 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, there is an explanation of this; he said: "When the believer dies, two places weep for him: a place in the heaven and a place on the earth. As for his place in the heaven, it is the ascent of his good deeds; and as for his place on the earth, it is the place of his prayer."

And in the hadith: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening. If he is of the people of Paradise, then he is of the people of Paradise; and if he is of the people of the Fire, then he is of the people of the Fire. It is said to him: 'This is your seat until Allah resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection.'" (1)

Thus the place where a person's deeds ascend grieves, because there is the loss of a righteous deed that passed through it; and the place of a person's prayer loses the prostration of a man in humility before Allah. Every created being has feelings, and everything in the universe performs its function by the law of direction and subjection, not the law of choice. Man alone lives by the law of choice in some of his conditions, because he is able to obey and able to disobey. Therefore, when we see prostration to Allah in the Qur'an, we hear the saying of the Truth:

﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures, and many among mankind? But many are deserving of punishment. And whoever Allah humiliates, for him there is no honouring. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 18)

Thus all creatures prostrate to Him, except that among mankind, some of each individual prostrates to Allah while many are deserving of punishment because they do not obey the Truth. Whoever disobeys the method of Allah without believing in it, Allah expels from His mercy, and whoever Allah humiliates has no honour ever. The universe is unanimous in prostration to Allah, except for man: among them is the righteous one whose deeds harmonize with the submission of the universe to Allah, and the universe rejoices at him; and among them is one at whom the universe is angry because he disobeys Allah.

The Arabic language makes this clear to us. The Arabs say: "So-and-so, the earth has rejected him (nabata bihi al-ardu) from nubuwwa, which is coarseness, distance and aversion," meaning that the earth dislikes a particular person, because there is no harmony between the earth and a disobedient being.

The Truth says of those from whom punishment is turned away, out of the abundance of His mercy toward His servants, because they obeyed Him, and their sins overcame them at times, so they repent of them:

﴿Whoever is spared it on that Day, He has indeed shown him mercy, and that is the clear triumph.﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 16)

We know that this triumph is the highest degree of triumph, for triumph has degrees. Worldly triumph, such as success, wealth or other things, is a triumph exposed to being lost; it is liable to be abandoned by man or to abandon him. But the triumph of the Hereafter is the lasting triumph that does not end.

This is the difference between the blessings of this world and the blessings of the Hereafter. A person enjoys comfort in this world according to his conception of comfort. For example, the villager imagines comfort as a bench in front of his house on which to sit, and a number of jars filled with pure water; but if this villager moves to the city, he imagines comfort as a spacious home with luxurious furniture and electrical appliances such as a refrigerator and so on. So the possibilities of comfort differ according to a person's conception. As for the comfort of the Hereafter, it is a comfort that a person neither misses nor is missed by, because it is a comfort made by the Creator, the Vast in giving... Indeed, Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Therefore, triumph in the comfort of the Hereafter is the clear triumph.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, encompasses everything in knowledge and power:

﴿If Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things capable.﴾ (17)

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from Ibn 'Umar.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 17:

Al-ḍurr (harm, affliction) is whatever befalls a living being and takes it out of the proper soundness of its life and condition. When a person lives without complaint or sickness and feels complete well-being, he knows that he is healthy, because he feels no pain in his eyes, no tightness in his breathing, or anything else. But the moment one of the organs of his body hurts him, he places his hand on it, complains, and thinks of going to the doctor. Thus the soundness of health for a human being is the smooth, unnoticed functioning of every organ in him, in a way that does not draw his attention to anything.

Affliction also draws the attention of those who possess blessings when they see someone around them who has lost some blessing. When you walk in the street and see a person who has lost his leg, you say, "Praise be to God," because you have sound legs. It is as if you do not perceive God's blessing in some part of you except when you see it lost in another. In this way we know that pains and afflictions are reminders of blessings. Also, the troubles of life may befall a person so that he knows he has not been given all of God's blessings, and the servant then says at that moment: "O Reliever of distresses, O Lord." That is why you find a person saying "O Lord" when an affliction comes upon him and he turns to God in fear. God has said this about man:

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing. But when We remove from him his harm, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us to remove a harm that touched him. Thus is made attractive to the transgressors what they have been doing.﴾ (Surah Yunus, 12).

So when man senses his weakness upon being struck by something disagreeable, he never tires of calling upon God, whether he is lying down, sitting, or standing. But when the Truth removes the harm from him, he may turn away from the side of God and resume disobeying God, as if he had never called upon God to remove the harm. This is the conduct of those who are wasteful against themselves through disobedience to God. The self or the devil makes disobedience appealing to the sinner after the harm has been removed, so that he plunges deeper and deeper into the wells of sins and the mire of vice.

A person may attribute the removal of harm to other than God, ascribing the removal of harm to the skill of the doctor to whom he turned, forgetting that the doctor's skill is itself one of God's blessings. Or he may attribute the causes of his escape from his distress to the knowledge or wealth that God gave him, forgetting that God is the Bestower of everything, as Qarun did when he thought his wealth had come to him from his toil, effort, work, and skill, forgetting that the Truth is the Causer of all causes, of harm or benefit. Glory be to Him, it is He who causes harm just as He causes benefit.

Harm also draws man's attention to the blessings of the Truth, glorified and exalted, in this world. When a person is content and patient, God removes the harm from him, because harm does not persist upon a person except when he meets it with anger and non-acceptance of God's decree. The Truth does not lift a decree over creation unless the creatures of God are content with what God has sent down, and the one who does not accept calamities is the one with whom calamities persist. As for the one who wants God to lift the decree from him, let him accept the decree.

The Truth, glorified be He, gives us models of this matter. Behold our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, who receives the command to slaughter his only son, and this command comes in a form that the one who does not believe in God's decree may see as extremely harsh. Ibrahim had to slaughter his son with his own hands, and this is an elevation of the trial. Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, did not seek an excuse to escape God's trial, and he did not say, "It is merely a dream and not revelation," but it was true. The command came to him in the lightest form of obligation, which is a dream, and in the most grievous form of obligation, which is slaughtering the son. We see the greatness of prophethood in receiving the commands of the Truth. God inspires him to make his son Isma'il share in receiving the reward by being content with the decree:

﴿And when he reached with him the age of exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I sacrifice you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if God wills, among the steadfast."﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 102).

Isma'il had reached the age of exertion in the affairs of life with his father when the command came to Ibrahim in a dream to slaughter his son. Isma'il's heart was filled with contentment with God's decree, and he was not preoccupied with resisting his father. He did not resist and did not enter into a struggle, but said:

﴿O my father, do as you are commanded.﴾ (part of verse 102, Surah al-Saffat).

The two of them accepted God's command with contentment, and therefore the Truth says of them both together:

﴿So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead, We called to him, "O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, this is the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 103-107).

The two of them shared in accepting God's decree, and each of them submitted to the command: Ibrahim submitted as the doer, and Isma'il submitted as the one acted upon. God knew their sincerity in receiving God's command. Here the Truth called to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: "You and Isma'il have responded to the decree, and this submission suffices for you. Therefore, kindness comes to you and to your son, namely the lifting of the trial." The ransom came as a sacrifice of great magnitude, because it was a slaughter that came by God's command. The Truth did not stop there, but gave Ibrahim the good news of another son:

﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 112).

God lifted the decree from Ibrahim, gave him good, and that good was another son. Thus we humans prolong the period of the decree upon ourselves after we have accepted it. But if an affair falls upon a person without his having any cause in it, and he receives it from its Sender, who is his Lord, with the station of contentment, then the Truth, glorified and exalted, lifts the decree from him. So when you see a person whose decree has lasted long, know that he lacks contentment.

We note that here the Truth says: ﴿And if God touches you with harm, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent.﴾ God, glorified and exalted, knows that no servant can bear that the Truth should harm him; the power of the Truth is limitless, and therefore it is a touch of harm, and likewise a touch of good. A person in this world does not attain all good, but attains only a touch of good; all good is stored for him in the Hereafter. We know that the good of this world either leaves the person or he leaves it, but all good is in the Hereafter.

No matter how far man advances in innovation and invention, he will not reach all the good that exists in the Hereafter, because the good of this world requires preparation and effort from humans, whereas the good of the Hereafter is in proportion to the Greatest Giver, who is God, glorified and exalted. Thus all the good of this world is merely a touch of good, because the good that befits the beauty and perfection of God does not cease, does not change, and does not alter, and it is stored for the Hereafter. There is no remover of harm except God. The sick person is not cured merely by going to the doctor, but the doctor treats with the skill that God has bestowed upon him, and it is God who heals:

﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me.﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara, 80).

Because God, glorified and exalted, created the disease and created the remedy, and made the physicians merely bridges from the disease to the remedy and then to the cure. God creates the means so that He may make His servants happy and pleased by them, making the gifts as means, though the matter in reality is in His hand, glorified be He. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Seek treatment, O servants of God, for God, the Exalted, has not placed a disease without placing for it a remedy, except one disease: old age."(1)

We see that the outstanding physician always declares that cure came with him, not by him, and acknowledges that God honored him by making the cure come at an appointed time through his treatment. Thus the Truth is the Remover of harm, and He is capable of granting you good and withholding it. His power has no limits.

1. Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim from Usama ibn Sharik.

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware (18).﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted, has arranged the universe and creation through causes and effects (asbab wa musabbabat). Every existing thing is an intermediary between one thing and another: the earth is an intermediary for the reception of plants, and the human being is an intermediary between his father and his son. Let us all understand that the Truth is above His servants; He is Dominant by His power, He manages the universe with wisdom and comprehensive knowledge, and He is Aware of everything hidden and Knowing of everything manifest. And He is the One who said:

﴿Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you into sects and make you taste the violence of one another. Look how We vary the signs that they may understand (65).﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

Glorified and exalted is He: He has absolute power to send punishment from the sky or from within the earth, or to make among the servants enmity and mutual strife, so that some of them repel others, so that the earth is not corrupted. ﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted.﴾

So beware, O human being, lest you suppose that when the Truth gives some of creation possession of causes, they are in fact the possessors of the causes. No! Allah, glorified, intended by this the arrangement of works in the universe. Therefore, whenever we see one wrongdoer oppressing in the universe, we find another wrongdoer who disciplines the first wrongdoer. The Truth does not discipline the wicked through the hand of a good man; rather He disciplines him through a wicked one like himself:

﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn (129).﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

Because Allah, glorified and exalted, honours the wronged one from among the people of piety by not letting him have a role in disciplining the wrongdoer; rather, Allah takes vengeance on the wrongdoer through a wrongdoer like him or stronger than him. This is what we see across recent and distant history. When the righteous servant gains power over those who wronged him, he says what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said when he entered Makkah, when he said: (O assembly of Quraysh, what do you think I will do with you? They said: Good, a noble brother and the son of a noble brother. He said: Go, for you are the freed ones (al-tulaqa').)(1)

As for when Allah wills the vengeance upon a wicked person, He sends upon him another wicked one like him who breaks his neck, or slits his nose, or humiliates him so that corruption does not spread and flourish. Glorified is He, the Subduer over His servants, and His subjugation is with wisdom and knowledge, not subjugation of arrogance, tyranny and domination. To clarify this: Allah may apply a decree (qadar) to one of His servants such that the arm of his son is broken; the man takes his son to an inexperienced doctor to set a splint for the son's arm, and the bones heal under this splint out of their proper place; so the man takes his son to a skilled doctor, who breaks the child's arm again in order to reset the bones in their correct place.

This breaking was for a wisdom, namely the straightening of the bones and their proper placement. No servant of the servants ever angers the Creator, but the Truth vindicates the one who has been wronged. We know that the human being is free to choose between faith and disbelief; if he disbelieves and disobeys, then in the Hereafter he has nothing but punishment. However, Allah makes the decree of illness apply to him so that he cannot rebel against it, because He, glorified, is the Subduer over His servants, as evidenced by His controlling things in which the servants have no choice. And as long as the human being among us is governed by two bows (qawsayn) and has no say in his birth or death, why then, rebellion through disobedience against the commands of Allah? Let us know that the Truth is the Subduer over His servants by the subjugation of wisdom, and He, glorified, places for every matter the domain that suits it, and He is Aware of the locations of ailments, and treats His servants of them according to what He sees.

1 Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan 1/118 and in Tarikh al-Tabari 3/61.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 19:

Then Allah, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say: "Allah is Witness between me and you. This Qur'an has been revealed to me so that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches. Do you indeed testify that there are other gods besides Allah?" Say: "I do not testify to that." Say: "He is only One God, and I am free of what you associate with Him."﴾ (19)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disagreed with the hostile people who opposed him. Disagreement requires a judge and proof. Witnesses are one kind of proof, so what of when the Witness is Allah? He is the Witness, the Judge, and the Executor. Allah's testimony involves no deception, His judgment involves no injustice, and His will does not wrong a servant even by the weight of an atom. So the greatest testimony is the testimony of the Truth to His Messenger that he is a messenger from Allah. Had Allah willed, He would have made you all believers, but He willed for humans to have choice. The compassion of the Messenger (ﷺ) toward mankind is what made him wish for their faith, but the Truth says to the Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Perhaps you will destroy yourself with grief that they do not become believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so their necks would remain humbled before it.﴾ (Surah ash-Shu'ara', 3-4)

That is, Allah commands the Messenger (ﷺ) to have pity on himself and not to kill himself with grief over them, because of their obstinacy and their unbelief. Had Allah willed, He would have made them all believers with a sign from Him. The task of the Messenger is only to convey. Had Allah willed, He could have compelled all creation to believe in Him, just as He subjected the universe to serve man and to glorify Allah's praise. But He, glorified is He, left creatures their choice, so that their faith comes as proof of the quality of being beloved to Allah, because the faith of one who chose is what establishes that beloved status. The Messenger (ﷺ) is only a warner and a bringer of good news by this Qur'an revealed to him through inspiration.

The warning comes here because the context is one of testimony, since testimony is given in cases of disagreement. He (ﷺ) calls to faith, while his opponents call to disbelief and to polytheism, and the testimony of Allah is greater than every other testimony. Therefore the Truth establishes here that the Messenger is a warner by the Qur'an. This address is directed to conveying the message to the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and to whoever received any part of the Qur'an after them, as if they had seen the Prophet (ﷺ) and the message from him had reached them. He, glorified is He, said: "whoever it reaches," meaning: so that I may warn you by it, and warn every human being whom the Qur'an reaches.

The Truth, through the tongue of His Messenger, directs to the opponents a rhetorical question: ﴿Do you indeed testify that there are other gods besides Allah?﴾ It is a question from one who is confident that whoever hears his question must deny the existence of other gods besides Allah. It is a question that draws out acknowledgment from the listener. An example of this is what the Truth presented to His Messenger about an event that happened in the year of his birth, when He says:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (Surah al-Fil, 1)

We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not see what happened in the Year of the Elephant, because it was the year of his birth. But when Allah informs him of it, this means it is a report from Allah, and a report from Allah makes the news that comes from Him greater than sight, more reliable and more emphatic than it. Here comes the rhetorical question: "Do you indeed testify that there are other gods besides Allah?" When this question left some of them unable to answer at certain stages of the call, some of them said:

﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in nearness.﴾ (part of verse 3, Surah az-Zumar)

As if they had finally acknowledged that the One sought for nearness is Allah. But the Truth settles the matter of polytheism, saying on the tongue of His Messenger: ﴿Say: "I do not testify to that. Say: He is only One God, and I am free of what you associate with Him."﴾ So the Messenger (ﷺ) does not testify to any gods other than Allah, and he cast the rhetorical question to them, perhaps they would turn their heads to be guided to the correct answer, which the Truth summarizes in His saying to the Messenger: ﴿Say: He is only One God, and I am free of what you associate with Him.﴾

The speech here is addressed to a group of the opponents of the Messenger of Allah, from among the idol-worshippers, who are some of those who disbelieved in the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the others are some of the People of the Book, those who neglected the scriptures revealed to them, and the leavening elements of faith that used to turn the disobedient away from disobedience were absent from them, so corruption spread through the world. For this reason the Truth sent His Messenger (ﷺ), because the disobedient one found no one to restrain him, and in that society at that time the self-reproaching soul disappeared and the commanding-to-evil soul prevailed.

The Truth, glorified is He, did not leave the matter of the Messenger hidden from mankind. Every nation's messenger used to foretell and announce the messenger who would come after him, so that people would prepare to receive the warner and the bringer of good news. For this reason every revelation foretold the coming messengers, so that no one would think that a claimant had broken into the sanctity of their religion. And because Islam came as a universal religion, the report about Muhammad (ﷺ) did not come only in the earlier scriptures, but his attributes and characteristics also came clearly and explicitly in them.

Those who read these descriptions, if they freed themselves from their worldly authority, would have believed immediately in the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as ('Abdullah ibn Salam) (may Allah be pleased with him) did when he said: "I recognized him when I saw him, and I recognized him as I recognize my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is stronger." Those people forgot that they had in fact supported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without realizing it, for they used to seek victory through him over al-Aws and al-Khazraj, and they said to al-Aws and al-Khazraj: "The coming of a prophet from among you is near; we will believe in him, follow him, and kill you with him, the killing of 'Ad and Iram." And al-Aws and al-Khazraj hastened to believe in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "Perhaps this is the prophet with whom the Jews threatened us. Come, let us hasten to him."

Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not burst upon the world with this religion; rather, everyone who had a connection to a scripture of the heavens knew the news of his coming, his mission, his appearance and his description. They know that he is the final Messenger, with whom the news from heaven to earth was sealed.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost their souls, they do not believe.﴾ (6:20)

So the Messenger of Allah was known in advance by the People of the Book, as they know their sons; but some of them preferred temporal authority (al-sultah al-zamaniyyah) over faith in the Messenger of Allah, and so they lost their souls. For loss, as we know, is the loss of capital or its diminishment. They lost their souls because those souls should have been eager for the welfare of the spirits which Muhammad (ﷺ) came to reform. By this they deprived their own souls of good, by preferring the worldly power that passes away over faith in God, and in that lies a great disappointment.

God teaches us that faith is only a gain for the soul. So beware, O believer, of thinking that your saying "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh) is a support for the Throne of God. No, it is a support for you yourself; for "there is no god but God" is the creation of the universe and of creation with the attributes of perfection, power, knowledge and wisdom, and an acknowledgment by creation of the divinity of God alone. The creatures' acknowledgment of God's sole divinity does not add to God's perfection, but it benefits the servants who believe, so that they receive well the command to build up the universe, so that the movement of life proceeds in the light of God's method, and they harmonize with the whole universe that glorifies God.

And when the Truth says:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost their souls, they do not believe.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

He is informing the people of Makkah that the cry of faith which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cried into their ears was not a surprise to the cosmos, but a cry foretold on the tongue of every messenger. If the people of Makkah were far removed from the messengers and prophets and were in a period of interruption between messengers (fatrah), they had as neighbours, in Madinah, People of the Book who knew this truth that their messengers had brought, confirming the covenant God had taken from them. For we know that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, when He created creation and settled them on earth, willed them to be endowed by His power with power, by His self-sufficiency with self-sufficiency, by His perfect knowledge with knowledge, by His absolute wisdom with wisdom, by His perfect mercy with mercy, and by God's dominance with dominance; for the universe cannot be upright unless these complementary attributes are found in it, even if they seem contradictory, because each attribute has its own sphere in which it operates.

Consider this example — and to God belongs the highest example: we find that a man who always shows mercy to his son spoils the son, and even if he never punishes him once, his fatherhood is deficient. Therefore, the one who dominates creation cannot be merely merciful, but must also be dominant, because the situation may require dominance. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, does not wish to stamp His creatures with one single trait, but He wishes to make them respond to the different situations; so in a situation requiring mercy they are merciful, and in a situation requiring severity and firmness they are severe. Therefore the Truth says concerning the believers:

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are hard against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from God and His pleasure.﴾ (part of 48:29)

The Truth tells us about the character of the believers. He, glorified is He, did not stamp them with harshness, for situations may require mercy; but firmness is required in confronting the people of falsehood. Nor did the Truth stamp them with gentleness, but gentleness is required among themselves, because each of them hopes for God's mercy and bounty; so in the situation requiring mercy they are merciful, and in the situation requiring firmness they are firm. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, also says of the believers:

﴿Humble towards the believers, mighty towards the disbelievers.﴾ (part of 5:54)

The Truth did not make the believer humble absolutely, nor mighty absolutely; rather He made him humble towards his believing brother, gentle of side and wide of character, and mighty towards the disbelievers who are obstinate against God.

Therefore, He, glorified is He, wants His creatures to be upon the character of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. Hence the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, as related by ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir (may Allah be pleased with him): "Good character is the greatest of God's creation" (1). And it is narrated: "Take on the characteristics of God."

God, glorified and exalted is He, has wise power; so take, O believers, His power and use it wisely; God has knowledge, so strive to be knowledgeable; God has mercy, so strive to be merciful; and God is the Compeller, so if the situation requires of you to be compelling, then do so, for the governance of the earth and the governance of society may not be set right except by this.

Since the Truth has willed that the creatures should populate this universe, He must guarantee for them a sound method based on "do" (if'al) and "do not" (lā taf'al). If we take God's method, we take what may be called the present convention: "the law of preservation." So let us do what God has said to do, and let us leave what God has said not to do, until the human machine performs its task as God wills it to be.

Corruption arises only from your moving actions, O human, from the sphere of "do" into the sphere of "do not," and from moving the actions God placed in the sphere of "do not" into the sphere of "do." If God commands us to establish prayer with "do," how can we place it in the sphere of "do not" after prayer? And if God commands us not to drink wine, how then would we drink it?

The corruption of faith that arises in the universe comes only from transferring the objects of "do" into "do not," and the objects of "do not" into "do." As for what is not marked by either "do" or "do not," God has left it to your choice, permitting you to do it or not, because the universe is not corrupted by any of these.

If you look at God's method of "do" and "do not," you will find that the Truth, glorified is He, has not abolished your freedom nor your choice; rather He has controlled you with a firm control in what gives rise to the corruption of the universe. As for what does not give rise to corruption, if you wish, do it, and if you wish, leave it. The Truth equipped all humanity with this method from Adam until the Hour rises. He, glorified is He, took upon Himself the promise not to punish a nation to which He had sent no messenger; therefore the procession of messengers continued. Why? Because heedlessness takes hold of a human being; a person may forget once the thing that limits his movement, and the forgetting is repeated until it becomes oblivion. So God wills to send a messenger for every period to alert to the law of human preservation, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and God granted security to the community of Muhammad that it would be the one to convey God's method until the Hour rises. Therefore He took a covenant from the prophets to convey the message of the final Prophet:

﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him and you shall support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My covenant on that condition?" They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ (3:81)

Therefore God took the covenant from every prophet that he should convey to his people that they should believe in the messenger whose call agrees with their call, and the Truth took acknowledgment from every prophet concerning that; the prophets bore witness against themselves, God bore witness against them, and they conveyed that to their peoples. Thus the support of the final Prophet is present in every message before Islam, and every messenger had to explain that covenant to his people, to take from them the covenant to support the messenger who would come to them, and to inform them that it is part of complete faith that they support that messenger for those who lived in his time.

The Truth here specifies the People of the Book, to whom the Torah and the Gospel were revealed, the two great religions that preceded Islam: ﴿those to whom We have given the Book recognize him as they recognize their sons﴾, meaning they know Muhammad (ﷺ) through the glad tidings of him, through reports about him, and through the description of his form and appearance. So if the disbelievers of Quraysh were in a period between messengers, let them ask the People of the Book. The Aws and the Khazraj heard from the People of the Book that there was a prophet soon to come, whom they would believe in, follow, and with whom they would slay the Arabs with a slaying like that of ʿĀd and Iram. Thus the cry of faith on the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not a surprise to the cosmos, even if those among the People of the Book who disbelieved concealed it. These are the ones of whom the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them, and before that they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (2:89)

The disease that denies this message from God afflicted some of the People of the Book; for they took, though they were the ones conveying from God, temporal authority (al-sultah al-zamaniyyah), and they brought into it fortune, rank and luxury. Among them were judges, to whom people turn to learn the ruling on blood, and they also took the alms. They became accustomed to a life of lordship and comfort. And behold, a new call has come to strip them of this lordship; and although they had been the ones announcing it beforehand, when the call came their temporal authority was shaken, and therefore they began hostility.

So the disease is taking a temporal authority from within the authority of God and then claiming that it is the authority of God. When we look at religious history in the world, we find that the temporal authority in the religions that preceded Islam is what exhausted the universe; for when the Truth, glorified is He, created the universe, He buried in it secrets that work in the service of humanity, even if humanity does not know of them. Human scientific aspirations are what lead him to these secrets and uncover the laws by which they operate; for example, the law of gravity, and the law of positive and negative, all these laws exist in the universe, just as God created the earth spherical and made the sun the source of heat, warmth, light and radiance.

Scientists take from these premises to arrive at discovering the laws of these celestial bodies and the laws of this universe. When the intelligent scientist arrives at discovering a law, he says: "I have discovered such-and-such," and this is a precise natural expression; he never says: "I have invented such-and-such," because he knows that what he discovered existed in the universe but was not known. Human ignorance of a law existing in the universe does not prevent benefit from reaching humanity, even if knowledge of the law would increase the possibility of benefiting from it.

Human beings enjoy the existence of the sun before knowing the energy in it; but when scientists specialized in studying the sun, they found that humanity can benefit from this energy far more than from its traditional use. Therefore some cities now light their streets with solar energy, and some buildings heat their rooms with solar energy and heat water with it as well. The discovery did not prevent the unlettered person or the Bedouin in the desert from benefiting from the sunlight. Likewise electricity, and the electrical and household devices which the ignorant can use just as the expert does. It is true that the unlettered person does not know how the factories that produce television sets operate, yet he benefits by watching television. Television is nothing but a material translation of a set of scientific laws which humanity discovered and put into practice to manufacture this device from which humanity benefits.

Every secret has a birth, just like the birth of a human being. When the time of a secret's birth arrives and there is no one searching for it, God reveals it by chance to whatever human He wills; and we often hear that a scientist was searching in one field but discovered a secret other than the one he was seeking. Therefore the Truth says, in the Verse of the Throne:

﴿And they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills.﴾ (part of 2:255)

So you, O human, do not comprehend the secrets of the universe except when God permits; and there is—

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 21:

The Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾

They fabricated a lie against Allah when they did that: they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of, they concealed some of the scriptures sent down to them, they distorted the verses sent down to them, and they brought statements of their own and attributed them to Allah. For this reason we find the Truth, glorified is He, saying about them:

﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah)

The Truth threatens them with punishment because they sold the religion for a small price in this world, and they claimed falsely against Allah, attributing to Him what He did not send down. Therefore, woe, all woe, is theirs, because they have sunk to the lowest depths of injustice and deliberately denied a binding universal principle, which is belief in Allah, in the revealed books and in the messengers.

Al-iftira' (fabrication) is the deliberate lie aimed at attributing to Allah something He did not say, and they have indeed done that. Hence "the wrongdoers will not succeed," whether they wrong people by taking their wealth or harming them, or wrong themselves by associating partners with Allah, which is the greatest injustice: ﴿Indeed, association [of partners with Allah] is a great injustice.﴾

Almighty Allah reminds us of the Day of Gathering, the Day when Allah will question those who associated partners with Him, who denied and fabricated lies against Allah: "Where are those you worshipped and associated with Me?" Allah will not leave people neglected; rather, every deed a person performs in the world is counted against him, and he will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection. Allah will ask the polytheists about those they worshipped besides Allah falsely: "Where are these gods whom the disbelievers associated with Allah in worship?" And why do they not come forward to rescue their worshippers from the punishment that Allah makes them burn in? And He, glory be to Him, rebukes the polytheists and gathers them together with what they worshipped besides Allah of idols and images, and in that is the utmost humiliation for them and for those gods.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 23:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿Then their trial (fitnatuhum) was only that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ (6:23)

We know that fitnah (trial, testing) means examination. Trials have many means. You test a thing in order to know the bad from the good and the genuine from the counterfeit. We test gold and refine it in fire, and likewise silver. Thus we see that fitnah in itself is not blameworthy; what is blameworthy or praiseworthy is the result we obtain from the trial. The examinations we set for our children are a fitnah: whoever passes the examination rejoices, and whoever fails grieves. So the result is what a person rejoices in or grieves over, and in this way fitnah is something required in one who has choice. Sometimes fitnah is also applied to a thing that takes hold of a person in falsehood.

Indeed, the Truth gathers the polytheists together with the gods they associated with Him, and asks them about these gods, and they say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ Outwardly they are defending themselves, and inwardly they know the complete truth, which is that the dominion belongs entirely to Allah. On the Last Day there are no partners of Allah, for there is no choice for a human being on the Last Day. But when a human being had choice in the world, he had before him the option either to believe or to disbelieve. The faith of the world, which results from choice, is what the reckoning of the Last Day is established upon. As for faith under compulsion on the Last Day, there is no reward for it except Hell for whoever disbelieved or associated partners with Allah in the world. Had Allah willed to give all of us faith under compulsion in the world, He would have compelled us to obey Him just as He did with the angels and with all the rest of His creation.

The Truth, glory be to Him, has subdued all kinds of existence except the human being, and subjugation of kinds was for establishing power, but honor for the human being came through choice, so that he might come to Allah through love.

The Truth confronts those who associate others with Allah on the Day of Resurrection by declaring that there is no god but Him, and they try to lie in an attempt to escape punishment, saying: ﴿We were not polytheists.﴾ They had indeed actually denied Allah in life, and on the Last Day they wish to lie against Allah in speech. But Allah knows the secrets of the breasts and what conduct occurred in the worldly life, and He shows them their deeds in the Hereafter and punishes them with painful punishment.

When the Truth asks them: ﴿Where are your partners?﴾ (6:22), this utterance is a question from Allah, and a question from the All-Knowing is not intended for knowledge; rather, it is intended to obtain acknowledgment from the one questioned. In our daily life we can see a question from a student to his teacher, so that the student may learn what he does not know. And we see a question come from a teacher to his student again and again, not so that he may learn what he does not know, but so that the student may affirm what he knows and what he has learned from his teacher. So when the Truth asks His creatures a question, does He ask them in order to know? Far be it from Allah that the matter be so. Rather, the Truth asks His servants so that it may be a question of acknowledgment. And acknowledgment here also contains rebuke, because it is a question that has no answer, for far be it from Allah that He should have partners. When the Truth says to them: ﴿Where are your partners?﴾, the meaning is the denial that He, glory be to Him, could have partners. Thus the Truth rebukes and reproaches them for having associated with Allah something that has no existence.

They associated partners with Allah in the world merely to be free of the obligations of faith. And here they are, in the great scene, recognizing that He has refuted them in the world, that no one has dominion except Allah and there is no worshipped one besides Him, so they speak what they bear witness to: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

One may say: but in another place in the Qur'an we find that Allah says of such people:

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers. This is a day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to offer excuses.﴾ (Surat al-Mursalat 77:34-36)

On the day of the Great Terror they know that they lied in the world, and they do not speak any word that benefits them, and the Truth does not permit them to present excuses or apologies. We say to whoever thinks that the deniers do not speak: indeed they do not speak in a way that rescues them from the punishment that awaits them, and they fall into utter astonishment and bewilderment. Indeed, some of these deniers of Allah and the Last Day may have done something from which humanity benefited, or by which the lives of people were advanced, and they think that this deed will save them. These may indeed take their share and reward from the people for whose sake they worked, and the honor of humanity toward them, but they will receive punishment on the Last Day because they associated partners with Allah. The Truth was not in their minds for a moment when they produced what they produced of inventions, and therefore the Truth says:

﴿As for those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and he finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ (Surat al-Nur 24:39)

Thus we know that the deeds of the disbelievers or polytheists, the Truth, glory be to Him, repays them for in justice in the world with wealth or fame, but they are deeds that avail them nothing in the Hereafter. Their deeds are like the glittering sheen that results from the sun's rays falling upon a wide expanse of desert, which the thirsty one takes for water, and as soon as he approaches it he finds it of no benefit to him; likewise the deeds of the disbelievers or polytheists, they find them worth nothing on the Day of Resurrection. The polytheist among them knows the reality of his shirk on the Day of Resurrection, and finds none before him but the One, the Irresistible, so each of them says: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ The polytheist among them denies his shirk, and this denial is a form of lying.

Indeed the polytheists lie, and He, glory be to Him, says of them:

﴿On the day when Allah raises them all up and they swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think they are upon something. Indeed, they are the liars.﴾ (Surat al-Mujadila 58:18)

When the Truth raises them on the Day of Resurrection, they swear to Him that they were believers, as they used to swear in the world, but Allah describes them as liars. They were able to deceive people in the world with false oaths, but what of Allah, whom no one can deceive?

Thus we see that the trial of these people is a great trial:

﴿Then their trial was only that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ (Surat al-An'am 6:23)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 24:

Then God says to His Messenger (ﷺ) after that:

﴿Look how they have lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them (24).﴾

God draws the attention of His Messenger (ﷺ) precisely to a process that will take place on the Day of Resurrection. When God reports a matter, let us accept that it has already come to pass, as if we were seeing it before us as an undeniable reality. He, glory be to Him, determines that they have lied against themselves. We know that all actions are stripped of their temporality when they are attributed to God, the Exalted. With God there is no past, present or future act.

An example of this is His saying:

﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him (1).﴾ (Surah al-Nahl)

No one may say: how can the Truth say that His command "has come", which is a past verb, and then forbid His servants from hastening it, when a person only hastens something that has not yet happened? No one may say that, because the Speaker is the Supreme Power, and nothing prevents the Truth from doing what He wills. As for us servants, we do not dare to say about an act we will do tomorrow that we have already done it, for tomorrow may never come, or tomorrow may come and we may be unable to do anything of what we were promised, or circumstances may change for us. Suppose all conditions have become favourable: what power does any of us have to do anything without God willing it? We, the believers, know this, and we must say as God has taught us:

﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed I will do that tomorrow," (23) except [adding], "If God wills."﴾ (Part of verse 23 and part of verse 24 of Surah al-Kahf)

In this way a person ensures that he has left the sphere of lying. When God says to His Messenger "Look" (انظر), and this concerns a matter whose time of seeing has not yet come, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) affirms his Lord's word as if he had seen this matter. The Truth describes these people as: ﴿they have lied against themselves⦆, meaning that their lie, which will occur on the Day of Resurrection, is a matter that has already actually happened. A person may lie for his own benefit in this world, but lying before God is at the expense of the person, not to his benefit.

The Truth continues: ﴿and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them﴾. This means that on the Last Day they will search for the partners, but they will be unable to identify those partners, because they said before God: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾. Their absence before God is what His saying clarifies: ﴿and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them﴾. Here "vanished" (ضل) means "disappeared" (غاب). Did they not say before:

﴿And they say, "When we are lost in the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?" Rather, they are in disbelief in the meeting with their Lord (10).﴾ (Surah al-Sajdah)

They, as deniers of the Resurrection, ask in astonishment: if they vanish into the earth and mix with their elements, can their Lord resurrect them anew? They do not believe that He who originated them the first time is able to return them a second time. We know that the word (ضل) has many meanings.

But its meaning here is "disappeared" (غاب). When God asks them, "Where are your partners?", they falsely deny that they associated anyone with Him. Those partners have vanished from them, that is, disappeared from them. A person worships the god who benefits him on the Day of Gathering, and when the gods disappear on the Day of Gathering, this shows the misguidance of those gods and their absence at the time of need for them, and nothing remains but the Face of God, who calls to account those who associated others with Him.

(ضل) is opposed by (اهتدى, guided). (ضل) means not taking the path that leads to the goal, and (اهتدى) means taking the path that leads to the goal. Whoever does not know the path that leads to the goal has also gone astray, but there is one who goes astray while knowing the path that leads to the goal, and this is disbelief (kufr). When the Truth speaks of those who disbelieve, He describes them as having gone far astray, because the way to guidance was before them and they did not take it, and this is the misguidance of the summit. A person may be a believer, but the foundations of faith are weak in him, so he disobeys his Lord.

The Truth says of such a person:

﴿And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ (Part of verse 36 of Surah al-Ahzab)

This is a misguidance short of misguidance, and a disbelief short of the disbelief of the summit. But what of one who goes astray because he does not know the way of guidance? This is what appears to us from the story of our master Moses (peace be upon him). When the Truth said to Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them both:

﴿So go to Pharaoh and say, "Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds (16), [saying], 'Send with us the Children of Israel.'" (17)﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara')

He issued the command to Moses and Aaron to go to Pharaoh so that he would send the Children of Israel with them. What then was Pharaoh's position? What did Pharaoh say?

﴿[Pharaoh] said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life? (18) And you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful." (19)﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara')

Here Pharaoh wants to remind Moses of a favour: that he raised him in his palace until he grew up, and yet Moses did not respect that, and killed a man of Pharaoh's people. In Pharaoh's view, this was a kind of ingratitude for his blessing. And here he is, again encroaching upon Pharaoh's divinity by calling him to faith in the true God, whom Pharaoh cannot imagine. Moses picks up the essential error in his behaviour at that time. The error was not disbelief in Pharaoh, but the killing. So he says:

﴿[Moses] said, "I did it, then, while I was of those astray." (20)﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara')

Thus we know that Moses, at the moment of killing a man of his enemy, did not possess the way of guidance. Rather, his misguidance arose from his not knowing that there was another path to guidance. Behold, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, addresses the Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿And He found you lost and guided you. (7)﴾ (Surah al-Duha). That is: before the prophethood you had no clear path to guidance, O Messenger of God. So the meaning of misguidance here is not deviation, but that before the revelation descended you did not know which path to take. Misguidance may also be forgetfulness, and whenever a person has forgotten the truth, he is astray. An example is the Truth's saying:

﴿So that if one of them errs, the other can remind her.⦆ (Part of verse 282 of Surah al-Baqarah)

Here the Truth establishes that a woman's testimony needs a guarantee, namely its confirmation by the testimony of another woman, because a woman by her nature cannot put her nose into every detail of what she sees; rather she hears superficially, so the picture is not complete for her. When the testimony of one woman is joined with that of another woman, each of them reminds the other of details that may lie in the realm of forgetting, because the female psyche and the nature of her make-up are built on protection and caution against being in a society where discord exists.

When the Truth describes these polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, He says: ﴿and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them﴾, that is, what they used to lie about and claim as God's partners has disappeared from them. The polytheists are the ones held to account and questioned for taking partners. Some of them may have taken a partner for God without any fault in that matter, such as some people taking Jesus (peace be upon him) as a partner of God. Jesus is free of associating anything with God or making himself a partner in divinity. The Truth has said:

﴿And [beware the Day] when God will say, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides God'?" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen. (116)﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah)

Rather, the idols themselves that the polytheists took as lords say: "They worshipped us, while we worship God more than those who stand in prayer in the dawns."

So the error lies with those who associated others with God, not with the stones that worship God and glorify Him, because they are subjected and facilitated for what they were created for. One of the poets imagined a dialogue between the cave of Thawr and the cave of Hira', and the cave of Thawr says:

How we envied Hira' when the trustworthy Spirit dwelt there, visiting you with lights.

When God permitted the Hijrah, the Prophet hid in the cave of Thawr, so the rest of the stones said:

Hira' and Thawr have become equal; by them I intercede for the state of the stones.
They worship us, while we worship God more than those who stand in prayer in the dawns.
They took our silence as proof, so we became for them fuel for the fire.
They transgressed in ignorance, as they transgressed against the son of Mary and the disciples. For the extremist is his recompense, and the one who exaggerates is saved by the mercy of the Forgiver.

So here are the stones saying that they are innocent of association and that they worship God more than those who stand in prayer in the dawns. The apparent silence of the stones has been taken by some as proof that the stones were content to be worshipped. But the stones will become the stones of Hell, prepared for those who disbelieve in God. The wronging by servants of the stones is like the wronging of Jesus, son of Mary. Those who exaggerated in worshipping stones or humans have a punishment, while the stones and humans who bear no fault in that matter hope for God's forgiveness and mercy.

So the misguidance here is the misguidance of those who took partners with God. But the partner that was taken is not described as "vanished" except in the sense that it disappeared from them on a day when their hope was that it would be with them to protect them from God's punishment.

Then the Almighty says, after that:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed veils over their hearts, lest they understand it, and deafness in their ears. And if they were to see every sign, they would not believe in it. Until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."﴾ (6:25)

Among these people are those who listen to the Qur'an not with the aim of understanding and being guided, but with the aim of seeking any path to find fault with the Qur'an. It is as though their hearts are closed to the capacity for understanding and for good deduction that leads to guidance. They dispute with the aim of confirming their disbelief, not with a pure intention to make clear the horizons of the verses of truth and to reach the straight path.

We know that the whole surah came to confront the issue of idols, idolatry and associating partners with God. We know that the miracle that came with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is the Qur'an, and it is a verbal miracle, which differs from the visible miracles that the contemporaries of Moses (peace be upon him) witnessed:

such as splitting the sea with the staff, or seeing the staff turn into a serpent that swallowed whatever the magicians had cast, or the miracle of Jesus (peace be upon him) in healing the blind and the leper. All of these are visible miracles limited to a time. As for the miracle of the Messenger of God, it is an audible and enduring miracle.

Hearing is the first of the tools of perception for the human soul. It is the first instrument of perception that alerts a person. It is the only instrument of perception that remains active during sleep and carries out its task, for its design includes the capacity to continue its task during sleep. We know that when God wished for the People of the Cave to remain for three hundred and nine years, He struck upon their ears so that their sleep would be a deep slumber. They were in a cave in a mountain, and the mountain is in the deserts over which winds, whirlwinds and storms blow. Had their ears been in their natural state, they would not have rested in the sleep that God willed for them. For this reason God struck upon their ears, and He, glorified is He, said:

﴿So We struck upon their ears in the cave for a number of years.﴾ (18:11) (Surat al-Kahf)

Thus the miracle of the Messenger of God came audible, and it can also be read. When a person receives a message, he receives it with his hearing, and afterwards he can read this message and understand it. No one knows reading except after he first hears the sounds of the letters and then sees them afterwards. His miracle (ﷺ) was distinguished by the foremost of the means of human perception, which is hearing. And the Almighty says: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾.

There is a difference between (yasma') and (yastami'). The one who (yasma') hears incidentally, whereas the one who (yastami') listens hears deliberately. The one who hears without deliberation has no choice but to hear, unless he plugs his ears. As for the one who listens, he intends to hear.
