They used to listen to the Qur'an not for the purpose of discovering the horizons of guidance, but for the purpose of insisting upon disbelief, by intending to hunt out faults in the Qur'an.

The Almighty says: ﴿And We have placed veils over their hearts, lest they understand it﴾. (Akinnah) is the plural of (kinan), which is a covering or a sheath. The Almighty continues: ﴿and deafness in their ears﴾, meaning We placed deafness in their ears. It is as though, by their choice of disbelief, God has prevented them from understanding the Qur'an. We know that all the contemporaries of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), heard the Messenger of God; some of them believed and some remained in disbelief. We know that every action has a future. The future may believe, and then the action has borne its fruit; or the future may persist in its previous stance and not believe, and then the action has not borne its fruit. The actor is one, but the recipient differs. Some of the disbelievers would hear the Qur'an and then leave without faith:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts God has set a seal, and they followed their desires.﴾ (47:16) (Surat Muhammad)

They are like disbelievers who listen to the Qur'an, then depart to say, mockingly, to the believers who have learned and believed: "What kind of speech is this that Muhammad utters?" These mockers are those whose hearts God has sealed with disbelief, and who turned away from guidance to misguidance. The one who speaks the words of God is the Messenger of God, conveying from God, and the listener differs: there is a believing listener who is affected by what he hears, and there is a disbelieving listener whose ear cannot convey awareness and understanding of what he hears. But the Qur'an is a guidance and healing for those who believe, whereas for those who do not believe, their ears are deafened to understanding and their depths lack insight, so they do not understand from God. You will find the soul of the believer eager to know what is in the Qur'an, whereas the one who wants to be a tyrant on earth does not wish to bind himself to the method.

To know the difference between these two types of people: the believer looks at the universe and contemplates it, and so he perceives that it has a wise Creator; whereas the disbeliever's insight is blinded from seeing this. When the believer listens to a message from the Creator of the universe, he strains his hearing, whereas the disbeliever turns away from it.

The chieftains of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl and Abu Sufyan, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Rabi'a, and Harb ibn Umayya, all of these chieftains of Quraysh used to gather, and one of them would ask al-Nadr: "O Nadr, what is the story of this speech that Muhammad utters?"

Al-Nadr was a transmitter of stories that he collected from various regions. He had travelled to the lands of Persia and Byzantium and roamed the Arabian Peninsula from end to end. So he said: "By God, I do not know what Muhammad says, except that he says the fables of the ancients."

Al-Nadr, Abu Sufyan and Abu Jahl argued with the Messenger of God, and this argument is evidence of their failure to understand what the verses of the Qur'an brought. God did not place deafness on their ears by compulsion against them; rather, it was because of their disbelief first. God sealed their hearts because of their disbelief, the disease of disbelief settled in their hearts, they preferred it over faith, and so God increased them in disease. The Almighty said concerning them:

﴿And if they were to see every sign, they would not believe in it. Until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."﴾ (6:25)

Asatir (fables) is the plural of ustura, and an ustura is something written down to be told, of wonders and imaginary events. It is as though the Almighty and Exalted is exposing them before themselves as they try to find a gap in the Qur'an and fail to find one. God said about them a decisive word:

﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾ (43:31) (Surat al-Zukhruf)

They know the greatness of the Qur'an, so how do they say it is the fables of the ancients? They were admirers of the greatness of the eloquent style of the Noble Qur'an, for they were a people of eloquence; but they know that what the Qur'an requires is difficult for themselves. Moreover, they wanted to remain in leadership, arrogance and domination over others, whereas the Qur'an came to make all people equal before the one, unique Truth.

Forcible events came by the will of God to be a cause of faith, as happened with Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) when he learned that his sister had embraced Islam, so he went to her and beat her until blood flowed from her. The shedding of blood stirred in him the feeling of brotherhood, and it removed the arrogance of obstinacy. He wished to read the sheet on which some verses of the Qur'an were written, and his sister made the condition that he purify himself, so he purified himself and sat down to listen. With the removal of his arrogance and obstinacy, and with his purification, his mind became ready to understand what was in the Qur'an. He went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and declared his faith in God as Lord, in Muhammad (ﷺ), and in his final message.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 26:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves; and they destroy none but themselves, yet they perceive not.﴾

The unbeliever among these people only keeps away from what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) seeks, does not want to be guided, and persists in his transgression, so he forbids others from faith. It is as if he has committed two crimes: the crime of his own disbelief, and the crime of forbidding others from faith.

Quraysh were certain that whoever hears the Qur'an would be guided by it. For this reason some of them urged one another not to listen to the Qur'an, and if they did hear it, they should distort it or make a clamour that would stand between the listener and reflecting upon it.

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during its recitation, that perhaps you may overcome."﴾ (Surah Fussilat).

They were confident that the Qur'an would overpower them with proof and silence them with clear evidence, and that if they listened to it they would find in it a sweetness and a grace that would draw out of their hearts denial and rejection. In doing so, they were in effect testifying that the Qur'an has an effect upon the natural disposition (fitrah) of man, and they were the masters of eloquence in the Arabic language. Yet the disbelievers remained obstinate in spite of their love for its style, its expression and its delivery. They were not content with their own misguidance, but wanted to misguide others, so it is as if they bear their own burdens and the burdens of those whom they misguide. This did not affect the course of the call nor the proclamation of faith by Muhammad (peace be upon him), for the Truth grants it victory despite all this. He, glorified and exalted, is the One who said:

﴿And My word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant.﴾ (Surah As-Saffat).

When the Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves; and they destroy none but themselves, yet they perceive not.﴾ (Surah al-An'am),

we know that the intended meaning of this statement is those who opposed the call of Muhammad (peace be upon him). They opposed it because it would strip them of their temporal power, of haughtiness and tyranny, and of the exploitation of the weak. This is what made them stand toward the call in a position of denial and disbelief.

Since they took this stance toward the call, faith was not their lot, and because they kept away and distanced themselves from the Messenger of God, they lost. As for others, they did not keep away from the Messenger of God (ﷺ); rather, he took refuge with God, and God gave him refuge.

Regarding these deniers who rejected the call of the Messenger of God: they stood before his call, turned people away from it, and forbade them from following it, because this call would strip them of their temporal power, of haughtiness and tyranny, of subjugating the weak and harnessing them to their service, and of extending their dominion over them. This – first – is what drove them to prevent others and forbid them from following Islam. Then they – second – keep away and distance themselves from following the Messenger. So it is in their interest – first – to forbid others before they themselves keep away; for if people believed in the Messenger of God while they alone remained in disbelief, would they benefit from this process? They would not benefit. Therefore their concern – first – was that no one should believe in the Messenger of God, so that their power would remain.

The Qur'anic expression came to convey the most precise details of this condition, saying: ﴿They forbid it and keep away from it﴾. The beginning was forbidding others from believing in the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and then afterward their distancing themselves from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so their lot became to remain in their disbelief, and loss became their portion, while others from among the people believed.

Thus we see that the Qur'anic expression always conveys the psychological state with the truest expression. The words of the Truth, ﴿and they forbid it﴾, are a logical statement expressing the stance of the opponents of the Messenger of God, while His words, ﴿and keep away from it﴾, are a depiction of what they did to themselves after they had prevented others from following the Muhammadan call and the final message. Thus they committed two sins: the first, misguiding others; the second, the misguidance of their own souls. By this, the saying of the Truth, glorified be He, applies to them:

﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they misguide without knowledge.﴾ (Part of verse 25, Surah An-Nahl).

Let no one say: this verse contradicts the saying of the Truth, glorified be He:

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.﴾ (Part of verse 15, Surah al-Isra').

This is because the two burdens are: their own burden, and the burden of their misguiding others, which is the result of their own action.

The Truth continues: ﴿They destroy none but themselves, yet they perceive not.﴾ We see that whoever stands before the call of truth and goodness to deny it, nullify it, oppose it and fight it, intends by that the good of his own self and the gaining of the world and taking it to his side. But they will not reach that either. Why?

Because God is dominant over His affair:

﴿And My word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant.﴾ (Surah As-Saffat)

The Truth, glorified and exalted, never defeats His soldiers, and the enemies of His call must perish because of their disbelief and their obstruction from the way of God; in reality, it is they who destroy themselves by themselves. The matter of the Islamic faith-based call will continue to rise. They will see the land of disbelief diminishing around them day after day. Therefore the Truth says in another verse:

﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ (Part of verse 41, Surah ar-Ra'd)

That is, the land of disbelief is diminishing and diminishing, and God judges, there is none to repel His judgment. Therefore the Qur'an, in the last of its order of revelation, explains this matter fully. It teaches us to cut every tie we have with the disbelievers, so He, glorified be He, says:

﴿Say: "O disbelievers! I do not worship what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship."﴾ (Surah al-Kafirun)

Thus we see that severing ties is a required matter between two groups: a group that sees that it is upon the truth, and a second group that is upon falsehood. Severing ties may be a temporary matter, and circumstances and events may press until worldly relations are restored, but the severance of ties must be firm in matters of belief, with no compromise in this. Therefore the Truth said it twice:

﴿I do not worship what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.﴾ (Surah al-Kafirun)

The believer sees the present and the future, and knows the impossibility that he should worship what the disbelievers worship, and the impossibility that the disbelievers should worship what he worships.

Someone may say: the Qur'an in its order of revelation must not contradict its reality, yet we see in His saying, exalted be He, ﴿I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾, repeated twice, that He has thereby closed the door before the disbelievers so that they do not believe, although some of them have entered the religion of God. We say: Yes, it does not contradict, because the Truth did not close the door before the disbelievers whom God willed to believe, as is evident from His saying, exalted be He:

﴿When there comes the help of God and the victory, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes, then glorify the praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ (Surah an-Nasr)

So the matter will not be settled at that point: the camp of faith will expand, it will confront the camp of the disbelievers, and people will enter the religion of God in multitudes. But there are those whom God has decreed not to believe, so that they remain in their disbelief and enter the Fire. Thus He, glorified be He, said afterward:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, with a rope of fiber around her neck.﴾ (Surah al-Masad)

So Abu Lahab and whoever is of his kind will enter the Fire and will never enter the religion of God. The saying of the Truth comes:

﴿And you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes﴾ (Surah an-Nasr)

This saying opens the door of hope. We see the entry into Islam of Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Amr ibn al-'As, and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl. The coming of Surah al-Masad after Surah an-Nasr in the arrangement of the Mushaf, as God willed, teaches us that there are people who will not enter Paradise because they are like Abu Lahab and his wife.

Followed by Surah al-Ikhlas:

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent.﴾ (Surah al-Ikhlas)

There is no god with God who can overturn what God has decreed, and no one can question the judgment of God. Thus whoever disbelieves and associates partners with God is among those who have lost themselves, destroyed them, and perceive not.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 27:

And after that, the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire, and they will say: "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."﴾ (27)

When we look at the words of the Truth, ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire﴾, we find here no answer (jawab) to the conditional, unlike what you find in your saying: "If you had seen so-and-so, I would have welcomed him," or "If you had seen so-and-so, I would have punished him." Each of these two sentences has an answer, but in this noble utterance we find no answer, and this is from the grandeur of Qur'anic expression. There are events which expressions cannot convey, and so the Truth, glorified be He, omits them so that every listener may go in the meaning whatever direction he sees fit.

In our own lives we find a criminal in some country whose corruption and crime spread among its people through killing, torture, theft and assault, and no one is ever able to stop him. Then Allah enables the security men to seize him, and we see this killer and corrupter transform from arrogance into a coward, a trembler, who almost kisses the policeman's hand so that he will not put the shackles on his hands. A person sees that scene and describes it to others, saying: "Oh, if only you had seen the moment the police seized this criminal!" This phrase conveys all the meanings of humiliation that the listener imagines. Thus, omitting the answer is always a kind of training (tarbiyah) for the benefit of the answer, so that every listener goes in his imagining of abasement wherever he goes. For if the observer wished, he would have narrated in detail what happened in the moment of the criminal's seizure, and by doing so he would have confined the humiliation and degradation within the frame of what he himself saw, and thereby would have blocked the imagination and picturing of the listeners.

As for the observer's being content with his saying: "Oh, if only you had seen the moment the policeman seized this criminal," this utterance generalizes what he saw, so that every listener imagines from the forms of humiliation whatever suits the capacity of his imagination. Thus the Qur'an wished to depict the terror of standing before the Fire, and so the Truth released the particle "if only" (law) without an answer when He said:

﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire, and they will say: "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

Some people have wished to pick at the methods of the Qur'an. Among them is one who said: How can they say the Qur'an is of lofty eloquence, eloquent in style, miraculous in expression, when it says what it says about the tree of Zaqqum?

The Noble Qur'an says about this tree:

﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of Zaqqum? Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire. Its emerging fruit is like the heads of devils.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat)

Every tree needs water and air, and has life that appears in the greenness of its leaves. So how does this tree come out of the Fire? Is there not in that an anomaly? Then the image extends, the image of the tree, and the Truth describes its fruit in His words:

﴿Its emerging fruit is like the heads of devils. Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat)

We have not seen the tree of Zaqqum, and we have not seen the head of a devil. Those who pick at the Qur'an mock, in their sayings: since none of mankind has witnessed the head of a devil, and likewise the tree of Zaqqum, how does Allah liken the unknown to the unknown? And they asked boastfully: What does the listener gain from likening an unknown thing to an unknown thing? We answer them: It is the dullness of their hearts and the loss of your natural faculty for the Arabic language that causes them not to understand the eloquence in this utterance.

When we bring the example close, we say: Suppose a person held a competition among cartoonists (caricaturists) in the world, each to draw an image of the devil. On the day of determining the winner, there would be more than one image of the devil, and the most hideous images would win, because the victory here is not in beauty, but in the skill of depicting ugliness. Thus many images of ugliness appear before us. So what of the Truth, glorified be He, when He wished to release the imagination to picture the tree of Zaqqum, and likewise to picture the head of a devil? By this eloquent method the Truth wished to spread the benefit of displaying the hideousness of the tree from which the people of disbelief eat.

Likewise here is His saying, the Truth: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire﴾. What happens to these people when they stand before the Fire is not reported here; rather the Truth is content to express to us that we see them in such a situation. For the Last Day is the Day of Recompense, either to Paradise or to the Fire. And Paradise, as we know from the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." We know that the range of sight is limited, while the range of hearing is wider, for the ear hears what you see and what others have seen, whereas your eyes see only what you alone have seen. The Truth does not stop at that, but informs His Messenger (ﷺ) that in Paradise there is what does not occur to the heart of any human being, meaning that in Paradise there are things that language cannot express, because language expresses people's conceptions of things. The meaning exists first, and then the word expressing it exists.

Thus we know that the bliss of Paradise has no words that convey all the meanings it carries for the believer, and likewise we know that in the Fire there is a punishment for which no words have been coined to express it. Had the Truth, glorified be He, said: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire﴾ and then gone on to describe it as a frightening, terrifying, humiliating matter, and so on through those words indicating the depth of the punishment, we would not have had the same effect that the omission of the answer produces.

When we read "they were made to stand" (wuqifū), we know that there is in it a construction and an existing entity, and that there is someone who made them stand before the Fire, while they had been deniers of the Fire in the world. Then they find themselves on the Day of Resurrection among those whom Allah has made to stand before the Fire, to see the punishment awaiting them, and to look upon the Fire as one standing looks upon a thing. Likewise the Truth makes them stand before the Fire which they had denied in the world. The report had come to them in the world, so whoever believed and knew that the one who informed him was truthful, that is knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn). If a person passes the stage of knowledge and sees a sensible image of the report, that is the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn). The believer, through the report of his Lord, reached things with knowledge of certainty from Allah, because he believes his Lord. For this reason Imam Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, said: "If the veil were lifted from me, I would not increase in certainty," because he is a rhetorical confirmer of it (mus­addiq bi-lagh bihi).

But what of the deniers? A person sees the knowledge of certainty on the Last Day as the eye of certainty, and believer and disbeliever share in this. But the disbeliever sees the Fire as the eye of certainty and enters it to be burned by it, and this is the truth of certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn).

Thus we know that the Fire, as the eye of certainty, is seen by believer and disbeliever, and the Fire as the truth of certainty is witnessed and by which only the disbeliever is punished. As for the believer in Paradise, he experiences the truth of certainty because he lives in and is made happy by its bliss. The Glorified depicts this in His saying:

﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would surely see the Hellfire. Then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾ (Surah al-Takathur)

The truth of certainty comes in His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿As for one who is among those brought near, there will be rest and provision and a Garden of bliss. And as for one who is among the companions of the right, "Peace be upon you, from the companions of the right." And as for one who is among the deniers, the astray, there is a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the truth of certainty.﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah)

And what will the deniers do when they see the Fire as the eye of certainty? They must fear that they will suffer from it when it becomes the truth of certainty, so they say:

﴿Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.﴾ (part of verse 27, Surah al-An'am)

They wish to return to the world to resume belief. And wishing, in some of its forms, is the seeking of the impossible, which is not possible, to indicate that the one who seeks it loves that it should be. Like the saying of one who said:

Ah, would that youth might return a day,
so I could tell it what old age has done.

Or the saying of one who said:

Would that the stars would draw near to me, so I could string them
as a necklace of praise; I would not be pleased with my words for you.

And they said: ﴿Oh, would that we could be returned﴾. If they said this as a wish, it is a request for the impossible, and it also implies a promise not to deny the signs of Allah. But are they able to do that? No, because the Noble Qur'an says in the following verse:

﴿But there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ (28)

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 28:

They ask to be returned to the world, not in order to carry out the promise they make in their request, which is impossible, because they would do exactly as they did before: disbelief, denial and obstinate rejection. They resorted to this statement out of extreme fear of what Allah has prepared for them, after everything they used to do in the world of disbelief and denial has become clear to them. The Day of Resurrection is called (the Day of Exposure), because every person will find his record around his neck, and it will be said to him:

(﴿Read your record. Sufficient is yourself today as a reckoner against you.﴾) [Surat al-Isra', 14]

If we in the world record events in sound and image, what then of the recording of the Truth concerning us? A person will see his deeds on the Day of Resurrection in sound and image, and every action he performed will be recorded in a way that makes it impossible for him to deny it, as if the Truth is making clear to every servant: "I will not hold you to account; rather, I will leave you to hold yourself to account." A person will be astonished that his limbs speak to bear witness against him: the hands speak of what he did, the tongue speaks of what he said, and the foot tells where its owner took it. These limbs, which used to obey the desire of their owner in the world, have a different position in the Hereafter, and on the Last Day they do not carry out the desire of the person, but the desire of the One who gave the person his desire.

(﴿To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾) [Surat Ghafir, 16]

An example of this—and to Allah belongs the highest example—is that we find a company or battalion of fighters with a commander who directs the soldiers. If he gives them wrong orders, they carry them out; and after the battle ends, the supreme commander questions them, and they say that the chain of wrong orders was issued by their immediate commander.

So beware, O human, of thinking that your limbs are always subject to your power over them. Your control over them is a matter that Allah has granted you, and He may take it from you whenever He wills in this world. On the Day of Resurrection your control over your limbs will come to an end. And in this world you see some images of limbs' affliction so that you remember the power of the Supreme Bestower; you see one who cannot see, and one who has lost control of a limb or more of his limbs. That is a reminder from Allah that a person's control over his limbs is only a gift from Allah. The words of the True One, glorified is He, about the disbelievers: (﴿But there will appear to them what they used to conceal before﴾) expose their deception in the life of this world. Then Allah responds to their earlier wish, full of humiliation and abasement, the wish to return to the world, saying, glorified is He: (﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾)

They are lying in their promise that they would believe if they returned to the world, as the words of the Truth, glorified is He, make clear: (﴿And they say, "There is not but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."﴾) [Surat al-An'am, 29]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 29:

They did not take on faith during their lifetimes in the manner of faith through inference from a world that is orderly, arranged, and firmly made. They did not notice that this order, firmness, and arrangement exists in the relations of human beings with one another, whether they are believers or atheists. We know that there are qualities that all people, believers and atheists alike, share in disliking. So if the atheist steals from his colleague, is he not punished? He receives punishment from his society, and in every society there is reward and punishment, and indeed there is repayment with kindness (jaza' bi-ihsan). Faith does not prevent people from agreeing upon some kind of good conduct, and those who deny faith are compelled by events to establish law to regulate reward and punishment.

We find that criminalizing what opposes goodness and beauty and what corrupts the universe is a matter natural (fitri) and necessary for man. They criminalize evil acts only after events bite them, and they do not notice that the heavenly method (al-manhaj al-samawi) came with reward and punishment for every act that protects human dignity. On the Day of Resurrection they will stand in humiliation and under compulsion, to see what they did:

﴿Nay, there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before. But if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 28)

If they were returned to the world with the choice they had there, they would act just as they acted before, and they would not have said this statement on the Last Day except because they are overpowered. Earlier they used to say:

﴿And they say, "There is not but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 29)

In their world they believed only in one life, which is this world. They did not notice that a person lives in this world according to his strength, and woe to the weak at the hands of the strong. The strong fear only a law that punishes them, or a God who will punish them for sin however they conceal it. For this reason we always find the believing judge saying: "If you are blind to the judgment of the earth, then do not be blind to the judgment of heaven."

Among the stupidity of the people of disbelief is that they call life on earth "the worldly life" (al-hayat al-dunya), while in its reality it is a lower world (dunya), and since they have judged and recognized that it is "lower" (dunya), there must be a higher life (hayah 'ulya) corresponding to it. All of this happens to them when they stand before the Fire, and the Fire is one of the soldiers of the Almighty. So what about them when they stand before the Creator of the Fire and the Lord of the worlds?

And if you could see them when they are made to stand before their Lord. He will say: "Is this not the truth?" They will say: "Yes, by our Lord!" He will say: "Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny."

They, then, have been struck with fear and confusion, and they seek to return to the life of this world, because what they witnessed is a great terror. So what of when they stand before God? It is a frightening situation. And since the Truth (al-Haqq) omitted the response earlier when He made them stand before the Fire, it is more fitting here that the response be omitted, so that the imagination is left to wander in many directions. It is an escalation in terror.

Thus we see the rebuke to them in the words of the Truth: "Is this not the truth?" They are taken by surprise at the existence of a God who, after they have witnessed the resurrection and stood before the Fire, says to them: "Is this not the truth?" And He, glory be to Him, does not ask them as one seeking information; rather He affirms, and He willed that the acknowledgment come from them, so they say: "Yes" (bala), because the matter then does not require obstinacy. ("Bala" is a particle that turns a negation into an affirmation.)

The Truth presents this matter in the negative form so that no one may suppose that an answer was being suggested to them. Then the judgment of the Truth is issued: "Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny." Thus they taste the punishment with which they used to call things false. And tasting the punishment is not a characteristic of coercion and tyranny, for God does not wrong anyone even to the weight of an atom; rather, it is because they committed what necessitates that they be punished for it:

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 31:

The Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says, after that:

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!" while they carry their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they carry.﴾ (31)

Every capital requires work that increases it. But if the work has caused the capital to be lost, this means loss twice: once because the capital has not remained at its limit but has perished, vanished and been wasted, and a second time because a human effort has been lost, and with it the capital has been lost too.

So, "those who denied the meeting with Allah have indeed lost," because they sold the long-lived deferred for the short-lived immediate. Each of us wants his work to bear fruit, and tries to give a little in order to take much.

For example, we find the farmer setting aside two measures of wheat from the grain in his storehouse to sow in the land after it has been ploughed. This means a small decrease in this farmer's storehouse, but it is a decrease for a coming increase: when he places the seeds in the ploughed earth, we find the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted making them grow for him many times over. The farmer, by this, sells the small immediate in order to take the great deferred.

These are the principles of the movement of the intelligent person who weighs his steps. If he wants to harvest fruits from his movement, he must exert effort. But if the movement brings him only a little, he will not move. And because the intelligent person does not love loss, we find him always balancing and comparing between the effort he exerts and the return that will come to him. As for those who denied the meeting with Allah, they have lost themselves, because they did not weigh between two lives: a life that is conjectured and a life that is certain, for the duration of our worldly life is conjectured, not certain.

We do not know how long we will live in it. The average lifespan of a human on earth is seventy years, for example, but no one knows exactly how long his life is in this world, and he has a limited term. He is perishing, departing and dying. But the life of the Hereafter is certain, with no term to it; it is everlasting. We know that the bliss of this world for a human is according to the causes available to him, whereas the bliss of the Hereafter is according to the extent of the unrestricted power of the Causer, who is Allah. Accordingly, the loss of those who disbelieved is great, grievous and bloody, because they did not trade with Allah.

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾ (part of verse 31, Surah al-An'am).

We know that (ḥattā, "until") is a bridge between two matters: the matter we want to reach is the goal, as when someone says: "I walked until I reached the house," where "the house" is the goal of the walking.

As for those who disbelieved, their disbelief and denial led to loss. The coming of the Hour suddenly is not the end of the journey, but the arrival at the beginning of the loss, for their loss does not end at once with the arrival of the Hour; rather it begins at the moment the Hour surprises them. They are confronted with the occurrence of what they used to deny, and they know well that what they did in the world merits nothing but punishment.

Here begins the regret which they cannot conceal, and therefore they say: ﴿Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!﴾... that is, over our neglect and our extravagance in that matter while we were in the world. Thereby we know that not neglecting the world and taking its means is not blameworthy, but neglect during the life of this world is the blameworthy matter, because it is a squandering of time and corruption on earth.

I say this so that no one will understand that enjoyment of the world is blameworthy in itself, and so that no one will understand that the Hereafter is the subject of religion, because the world is also the subject of religion, and reward in the Hereafter is only given for the various kinds of conduct in the world: whoever behaves well in the world gains the reward of the Hereafter, and whoever behaves badly receives the punishment of the Hereafter. Therefore it is not at all correct to set religion against the world.

We must know the error of those who say: "religion and world" (dīn wa-dunyā). Religion is not the opposite of the world; rather, the world is the subject of religion. I say this in response to those who think that the reason some countries have progressed in our time is that their people neglected religion and were captivated by the pleasure and enjoyment in the world, so they worked to build civilizations.

We say: Turning to religion with a spirit of understanding is what builds civilizations, and the reformer is rewarded in the world on the Day of Reckoning. We should know that the opposite of the world is the Hereafter, and religion encompasses both together: it encompasses the world as subject matter and the Hereafter as recompense. Those who are captivated by the world and do not believe in the Hereafter are the ones who say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it, while they carry their burdens upon their backs.﴾ The immaterial burdens of the world, which are sins, will be embodied as tangible things, so that the disgrace may be public. Whoever stole a sheep will be raised on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his back; whoever stole a cow will be raised on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his shoulder, and it will be lowing; and likewise whoever stole a ton of iron from a building will be raised on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his back. Thus Allah will disgrace him on the Day of Resurrection.

Such is the state of the people of the Fire. Therefore the Truthful says: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is that which they carry.﴾ We know that they do not carry only their own burdens, but they also carry the burdens of those whom they took as exemplars; this is the burden of misguidance. And they all know that the bearing of a burden is embodied in the feeling of its weight, for these burdens led them to Hell. We know that the outcome of every deed is its purpose: whoever does righteousness will find the righteousness of his deed, and whoever does evil will find his evil deed.

We see practical examples of this in our daily lives: here are two brothers who work in agriculture, and each owns two feddans of land, for example. The first rises at daybreak to tend his land, plough it, bring manure to it, attend to the schedules of irrigation, and strive toward the day of harvest with diligence and care. The other stays up all night in front of a television screen, does not rise from sleep until midday, and tends his land with the least possible effort. Then the day of harvest comes: the first obtains the product of his labour, an abundant harvest, while the other obtains a small harvest, in addition to the regret he swallows because of his neglect and laziness. Thus the intelligent person is one who studies what his movement in life yields, and chooses the kind of movement in life that secures for him the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, and tranquillity of soul in both.

Whoever sleeps and does not go to his work is a person who loves himself, and whoever rises at the crack of dawn for his work also loves himself; but there is a difference between a foolish love whose outcome is regret, and a deeper love for the meaning of life whose outcome is abundant reward.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 32:

The Exalted Lord says to us:

﴿And the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement, and the Last Abode is better for those who fear God. Will you not then reason? (32)﴾.

This is how life appears to one who stops at describing it as "the life of this world" (al-hayat al-dunya), merely as play and amusement. Play (la'ib), as we know, is engaging in an action and undoing it at the same time. An example of this is a child on the seashore who builds a house of sand and then knocks it down; he has built a sand house only in order to knock it down. Play is an activity intended to kill time in a work that may be undone, so building and undoing in this case is play, and play does not distract a person from a duty. As for amusement (lahw), it is killing time in a work that may be undone, and which also distracts a person from a duty.

A small child, for example, receives some [attention] from his parents in order to spend his time with them; he may damage and knock it down, and he may rebuild it. The child's play is at the same time amusement, because the child is not charged with any duty. But once he enters school and has some responsibilities, we find the family teaching him to distinguish between the time for fulfilling his responsibilities and the time for play, because if he plays at the time of fulfilling his responsibilities his play becomes amusement, since it has distracted him from a responsibility required of him.

Likewise, the life of this world, stripped of the method of the One who created it and created man within it, is amusement and play. But if a person takes life according to its specifications from the One who created it, it is a life that produces good in this world and in the Hereafter. The One who created the life of this world made it for us a field (mazra'a) for the Hereafter. The believer, therefore, has two lives: a life of righteousness in this world and a life of bliss in the Hereafter, because he lives the life of this world according to the purpose of the One who created it.

It is remarkable that the One who created us charged us only after a person among us reaches puberty (al-bulugh), that is, when a person is fit to beget a human like himself if he marries. Obligation comes in proportion to maturity and at the completion of reason. The Truth permitted us to play in the years before maturity, but such play must be under the supervision of adults, so that play can turn into training (darba) that benefits us in the fields of life, and makes us know how in the modern age we have reached a degree of advancement in the manufacture of toys from which the child learns, and which he can take apart and reassemble. Even adults in our time learn to drive cars in closed rooms with a television screen in front of them, as though they were on a real road and in a busy street, and whoever masters this practical training goes out to drive a car. Thus we find that training is beneficial to man: it teaches children the play that will benefit them when they grow up, and training likewise benefits adults too.

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) enjoined us to teach our sons horsemanship, swimming and archery, horses at the time of the Message were among the important weapons for those calling to God and striving in His way to ride. When we were asked to teach sons swimming, this is building the body and strength, benefiting the young man and teaching him to face hardships; and when we were asked to teach sons archery, this is because fixing a target, whether material or moral, and knowing how to reach it, is something required of every young man. All of these are games, but they are not amusement; they are enjoyable games that can continue with a person after he has become responsible. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Teach your children swimming and archery" (1). So what of the games of our age and time?

We find that football has captured the attention of men and women, old and young. It is a game that teaches no one anything, because it is a game for the sake of play itself; it is a game that consumes the time of most people, and this game has taken on all the rules of serious affairs. It begins at a fixed time, and spectators go to it two hours before the appointment, and the state mobilizes sufficient numbers of security forces to maintain order, even though it is amusement and of no benefit to the spectator.

It may also prevent, divert and disrupt some people from their work, and others from their prayers. All of this happens while we find that some fields of seriousness have no regulation.

I say this so that people may awaken and know that this game will benefit them in nothing at all. I say this opinion and ask every head of household to exercise control over his family, and to advise them calmly and with awareness, so that every member of the family becomes attentive to his responsibilities, and we know that this is a kind of amusement which takes much of the time of work and of the duties and responsibilities of life, lest we complain and tire from low productivity.

The state must turn its attention to such matters. Let each matter be given its due: it is not right that we transfer seriousness into the rules of play; rather let seriousness have its own rules, and play its own time, and let us not transfer play into the sphere of amusement, because the meaning of amusement is that we devote ourselves to a work that has no aim and no benefit. If we look at life stripped of the method of God, it is play and amusement.

Here we notice the precision of the Truth in mentioning play first and then amusement, and then He says: "and the Last Abode," clearly indicating that when a person withdraws from the method of the Truth in life, events surprise him with a sudden transition to evident seriousness. Therefore let us take life in the light of God's method, because when He informed us that He created man from clay, shaped him and breathed into him of His spirit, He thereby gave him a first life, in which believer and disbeliever, obedient and rebellious, and every human being who has sense, movement, thought and will, share. God sent the Messengers with the method so that life would proceed toward its goal, which is the second life, the Last Abode, for it is the complete and enduring life. Let us hear the saying of the Exalted Lord:

﴿O you who believe, respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ (part of verse 24, surah al-Anfal).

The Truth, the Exalted, offers us a high, lasting life that outlasts the life that ends. Whoever stops taking God's method into his life is content with what an animal takes of life, which is the breathing of the spirit; but whoever takes God's method takes the high life, the life of goodness, beauty, reform and kindness. We know that beauty in life is the beauty that does not inherit ugliness, and true goodness is that which spreads God's goodness among the servants, so that a person does not take goodness for himself and leave its evils to others. Therefore I say: O Muslim, do not take goodness for yourself at the expense of evil for others, because you do not like others to achieve good at your expense; and whoever wishes to unleash his evils upon people, let him receive evil from others. Whoever wishes to take goodness from people, let him give them of his goodness so that existence remains beautiful. Thus life without God's method is ugly, because the strong moves about in it corrupting by his strength, and the weak retreats into a feeling of humiliation and loss.

But the Exalted wanted life for the believers in the light of His method. When they apply His obligations, "do" and "do not do," they protect life from corruption according to the commands of the Supreme Creator of life; He is the One who brought us into being and set down for us the laws for preserving life. When He prevented one believer from evil, He prohibited and forbade every believing person from doing evil to his brother, and thereby protected man from evil. God singled out the believers with the call and the summons because they are the people of response and obedience; as for others of the disbelievers and polytheists, they have refused God and disobeyed Him and did not believe in Him. When God commands the believer to good, He commands all believers to do good for themselves and for others, and thereby they gain a tranquil life. Therefore He says:﴿Respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾.

Whoever does not respond to God and His Messenger when they call him to that which gives him life remains in this world immersed in amusement and play; they are like the dead. And so that we know that the Exalted wanted for us, the believers, a high life: He has named the method that lays down for us the commands and prohibitions "spirit": ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command﴾. The Exalted named by this the angel who descended with the revelation: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down (193)﴾ (surah al-Shu'ara').

Thus the life that gives man sense and movement is the first life, through which he plays and amuses himself, and it is not the life desired by God; for the life desired by God is the life of faith, and therefore the Exalted named it "the living" (al-hayawan), that is, the complete life, and named the method "spirit."

﴿And the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement, and the Last Abode is better for those who fear God. Will you not then reason? (32)﴾ (surah al-An'am).

Mere reasoning gives man good, and reasoning is the attempt to understand the laws of the universe, its causes and effects. We see the light of the sun fill the day and spread brightness and warmth, and the setting of the sun and the appearance of the moon achieve the clarity of stillness and guide people in the darkness of land and sea; the flowing of water quenches the thirst of man and crops; the movement of winds stirs the clouds, drives ships, helps navigation in air and sea, and pollinates plants. All of this are causes that God willed so that balance may be achieved in the universe. Man takes his share of life through the causes in which he works, and does not take from the causes of others.

It is true that there are people who live without causes and take the toil of others, but they must beware of God. Beware, O Muslim, lest you build your flesh and the flesh of your children from exploiting others; for the vicissitudes of life will pass over you, and your strength may turn into weakness. A person's security against his weakness comes through giving zakat to the weak, and helping and assisting him in everything he needs. We find non-believers who have taken the idea of insurance from zakat: you give your zakat to the poor in order to secure yourself as a believer, and they have taken this idea and turned it into insurance on life, and therefore it enters into the decree of God.

But the Truth willed through zakat that the whole society be reassured, not that only the one who insures himself be reassured. We know that what frightens a person and makes him hoard, gather and treasure wealth is fear of weakness; but if the rich man gave some of his wealth to the poor, it would spread tranquillity in his soul and the souls of the weak.

What makes people gasp in life to save for their children is their lack of conviction in the social solidarity (al-takaful al-ijtima'i) that Islam has prescribed. They see the orphan being lost in society; but if people in society believed in social solidarity, every orphan would find the fatherhood of the whole society upon him.

The person who strives after gain in order to secure his children's future may turn his children into orphans, because he is preoccupied from raising them; therefore the prince of poets Shawqi, may God have mercy on him, says:

"The orphan is not the one whose two parents have passed
away from the cares of life and left him humiliated;
Rather the orphan is the one to whom, though his mother
or father is alive, neither has become free for him, being preoccupied."

Society must take the matter of good from the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾. Just as the Truth gave life to bodies through the spirit He breathed into the clay form so that it acquired sense and movement, so He also sent down the method as a spirit from Himself, so that the spirit of sense and movement might be elevated through it, lest man become like cattle, or even further astray:

﴿And the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement, and the Last Abode is better for those who fear God. Will you not then reason? (32)﴾ (surah al-An'am).

The Last Abode is better, because however long the world lasts, it ends; but the life of the Hereafter is everlasting eternity, and bliss. In this world we take bliss through causes, but the bliss of the Hereafter we take according to the measure of the breadth and vastness of God's power. The bane of this world, even for the people of luxury, power and wealth, is fear of poverty or death; but in the Hereafter the people of Paradise do not miss bliss, and bliss does not miss them.

1 Narrated by al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya.

Al-Sha'rawi then says (may Allah have mercy on him):

Allah, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you, [O Muhammad]. But it is not you that they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ (6:33)

The Truth (al-Haqq) has explained the condition of the disbelievers and their position in the Hereafter, when they will be made to stand before the Fire and will stand before Allah. After that, the address turns to the Messenger (ﷺ), upon whom falls the burden of conveying the message of Allah to these disbelievers. The Messenger (ﷺ) was grieved because his people did not taste the sweetness of faith. He is the Messenger of whom the Truth, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and, to the believers, kind and merciful.﴾ (9:128)

The Messenger (ﷺ) was eager that all people should be believers, and he was pained by some people's resistance to the call of faith. He (ﷺ) was keen that even the disbeliever should believe, although the Messenger's task is only to convey. Had Allah willed to make all people believers, He would have sent down upon them a sign that would make them all believers:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself [with grief] that they will not be believers. If We willed, We could send down upon them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain bowed to it.﴾ (26:3–4)

But the Truth, glorified and exalted, does not desire the subjugation of necks; He desires the submission of hearts. He, glorified is He, wants people to come willingly and by choice, so that they establish love for the Creator. Therefore the Truth says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you.﴾

When you hear "qad" (قد), know that what follows it is something certain. This is the case when it precedes a past-tense verb: it then comes to confirm that something has occurred. Sometimes it comes to express rarity or frequency when it precedes a present-tense verb, which indicates the present or the future. If the cause and the effect are linked by a causal connection, it is for frequency; if the link is apparently not a clear one, it is for rarity. An example of a link that indicates frequency is the saying: "Qad yanjah al-majid" (the diligent one may well succeed), because diligence and success are causally linked. But a sudden accident may befall one of the diligent, so that he cannot succeed, such as falling ill on the day of the examination; yet the likelihood of health is greater than the likelihood of illness, so it is for frequency.

An example of "qad" indicating rarity is the saying: "Qad yanjah al-kasul" (the lazy one may succeed), meaning that the lazy person may succeed by coincidence and without logical causes, such as reading a number of lessons on the night of the examination and the examination happening to fall on them, so he passes. Thus "qad", when it precedes the past, is for confirmation; when it precedes the present, it is for frequency if the causes are logical, and for rarity if the causes are not logical. But we all know that Allah's knowledge is eternal, and nothing and no matter can escape what Allah knows. Therefore "qad" here is for confirmation, and it precedes the present-tense verb. The Truth wanted to inform us that He knew from eternity what would occur, and He used "qad" to bring to mind the image of the verb:

﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you.﴾ Grief (ḥuzn) is the soul's departure from its state of ease; a person is at his utmost uprightness and joy when every one of his faculties performs its task, and if something happens that disrupts the work of one of them, that produces grief. Or grief may be an emotional reaction to the arrival or occurrence of something the soul does not desire.

The aim of the Messenger (ﷺ) was that everyone who heard the message from him should believe. But some resisted faith, and some accused the Messenger of sorcery, madness, or poetry. Here the Truth consoles His Messenger, saying: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you.﴾ That is, O Muhammad, you must know that these words are not directed at you personally, because—by the unanimous agreement of them all—you are the truthful and trustworthy one. They deny only My signs that I have sent to them with you, for your past among them is truthfulness and trustworthiness. The proof is that the disbeliever among them would not trust anyone with any of his wealth and treasures except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). A person does not deceive himself regarding what concerns him. So it is as if Allah wished to bear on behalf of His Messenger, for whoever directs an insult at the Messenger is directing it at the One who sent him, Allah, exalted be His power.

Therefore the Truth says: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you; but it is not you that they deny, rather the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ Allah, glorified is He, shows us that His Messenger (ﷺ) was intensely eager that his community respond to the summons of the Truth, so that the believers may be assured of the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted, concerning His Messenger:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and, to the believers, kind and merciful.﴾ (9:128)

Eagerness means nothing other than that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wishes that none of his people should stray from his method and his religion. But the Truth, glorified and exalted, made the matter of religion a matter of choice, so that He may know who comes willingly and who is able to come but does not.

Allah, glorified and exalted, has cosmic laws in the universe which He applies to all creation. Someone may ask: what causes Allah, glorified and exalted, to leave room for disbelief in His worldly domain? Why does He allow evil room in His world, rather than governing it with wise design? We say: if evil had no harms that frighten people, they would not have known the sweetness of the Truth. Thus the existence of evil, the existence of disbelief, and the effects of disbelief upon people—tyranny, oppression, and subjugation—proclaim to people that faith is necessary and that the presence of good is necessary. Had there been no place for evil in the universe, what would draw people to good? That is why you find that the outpourings of faith in believers only reach their full vigour when they find a people among the opponents of faith who provoke, harm, and incite the believers. But when the world becomes monotonous, the matter of Islam may grow faint in the hearts of Muslims. That is why we find believers in Allah in constant zeal, because there are those who disbelieve in Allah. So He says to His Messenger: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you,﴾ as if He, glorified is He, is informing us that He willed His creation so that there would be both believer and disbeliever in it.

Therefore, if you ask, O Muslim, how there can be disbelievers on earth: know that they are among the creation of Allah, whom the Truth willed to choose disbelief; but He did not make them choose disbelief by compulsion, glorified is He. Our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would grieve because there were people who did not believe, and the Truth, glorified and exalted, consoled him, telling him that He knows that what grieves him is what they say of disbelief and of accusations against the Messenger of Allah. Did they not say he is a sorcerer? Did they not say he is mad? Did they not say he is a liar? Did they not say he is a soothsayer? Did they not say he is a poet? Allah, glorified and exalted, knows what they said and knows that these sayings grieve the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Truth wants to lift and repel this grief from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so He informs him that they do not deny you, O Messenger of Allah, for you know your rank among them, which is the rank of the truthful and trustworthy; and no one dares to deny you, but they deny the signs of Allah. Is there any consolation greater than that? There can be no consolation greater than that.

We know that what the people of polytheism said about the Messenger of Allah is rejected speech, for they are a nation of eloquence, fluency, and clear expression. How could they say the Qur'an is poetry when they are masters of the styles of it, both its unrhymed prose and its rhymed prose, its verse and its prose? Is it reasonable that the style of the Qur'an could be confused with poetry for them? It is certainly not possible. And they said of the Prophet (ﷺ) that he is a sorcerer: but how could the sorcery be one in which they believed yet which did not bewitch the rest? Had it been sorcery, it would have bewitched them too, and their remaining in disbelief refutes this. They said he is a liar: by this saying they lie against themselves, because they know of him that he is the truthful and trustworthy one. Here is the dialogue between al-Akhnas ibn Shariq and Abu Jahl.

Al-Akhnas said: "O Abu al-Hakam, what is your opinion of what you have heard from Muhammad?" Abu Jahl said: "What did you hear!" Here we hear the speech of jealousy, envy, and hatred, and we hear about those distant matters far from the subject of the luminous Muhammadan message. Abu Jahl says: "We and the Banu Abd Manaf have competed for honour. They fed, and we fed; they carried, and we carried; they gave, and we gave, until when we were neck and neck, like two horses in a race, they said: 'From us is a prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven.' So when shall we attain the like of this! By Allah, we will never believe in him or accept him." Al-Akhnas then rose and left him.

So this is a matter of angry jealousy over positions and worldly authority. Therefore Allah answers them, saying:

﴿Is it they who would apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We raised some of them above others in rank so that some may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ (43:32)

Here the Truth consoles His Messenger (ﷺ), saying to him:

﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you; but it is not you that they deny, rather the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ (6:33)

They are wrongdoers, because wrongdoing is placing a right in other than its deserving place. The most abominable kind of wrongdoing is polytheism, for the Truth, glorified and exalted, alone deserves worship. The lighter form of wrongdoing is when a person transfers an acquired or granted right to someone other than its owner, and this kind of wrongdoing exists among people. The polytheists transferred the right of the Divine Essence to other than its rightful recipient, namely idols and images; but the believers are those who acknowledge the right of the Divine Essence in worship.

There is another kind of wrongdoing I wish to speak about: that a person wrongs his own name. For example, his father names him "Mahdi" (the guided one), yet he fills the world with corruption, harming himself and harming others. To such a person we say: it is your duty to honour your father's hope in you, so do not wrong your name "Mahdi"; let there be justice between the name and the named, by your conduct being in harmony with the name your father gave you.

But if his father named him "Mahdi" and did not teach him anything of the teachings of guidance and religion, and then the young man went out into the world to fill it with misery for himself and others, and was guided afterwards, then this is a young man who was able to learn guidance, and so his name became true to what it names.

In the 1930s, when we visited Cairo, we used to hear warnings: "Beware lest you set foot in 'Ama al-Din Street, for all vices are in this street." I was surprised that the street's name was "'Imad al-Din" (the Pillar of Religion) while it was a place of vices, and so I said about that:

Most loathsome of wrongs after polytheism is
that a name be wronged whose opposite is a mountain.
A street like "'Imad al-Din" in its naming,
yet for the obstinacy of religion it has been made so.

In life there are many cases of names wronged by their bearers. But the greatest and most loathsome degree of wrongdoing is polytheism with Allah: ﴿but the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ Denial (juḥūd) is the tongue's refusal and haughtiness, and its unwillingness to utter the word of truth. If the polytheists were to be alone with themselves and examine the matters of Muhammad and the matters of the message, they would find that their hearts are convinced that he is truthful, that he is a Messenger, and that the method came for guidance. But their tongues are unable to acknowledge that.

That is why the method of faith commands that when one of us wishes to discuss a question—whether it is truth or falsehood—he should not discuss it in a crowd of people, but let him first discuss it within himself, so that he may distinguish the truth in it from error. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand before Allah in pairs and individually, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion.﴾ (34:46)

It is as if the Truth is guiding us to how to distinguish: either we discuss with ourselves, or two people discuss together so that one of them may be convinced of the other's opinion without a third witnessing his defeat, which would make him obstinate and argumentative. The Truth advised this to those who accused the Messenger of Allah of being possessed—God forbid—by madness. For madness is when actions occur without foundations, without reflection or consideration of their consequences, and devoid of wisdom, so

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 34:

As long as Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger to all mankind, he must bear many hardships and endure them. God has prepared him and equipped him for this, and the earlier messengers likewise suffered harm in proportion to their call. As for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he is for all mankind, and there is no message after him; therefore many peoples gather against this Messenger and this message. For this reason, the Truth, glorified is He, says to him:

﴿Certainly messengers before you were denied, but they patiently bore their denial and their harm until Our help reached them. None can alter the words of God. And certainly there has come to you some of the news of the messengers (34)﴾.

If the messengers who came before you were denied and patiently bore it, though they were messengers to their own peoples or to a particular nation, and for a particular time, then what of you, O Seal of the Messengers, who are sent to all mankind and to all times? You must bear this, because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has chosen you for this mission, and He is the All-Knowing that you are fit for it. The Truth is bound to give victory to His messengers; it is not conceivable that evil or falsehood should be left to overcome the messengers, and as long as God, glorified and exalted is He, has sent the Messenger, He must surely support him.

Thus He says:

﴿And certainly Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers (171). Indeed they would be the ones given victory (172). And indeed Our army, they would be the victors (173)﴾ (Surat al-Saffat).

Since the word of God has preceded regarding the messengers, there is no one who can change the words of God, and no one is able to alter the principles that God has laid down by His saying, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿None can alter the words of God. And certainly there has come to you some of the news of the messengers (34)﴾ (part of verse 34 of Surat al-An'am).

God, glorified is He, has related to His Messenger the stories of the messengers. He did not content Himself with telling His Messenger that the messengers before him had been denied by their peoples; rather, the Truth showed His Messenger what happened to every messenger whose mention came in the Noble Qur'an, and what happened to the Messenger – any messenger – of steadfastness before enemies, and then He made clear that the word of truth had always prevailed. The Truth has related some of the stories of the messengers, and He said:

﴿Among them are those whose stories We have related to you, and among them are those whose stories We have not related to you﴾ (part of verse 78 of Surat Ghafir).

Thereafter, the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And if their turning away is grievous to you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign—(you could do so). And had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance. So do not be among the ignorant.﴾ (6:35)

O Muhammad, you are a messenger from Allah, and with you is a method, which is the miracles that indicate the truth of what you have brought. If their turning away is grievous to you, and it weighs heavily upon you that they turn their backs and disregard you, then if you are able to make for yourself a tunnel in the earth to bring them a sign, or to build a ladder to ascend with into the sky in pursuit of this sign, then do so. But you will not be able to do that, because it is beyond the limits of your capacity. The polytheists and the hypocrites will meet punishment, because you, O Messenger of Allah, came to scatter the scepter of their worldly authority and to establish the justice of faith. Therefore they tried to mock you and harm you.

The disbelievers asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to descend to the earth so that he might cause a spring to gush forth for them from it, and they asked him to ascend into the sky and to make it fall upon them in pieces, to destroy them. These were things that were not in Mecca and not within the power of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says to him something that closes the doors of sorrow upon him and eliminates the causes of grief and regret in him because of their turning away, and that he should know that mockery and opposition are a natural matter for every messenger of the messengers, and you, O Messenger of Allah, are more deserving of this, because your mission is greater than all the messengers. We notice here that the Truthful removes the answer of "in" (إن). He says:

﴿then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder, then bring them a sign﴾ (part of 6:35)

The Truth did not say: "then do that," as if the matter were a calming of the Messenger; because the answer in such a case is known, for the Messenger does not compel anyone to faith. The turning away of these people is an intended matter of the Necessary Being, in order to test them; and if He had willed to subdue them, He would have done so, for no one can defy Allah. The whole universe obeys Allah: the sun, the moon, the stars, the air, the water, the mountains, the earth, and everything in the universe belongs to Allah, including the animals subjected to serve man. But He—glorified is He—gave man the choice, so that he may come to Allah out of love.

We know that the Truth has left some of the subjected things not made docile, to prove to man that he did not tame things by his own cunning, but that He—exalted is His majesty—is the One who created them and made them subservient to him. Therefore we see a small child pulling a huge camel, and we see any man, however strong, taking caution and precaution against a small snake.

﴿Do they not see that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners? (36:71) And We subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat (36:72).﴾ (Surah Yasin)

Had Allah not made them docile, no one could approach them. I always give this example, when someone said: "Why did Allah create the fly?" A man of the people of illumination (ishraq) said: "So that He may humble the tyrants with it; their authority does not extend to these insects." The Truth has given man the honor of sovereignty, and He has also taught him to be humble before the Creator.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, conveys to His Messenger:

﴿And had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant.﴾ (part of 6:35)

That is, He—glorified is He—if He had willed, would have made all people believers. Someone may say: How does Allah address His Messenger, saying to him: ﴿So do not be among the ignorant﴾? We say: when the Truth says that to His Messenger, He says it not from a suspicion that the Messenger would do it; for the Messenger is protected from ignorance, but it is a statement that exalts the Messenger, freeing him from being in this category of the ignorant.

Al-Sha'rawi continues, saying: Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿Only those who listen respond. As for the dead, Allah will raise them up; then to Him they will be returned.﴾ (36)

Yastajību (يستجيب) means that they obey the command of the one who commands and the prohibition of the one who prohibits. There is a difference between *al-istijaba* (الاستجابة) and *al-ijaba* (الإجابة). *Al-istijaba* is that the one from whom you ask responds to you with what you asked for and makes it happen for you, whereas *al-ijaba* is that the one you ask answers you, even if by refusing what you say; the answer may be contrary to what you asked. Allah says: ﴿Only those who listen respond﴾, meaning that those who respond to the call of truth are those who listen with their ears and hearts, affirming it. This is because there is a difference between a hearing whose outward form is hearing and whose inner reality is turning away, and a hearing whose outward form is obedience and whose inner reality is love for that obedience. We know that receiving what is heard is one thing, and a person being moved by what is heard is another.

When good listening is united with the emotion of love to carry out what a person has heard, this is what faith demands. The believers are those who listen to the words of Allah with the emotion of love, and they differ from those who hear speech through one ear and let it out through the other, leaving the words unapplied, so that no trace of the speech remains in the conscious soul.

Thus we see that Allah has created and made in man senses that guide and direct him either to faith or to disbelief. The ear of the believer hears, the heart affirms, and the intellect scrutinizes and believes. As for the disbeliever, his ear hears but his heart opposes, and his intellect searches for the causes of disbelief, desiring it and striving toward it. Therefore the senses do not perform their functions in harmony, and those who hear but do not respond are among the dead. The matter, then, is not restricted to hearing; rather, what is required is a hearing that is moved by what is heard and submits to it. Do not think that Allah is unable to make the one who does not hear with obedience become guided and upright, for nothing and no being can resist Allah, because He, glory be to Him, gives life to the dead.

Since He, glory be to Him, gives life to the dead, He does not demand compelled faith; rather, He demands faith of choice and conviction. Had He willed, He would have sent down upon them a sign from heaven so that their necks would remain humbly subject, but He, glory be to Him, seeks hearts, not mere shells. Those who respond to the call of faith are indeed the living, while those who do not respond are in the status of the dead. After their death and the end of their lives, Allah will raise them to question them about their deeds in the life of this world. When they return to Allah, they will find the reckoning. We know that the final and constant return is to Allah. Whoever returns to Allah with good deeds hastens to a good reward and longs and yearns for it, whereas whoever is returned by Allah by compulsion fears the painful punishment.

The Truth (al-Haqq, Allah) then says:

﴿They say: "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say: "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."﴾ (37)

Allah, glorified is He, makes clear to us their persistence in disputation and their demand for some sign. The sign (āyah) is the extraordinary matter that Allah sends through the hand of a prophet to establish the truth of his message in conveying what he brings from Allah. It is as though they do not want to acknowledge that the Qur'an is clear signs, despite their acknowledgment of the greatness of the Qur'an. They said:
