﴿And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two towns?"﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 31).

But they did not acknowledge the Qur'an as a miraculous sign, because they knew that each of the earlier messengers had come with a miraculous sign separate from the method (manhaj) he brought. Mūsā (peace be upon him) had the staff, and his hand which he took out from his pocket and it was white without blemish, and the parting of the sea; and his method was the Tawrah (Torah). ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) had the miracle of speaking in the cradle by Allah's permission, healing the blind and the leper and raising the dead by Allah's permission; he brought the Injīl (Gospel), completing with spiritual matters those material things that had filled the souls of the Jews. After they said of the Messenger of Allah that he fabricates lies, the Truth challenged them to bring the like of the Qur'an, then lowered the challenge to bringing ten surahs like it, then to bringing a surah like its shortest surah. So, fabrication is also possible for you: just as Muhammad fabricated, you too may fabricate in what you have excelled in and surpassed others in, namely the methods of eloquence. The Qur'an has challenged them, and since it has challenged them, it is a miracle, because the essence of a miracle is the challenge. Allah challenges them to bring a surah like the surahs of the Qur'an, and they cannot. He challenges them in the matter of language, and they are the masters of language and the most brilliant in it.

The Qur'an came to challenge them in the field of their excellence, but some of the Arabs demanded from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a tangible cosmic miracle that they could see. Foolishness blinded them from knowing that sensory evidence has limited effect: whoever sees it says it is a miracle, and whoever does not see it may believe and may disbelieve. We Muslims do not believe in sensory miracles except because the Qur'an reported them; and because the Qur'an has come to all people, it was not reasonable that the final method be separate from the miracle of the Prophet who brought it.

The Qur'an, therefore, came as the miracle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it is a lasting moral sign forever, with its rulings and systems, its cosmic signs and scientific matters. If creation differs in languages, what the Qur'an contains of miracles will never end its wonders until the Day of Resurrection. Every day we derive from the signs of Allah new miracles that silence every denier, because they are cosmic miracles. And strangely, some of those who derive them are neither Muslims nor believers in the Qur'an.

But some of the polytheists were not content with the Qur'an as a sign and miracle indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger, and they demanded a tangible miracle. Was that demand for a sign genuinely sought, hoping through it to know the truth and believe in it, or was it merely a pretext behind which they hid so as not to believe? If the demand for a sign was a real matter arising from their hearts, we take them by the hand, guide them, direct them and say to them: the messengers who came with miracles other than the book of the method were messengers to specific peoples and for a limited time, so there came with them cosmic signs that are seen once and then end. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came for all time and for all places, and therefore his sign and miracle could not be tangible, so that it would not be confined to a specific time and place. The Truth willed that the miracle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) be the lasting method. The treasure of the Qur'an has manifested and revealed of cosmic signs what has been realized of knowledge and seen by humankind, and what humankind will continue to discover until the Hour comes. Therefore the Truth said:

﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ (Surah Fussilat, part of 53).

That is, humankind will be shown by Allah, and He will reveal to them of His signs until the face of the truth appears and becomes clear to them. And if you propose a sign merely as an evasion and a delay in declaring faith, then know that other peoples before you proposed signs, and Allah sent down these signs, yet they disbelieved:

﴿And We did not withhold from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ (part of 59, Surah al-Isra').

Just as the people of Ṣāliḥ demanded the she-camel, and it came to them, yet they denied that sign and slaughtered the she-camel: ﴿So their Lord destroyed them for their sin and leveled them﴾. So the matter of demanding signs had already occurred in earlier nations. He, glorified is He, is able to send down signs, but most of the polytheists do not know. And they will say what those whom the Truth, glorified is He, spoke of said:

﴿And We did not withhold from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ (part of 59, Surah al-Isra').

Allah, glorified is He, has sent down the Qur'an to His Messenger (ﷺ), and in it are many signs, so great and so exalted that they cannot be counted or confined. Had they proposed a sign and Allah fulfilled it for them and they still did not believe, it would have been binding upon Allah to destroy them all. Allah gave His Messenger (ﷺ) a promise that He would not destroy them while he (ﷺ) was among them:

﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾.

Therefore, Allah's not responding to send them a sign is a kind of concern for them, for among them are those who will believe, and among them are those whose descendants will be believers who carry the method and uphold it until the Hour comes, because they are the followers and bearers of the final message.

Afterwards, the Truth comes with an explanation that rises step by step:

﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then unto their Lord they shall be gathered.﴾ 38

He, glory be to Him, makes clear to us: I give the signs which I know the sound nature (al-fitrah al-salimah) receives as signs and believes in. I have sent down the Qur'an to you so that you believe in the Messenger who bears it as a method that sets your lives right. I have made you lords of the universe; all created beings serve you, because you are the children of Adam. It would have been more fitting for you to notice that animals are at your service, plants serve animals and humans, and all beings in existence direct their effort, made subservient, to your service. If I have brought all the species and made them beneath you, given them what sets them right and sustains them, placed for them a system, and given them instincts sufficient for the good of their affairs, so that they fulfil their task with you in a form that comforts you, then if this is our conduct and our work with those who serve you, how then will it be with you? I have sent down the method that sets right the life of the one whom I have appointed as a lord (khalifah) on the earth.

﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then unto their Lord they shall be gathered.﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 38)

All creatures other than man, God gave faith by nature (bil-fitrah), and guided them to provision by instinct (bil-gharizah). He distinguished man above all creatures by reason ('aql), but man uses his reason once in a sound and correct way, and so arrives at faith, and uses it once in a bad way, and so goes astray from faith. It was incumbent upon man to know that he learned by imitating what is below him among creatures; Qabil learned from the crow how to cover the nakedness of his brother. The designer of aircraft learned the craft of flight from studying birds. Therefore it was necessary for man to learn that he has a Creator who made for him, from among the species, those that serve him, so that he might develop his life and the care of his dignity after death. An example is what an ant said to the rest of the ants:

﴿When they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said: "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you unknowingly."﴾ (part of 27:18)

The ants are a community that has guards; one of their guards spoke this statement as a warning to the rest of the ants.

And God, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And there is nothing but that glorifies His praise, but you do not understand their glorification.﴾ (part of 17:44)

So every community among those many communities that God created in the universe glorifies His praise, but no one understands the languages of those communities. God informed us that He taught Prophet Solomon the languages of all peoples and all the communities created by God. For this reason, when Prophet Solomon heard what the ant said, he smiled (laughing at her words).

Thus we learn that God gave Solomon's hearing (udhn) what enabled it to possess a sensitivity that picks up the vibration issuing from the ant's voice and understands what that vibration conveys and performs; therefore Solomon, peace be upon him, smiled at her words, because God had taught him the speech of those creatures. Had God taught us the speech of these creatures, we would understand their glorification of God, but we do not understand their glorification because we have not learned their language. An example of this — and to God belongs the highest likeness — is that an Arab may travel to a country that speaks English while ignorant of that language, so he understands nothing of what is said. Therefore, if God taught you the speech of birds, the speech of inanimate things, and the speech of plants, you would know their languages.

Did not the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, say:

﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] along with David.﴾ (part of 21:79)

Inanimate things, the mountains, glorified along with David. Likewise birds: behold the hoopoe, who recognised the question of tawhid and was grieved in himself that he saw the queen of Sheba and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God:

﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun other than God, and Satan has made their deeds appear fair to them.﴾ (part of 27:24)

Thus the hoopoe recognised the question of tawhid, and knew that Satan has entrances into the living being, and knew that prostration is only due to God, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿Why do they not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (part of 27:25)

So every creature is a community like them. Someone may say: "But there are creatures that are neither in the sky nor on the earth, such as fish in the seas?" We say: water is three-quarters of the earth, and the fish swims in a part of the water which is a part of the earth. So it swims in a part of the earth. Glory be to Him who created the creatures on the earth and created the birds, and created the lower of these communities and guided them to their interest and the source of their life: ﴿Who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided﴾.

We see scientists now trying to discover the language of fish, and to uncover all the secrets of the bee's kingdom and its order, how ant nests become storehouses in summer for the food of winter. They have studied the behaviour of ants with a grain of wheat, and how the ant removes the germinating cells from the wheat seed, because if the germinating cells enter with the grain of wheat into the ants' food store, they may sprout and destroy the ants' nest. Thus we see the truth of the Supreme Truth.

﴿Who created and proportioned (2), and who determined and guided (3).﴾ (Surat al-A'la)

The antennae of the ant astonish scientists, because a single ant, for example, sees a piece of sugar, and does not approach it, but goes to summon an army of ants capable of moving the piece of sugar. Scientists found that when the weight of the thing the ants feed on exceeds the capacity of one ant, it summons numbers of ants to perform the task.

Scientists asked: from where do ants have this ability to determine mass, volume and weight? Determining the number that carries a specific volume is strange and wondrous. How can we imagine that the ant distinguishes between two things of equal volume but different weight, such as a mass of iron and another of the same size made of sponge? The ant summons many times more for the mass of iron than it summons to carry the mass of sponge although they are equal in volume; it is from the power of the Truth who created and proportioned and who determined and guided.

Then you turn to animals and find the male and the female, and find that all beauty is in the males of animals, while this is not the case among female animals; the overwhelming majority are females and the minority males. A male does not approach his female except in a particular season, and until the season of mating arrives, the female turns to preparing the nest and readying it for whatever offspring may come. This process is for a lofty wisdom, perhaps for the survival of the animal species when man helps in the building up of the earth.

In the world of birds, we find birds build the nest with a beautiful art to receive the chick that has emerged from the egg, and they line the nest for it with the finest things; they do that with excellent perfection, in a manner that perhaps humans would be unable to do like them. Then we find in the world of animals and birds that as soon as the creature becomes able to rely on itself, the mother does not recognise her son from another's son. So all creatures are communities like them in provisions, lifespans and deeds, and God spoke truly when He said: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book.﴾

The Book here may be the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), but we say: it is the Qur'an, and everything that exists and is mentioned or hidden is in the noble Qur'an. The Qur'an mentions that these communities know tawhid, that they glorify God, and contemporary work discovers every minute the truths of this ordered universe. We find reason guiding us to create things for the benefit of our lives, but when we follow desire, we corrupt this universe. God, glory be to Him, has made for the subservient animals of the earth a scope for work, provision and lifespan by the dictate of instinct; likewise He made it for birds and for all creatures:

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says in His noble, decisive verses:

﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then unto their Lord they shall be gathered.﴾ (part of 6:38)

So every creature will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. Did not the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, say in what Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, narrated: "You shall surely render the rights to their owners on the Day of Resurrection, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned sheep."

That is, the Truth, glory be to Him, takes retribution from the horned sheep that gored the hornless sheep, and compensates it for the pain that befell it. After every creature other than humans and jinn takes its right, it turns to dust. As for those who hear and do not respond, they are the deniers of the signs, and therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says of them:

﴿Those who denied Our signs are deaf and dumb in darknesses. Whomever God wills, He leads astray; and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path (39).﴾

1 al-jalha': the one without horns, in contrast to the qarna' (horned).
2 Narrated by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

Deafness is an affliction that strikes the ear, so it does not hear. Muteness is an affliction that strikes the tongue, so it does not speak. Muteness is tied to deafness, because a person does not speak except when he has heard, since language is the child of imitation (muhakah). A person does not speak except when he has heard.

Human beings grow up in different environments, and they speak only the language of the environment in which they were raised, because language is neither blood nor lineage. Rather, language is hearing. What the ear hears, the tongue reproduces. A person does not read except when he has heard and understood the connection between what he hears and what he sees. Therefore we know that hearing is the first gateway to perception, and for this reason deafness came before muteness.

But is perception tied only to deafness and muteness? No. A person hears first, then sees, then tastes, then smells, then touches, and then intellectual knowledge comes to him. An example of this is that every person knows that fire burns, and he knew this only because he found that it had touched a living thing and burned it. Another example: people agree that the song of the nightingale (al-andalib) is beautiful, and this agreement came from people's hearing the nightingale's voice. Thus intellectual knowledge comes as a result of sensory knowledge.

﴿Deaf, mute, in darkness.﴾ They have no ability to see guidance from any direction. They are deaf, not hearing the word of truth; mute, not speaking; and in darknesses, they are not guided to the perception of things or to faith. All of this is referred back to the divine will: ﴿Whomever God wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path.﴾ But does the will force itself upon people and overpower them? No. For the Truth says: ﴿Indeed God does not guide one who is a transgressor, a liar.﴾ (Qur'an 40:28). And He, glory be to Him, also said: ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ Therefore, by their advancing wrongdoing, defiance, and disbelief, and they did this by choice, sickness became established in their hearts, and God increased them in sickness. He, glory be to Him, is the most Self-sufficient of the self-sufficient regarding association with Him; whoever associates anything with God, it is for him (the associate).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 40:

After that comes a command to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

﴿Say: "Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, would you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful?"﴾ (6:40)

"Ara'aytakum" (أرأيتكم) is composed of an interrogative particle and a verb, and of a pronoun, namely the open tā' addressed to the second person, as when you say: "Ara'ayta fulanan" (أرأيت فلانا), as if you were saying to him: "If you have seen him, then tell me about him." When you say this to the addressee, you are asking him about something he has seen and observed. Then you add the second-person kāf, as if you are saying to him: "Tell me about yourself." So the meaning is: "Tell me about yourselves," and thus "ara'aytakum" means: inform me about your condition, as one who sees. The command is therefore to the Messenger of Allah to ask the polytheists to tell him what they do when harm befalls them, or anything beyond the ordinary causes: do they call upon al-Lat and al-'Uzza?

No, they cannot, at the time of imminent danger, lie to themselves. Rather, they call upon Allah, whom they do not openly profess to believe in. Had they been truthful in their disbelief, they would not have called upon Allah; rather, they should have called upon their gods. But in the moment of danger they say: "O Lord," as if they know that there is no savior for them except Him, glory be to Him. Thus the falsehood of their disbelief and their associating others with Allah is laid bare before them. No one deceives himself, not even the charlatan who claims to heal people: if illness strikes him, you find him turning to a specialist, a trained physician. No one deceives himself; and at the moment danger touches a person, you find the truth welling up from the person himself.

The Prophet (ﷺ) asks them: whom do they call upon in the moment of danger? They call upon Allah, as though they do not trust their gods:

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing﴾ (part of 10:12)

But what happens when the heart returns to its hardness?

﴿Then when We remove from him his harm, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him﴾ (part of 10:12)

Why, then, does he seek Allah's help at the time of danger and not follow the obligation? The command comes to the Messenger to ask them: whom do you call upon in the moment of danger? And the answer also comes from the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon, so He removes what you call upon Him for, if He wills, and you forget what you associate with Him﴾ (6:41)

You, O polytheists, call upon none but God to remove the harm from you. If He sees that it is wise to answer your supplication, He answers it; and if He sees that it is wise not to answer, He does not answer. Yet they call upon God and forget their gods, and those whom they associated with Him in worship.

The Exalted Lord says:

﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] to communities before you, and We seized them with misfortune and adversity, that perhaps they might humble themselves.﴾

Indeed, the Truth (al-Haqq) sent messengers to earlier communities with the signs and the method, but their peoples denied them, so God seized them with hardships and calamities that cause harm, whether to the self or to property: through sickness and poverty, that perhaps they would humble themselves before God, glory be to Him and exalted be He.

So when the Truth touches a human being with al-Ba'sa' (hardship) and al-Darra' (adversity), that is, with hardships or with that which harms and injures, He intends for the human being to test himself. If he is a believer in something other than God, let him go to the one in whom he believes, but He will not remove that hardship or that harm from him except when he returns to God. And when he humbles himself before God, God may not accept such humbling from him, and He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So why, when Our might came upon them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hard, and Satan made attractive to them what they used to do.﴾

He, glorified is He, urges them and exhorts them to humble themselves and submit before God, so that He may lift from them what has befallen them. But their hardened hearts prevent them, even in the moment of being touched by harm, from turning to God, out of fear of following the obligation (al-taklif, the religious duty). The hardness of the heart takes such a form that guidance cannot penetrate it, and as the Truth (al-Haqq) said:

﴿Nay, but on their hearts is the rust of what they have been earning.﴾ (Surah al-Mutaffifin, 83:14).

That is, their hearts have become closed and covered after God has sealed them and set a seal upon them, so they accept no good and do not incline toward it, and so they do not believe.

Continuing, the Truth (al-Haqq) says in His noble words:

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair.﴾

When they forgot the reminder that had come to them from the Truth, concerning the method (al-manhaj) and monotheism (al-tawhid), through the messengers, He, glory be to Him, afflicts them with a punishment that takes them by surprise. They fall into a bewilderment that seizes their minds, scatters their hearts, and cuts off their hope.

The messengers come only to remind, because faith (al-iman) already exists in human nature (al-fitrah). What hides faith is heedlessness (al-ghaflah). Man lives in a universe full of blessings, for which no one has any claim or hand, and which no one has bestowed upon himself. This man should have lived always within the expanse of praise to God, the Lord of this blessing.

Reminder from the Truth to His servants comes through blessings or through the messengers who bring successive revelations. Suppose a man has been heedless of God's blessing of food; then the moment of hunger arrives, and he sits craving food, and God grants him that food. How can he forget the moment of satiety, the one who gave him this food?

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ may refer either to the informing through the messengers, who remind people that the Bestower is God, and that God sent down the method so that the universe may be set right by it; or it may refer to the blessings that pass over a person at every moment, because they alert him that there is One who gave them. For example, when a person covers his nakedness and body with beautiful clothing, does he not wonder who granted the craftsman that talent by which the garment was designed? So how does a person take the blessing and not remember the Giver? God, glory be to Him, does not deprive them of blessings at the very time they abandon thanking Him; rather, He opens for them the gates of everything, that is, He gives them more and more blessings, so they live in luxury, in kinds of life of power, health, abundance, rank, dominion and standing. Then what happens? ﴿We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair.﴾

We said before this rural proverb: "No one falls from atop the mat." But the Truth may elevate the disbelieving polytheist at times, then seize him suddenly, so that he falls and the pain is great. If you see a man who has been wasteful against himself and whom the Truth has widened in the order of life, beware of being tempted and saying: "Ah, the wrongdoing disbeliever rides the finest cars and lives in the most splendid palaces." Do not say that, for you will see the dreadful end of this wrongdoer.

Look at the precision of expression in the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted: ﴿We opened for them the gates of everything﴾. He opened upon them (fataha 'alayhim)... that is, He gave them power over things, not "opened for them" (fataha lahum). In another place in the noble Qur'an the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed We have opened for you a clear opening﴾.

Thus we know that opening for you (fath lak) is other than opening upon you (fath 'alayk), because opening upon someone means enticing him (istidraj) toward a forced humiliation that will befall him. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair﴾ (part of verse 44, Surat al-An'am)

The seizing comes at the moment of joy. We often see such events in life: we notice a calamity befalling the bridegroom or bride on the day of the wedding. The poet's saying holds true:

"The calamities walked into the red chambers,
the news of death walked into the house of a wedding."

This explains the noble words:

﴿until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly﴾ (part of verse 44, Surat al-An'am).

When we examine the phrase ﴿what they had been given﴾, we find that the blessing they obtained came as a divine preparation that eases these matters; then the Truth seizes them suddenly, that is, the harmful event comes without preliminaries, because the coming of preliminaries might make a person awaken, take precautions, or anticipate it. We know that the Truth says in another place in the noble Qur'an:

﴿Say: Have you considered, if the punishment of God comes upon you suddenly or openly?﴾ (part of verse 47, Surat al-An'am).

That is, punishment may come suddenly, and it may come another time openly. Punishment that comes suddenly is a retribution, while punishment that comes openly is so that no one may say: "Had the punishment come suddenly, he would have taken precaution against that matter." Punishment comes to them while they are in despair (mublisun), that is, hopeless, with no rescuer, no deliverer, and no escape for them.

The true Reality continues with what happens to these people:

﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.﴾

Since these people have forgotten what they were reminded of, and God opened to them the doors of everything, then they rejoiced in what they had been given, and the Truth seized them suddenly, all of this draws our attention to the fact that we must praise God, because He raises His creation through vengeance and blessing, and purifies the universe of the corrupters. Cutting off the remnant of the corrupters is a calamity for these corrupters and a blessing from the blessings of God upon the believers. Some may ask: how does the Qur'an present vengeances as though they were blessings?

We find the Almighty and Exalted Truth saying:

﴿O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass through except with authority. (33) So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? (34) There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and bronze, and you will not be victorious. (35) So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? (36)﴾ (Surah ar-Rahman).

These are vengeances of which the Truth speaks, such as the sending of a flame of fire and bronze. They are vengeances with respect to the disbelievers and upon them, and they are blessings for the believers. We know that making the punishment appear dreadful deters people, and this warning is a blessing from God. When the Truth manifests His blessings upon His creation and cuts off the remnant of the wrongdoers, the believers say, "Praise be to God":

﴿And the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

Return to questioning them by informing them about what is seen:

﴿Say: Tell me, if God took away your hearing and your sight and sealed your hearts, what god other than God could bring them back to you? Look how We vary the signs, yet they turn away (46).﴾

Here the Truth commands His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to question them: what would they do if God took away their hearing, covered their hearts so that they could perceive nothing, and deprived them of the blessing of sight? Is there any other god who could restore to them what the Truth, glory be to Him, has taken from them? They received God's blessings and used them for opposing and hostility toward God. They were given hearing, but they were deaf to hearing guidance; they were given sight, but they were blind to seeing God's signs; they were given hearts, but they closed them against matters of goodness. So what would they do if God took these blessings from them? Is there another god to whom they could turn to recover what God has taken from them?

In life you see that the Truth has deprived some of His creatures of blessings which He has kept for others. In that there is a means of clarification within the universe. Beware, O human, of thinking that when the Truth takes a blessing from a person, He hates that person. Rather, He, glory be to Him, wants to remind people that there is a higher Bestower whom they must believe in. So if the Truth takes these blessings from any disbeliever, what will he do? He will be unable to do anything in the face of God's action.

Here is the Prophet making things clear to them with manifest proofs, yet despite that they turn away from reflection, contemplation and faith: ﴿yet they turn away﴾.

When the believer sees a person afflicted with a disability, he thanks God for His blessings. Indeed the Truth, glory be to Him, in the vastness of His mercy, grants the one with the affliction a distinction in another field. Let us recall the words of the poet:

I was made blind while the intelligence from blindness
Brought me a wondrous opinion, a refuge for knowledge.
And the light of the eye ebbed, becoming a tributary to the heart
Of knowledge, when people neglect its acquisition.

We indeed see a blind man who by his insight guides the sighted to guidance. And we see a deaf man, Beethoven, for example, who captivated people with his music while he was deaf. Thus we find that whoever is struck with an affliction, God compensates him with His bounty and grace in other aspects and fields of his life. There is no other god who could compensate a disbeliever whom God has tried, because God is the One, the Unique: ﴿Look how We vary the signs, yet they turn away﴾, that is, look, O Muhammad, and marvel at how We clarify the signs for them and vary them from one style to another, between rational proofs, the directing to cosmic signs, encouragement and warning, admonition and reminder; yet these disbelievers do not reflect or contemplate, but rather they turn away and withdraw from the truth after its clarification and manifestation.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 6, verse 47:

The Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿Say: "Tell me, if the punishment of God came upon you suddenly or openly, would any perish except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ (6:47).

We observe that the pronoun "tā'" (تاء الضمير, the pronominal "ta") in this verse is vowelled with a fatḥah, whereas in the verse before it the pronominal "ta" carries a ḍammah, where the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Say: "Tell me, if God took away your hearing and your sight and sealed your hearts, what god other than God could bring them back to you? Look how We vary the signs; yet still they turn away."﴾ (6:46) [Surah al-An'am].

We also observe that the verse we are now dealing with contains the second-person particle of address kāf: (أرأيتكم, "a'ara'aytakum"), whereas the verse before it does not carry the kāf of address (أرأيتم, "a'ara'aytum"). We know that each of these words has come to convey a meaning that cannot be conveyed by another, even if the styles are similar. His saying (أرأيتكم) includes and gathers the pronoun of the addressee, which is the open "ta", and also includes the kāf of address; and the combination of the two marks of address, the "ta" and the "kāf", indicates that this is an alert to something beyond it. It is an alert that their destruction will be a uprooting and annihilation. And at another time the Truth says (أرأيتم), meaning: inform me, you, and make me know, an informing that confirms to me the truth of the matter. The interrogative here comes from the root (أرى, ara) and (رأى, ra'a).

The reason for this is that when you ask about something, either the one you ask has witnessed the occurrence of the thing, or the one you ask has not witnessed its occurrence. If he has witnessed it, you say to him: "Did you see what happened to so-and-so and so-and-so?" and he says to you: "Yes, I saw such-and-such." If the one asked has not known of the matter and has not seen it, he answers in the negative. This is what happens among human beings. But when the question comes from God, and the event asked about occurred before the one questioned existed, then faith requires that the one questioned answer about this event with "yes".

An example of this is the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, to the Messenger of God (ﷺ):

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (105:1) [Surah al-Fil].

This address from God to His Messenger (ﷺ) concerns what happened to the companions of the elephant in the year of his birth (ﷺ), and the event was not something the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had seen. One may say: how does God address His Messenger with a question about an event he did not see? We say: by this question the Truth makes clear to His Messenger: listen to Me, and your hearing from Me is above your seeing the event with your eyes. When I say to you "Have you not considered" (ألم تر), its meaning is: know with certain knowledge. This certain knowledge you must trust in its truth as if you had seen it with your own eyes, and beyond that, your eyes may deceive you or lie to you, but when your Lord informs you, He never deceives you or lies to you.

Thus the Truth wants to put these styles in the form of certainty. Let me strike this example, and to God belongs the highest likeness: when a person to whom you have done much good tries to deny your kindness, you do not say to him, "I did good to you," but you say, "Did you see what I did with you on such-and-such a day, and such-and-such a day?" Here your speech appears as a question from you, because you are certain that when he turns his head to answer, he will find nothing but what supports your position, that you stood by his side and were kind to him, and he will find nothing but to say to you: "Yes, I saw that you stood by me in every situation you mention." In such a saying there is a binding, not from the position of the speaker, but from the reality of the addressee.

After the Truth spoke of the obstinacy of the disbelievers before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and their not being content with the signs God sent down confirming the truth of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and then their persistence in proposing signs of their own, which they proposed with some insolence and crudeness, they said:

﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes, and you make rivers gush forth within it abundantly, or you make the sky fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (17:90–93) [Surah al-Isra'].

All of these are questions full of obstinacy, and the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who chose the Qur'an as the miracle and method for His Messenger (ﷺ). He, glory be to Him, knows the truth of His Messenger in conveying from Him, and for all this the Truth shows His Messenger to tell these disbelievers that He, glory be to Him, will not gain any benefit or harm from their belief in Him, but the benefit of belief returns to the servants, and its good returns to them; because He, glory be to Him, possesses all the attributes of perfection before He created creation. They are His from eternity and to eternity.

By the attributes of perfection—knowledge, power, wisdom, and will—He created all creation. Beware, O people, lest you understand that your faith in God adds to Him any attribute of majesty or beauty; rather, faith returns to you yourselves. If among you there are arrogant and obstinate ones, the Truth, glory be to Him, does not leave those who are arrogant and obstinate to stand against His method which governs the movement of life on earth, but He, glory be to Him, seizes the people of arrogance and obstinacy with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. And O people, learn from what happened to those who denied the messengers of God, and what God did to them. He, by His power, glory be to Him, is able to do to you what He did to them. When you survey the stories of the messengers with those who denied God, you find that punishment came upon the people suddenly. Here the Truth says about the people of 'Ad:

﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right and said, "Who is stronger than us in power?" Did they not see that God who created them is stronger than them in power? And they were denying Our signs. So We sent upon them a furious wind during days of misfortune, that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world; but the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ (41:15–16) [Surah Fussilat].

The people of 'Ad became arrogant toward our master Hud (peace be upon him) and those who believed with him, and thought they were the strongest of the strong, and they forgot the power of the Supreme Creator, who is the Greatest Mighty, and they denied the signs of God. So what was their fate? The Truth surprised them by sending a wind of loud sound on days full of ill omen, to make them taste the punishment of humiliation, disgrace and abasement in this world. The Truth swears that the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful, because on that day they will find no helper for them, since they disbelieved in the One who gives justice and victory, who is the Truth, may His power be exalted.

And what of the people of Thamud? The Truth made the path of guidance clear to them. But they chose misguidance and preferred disbelief over faith, and they denied the prophet of God, Salih (peace be upon him), and hamstrung the she-camel. So the thunderbolt descended upon them to burn them in humiliation because of their denial of their messenger:

﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of the punishment of humiliation seized them for what they had been earning.﴾ (41:17) [Surah Fussilat].

And what did the Truth do to the companions of the elephant? The people of Abraha came to demolish the Ka'bah, and the birds of the ababil met them—that is, birds that came in many successive flocks, one after another, carrying stones of baked, hardened clay, which had been decreed and recorded against them to punish them with:

﴿Did He not make their plot into misguidance? And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and made them like eaten-up straw.﴾ (105:2–5) [Surah al-Fil].

Each of those events God brought about suddenly. The meaning of "suddenness" (بغتة, baghtah) is that a calamity surprises a people without any prior notice of it. There are also great events that God sent upon the disbelievers openly (جهرة, jahrah): here are the people of Pharaoh whom God drowned in plain view. Likewise, God destroyed Qarun openly:

{Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses, but he oppressed them. And We had given him of treasures whose keys would weigh down a group of strong men. When his people said to him, "Do not exult; indeed, God does not love the exultant. But seek, through what God has given you, the home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of this world; and do good as God has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land; indeed, God does not love corrupters." He said, "I was only given it on knowledge I have." Did he not know that God had destroyed before him generations stronger than him in power and greater in accumulation? And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins. So he went out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the life of this world said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is of great fortune." But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of God is better for one who believes and does righteousness, and it is not granted except to the patient." So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And he had no company to support him against God, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.}﴾ (28:76–81) [Surah al-Qasas].

Qarun took God's blessing and attributed it to himself; he became enamoured of what he possessed and drowned in pride. So what did God do to him? God caused the earth to swallow him openly, before the eyes of those who had wished for his position. Thus it is possible that God's punishment comes upon the disbelievers suddenly, or that He punishes them openly. What is the reason for the variation between (بغتة, suddenly) and (جهرة, openly)? Suddenness proves to whoever worships other than God that he is deceived in his worship of other than God, because if he were worshipping a true god, that god would not allow his followers to be punished without their awareness. Thus suddenness proves the powerlessness of the objects worshipped, such as idols and others, for those idols were unable to guard their worshippers. Someone among them may say: "The punishment came upon us suddenly; but if it had come to us face to face, we would have been able to confront it and stand before it."

So God also brings punishment openly, and they cannot confront it, and their argument is cut off. Yet despite that, the capacity to perceive the necessity of faith dies in the hearts of these obstinate people. God treats the opponents of our Messenger (ﷺ) in this same manner: when the people opposed him, God brought them matters of wonder, perhaps they would reflect.

Here they agreed to kill him before the Hijrah, standing at the door of his house, but the Truth took him out from among them while they did not see, and they did not succeed in plotting against the Messenger of God, nor did their nightly scheming against the Messenger of God succeed, and God's plan was above every scheme by which the enemies of the Messenger (ﷺ) wished to harm him. They went to the jinn to bewitch him, but neither that magic benefited nor that scheming produced a result. God's honouring of His Messenger (ﷺ) was above everything. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: "Tell me, if the punishment of God came upon you suddenly or openly, would any perish except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ (6:47) [Surah al-An'am].

The verse is also concluded in the form of a question, and the question here—as we have known before—came to affirm the meaning, and so that the acknowledgment comes from the mouths of those who receive this question, and from certainty on their part, and so that the confession from them is an answer by affirmation; and affirmation, as we know, is the chief of proofs.

Suppose a thunderbolt descended or an earthquake occurred in which punishment took place; how would God save the believers from this punishment or that sinking?

Indeed, destruction only falls upon the wrongdoing people, because—

The Almighty did not give the messengers the power to do whatever they wished. They are only conveyors of the message from God. So no one should demand signs from them, because they cannot bring signs at will. Every messenger knows that he is a human being, and he receives only from God. Therefore let us take the messengers as bringers of good news and warners: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners﴾.

We know that good news (bushra) is the announcement of what gladdens before it occurs. Its purpose is to prepare the listener, so that he hastens to what makes the good news come true, by complying with the method of the Creator God. We also know that warning (indhar) is the announcement of what grieves before it occurs, so that the listener may guard himself against falling into the prohibitions that God has forbidden.

As we know, good news stirs the desire of the one who wants to act and loves to do good deeds, and warning alarms and frightens the one who inclines toward evil deeds, so that he may restrain himself and desist. Thus the task of the messengers is good news and warning. So, O people, do not elevate them to another rank or station that is not theirs, and then demand from them signs or other things. For signs and all other things are under the disposition of the Truth, blessed and exalted. It is a breach of good manners for us to dictate to God regarding the signs He has sent with the messengers and to demand other signs. By doing this you would be presuming to correct God.

The Truth then clarifies for us the limits of the messengers' task, saying:

﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners﴾ (part of verse 48, Surat al-An'am).

This is the work of the messengers. What, then, of the work of those who listen to the messengers? The Truth says:

﴿Whoever believes and reforms, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve﴾ (part of verse 48, Surat al-An'am).

What is required, then, of those who listen to the messengers is that they turn towards choosing faith (iman), that they listen to the essence of the method, and that they apply it. Whoever among them believes and reforms, there is no fear for him, because he has secured the great success, and no sorrow will touch or reach him, because the outcome of all his deeds will meet him in his record on the Day of Resurrection. Faith is the tranquillity of the heart in a doctrinal matter that does not float up into the mind to be debated afresh. That is why we call faith ʿaqida (creed), meaning something that has been firmly tied in a knot that never unravels.

The believer in his Lord must summon the proofs and signs that make his faith in his Lord strong and firmly tied. This is the work of the heart. The believer knows that the work of the heart alone is not sufficient as an expression of faith, because the living being is not only a heart, but a heart, limbs, and many organs. Everything in the believing living being must submit to the method of its Lord, so faith must be expressed by the person putting right every action he performs with his limbs, performing it correctly and soundly.

I say this so that the one who says, "My heart is believing and sound," will hear: No, the matter of faith is not like this. It is true that you have believed with your heart, but why have you disabled all your limbs from carrying out what faith requires? Why do you not give your mind the chance to reflect, think, plan, and remember? Why do you not give the eye the chance to take heed and benefit from what it sees? And likewise the hand, the tongue, the ear, the foot, and all the limbs.

Reform (islah) is the work of the limbs: a person thinks with his mind about the idea that benefits people, listens to speech and follows the best of it, and sets right with his hands all that he does. The believer knows that when he looks at the universe, he finds it perfectly arranged, and he sees things(1) that have no role of his in this universe, which are at the highest degrees of refined soundness. The rain falls in its season, the winds blow in their seasons and courses, the movement of the sun is coordinated with the movement of the earth, and every operation of the supreme laws is in absolute soundness.

Corruption comes only from what humans have a hand in. The air becomes polluted by densely packed buildings and the lack of sufficient green spaces, and the air is also polluted by machines that operate and expel poisons resulting from the burning of fuel. When man made machines, he looked to his own comfort and overlooked things he should have taken precautions against. An example is the car exhaust, which increases environmental pollution, although some means have been discovered that could prevent this pollution. Yet some people are lax in adopting them.

When we take the rest of civilization and ride in cars, why do we forget the foundation on which civilization rests, which is precise scientific study, so that we manufacture machines and take from machines what benefits people? Let us work to adopt the means of purifying the environment from pollution and prevent harm to people's lives. The exhaust that comes from our manufacture, like car exhaust and machines, corrupts the air for us, and thus corrupts the lungs of the human being.

We must know that the responsibility of faith is that we look at the thing we make and the quantity of harm resulting from it. Every person who lives in a crowded city is harmed by the effects of car exhaust, even though not every person can afford to buy a car to ride. How then can a car rider accept for himself that he not reform those machines that make his life easy, while his exhaust causes harm to himself and to other people? Therefore the Muslim must not take civilization merely by its appearance and form; rather, the Muslim society must work to adopt the causes of civilization from its original foundations, and study how to avoid harms, so that we do not fall into the circle of "the greatest losers in deeds," those about whom the Truth, glorified be He, said:

﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good works﴾ (Surat al-Kahf).

We should always take the highest example from the universe that God created for us to preserve. The exhaust and by-product of anything created by God benefits humans and benefits the universe. Even animal waste is used to fertilize the land and increase its fertility. Thus we understand the meaning of: ﴿Whoever believes and reforms, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve﴾.

So faith is the work of the heart, and reform is the work of the limbs. Therefore we must reform in the universe in a way that increases its soundness. And let us know that the universe was not deficient, and that by our work we complete what deficiency is in it. The matter is not so; rather, we wanted to live in luxury. And since we want luxury, let us increase the work of the mind, which God created, on the materials and elements before us, which are also created by God, and let us interact with them through the energy and limbs created by God, as long as we want to enjoy blessings beyond the necessities of life.

For example, in ancient times, at the early stage of human life, a person suffering from thirst would drink from the river. Then humans found that they were not made happy by quenching their thirst when they reached out to take a handful of river water, so they made a vessel of clay to drink water from, then made a vessel of copper, then made a vessel of crystal. Did these things affect the necessity of life, or are they the luxury of life?

They are the luxury of life. So if you want to make your life luxurious, then employ your God-created mind on God-created elements, through God-created energy and limbs, and by this God will grant you the insights through which you discover the signs of knowledge in the universe. For example, in the countryside in former times, people depended on their women to fill the jars from the wells or canals, and then the lady of the house would filter the water. When we advanced a little, there were men who worked as water carriers, passing by houses with waterskins full of water. When the people of knowledge applied deduction and reflection, they discovered the law of flow (istitrāq), so they raised the water to a high reservoir, and from the reservoir pipes and conduits of various diameters and sizes extended, and water became present in every house. This is what people did who used the minds God created.

Before that, people had been content with the necessary quantity of water: a family would be content with filling one or two waterskins. But after water came into every house, many people misused water, wasting quantities beyond their need, which put pressure on the sanitation pipes, so they burst and people complain of the overflow of sewage.

The Muslim must observe God's right in his use of everything. The water that a person wastes may be needed by another person. When we stop wasting it, we prevent harm from ourselves and from others, from the overflow of sanitation pipes. Let each of us consider, for example, how much water he consumes during ablution. A person opens the tap, washes his hands three times, rinses his mouth three times, sniffs water into his nose three times, washes his face three times, washes his arms three times, wipes his head, and washes his feet. A person leaves the tap open for all that time, wasting quantities of water. If he thought about using the water that flows from the tap well, others would not complain of scarcity of water. So why does the Muslim not think of taking an amount of water that suffices for ablution and using water well? In the past, a person would perform ablution from a vessel containing half a litre of water, so why do we not use well what God has entrusted to us?

A person must know that faith, as it requires or obliges and enjoins prayer so that the person reforms himself, also requires reforming conduct: we must not squander or waste what we possess of means, and we must study how to advance in righteousness, so that we do not escape the troubles of one thing only to fall into troubles resulting from our mismanagement of the previous thing. Rather, we must study every matter with thorough care, so that a person does not contradict the saying of the Truth:

﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all those one will be questioned﴾ (Surat al-Isra').

That is, you must know, O Muslim, that you are accountable for hearing, sight, and heart, and you will be questioned about that on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore it is not proper for you to neglect taking the best knowledge, so that your speech and action are good. Thus there will be no fear upon you in this world or the next, because you believed and reformed, and likewise no sorrow will grip you in this world or the next: ﴿Whoever believes and reforms, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve﴾.

By this you preserve yourself in the Hereafter and in this world as well, because you walk through life with faith and reform in this world, following the laws of God. If you see, O Muslim, a weakness in the universe, know that one of God's rulings has been disabled. If you see a poor person who is hungry or naked, know that a right of his has been consumed or denied by another. For the One who created the universe created what the rich gives from his surplus to the poor to meet his need, but the rich withheld his hand from God's right. Likewise, there are people who beg without need to beg. Corruption here comes from two sides: the side of a person who has come to find it acceptable to build his body from the sweat of another, or from another wealthy person who does not pay God's right in his wealth. Thereby society suffers hardships.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 49:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And those who denied Our signs, the punishment will touch them for what they used to defiantly disobey (fisq).﴾

Those who denied the signs of God are either those who denied the Messenger in the signs that attest to his truthfulness, and he is the one who conveys from God; these have entered the circle of disbelief (kufr). Or they are those who denied the signs of the method (manhaj), so they did not make use of the method according to its foundations, and they deviated from the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim) and the even way (al-tariq al-sawi). These and those have both committed fisq, that is, they went out of obedience. We know that the word (fisq) is derived from the emergence of the date (al-rutabah) from its skin when its size becomes smaller than what it was, due to the completion of its ripening. Whoever commits fisq against God's method is the one who falls into loss, because the aim of God's method is to preserve the human being, whom God created, through (do this) and (do not do this).

Man commits fisq when he does not do what God commanded him to do, or does what God forbade him to do. We find one of us fearful for the tape recorder or the television set, lest it break, so he follows the established rules for its use. He does not – for example – supply any of the electrical appliances with a type of energy other than that which the manufacturer specifies. If the manufacturer says: use electricity of two hundred and twenty volts so the machine does not break, the person complies with what the manufacturer said. So what about the human being? God – may His power be exalted – created the human being and set down for him the laws of his preservation. Therefore whoever corrupts the laws of preserving his own self, the punishment will touch him. The expression "the punishment will touch them" conveys and suggests that punishment is eager to fall upon the criminal, as if the punishment strove toward him to reach and touch him. Behold the word of the Truth about the Fire:

﴿It almost bursts with rage. Every time a company is cast into it, its keepers ask them, "Did no warner come to you?"﴾ (Surat al-Mulk).

And He, glorified is He, says about the Fire:

﴿On the Day We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Are there more?"﴾ (Surat Qaf).

Thus the punishment itself is keen to reach the one who did wrong. For this reason the punishment insists on touching those who committed fisq. The Truth uses here the word (al-mass, touching) for a wisdom: God's punishment does not approximate to humans.

A person punishes another person according to the measure of his own power and strength, and no one among creation may embody God's power in punishment. Therefore touching alone suffices, because torment varies with the power of the one who tortures. If we attributed the torment to the power of God, the punishment would be terrifying, beyond anyone's capacity to bear.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 6, verse 50:

Then the Truth says:

﴿Say: I do not tell you that I have with me the treasuries of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me. Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not then reflect?﴾ (50)

The word "Say" (qul), as we know, is a command from God to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger conveys what God commands him. It would have been sufficient for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say: "I do not tell you that I have with me the treasuries of God." But this is the precision of conveying from God. The Qur'an is tawqifi (revealed in its exact wording), meaning that every word in it was sent down from God exactly as it is, and the Trustworthy Spirit conveyed it to our master, the Messenger of God, and he conveyed it to us, may God bless him and grant him peace, exactly as it is. This indicates that no one has the right to alter it even in its wording; rather, there must be absolute trustworthiness in transmission.

The Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that the Truth sent him as a guide, a bringer of good news, and a warner, with a sign indicating the truthfulness of his message from Him, which is the Qur'an. Whoever receives this message from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is required to receive it rightly, and not to ask of him anything except what accords with the description he claimed for himself, may God bless him and grant him peace. No one has the right to demand from the Messenger signs other than those God has sent down, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, claimed only that he is a conveyer from God, so the response to him must remain within the framework of this claim.

The disbelievers exceeded this when they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for other signs, such as that springs of water should gush forth from part of the earth, or that he should have a house of gold. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, instructs him to tell them that he does not possess the treasuries of the heavens and the earth with God. How then can you ask for houses and palaces, and how can you ask for knowledge of the unseen so that you may pursue what benefits you and avoid what harms you? Is not the divine method sufficient for you, the method that guides you to produce everything beneficial for you and protects you from everything harmful to you? Furthermore, the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not tell them that he knows the unseen. And by their own testimony, they say about him what the noble Qur'an reports:

﴿They said: "What is this messenger who eats food and walks in the markets? Why was not an angel sent down to him to be a warner with him? Or a treasure thrown down to him, or a garden from which he might eat?" And the wrongdoers said: "You follow only a man bewitched."﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:7-8)

They mocked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and demanded that other signs be given to him. They wondered how he could claim to be a messenger while eating food as they eat and frequenting the markets to earn a living as humans do. Had he been a messenger, God would have spared him the hardship of earning a living, and would have sent down to him an angel to help him convey from God, or would have cast down to him from heaven a treasure from which he could spend, or he would have a lush garden from whose fruits he could eat.

These were the words of the leading polytheists, who wronged themselves through disbelief and wanted to turn people away from believing in the call of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. At one time they accused him of being bewitched, at another of being mad, a third time of raving, a fourth time of being a liar, and a fifth time of receiving the Qur'an from non-Arabs. The Truth refutes all these lies and all those fabrications by which they went astray and led others astray. Indeed, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, is among the messengers:

﴿We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We made some of you a trial for others; will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing.﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:20)

Indeed, the messengers before you, O Messenger of God, used to eat food, earn their livelihood through work, and frequent the markets. So if the polytheists reproach you for that and try to mislead people by every means, then you and those who are with you, O Messenger of God, among the believers, God will surely grant you victory and will recompense each according to what he did. Moreover, the signs the polytheists demanded from the Messenger of God were all obstinacy. He never told them that he was an angel. He told them that he is a messenger conveying from God, and all he delivers is the truthful delivery from God. So how can they ask of him things that relate only to God's ownership of the treasuries of the earth? And how can they ask him to teach them the unseen? And how can they object that he is a messenger and a human who eats, marries, and walks in the markets?

All these statements are evidence of obstinacy, because they asked for things that lie outside the scope of what the Messenger of God claimed for himself, namely that he is a messenger conveying from God. They asked for beneficial goodness, flowing springs, gardens and palaces, and things that are all beyond the power of a messenger conveying from God, because the One who bestows them is God, glory be to Him and exalted:

The word "treasuries" (khaza'in) is the plural of "treasury" (khazana), which is the thing in which every precious item is stored so that it may be brought out at the time of need. One says "khazana" only of something in which you place a precious item that you fear to bring out at the wrong time or place. All the treasuries of the earth belong to God, and He, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿And the earth—We spread it out, and cast into it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it of every well-balanced thing. And We made therein means of livelihood for you and for those whom you do not provide for. And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.﴾ (Al-Hijr 15:19-21)

Thus the Truth has presented the universal principle: the secrets of God and His precious things in the cosmos are in God's hand, in His treasuries, and He, glory be to Him, reveals them, manifests them, and uncovers them at their appointed time. How? The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, spoke about the beginning of creation, about the creation of the heavens and the earth, and spoke of this matter in a general way that the other verses explain. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ (Fussilat 41:9-11)

The Truth commands His Messenger to convey to these polytheists how they disbelieve in God who created the earth in two days, and how they set up partners with Him, though He is the Creator of the earth, which is the arena of human movement. He, glory be to Him, created in it what sustains the son of Adam and by which his life continues until the Hour arrives. Sustenance (qut), as we know, is that which keeps a person alive; and if he desires luxury, he must still have ambition in life. He, glory be to Him, placed in the earth firm mountains (rawasi), that is, mountains, and blessed the earth and the mountains. Then He brought the measuring of sustenance after mentioning the mountains, as if the mountains in their true reality are storehouses of sustenance. Someone may ask: how is that?

We say: Reality has confirmed this truth. If you look at the rivers that flow, you will find that they are formed from water that fell as rain on the mountains. The water, made of tiny fine particles, descends upon these mountains and breaks them down, and the water acts as the "file" that removes from the surfaces of the mountains those sands full of nutrients for the earth, which we call silt (ghareen). Silt, as we know, is what descends with the water from the mountain surfaces into the riverbed; as the water rushes along the riverbed, the fertile material is carried onto the land, and that fertile layer forms from which plants feed. Had God, glory be to Him and exalted, willed, He would have made the entire surface of the earth level, with fertility in it that causes plants to grow.

But His wisdom willed to make nourishment for plants in this way. If you look at plants, you find that they differ from one kind to another in the manner by which they absorb the nutrients they need: one kind draws its food from a depth of half a meter, another from a depth of one meter, and so on. If we do not bring fertilizer, manure, or silt to cultivated land, the land weakens, because the Truth wants the process of cultivation to continue, extend, and follow on; so He made the mountains solid in form, and weathering passes over them through heat, cold, and cracks, and then rain falls on them and dissolves from their surfaces some of those nutritive materials needed by the earth. These nutritive materials are carried by the water to the land, and thus the supply of fertility continues from the mountains to the earth. In this way we find that the mountains in their reality are storehouses of God's bounties.

Are the requisites of life only crops? No. If you look at a small model of the terrestrial globe, you will find it resembling a large watermelon. If you cut a triangle from the crust's surface to the center of the watermelon, making this triangle resemble a pyramid, and then take another triangle from any direction, whether from fertile land, the seas, the mountains, the valleys, or the deserts, and then look at the good hidden in each part of these parts, you would find it equal to the other part. Why? Because life does not depend on a limited range of foodstuffs, but in its building it needs tools and materials of civilization, such as iron, petroleum, manganese, and other treasures of the earth on which civilization rests.

We find these goods stored either in the mountains or in the deserts. But each of these goods has an appointed time and a birth. If you measured and weighed the goods present in any pyramidal triangle of the earth from its center to its surface, and compared them with the weight and measurement of goods in another pyramidal triangle equal to it from the terrestrial globe itself, you would find the goods equal in each of the two triangles. But each kind of these goods has its birth and its appointed time.

﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure (21).﴾ (Al-Hijr)

So whatever is called a thing, it has a treasury with God, from which He sends it down in measure. We see this at the summit of existence, which is the intellect: the intellect is a thing, and it has treasuries with God. The ideas that existed among all humanity over ten centuries cannot be measured against the quantity of ideas possessed by the collective intellect of the world now, because each generation benefited from the premises of the ideas of the generation before it to arrive at a new product. Thus there are treasuries of ideas and of thoughts. Likewise, everything in existence has with God treasuries from which it is sent down only in known measure: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.﴾

When He wills that the birth of some secret should appear, He, glory be to Him, prepares the causes for it. For example, — and to God belongs the highest likeness — in earlier times we used to cut wood from trees to make fuel, and after cutting the wood we feared it would decay. So the Truth placed some of His inspirations in the human intellect so that man could transform wood into charcoal, ensuring the preservation of wood and ensuring a source of energy, which is vegetable charcoal. After that, man discovered mineral coal. After that we discovered petroleum. All of this, the energy goods, was stored in the earth, and man did not discover it until God gave them the readiness to receive this good; and God's giving will continue until the Hour arrives. With coal we entered the age of steam, then we entered the age of electricity, then we entered the age of the atom.

All these things had a birth, and each had a place in God's treasuries. When God sends down any inspiration upon one of His servants, the servant takes the causes and discovers the birth of the hidden secret. And every...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 51:

When God asks us to reflect, to remember and to ponder, He is only awakening in us the true measures by which we reach the goal that God wants. For this reason, the Truth says:

﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor, that they may become righteous.﴾

That is: warn, by the revelation that you follow, those who fear the meeting with God on the Day. Warning (indhar), as we know, is informing someone of a frightening matter before it occurs, so that it may be avoided. Who, then, are those whom the Truth commands His Messenger to warn by the revelation? In the early days of Islam, the enthusiasm of some believers for the works of faith was weak. As long as there is faith in their hearts and they fear meeting God, the revelation is a warning to them of the necessity of earnest works of faith. It is also permissible that the warning by revelation is directed at the People of the Book, because they know that there is another Day on which they will meet God. The warning may also be for a person who believes in the Resurrection but doubts the prophets and their intercession. This kind of person may, through fear and warning, be led to reconsider the matter of faith and accept the true news brought by the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

We may take the warning by revelation in any of the aspects mentioned above. But does the believer fear being gathered to God? No. The believer only fears being gathered stripped of a protector and a helper, for in reality there is no one who protects and helps against God, nor any intercessor who delivers from the punishment of God except by His permission: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ This is what the believers hold to.

The Truth has specified this in His saying:

﴿having besides Him no protector and no intercessor, that they may become righteous﴾ (part of verse 51, Surat al-An'am)

They are the believers who believed in God and His Messenger, but who fell short in some of the obligations and duties contained in the Truth's saying: ﴿Whoever believes and does righteousness﴾. When these believers receive the warning, they may set their affairs right out of fear of being gathered without a protector or intercessor. The believer, therefore, has hope that on the Day of Gathering he will be under God's guardianship and mercy, and these are the ones of whom the Truth said:

﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins, having mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad; perhaps God will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surat at-Tawbah, 102)

If the noble verse includes and comprehends others among the People of the Book, and also includes those who believe in the Resurrection but have not followed prophets:

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 52:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord at morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their reckoning in any way, nor are they accountable for yours in any way, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (6:52)

We know that Allah, glorified and exalted, created man and made him a steward (musta'mar) on the earth, and made him a newcomer to this existence, in which Allah has deposited everything he needs for the sustenance of his life and his happiness.

The Truth desired that among mankind there be a relationship of servitude (istitraq 'ubudi) such that there is no one exalted over the weak, and no tyrant over the oppressed, so that the movement of life may be upright, with each individual given according to what has been prepared for him of talents. When the balance of human relations is disrupted, the Truth, glorified and exalted, returns them to a proof that cannot be doubted: that you, O humans, are equal in the origin of existence, from dust; you are equal in returning to dust; and you are equal in your standing before Allah on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning. So why do you differ in the rest of your affairs? Equality must indeed exist. And here is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), eager for the guidance of his community, imposing upon himself more than his Lord required of him, so his Lord rebukes him, because he was burdening himself out of eagerness for the faith of his people.

Some people may think that Allah's rebuke of His Prophet is a reproach for a shortcoming. We respond to these: that you may understand this kind of rebuke in its true sense. There is a difference between a rebuke for the benefit of the one being rebuked, and a rebuke to blame and reprimand him, because the one rebuked has deviated and disobeyed. Let us give this example – and to Allah belongs the highest likeness – if on an ordinary day you look at your son and find him playing, not going to school, and not studying his lessons, then you rebuke him and reprimand him because he has deviated from what is required of him. But if you find your son spending all his energy, and devoting his times of rest to studying, then you ask him not to burden himself with all this hardship, and you snatch the book from him and say to him: go and rest. In this case you are blaming him for his own benefit, so the blame and rebuke are for him, not against him. Thus, this difficulty that they raise is resolved, in which they say: Allah often rebuked His Messenger.
