We clarify that the Truth rebuked the Messenger for his own sake, not against him, because the Messenger found the path of faith in his message proceeding smoothly among the weak, but he occupied himself and exhausted himself, hoping that the arrogant and tyrannical would taste the sweetness of faith. And the words of the Truth concerning this are:

﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him. As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you attend. Yet it is not upon you that he should not purify himself.﴾ (Surah ʿAbasa, 80:1–7)

So for whose benefit is the rebuke here? It is a rebuke for the benefit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And when the Truth, glorified and exalted, says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surah al-Tahrim, 66:1)

the verse points to a matter that angered the Prophet (ﷺ), so he refrained from some of what the human soul desires of things Allah had made lawful. The rebuke here too is for the benefit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Because of his intense eagerness for the guidance of all the people, he loved to treat the tyrants with some gentleness, in order to win their hearts. But the tyrants do not want to be equal with the weak. The chiefs of Quraysh passed by and found with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, Suhayb, Bilal, 'Ammar and Salman al-Farisi, who were among the weak, and they said: O Muhammad, are you content with these from your people? Are these the ones whom Allah has favored from among us? Shall we become followers of these? Drive them away, perhaps if you drive them away we will follow you.

It is as if they were saying to him: you have been satisfied with these weak ones and left us, the strong; we will not sit with you unless you remove these from you so that we may sit. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with the spontaneous instinct of faith, said only: I am not one to drive away the believers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knows that there were among the likes of them those who said to other prophets the same as they said. The people of Noah (peace be upon him) said to him what the Noble Qur'an related:

﴿So the chiefs who disbelieved among his people said: We see you only as a human like ourselves, and we see none following you except the lowest of us, those of immature judgment, and we see in you no merit over us; rather, we think you are liars.﴾ (Surah Hud, 11:27)

Some of the disbelievers tried to present a middle position to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: when we come, remove them from you so that we may sit with you, and when we rise from you, let them sit. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) found in this opinion a middle solution that could bring the viewpoints closer, and he consulted 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and 'Umar said: If you did so, then we would see what they want. The wealthy chiefs of Quraysh demanded that the Messenger write them a document to that effect; the inkwell and pens were brought, and before the writing, the words of Allah were revealed:

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord at morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their reckoning in any way, nor are they accountable for yours in any way, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 6:52)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw aside the sheet that had been brought for them to write upon, containing words that would separate the sitting of the chiefs of Quraysh with the Messenger of Allah from the sitting of the weak followers of the Messenger. The Prophet (ﷺ) had only inclined toward writing that out of hope for the Islam of these polytheists and the Islam of their people through their Islam, out of mercy for them and compassion toward them. He (ﷺ) saw that this would not cost his companions anything or diminish their rank for them. So he inclined to it, and Allah revealed the verse and forbade him from what they had intended of driving away, not because he (ﷺ) had actually done it and driven them away and distanced them, and then afterwards called the weak, and they came to him.

Previously the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to sit with the weak, and if he wished to rise from the gathering, he would rise. But Allah willed that He honor these weak people after He had forbidden him from driving them away, and that He honor them, glorified be He, with what they had been pained by. Another divine command came that the Messenger of Allah should not rise from his gathering with the weak until they rose themselves. So the Truth, blessed and exalted, said:

﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord at morning and evening, seeking His countenance; and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life; and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 18:28)

When this verse was revealed, he (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed in my community one whom He commanded me to keep patient with." (1)

By this noble statement, the Truth, glorified and exalted, intended to honor the weak and the oppressed. Salman al-Farisi and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: it was about us that this was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us and draw near to us until his knee touched our knee, and when he wished to rise he would rise from us. Then the verse was revealed: "And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord," and he left rising from us until we rose, and we used to recognize that and hasten to rise. That is, they were the ones who would rise first from the Messenger of Allah's gathering. So the words of the Truth: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord at morning and evening, seeking His countenance" – this is the word of Allah, the Glorified, which the Messenger of Allah was commanded with, and every person after the Messenger of Allah is likewise commanded with it. In this is the pinnacle of honor for those among the weak who constantly remember Allah, because they are the people of love of faith, and they are the ones who preceded to it.

Here is one of the caliphs of the Muslims, to whom the chieftains of the Arabs who had embraced Islam came and asked permission to enter. He did not permit them until he had first permitted the weak among the Muslims. The noses of each of these chieftains swelled, and they said:

Does he permit these and leave us? We have become Muslims! One among them who understands and comprehends the matter of religion said: Has every one of you become proud that these were permitted before you? They were called and they answered; you were called and you delayed. How will it be with you when they are called to enter Paradise and your entry is delayed?

These weak ones desire by obedience the countenance of Allah, and the phrase "the countenance of Allah" indicates that faith has permeated their hearts, and that they came to faith fleeing with their religion from the oppression of the oppressors and the tyranny of the tyrants who wanted them to disbelieve and go astray. They have found faith sweet, and the countenance of Allah sweet to them; it was sweet for them that all reward be deferred to the Hereafter.

When we hear the words of the Truth: "seeking His countenance," this is a description of Allah, exalted be He, as having a countenance, and in this case we apply what we apply when we hear a description of Allah: we take the description within the frame of His saying: "There is nothing like unto Him" (42:11).

The face is used to mean the essence, because the face is the distinguishing mark of persons. If you meet people who have covered their faces, wrapped themselves in their garments and concealed their heads with them, you will not be able to distinguish between them.

It is said: so-and-so met the faces of the people, meaning he met the great ones among the people. The Truth, glorified and exalted, says: "Everything perishes except His face" (28:88), and says: "You are not accountable for their reckoning in any way." In this statement there is concern for the dignity of the weak. Someone may say: these weak ones sought refuge in religion in order to flee the oppression of the oppressors, and not out of love for religion. So the Truth clarifies: this is not your task, and it is not for you except to take the outward of their deeds and to leave their inner states to Allah.

"You are not accountable for their reckoning in any way, nor are they accountable for yours in any way, so that you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers" (part of verse 52, Surah al-An'am).

It is as if the Truth were clarifying to His Messenger: had you been accountable for their reckoning in any way, it would have been permissible for you to drive them away. But you, O Messenger of Allah, know that every person is recompensed for his deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil, and Allah has sent down upon you the true word: "And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another" (6:164). So every person has his book, in which his deeds are inscribed and recorded, and he is recompensed according to this.

1. Narrated by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id, and narrated by al-Tabarani; al-Haythami said: its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih.

And God says, after that:

﴿And thus have We tried some of them through others, so that they say, "Are these the ones whom God has favoured among us?" Does God not know best those who are grateful? (53)﴾

Here we are before two kinds ("ba'dayn"): one part that has risen above gathering with another part, the weak, who sit with a Messenger sent by God. God tests some through others by means of trial (fitnah), and fitnah is examination. Some people think that trial is blameworthy in itself. No, trial is not blamed for its own sake; it is blamed for what it leads to. So examination too is not blamed for its own sake, but for what it leads to. Trial comes so that the truth of faith's certainty may be seen. And here the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? (2) And We certainly tested those before them, and God will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars. (3)﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabut)

God, glory be to Him, tests the extent of a person's sincerity when he declares faith. He tests them with afflictions and blessings. God tested earlier nations with obligations, blessings and afflictions, and there comes into view and manifests in existence what He had known beforehand from eternity, and He distinguishes the people of sincerity in faith from the liars in faith. Whoever is patient under the test and trial has proven his truthfulness and certainty; whoever is not patient has shown by this act that he was worshipping God on an edge: if good befalls him he is content and satisfied, but if evil and trial befall him he turns on his face and draws back on his heels, and so he loses this world and the next.

So trial is merely an examination. The existence we see is built entirely on contrasts, and on these contrasts the movement of life arises. One must believe in God's decree in His creation: this one is tall, that one is short; this one is white, that one is black; this one sees, that one is blind; this one is rich, that one is poor; this one is healthy, that one is sick. This is so that each opposite becomes a trial for the other.

The sick person, for example, is a trial for the healthy, and the healthy is a trial for the sick. The sick person accepts God's decree within himself and does not look at the healthy with spite or resentment; but he may look to see whether the healthy man lords it over him and humiliates him, or offers him help. The poor man is a trial for the rich; he looks at the rich to know whether he will despise him, hurt him, or exploit him. The rich man is a trial for the poor; the rich man asks himself whether the poor man looks at him with the gaze of an envier, or with contentment at God's giving to others. Thus are trials.

Among humans there is one who is gifted with some talent, and there is one from whom God has taken this gift; both this giving and this taking are a trial. So that we believe that the Creator of existence scattered talents among creation and did not make one person a collection of all talents, so that every person needs the talents of others, cooperation arises among people, and social bonds come into being.

When God creates a person with some defect, He compensates him with some talent. Thus we see that the whole world is a trial, God making some of it a trial for others. Likewise the believing community was a trial for the disbelieving community, the disbelieving community was a trial for the Messenger of God, and the Messenger of God was a trial for them. When the Messenger of God sees the disbelievers daring against him, saying:

﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?" (31)﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf)

he knows that these people consider it too much for this great Qur'an to be sent down to him. In this saying there is a trial and examination for the Messenger of God; he endures that, proceeds to complete the delivery from God, and does not turn to what they say, but takes this as evidence of the strength of the miracle which shows the truth of his message.

The group that acted arrogantly and demanded the expulsion of the weak are a trial for the weak, and the weak are a trial for them. Had faith truly matured in the souls of the arrogant, they would not have been too proud to be preceded by the weak in believing in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

So each of us tests the others. Whenever a person sees someone gifted with a talent he does not have, let him know that it is a trial for him, and he must accept it and be pleased with it in others. Nothing worships God better than respecting the decree of God in one another, and therefore the Truth tests us all. If you are a believer in God, then respect God's decree in God's creation, so that God makes others respect God's decree in you.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And thus have We tried some of them through others, so that they say, "Are these the ones whom God has favoured among us?" Does God not know best those who are grateful? (53)﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

The aspect of the trial here is that a people demanded the expulsion of the weak and said, as God related of them: ﴿Are these the ones whom God has favoured among us?﴾ It is as though they questioned the social standing of the weak among the believers, and the reply comes from God: ﴿Does God not know best those who are grateful?﴾ He, glory be to Him, is the All-Knowing from eternity about mankind, and no one can propose to Him what He should decide. The disbelievers had already said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?﴾

The reply came from the Truth, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some may take others in service.﴾ (part of verse 32, Surah al-Zukhruf)

Thus we know that God, glory be to Him, did not place the keys of the message in the hands of the polytheists or others, that they should distribute affairs and manage the matter. Rather He, glory be to Him, is the One who distributes talents among humans as a provision from Him, so that each person depends on others for the talents he lacks, and others depend on his talent which they lack. Prophethood is a divine choosing which is greater and exalted above all worldly ranks. The context therefore indicates that some of the great Arabs demanded that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expel some of the weak, so God wanted to reassure the weak with something He hastened for them in this world, although He had reserved its like for the rest of the believers in the Hereafter. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And when those come to you who believe in Our signs, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: that whoever of you does evil in ignorance and then repents after it and makes amends, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful. (54)﴾

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 54:

To ask for the removal of these weak believers was an affront to their dignity and their standing, and to the fact that they were poorer than the wealthy and the notables of the people. So the Truth reassures them with peace from Him in this world, and He commands His Messenger: ﴿Say: Peace be upon you.﴾ From "peace" we understand freedom from psychological afflictions and from physical afflictions. It is as if Allah, glorified is He, wanted to compensate them with the peace that comes from Allah: ﴿Say: Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy.﴾ We see the word "mercy" (al-rahma) recurring often in the Noble Qur'an. Here the Truth says in another place:

﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 82)

What, then, is the difference between healing (al-shifa') and mercy (al-rahma)? Mercy: Allah does not afflict a human being with illness; it is prevention (al-wiqaya). Healing is that the Truth removes whatever illness has befallen a person. This is recovery after treatment.

So in the Qur'an there is healing and mercy, that is, prevention and treatment. Whoever adheres to the Qur'an's method is not struck by social and psychological diseases, and whoever neglects it and strays from it is afflicted by social and psychological disease. If he returns to the Qur'an's method, he is healed of any disease. When He, glorified is He, commands His Messenger to say to those who were provoked by the request to expel them, despite their faith in the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy,﴾ this means that what happened to them in this matter was their last trial, and by this provocation they received lasting peace. Since Allah has prescribed mercy for Himself, it is as if He has protected them from what He afflicts others with.

When you hear the words of Allah: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy,﴾ "prescribing" indicates recording. No one obligates Allah to anything, since He is the Creator of the universe and has absolute freedom of will in it. No one can prescribe anything upon Him to bind Him to it. Rather, He, glorified is He, is the One who made mercy obligatory upon Himself. We take the word "Himself" (nafsihi) within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him,﴾ because the "self" (al-nafs) for humans is the body, the blood, the movement and the life. But what happens when the word "self" is attributed to Allah? The meaning, then, is the Divine Essence. If you do not take the word in this sense, you fall into many errors, and may Allah protect us and you from their evils.

I affirm this meaning so that it settles in the mind of every believer: the "self" in relation to a living being is other than the "self" in relation to Allah. We must always take anything attributed to Allah within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him.﴾ For the self of a living being is a composite of spirit and matter, and matter is made of parts. If you do not take the meaning of the self of Allah in the light of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him,﴾ you are, God forbid, denying the Truth His oneness (al-ahadiyya).

We know that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has two attributes that share the same root and letters: the first is (wahid), "one," and the other is (ahad), "one" in a different sense. Superficial thinkers assume that (wahid) means (ahad). We say: no, (wahid) has one meaning and (ahad) has another. When we say, "Allah is wahid," it means there is no second individual of His kind, so He has no equal, no like and no peer. When we say, "Allah is ahad," it means that He is not composed of parts, some of which need the others to form the whole, because a thing may be one (wahid) without being indivisible (ahad). Therefore we stress the difference between (wahid) and (ahad), so that every sound believer may know it. He, glorified is He, is wahid: there is no second individual who shares His oneness, so He is one with no partner. He is ahad, may He be exalted: He has no parts that need one another. We have previously explained that there is something called (kull), "whole" or "totality," and something else called (kulli), "universal." The (kull) is that which is composed of parts, none of which by itself accomplishes the reality, and the whole is not achieved except by the parts being joined to one another.

An example of this is the chair. It is made of wood, nails and glue. The wood is not called a chair, the nails are not called a chair, and the glue is not called a chair. But the thing made of all these in a specific form is called a chair. So the (kull) has parts that come together to constitute it. The (kulli) can be applied to the human being, but within the human race there are many individuals of him.

Accordingly, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is neither (kull), that is, He has no parts because He is ahad, nor (kulli), because nothing is like Him. Glorified and exalted is He: He is wahid and ahad. Therefore we all understand that everything attributed to Allah must be within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him.﴾

We do not understand the meaning of the word "self" (nafs) in relation to Allah in the way we understand it in relation to human beings. Therefore the self of Allah is not like the self of human beings, because Allah is independent and needs nothing else, and He, glorified is He, is not composed of parts. He, glorified is He, possesses all perfection and majesty in His oneness, His ahadiyya, and in all His attributes and acts. When He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy,﴾ someone may ask: what is the meaning of mercy?

The answer comes in His saying, the Truth: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance and then repents after it and makes amends, then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ When the Truth sent down a law from heaven, that law includes texts of prohibition, such as the texts on the punishment of the adulterer or the thief, and others. No punishment can come except after a prohibition. For example, bribery, slander, and every violation of the law: there is no punishment without a crime, and no crime without a text. The Truth, who created creation, knows that some of His creatures are weak of soul, and a person may be overcome by his own self and commit a sin or disobedience. An example of this is His saying, the Truth:

﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, an exemplary punishment from Allah. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'ida, 38)

This is the punishment of the thief, male and female.

Likewise the Truth says about the adulterer and the adulteress:

﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, lash each one of them with a hundred lashes. Let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 2)

What is the meaning of the revelation of such texts? The meaning of revealing these texts is that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, knows that a person may weaken in some of the requirements of religion and fall into disobedience, and there must be a punishment for it. Respecting the Truth in that is the constitution of the human being, since He granted him choice and set reward and punishment. Just as the Truth placed the text on crimes and their punishments, He, glorified and exalted is He, has opened the door of repentance to His creatures, so that one who disobeyed Allah once is not left without hope, and so that society is not made miserable by these sinners. The Truth legislated repentance for creation to protect them from the evils of those who committed sins, and also to show mercy to the sinners as long as they have repented from them. Sometimes Allah shows mercy to some of His creatures by preserving them from sins.

He is the Truth who says:

﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ (From verse 118 of Surah al-Tawba)

So He, glorified is He, guides to repentance and pardons, and He is of great mercy toward His repentant servants.

Among the manifestations of Allah's mercy, glorified is He:

﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance and then repents after it and makes amends, then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (From verse 54 of Surah al-An'am)

Evil (al-su') is what Allah has forbidden. Is there anyone who does evil in ignorance? Some of us understand ignorance (al-jahala) superficially, as "lack of knowledge." No. The one who does not know is the illiterate, the empty-minded. Ignorance (al-jahala) is not the same as (al-jahl), ignorance in the sense of a deficiency of knowledge. Rather, (al-jahl) is that a person knows a ruling contrary to reality, such as believing in a doctrine that contradicts reality. Treating ignorance requires that we remove from him this doctrine which is contrary to reality, and then persuade him of the doctrine that corresponds to reality.

Those who cause trouble for people are the ignorant (al-jahala), because the ignorant person holds a belief in a matter and adheres to it while it contradicts reality. When the scholars came to this wise saying: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance,﴾ they said: "Ignorance here is foolishness (al-sufh) and recklessness (al-taysh), and recklessness is failing to consider the consequences of an action. Foolishness is failing to appreciate the value of the reward that one forfeits and the punishment that one incurs." A person may be a believer, yet commit evil because he did not keep in mind the reward and the punishment, and commits evil that achieves an immediate desire without reflecting on its future consequences. Had he kept the reward and the punishment in mind, he would not have done that evil.

We can also understand ignorance as committing a bad act without the person having planned or premeditated it. For example, a person plans a trip to Paris to acquire knowledge, and when he arrives there, a woman comes to his hotel room in full allure and adornment and insists that he commit indecency, and he cannot control himself. This is doing evil in ignorance, because he did not plan that evil, and he regrets it afterward and never boasts of that act.

There is a difference, then, between this person and another who researched the addresses of pleasure houses in Paris before traveling there. That person is planning the commission of wrong and the committing of indecency. He persists in evil, boasts of it, and does not repent of what he did. Such a type of person, Allah does not forgive if he continues in this state until he approaches death or death overtakes him. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿Allah accepts repentance only from those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon after. Those are the ones whose repentance Allah accepts, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 17)

Because the Truth, glorified is He, accepts the repentance of one who committed a sin in a state of folly and recklessness, and they hasten to repent immediately, the Truth accepts their repentance. As for those who do not regret the doing of evil, the Truth says about them:

﴿Repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers. For those, We have prepared a painful punishment.﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 18)

Those who do not hasten to repent immediately after committing a sin, and expect death to come before they repent, that is, while in the death rattle (al-gharghara), which is the soul rattling in the throat at death, these people will not have their repentance accepted. Likewise those who die in disbelief, may Allah protect us. For both, Allah has prepared a painful punishment.

The Truth, glorified is He, had already made this clear to us earlier, when He said:

﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance and then repents after it and makes amends, then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (From verse 54 of Surah al-An'am)

Therefore repentance must be followed by reform and righteousness, because good deeds erase bad deeds. The Truth, glorified is He, is Forgiving, and does not punish for a sin from which the servant has repented, and Merciful, because He rewards a good deed, and indeed He rewards a person who repeatedly regrets a bad deed and records for him a good deed for that. Indeed, in the vastness of His mercy, He changes his evil deeds into good deeds.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 55:

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿Thus do We detail the signs, that the way of the criminals may become clear.﴾

When you hear the words of the Truth, ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾, know that there is a detailing that follows this, resembling a detailing that came before. In the preceding verses Allah has detailed many matters: He has detailed for us the proof and the soundness of the Oneness of Allah, the glorified; He has detailed for us the validity of prophethood; and He has detailed for us the validity of al-qadar (divine decree and predestination). After all of this, the Truth gives us the criteria that establish the realities which the people of falsehood deny. So He details for us matters of belief, and He details for us the movement of life and the devotional movement by which we discharge the obligations of faith. Just as He, glorified, detailed for us the validity of the Oneness, the validity of prophethood, and the validity of al-qadar, He details for us the signs that establish the realities:

﴿Thus do We detail the signs, that the way of the criminals may become clear.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

In some readings (sabil) is read in the nominative (marfu'ah), meaning that the way of the criminals becomes manifest, clear and evident. In some readings it is read in the accusative (mansubah), meaning that you, O Muhammad, make clear the way that the criminals will tread.

The word (sabil) occurs in the Qur'an in the feminine, as in His saying, the Truth:

{Those who bar (others) from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked} (part of verse 45, Surah al-A'raf)

It also occurs in some verses in the masculine:

﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they do not take it as a way﴾ (part of verse 146, Surah al-A'raf)

The Truth intends by this to teach us that the Qur'an, which was revealed in clear Arabic tongue, was received by Arab tribes, some of which had supremacy, such as the tribe of Quraysh because it dwells in Mecca, and the Ka'bah is in Mecca, and all the tribes make pilgrimage to the Ka'bah.

He intends to abolish this supremacy, and for this reason the Qur'an came with some words that other tribes pronounce. An example of this is the word (sabil), which is feminine in the dialect of (al-Hijaz), and which came once as masculine, as the tribe of (Tamim) pronounces it. The Truth did not bring all the words of the Qur'an in conformity with the style of Quraysh, lest Quraysh think that the supremacy they had in the Jahiliyyah had carried over into Islam, for the Noble Qur'an came for everyone. ﴿Thus do We detail the signs, that the way of the criminals may become clear.﴾ That is, Allah will deal with every person according to what he holds of faith-based certainty.

Those who are obstinate have the treatment that suits them, and likewise the one who persists in sins and proceeds to disobedience; this differs from the treatment of the believer. Yet it is within the framework of divine justice. So for each person there is the treatment that befits his position in faith.

The counterpart of the criminals are the believers. So if you have made clear the way of the criminals, or if the way of the criminals has been made clear to you, do you not recognize the counterpart, which is the way of the believers?

When the Truth mentions one thing paired with another, He states the judgment on one thing and leaves the other judgment to the understanding of the hearer. If the Truth has made clear the way of the criminals as curse and expulsion, then the way of the believers differs from that: it is mercy and honor. An example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, is that you say to a pupil who attends to his lessons and studies in his free time from school: "Your way is success." Whoever hears this statement knows that for the one who does not attend to his lessons and does not study in his free time from school, the outcome of his affair is failure and disappointment.

Thus the Truth leaves to the acuity of the hearer of His speech to bring the counterpart and to know the judgments of this counterpart. So if the Truth has said ﴿that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾, this is also an indication of the way of the believers, which is mercy and honor. We know that the Qur'an came in the most eloquent styles, and these styles require that one know the import of every word and every letter, so that we understand the requirements of the situations and circumstances to which we match each context. An example of this is the Truth's saying, glorified be He:

﴿There has already been for you a sign in the two armies which met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving﴾ (part of verse 13, Surah Al 'Imran).

The Truth has left to the acuity of the hearer of this verse to know that the disbelieving army fights in the way of Shaytan, and that the army which fights in the way of Allah is the believing army. And the Truth has left to us that, at that great scene, they will recognize the measure of their lying in the world, for there is no sovereignty for anyone except Allah, and no one worthy of worship besides Him, so they will say what they testify to: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

One might say: but elsewhere in the Qur'an we find that Allah says the Truth concerning such people:

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers. This is a day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to offer excuses.﴾ (Surah al-Mursalat)

On the Day of the Great Terror they will know that they lied in the world, and they will not speak any word that benefits them, nor will the Truth permit them to offer excuses or apologies. We say to whoever thinks that the deniers do not speak: indeed they do not speak any utterance that would rescue them from the punishment awaiting them, and they fall into utter bewilderment and perplexity. Indeed, some of these deniers of Allah and the Last Day may have done something from which humanity benefited or by which people's lives developed, and so they think that this deed will save them. These may indeed receive their share and reward from the people for whom they worked, and the honor humanity gave them; but they will meet punishment on the Last Day because they associated others with Allah. The Truth was not in their minds for a moment when they produced what they produced of inventions. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing; and he finds Allah with him, so He will pay him in full his account. And Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ (Surah al-Nur)

Thus we know that the deeds of the disbelievers or polytheists Allah, the glorified, requites them for in this world by His justice, with wealth or fame, but these are deeds that avail them nothing in the Hereafter. Their deeds are like the glittering sheen produced by the sun's rays falling on a vast expanse of desert, which the thirsty man takes for water; and as soon as he approaches it, he finds that it is of no benefit to him. Likewise the deeds of the disbelievers or polytheists, they will find, are worth nothing on the Day of Resurrection. The polytheist among them will know the reality of his shirk on the Day of Resurrection, and will find none before him but the One, the Irresistible. Therefore each of them will say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ Indeed the polytheist among them denies his shirk, and this denial is a kind of lying.

[Note: The following passage, on the classification of beings, appears in the source text as a continuation of the same discussion.]

A particular thing is distinguished from the other genus either by the elevation of a degree or by the descent of a lower degree. The summit of the genera of existence is man, whom the Truth honored with sense, movement and thought. Next to man in rank is the genus of animal, which has sense and movement without thought. Next to the genus of animal is the rank of plant, which has growth without movement and thought.

When the faculty of growth is stripped from a plant, it becomes inanimate matter. Thus the arrangement of the genera from highest to lowest is as follows: man, then animal, then plant, then inanimate matter. Each of these genera has its own properties, and the higher genus takes an additional property.

The lowest genus is inanimate matter, which serves the plant, and the plant serves the animal and man; the animal serves man. Thus we find that the highest genus, which is man, has as its lowest genus inanimate matter. How then does the highest of the genera, man, take as a lord one of the lowest genera, which is inanimate matter?

Consulting human nature on this matter leads to a clear judgment: the folly of this kind of thinking. The natural disposition of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, before the mission, guided him to reject this; and the mission came to make the habit and natural disposition of the Messenger of Allah an object of worship of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and of everyone who follows him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 56:

﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah.﴾ (part of verse 56, Surah al-An'am)

So the matter of the idolaters' worship of idols does not stem from guidance (hudaa); rather, it is submission to desire (hawa). For guidance (hudaa) is the path that leads to the recognized goal, whereas desire (hawa) is the promptings of the soul that fulfil a appetite. And for this reason we see some of those who wish to lead mankind astray have come out with doctrines that have nothing to do with religion, such as the Qadianis, the Baha'is, the Babis, and other such sects. These people claim to be religious and yet, despite that, they make concessions in matters that touch upon morality. We have seen something like this in some of the cases that the courts have recently heard, such as the one who claims religiosity yet accepts every woman, and does not regulate relations between people by the rules of religion, but rather lets the instincts loose according to desire. Some people who have a great share and a level of education have gone along with this; they have deceived themselves with a great deception and thought that they have adopted religiosity, while in fact they are taking the share of desire that contradicts religion.

﴿Say: I will not follow your desires; I would then have strayed, and I would not be among the guided.﴾ (part of verse 56, Surah al-An'am)

That is, O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it is incumbent upon you to inform these idolaters that you do not follow their desires, which lead to error; for whoever follows such desires deviates from the truth and does not become one of the guided.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 57:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Say: "Indeed, I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it. I do not have that which you are impatient for. Judgment belongs only to Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders."﴾

Here the Truth informs His Messenger ﷺ that his abandonment of the worship of idols, although it was a matter to which he ﷺ had been guided by his sound natural disposition (fitrah), has now, after the mission (ba'tha), become a form of worship. This is because Allah's choosing him caused him to make clear His guidance through the clear law (shari'ah) concerning what is to be done (af'al) and what is not to be done (la taf'al). The Messenger ﷺ is therefore the excellent example (al-uswah al-hasanah) for people, performing every act according to what Allah has legislated, and the believers who follow his message follow him.

An example of this from our contemporary life: The Qur'an has revealed the prohibition of wine (khamr), and believers do not drink wine because the Truth has forbidden the commission of this act. And today we find physicians in every country of the world forbidding the drinking of wine, because it attacks all the body's systems: the liver, the brain, the nervous system, and the digestive system. We also find "films" (aflam) showing the effect of a glass of wine on human health. A non-believer may see such a "film" and refrain from wine out of a desire for benefit (imtina' ibtighaa' al-maslahah), not out of a desire for religious devotion (ibtighaa' al-tadayyun). But it is incumbent upon us, the Muslims, to embrace such abstention, because it is part of faith (min al-iman).

For this reason the Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous work, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ (33)

(Surah Fussilat)

Thus we know that none is better in speech than one who submits to the commands of the Truth, because he affirms the oneness of the Truth, glorified be He, performs every righteous deed, and acknowledges that this deed is an application of the law of Allah.

﴿Say: "Indeed, I am upon clear evidence from my Lord."﴾ The word "clear evidence" tells us that without clear evidence from Allah we do not know the method (manhaj), but with clear evidence from Allah we know that He is one God who has sent down a method of "do" and "do not." The Truth has used the word "my Lord" here so that we know He is the Creator who takes charge of our upbringing (tarbiyah) altogether. And since He, glorified and exalted be He, has created us and taken charge of our upbringing, we must comply with His method. Allah has sent down obligation (taklif) because He is the One worshipped, and at the same time He is the Lord who created and provided sustenance; therefore we comply with His method. As for the deniers, what of them?

﴿And you have denied it. I do not have that which you are impatient for. Judgment belongs only to Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders.﴾ (Part of verse 57, Surah al-An'am)

Those who denied Allah took rivals (andad) besides Him and did not comply with His method. Rather, some of them persisted in disbelief and said what the Truth has related of them:

﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ (32) (Surah al-Anfal)

When we examine what they said, we find that they said "O Allah" (Allahumma), and this is an acknowledgment from them of a God they turn to. Since they acknowledged a God, why do they turn away from complying with His method and worshipping Him? They do so because they are a model of arrogance and obstinacy, as expressed in their saying: ﴿If this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾

Would it not have been more fitting for them to use reason through reflection and say: "If this is indeed the truth from You, then guide us to it"?

We also find that they did not address the Messenger of Allah; they did not say, "O Allah, if this is the truth from Muhammad," but rather said: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You.﴾ They are rejecting the command of Allah and asking for the punishment, and that is the peak of obstinacy and persistence in disbelief, through their request to hasten the punishment. Therefore the Messenger of Allah says to them: ﴿You have denied it. I do not have that which you are impatient for.﴾

Istti'jal (impatience, seeking to hasten a matter) is the request to speed up a matter; it derives from 'ajalah (haste), which is rushing toward an end, that is, seeking an event before its time. Since they sought the punishment hastily, this punishment will certainly come to them, but at the appointed time that the Truth has determined, because every event in the existence of the universe has an appointed moment that Allah, glorified be He, has fixed:

﴿That which you are impatient for is not with me. Judgment belongs only to Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders.﴾ (Part of verse 57, Surah al-An'am)

Judgment belongs to Allah alone. If He wills to send down a punishment and hasten it in this world, as He sent it upon some peoples before, then none can repel it; and if He wills to delay the punishment to a term or to the Hereafter, none can question Him.

It is part of the wisdom of the Truth that the continued existence of those who oppose the method of faith serves as a confirmation of the method of faith. We must understand that the evil that occurs in the universe does not happen far from the will of Allah or against the will of Allah. Allah created man and gave him choice, and He, glorified be He, is the One who permitted man to act upon what he chooses, whether good or evil. Therefore nothing happens in the universe against His compulsion, because He is the One who brought choice into being. Had the Truth willed that no one be able to do evil, no one would have done evil. But you, O believer, if you look at the reality of certainty in its philosophy, you will find that the persistence of evil and the persistence of disbelief are among the causes of the confirmation of certain faith.

How? Because if we lived in a world in which there was no evil, there would be no victims, and if there were no victims, there would be no urging toward good and no incitement and impulse toward it. Therefore you find the spirit of faith growing stronger when Islam is attacked by any of its enemies, and you find Islam awakening in the souls of people. Had there been in the universe no harmful effects of evil, people would not have turned toward good. Likewise, disbelief is among the causes of certain faith. When the people of disbelief tyrannize the earth with corruption and despotism, people take refuge in certainty and fortify themselves with faith, because it protects a person from the many evils of other people. Therefore the existence of evil and disbelief is a service to certain faith.

﴿Indeed, judgment belongs only to Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders.﴾ (Part of verse 57, Surah al-An'am)

Yes, judgment belongs to Allah, because He, glorified be He, decides between situations without caprice, since He gains nothing from anything He does. The Truth brought this universe into being while being free of need for it; for Allah, glorified and exalted be He, possesses all attributes of perfection, and the creation of the universe added to Him no additional attribute, and He, glorified be He, created the universe only for the benefit of His creation. The Messenger conveys to us:

﴿Say: "If I had what you are impatient for, the matter would have been decided between me and you. And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers."﴾ (58)

This is a message from the Messenger of God to all creation: that the events of the universe are brought about by the Truth through His will, and at times that none knows except Him, glorified is He, and He—exalted is He—is the One who permits them.... That is, say to them, O Prophet: If it were within my power and capability to bring you the punishment you are hastening, the matter would be settled between me and you, and I would destroy them with a punishment and a swift torment, out of zeal for my Lord and anger at you for your denial of Him—glorified is He—and I would quickly rid myself of you. But the matter is not in my hands; it belongs to God, the Wise, who knows what the wrongdoers deserve. He—glorified is He—says in another place in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted community, they would surely say: "What is holding it back?" Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and what they used to mock will surround them.﴾ (Surah Hud, 8)

So the wisdom of God is what required the postponement of the punishment until a time that God determines. And in this is something that makes some of the disbelievers audacious toward God and deepens them in disbelief, so they say: "What is preventing the punishment from us?"

They say that in mockery and derision, and they do not know that the punishment is surely coming and there is no escape for them from it, because God is true to His promise and His threat, and the punishment will come upon them because they mocked and derided; there is no refuge for them from it and no escape for them from it.

In another place the Truth says:

﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment; had it not been for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them, and it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive. They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers. On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and it will be said: "Taste what you used to do."﴾ (Surah al-Ankabut, 53–55)

Thus we see the disbelievers' challenge to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to bring them the punishment, but it is a challenge answered by the fact that the Truth is the One who decrees the emergence of every matter; the punishment will surely come upon them suddenly, it is an inevitable reality, and Hell will indeed encompass them, and the punishment will overwhelm them from above them and from beneath them, and they will hear the voice of the angel appointed over their punishment: "Taste a punishment you denied, and it is the recompense of your deeds."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 59:

The Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that:

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear Book. (59)﴾

"Mafatih" (keys) is either the plural of "miftah" or the plural of "maftah." The "miftah" (key, the instrument of opening) is like "mibrad" (file, the instrument of filing). The instrument of opening is the key. "Maftah" is the thing upon which the opening falls, such as a treasury (khizanah). We know that some nouns come in the pattern "mif'al" or "mif'al." If we take "mafatih" as the plural of "miftah," the meaning is that the Truth, glorified and exalted, possesses the keys that open the unseen. If we take "mafatih" as the plural of "maftah," meaning a treasury, the meaning is that with the Truth are the treasuries of the unseen. Both meanings are valid. Treasuries contain only what is precious, and it is stored until its time, and every treasury has a key. The Truth says concerning Qarun:

﴿And We gave him treasures whose keys would surely burden a company of strong men﴾ (part of verse 76, surah al-Qasas).

Thus we know that nothing is stored away except that it is a treasure. With the Truth are the keys of the unseen, and the unseen is that which is hidden from you. It is of two kinds: a matter hidden from you but known to others; this is a relative unseen, not an absolute one.

An example of this: when a pickpocket steals your wallet while you are walking, you do not know where your money is, but the thief knows exactly where what he took from you is. Thus you see there is a difference between what is hidden from you but not hidden from others.

There is also what is hidden from you and from others, and this unseen has preliminaries; if a person takes up those preliminaries, he reaches knowledge of this unseen. This is what we see in scientific discoveries, whose secrets are unveiled when scientists take up the causes God placed in the universe, and this is a kind of relative unseen. There is a third kind of unseen, the absolute unseen, which none knows but God, such as the appointed time of the Last Day and other unseen matters that God keeps for Himself.

Therefore we say: there is never in this world any knower of the unseen except God. With Him, glorified is He, are the keys of the unseen, this unseen which we do not perceive through the senses as something witnessed, or which is unseen by its preliminaries, that is, it has no causes that anyone can take up.

The Truth says:

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear Book.﴾ (surah al-An'am)

The Truth, glorified and exalted, out of consideration for His creatures, when He brings them a matter not perceptible to them, clarifies it by means of the perceptible. The world of the witnessed is either heard, or seen, or tasted, or touched. And there is the world of the unseen. God may choose some of His creatures to cast upon them gifts from His overflowing bounty and generosity, which clarify certain matters. An example is the righteous servant with whom Moses, peace be upon him, travelled, and who said:

﴿And I did not do it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾ (part of verse 82, surah al-Kahf).

Such a gift comes to confirm for its recipient that he has a relationship with his Lord. The Truth, glorified is He, does not give these gifts so that they become a constant habit of a person, a part of his nature, such that we go to Him in every matter and He informs us of what we should do. The matter is not like that; rather they are merely pure gifts, which He grants, withdraws and withholds, glorified is He. He possesses the keys of all the unseen, and He brings us the perceptible world: ﴿and He knows what is on the land and in the sea﴾. The Truth mentioned the land first, before the sea, and the land is perceptible to all people with what it contains of inanimate things, plants, trees, animals, humans, lands and roads. There are lands that do not overlook any seas at all, and therefore the Truth mentioned the land first; then He mentioned the sea, which can be witnessed, but the world of the sea is more hidden than the world of the land. The worlds of the sea occupy an extremely large area of the earth's surface, and every day we discover something new in the world of the seas.

Then the Truth returns us to the land again, saying:

﴿Nor does a leaf fall but He knows it﴾ (part of verse 59, surah al-An'am)

To this degree the Truth clarifies His eternal knowledge: He knows everything related to a leaf of a tree after it has fulfilled its task of photosynthesis, nourishing the tree and ripening the fruit, and then falling to the ground. Falling, as we know, is the descent of a material thing downward, and scholars afterwards explained it by terrestrial gravity.

When a leaf falls from the tree it is light in weight, and the Truth, glorified and exalted, is the one who disposes of the atmospheres surrounding the course of its descent and of the wind that moves it. Why did the Truth bring up the matter of this leaf? The Truth brought this example so that we know that when the Truth, glorified is He, appended the previous verse with His words:

﴿And God knows best the wrongdoers﴾ (part of verse 59, surah al-An'am)

this appendix needed the Truth to explain it to us by knowing the times of the movements of every leaf of every tree, and this shows the completeness of encompassing knowledge. Moreover, matters that carry no reward or punishment are known to Him; how then could matters that carry reward and punishment not be known to Him? He, glorified and exalted, must know them and decide concerning them.

﴿Nor does a leaf fall but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth﴾ (part of verse 59, surah al-An'am)

He, glorified is He, also knows the grain that is hidden in the inner part of the earth and its conditions.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear Book﴾ (part of verse 59, surah al-An'am)

That is, He, whose power is exalted, knows the affair of every existent in this world, because every existent in this world is either fresh or dry, and He not only knows this but all of it is known to Him and written down. The angels who are "those who arrange the affair" oversee the movement of these existents, and when the angels find that the movement of the universe proceeds with a firm, precise order in accordance with what is in the Book, they do not cease glorifying God night or day:

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and those who are with Him do not disdain His worship, nor do they weary. They glorify Him night and day; they do not slacken﴾ (surah al-Anbiya', verses 19-20)

To the Truth belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and His right alone is to be worshipped. The angels do not grow arrogant against His worship and submission to Him, and they do not feel weariness from worship and from glorifying Him, glorified is He. You, O servant, are in some matters subjugated, and in some matters you have choice, and He, glorified is He, knows what you will choose.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 60:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿It is He who takes your souls by night, and knows what you have committed by day. Then He raises you up therein, that a term appointed may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ (6:60)

We all know that sleep is not a voluntary process. Sometimes we see someone upon whom God lets worries prevail, so that sleep finds no path to his eyelids. We know that sleep is a compelled process which God creates in the human being to restrain him from movement after he has exhausted all his capacity to move. Sleep is a kind of self-restraint.

Why did the Truth make sleep like death?

Some know that death, in its meaning, is the separation of the soul (rūḥ) from the body. It is as if the Truth were saying to us: Beware lest you think that the presence of the soul in the body is what gives the human being life, movement and action. No! I will keep the soul in the body but will not empower it to act voluntarily. This is so that you will not be tempted by the soul; for there are systems over which your choice has no say, such as the beating of the heart and breathing, and other movements of the body's systems. The Truth has given us the example of the People of the Cave, whom He put to sleep for three hundred years and nine more:

﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and gained nine more.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 18:25)

Sleep, then, is a blessing from God which He placed in the self's constitution. For this reason, if you want to sleep, that is not within your power, but within the power of the Truth. It is said of sleep: "It is a guest: if you seek it, it wearies you" — that is, it tires you — "and if it seeks you, it refreshes you." Sleep comes to the weary even if he sleeps on pebbles, and it may not come to one who prepares for it even if he is on a bed of silk.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who hear.﴾ (Surah al-Rum, 30:23)

Sleep, then, is a complete sign in itself. Sleep does not come only at night, but comes by day too, because there are tasks demanded by the movement of existence which some people carry out during the night; therefore they sleep by day.

He, glory be to Him, takes us in death by night and knows what we have committed by day; then He sends us to a term which He alone knows; then He raises us on the Day of Resurrection to inform us of all our deeds. The Truth called sleep "death" and called waking "resurrection," because in such states a person does not possess his voluntary movement. For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when he stood to declare his mission after three years of secret preaching, said:

﴿Indeed I am a plain warner to you before a severe punishment.﴾ "Indeed you will die as you sleep, and you will be resurrected as you awaken, and you will be recompensed with good for good and with evil for evil, and it is indeed either Paradise forever or Fire forever."

On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), who said: One day the Prophet (ﷺ) ascended al-Ṣafā and cried: "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" The Quraysh gathered to him and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "Tell me, if I informed you that the enemy would attack you in the morning or in the evening, would you not believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: ﴿Indeed I am a plain warner to you before a severe punishment.﴾ Abū Lahab said: "Perish you! Is it for this that you gathered us?" Then God, glory be to Him, revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abū Lahab.﴾(1)

The Truth, glory be to Him, either paralyses the limbs, disabling them and preventing them from movement, or takes the soul from the body. When He paralyses the limbs and prevents them, a person sleeps; when He takes the soul and holds it back, death occurs. Therefore we must understand that sleep has a law, wakefulness has a law, death has a law, and each law has its rules. The law of wakefulness is not like the law of sleep, nor is the law of sleep like the law of death, nor the law of resurrection like the law of death. There is wakefulness, sleep, death and resurrection, and it is an error to take the law of one state and apply it to another.

The Truth gives us a clear example within ourselves: a person has a state of wakefulness in which the soul controls his voluntary movement; when he sleeps, the soul is unable to move voluntarily and only involuntary movements remain. When a person sleeps, he may see some visions and dreams: he meets someone and sees him wearing a particular garment in particular colours. With what did he perceive the colours while his eyes were closed? Thus there are means of perception other than the eye. Likewise time takes its share during wakefulness, but during sleep a person may see a dream in seven seconds and recount it in half an hour. Two people may sleep on one bed, one dreaming that he met his beloved and friends, ate, drank, rejoiced and was content, while the other dreams that he met his enemies and fought with them and struggled against them; thus time differs, and so does companionship. Thus the law of sleep differs from the law of wakefulness. Likewise the law of death differs from the law of life:

﴿It is He who takes your souls by night, and knows what you have committed by day. Then He raises you up therein, that a term appointed may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ (Surah al-Anʿām, 6:60)

And the limb, as we have said, is what acts so that the human being may earn. Thus the Truth has brought us all the states of wakefulness, sleep, death and resurrection. But each state has its law; we know the law of wakefulness and the law of sleep because we experience them. So when we are told that there is a law of death, we measure that by the progression of laws from wakefulness to sleep; and when we are told that there is a resurrection, we also believe.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhārī, al-Tirmidhī in the Tafsīr chapter, al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil, Aḥmad and al-Ṭabarī.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 61:

Then the Truth says:

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail (in their duty).﴾ (61)

Al-Qahir (the Subduer) is the One who disposes (of all things) with a supreme, encompassing and all-comprehensive power. Someone may say: since the Truth is al-Qahir, how does the disbeliever disbelieve, and how does the sinner disobey? We say: the disbeliever disbelieves by means of the choice that God has created in him, and likewise the sinner's disobedience. But the Truth has also placed in man compulsory and overpowering matters which show us that He, glory be to Him, does whatever He wills. None of those who rebel against the (divine) method dares to extend this rebellion to what God brings upon him of sickness or death.

The rebel or the disbeliever is only (acting) from within the choice that God created in him, while God is the One who decides birth and death, and man has no share in either. Likewise, He, glory be to Him, directs the affairs of wealth and poverty, and no rebel dares to rebel against the calamities that befall him, even if he rebels against the method of God; for rebellion arises from within the choice which God created and deposited in man.

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail (in their duty).﴾ (61) (Surah al-An'am)

When the Truth, glory be to Him, speaks of His essence and self, He may speak in the first person singular, saying:

﴿Indeed, I am God﴾ (part of verse 14, Surah Ta-Ha)

And He may say, glory be to Him:

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We are its guardian.﴾ (9) (Surah al-Hijr)

And at times He speaks of His essence with what we call the third person pronoun, as in His saying here:

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-An'am).

This is because the first person pronoun has its indication: the speaker says "I", and addresses you saying "you". But the one who speaks with the third person pronoun must have a referent to which the pronoun returns. When the Truth speaks of His essence with what is called in our terminology the third person pronoun, He, glory be to Him, wishes to show us that He is in the clearest sphere of witnessing and presence; as if, when He says "He" (huwa), it refers to none other than His exalted essence; as if there were no referent for the pronoun but Him. Therefore He says:

﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾ (1) (Surah al-Ikhlas).

He, glory be to Him, says "He" before mentioning the referent, which is "God"; though the original rule is that the referent should come first. Yet He says:

﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾ (1) (Surah al-Ikhlas).

So when this pronoun is used without qualification, it refers to none other than His essence. When He speaks with the first person pronoun, we see Him speaking of His essence with the singular form, saying:

﴿Indeed, I am God﴾ (part of verse 14, Surah Ta-Ha)

And He says in another place:

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We are its guardian﴾ (9) (Surah al-Hijr).

Why? When He speaks of one of His acts, each of His acts requires all the attributes of perfection in it, because it requires knowledge of what is spoken of, requires power to bring it forth, requires wisdom, and requires many attributes. So when He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We are its guardian﴾ (9) (Surah al-Hijr)

the sending down is an act, and an act requires multiple attributes. Therefore He must use the pronoun of magnification, which is the plural, because all the attributes of perfection are manifest in the sending down. But when He speaks of the essence in matters of divine unity (tawhid), He never uses the plural pronoun, because He wishes to negate from His essence any plurality, since He is the One who has no partner. So when He speaks of the essence He says: "Indeed, I am God. . . (14)" (Surah Ta-Ha).

And when He speaks of the Reminder He says:

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder. . . (9)﴾ (Surah al-Hijr)

In the sphere of magnification and sending down, which requires the manifestation of many of His attributes, glory be to Him, He uses the plural pronoun; and in unity, singularity and negation of partners He uses the singular pronoun.

Here He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants. . . (61)﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

The word "subduer" (qahir), when you hear it, requires one who is subdued. Since there is a subduer and a subdued, there are two sides to a balance between two spheres. And since He is the Subduer, in what sphere and in what manner would the second party be subdued to Him? We know that everything in the universe is subdued to Him: He subdued non-existence and brought things into being, and subdued existence and caused it to cease. He subdued wealth and made people poor, and subdued poverty and made them rich. He subdued health and made them sick, and subdued sickness and made them well.

Thus everything in existence is subdued to God, even the soul, which He made the source of sensation and movement for man; He, glory be to Him, subdues it. If a person comes and kills another by striking him in a place where, upon its loss, life is lost, depriving it of its capacity to remain, the soul withdraws. This shows us that the soul is dominant in the body; yet whoever destroys the structure that the soul inhabits makes the soul depart and leave the body. And at times He subdues matter by the soul, taking the soul without any affliction or any injury, and the body turns to dust. So He, glory be to Him, subdues the soul and subdues matter, and there is no opposite in existence, exalted, obstinate and rebellious against Him, glory be to Him:

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-An'am)

Al-Qahir is the One who disposes with comprehensive power over the subdued. Look at any opposite in life and you will find it indebted to and submissive to the attribute of subjugation. ﴿He is the Subduer over His servants﴾. The word "over" (fawq) implies spatiality. But spatiality is a limitation; and since subjugation requires power, does that mean that the powerful must be in a higher place? For we find, by way of example, and to God belongs the highest likeness, one who places a bomb beneath a high building and subdues those within it. Therefore subjugation does not entail spatial superiority. Thus the superiority intended is superiority of dominance (istila'), and when we have spoken of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, we have made clear that we must keep within the frame of "There is nothing like unto Him" (42:11). He is an essence unlike all essences; His attributes are not like all attributes; and likewise we say concerning His act. For example, we find that God's creatures need time and need treatment, and every part of an act requires a part of time; but as for Him, when He acts, does His act require time? No, because He does not act by treatment, nor does He sit to undertake the process; rather He acts, glory be to Him, by "Be" (kun). Thus the subjugation in His saying ﴿He is the Subduer over His servants﴾ is the subjugation of dominance.

Therefore the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, tells us: "Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven every night in the last third of the night."

On which night does God descend? Your night or the night of the one opposite you? Or the night in which the sun rises in one place and sets in another? Thus, every one millionth of a second a night begins and a day begins, and so we know that God is with you and with others, extending His hand to you and to others.

﴿Rather, His hands are outstretched﴾ (part of verse 64, Surah al-Ma'idah)

Therefore we do not understand the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: "God extends His hand by night so that the sinner of the day may repent, and extends His hand by day so that the sinner of the night may repent, until the sun rises from the west" (1). Do not understand this as restricted to a particular night or a particular day; for His hand is outstretched at every time and in every place, and there is nothing like unto Him.

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants﴾. "His servants" (ibadihi) derives from the root ʿayn-bāʾ-dāl; its singular is "ʿabd" (servant), and its plural may be "ʿabīd" or "ʿibād". "Servants" (ʿibād) are those who are subdued to God in what they have no choice in, and they are also those who submit to the judgment of God in what they have choice in; for man is subdued in some matters and has no disposal over them: he has no disposal over his own self, no disposal over the beats of his heart, no disposal over the movement of his stomach, no disposal over the movement of his intestines, no disposal over the movement of the ureters, no disposal over the movement of the kidney; all of these are matters which include the believer and the disbeliever, and all are subdued in them.

It is among God's mercy that we are subdued in these and have no opinion; for if we had an opinion in such matters, we would have to ask: how do we organise our breathing during sleep? Thus it is by God's mercy that He withheld from us choice in some matters that touch our lives. And it is by God's mercy that each of us is subdued in them: who can tell his stomach, "Digest the food"? Who can order the kidney to work?!!

Thus in every matter in which man is subdued, he is submissive to God and has no choice. As for the matter in which you have choice, it is the locus of obligation (taklif). Therefore the method does not say to you "Do" unless you are capable of not doing, and it does not say to you "Do not" unless you are capable of doing.

Thus the matters of choice are those in which "Do" and "Do not" have been revealed; these are the matters in which there is obligation. Whoever obeys our Lord in the method of obligation becomes, as it were, subdued to the rule, and is among those whom God calls "servants" (ʿibād); as if they had relinquished their choice in the legal rulings and said: "O Lord, we will not do except what Your method desires." Each of them carries out God's ruling in what he has the choice not to carry out. As for the slaves (ʿabīd), they are those who rebel against obligation. So the believers in God are His servants. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God; indeed God forgives all sins. . . (53)﴾ (Surah al-Zumar)

And He, glory be to Him, describes the traits of these servants, saying:

﴿The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace." (63)﴾ (Surah al-Furqan)

These are the servants who have relinquished their choice in action and accepted to be commanded and obedient to God in what He has obligated them with; and in matters where they have no choice, they are like the rest of creation. All creation and the universe are slaves of God in what they have no choice; but the believers in Him are the servants of God. Yet there is one verse in the Qur'an which stirs some dispute on this subject, when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, speaks of what happens in the Hereafter:

﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray. . . (17)﴾ (Surah al-Furqan)

As if "My servants" here were applied to the misguided; and He says: yes, because in the Hereafter all are servants, since no one there has any choice. But in this world only the believers are servants, while the disbelievers are slaves, because they are rebellious in their choices.

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-An'am)

Along with the meaning of subjugation, the Truth sends guardians; if subjugation means domination, possession, control and power, then He is the Subduer over His servants and also sends guardians.

He says in another place:

﴿For him are successive angels before and behind him, guarding him﴾ (part of verse 11, Surah al-Ra'd)

Thus is God's subjugation of us, for our own benefit; for when a weak person is subdued by a tyrant, he can say: God is the Supreme Subduer; and in this there is a reminder to the relatively strong that there is a subduer above all creatures, so God is Subduer above all. Thereby the strong is restrained from subjugating others, so he refrains from sin, and punishment refrains from him, and in that is mercy for him.

﴿and He sends over you guardians﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-An'am)

The meaning of "guardians" (hafaza) comes in the Qur'an in His saying:

﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him an observer ready (to record). (18)﴾ (Surah Qaf)

Thus every utterance has a ready observer; "guardians", that is, angels who guard and count your deeds, record them, and they are the Noble Scribes. And as knowledge advances it gives us understanding of the unseen meanings; yet although the unseen meanings we receive from God have as their proof hearing, here there is an observer and a ready one who record only; so our Lord has said, and we have believed in what He said, and the matter is settled; and this is what is required.

Therefore the Truth said:

﴿Who believe in the unseen﴾ (part of verse 3, Surah al-Baqarah)

For if faith were in what is witnessed, what difference would there be between people? The perfection and summit of faith is faith in the unseen. So when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him an observer ready (to record). (18)﴾ (Surah Qaf)

this is news about the angels who record good deeds and record evil deeds. And when we look at human beings, we find them differing, and some rising above others in qualities and capacities.

1 Narrated by Ahmad and Muslim from Abu Musa in the chapter on repentance, and narrated by al-Nasa'i in the Tafsir.

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿Then they will be returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.﴾ (6:62)

The word (radau) (they were returned) indicates that they had a prior encounter with Him, and after that they will return. How? They were brought into existence by Him, and then they are returned to Him for reckoning, reward and punishment. This is because the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who says:

﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you...﴾ (20:55) (Surah Ta-Ha).
