﴿Then they will be returned to Allah, their true Master.﴾ The word (mawla) (master) means the one who is closest to you, and only one who is close to you can be your (mawla). This close one may be a helper for you if something happens that frightens you; he is the one who gives aid. Thus the word (mawla) has taken on the meaning of the one close, the supporter and helper to whom you turn in your hardships. In this world you may have a (mawla), but he is one of the changeable things (aghyar). He may change and turn his heart against you; events may befall you that are beyond his power and capacity; you may have a (mawla) whom you seek and ask to support you, and he refuses, because your opponent has with this (mawla) a stronger and more intense loyalty, so he stands by your opponent and may give you the illusion that he is with you, but he is not with you.

But there is in the Hereafter one true (mawla): ﴿and they are returned to Allah, their true Master.﴾ The word (mawla) is also applied to a master who frees his slave. And when our Lord frees us from the Fire, is that not the greatest guardianship? He is the true (mawla); there is no higher power than Him, and He does not change, because changeability is the nature of creatures.

When the Truth asks you to use your reason, because when you rely on someone who benefits you in your affairs, you place your trust in him and seek his help, here He commands you to place your trust in the Living One who does not die, and not to rely on any of the changeable things, for morning may come and you find that he has left you alone and abandoned you. But if your (mawla) is the Truth, He will not fail you.

﴿Then they will be returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him.﴾ And why does He use the word (judgment) here? Because in the world of changeable things, He may assign some judgments to some of His creatures: this one judges, that one manages, another issues decisions about appointments, and all of these are judgments. But in the Hereafter the Truth says:

﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16) (part of verse 16, Surah Ghafir).

In this world you possess something: your son's provision may, for example, be in your hand; you may have the power to issue a decision promoting someone lower than you; you may have the power to pass on reward to another if that is your profession. In the world each of us possesses some of the causes of another. But in the Hereafter none of this exists:

﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

When you hear ﴿Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him﴾, then (alā) (unquestionably) in the language is a particle of alerting to what follows it. And why does the particle of alerting come here? Because the judgment that comes after it is an important judgment. Speech, as we know, is a link between a speaker and a listener, for the speaker conveys his ideas, thoughts and wishes to the hearer. Before he speaks, he turns the matter over in his mind: should he speak or not? But the listener is surprised by the speaker's words, whereas the speaker, before he conveys his thoughts, has a mental image in his imagination; that is, he lives through the project of speech and reflects on it before he speaks. The listener, however, is taken by surprise. When you want to say something important, you try to secure the listener's attention so that he misses no part of your speech, so you say (alā) to draw the listener's attention completely. The Truth here says (alā) to capture the listener's attention, and after it comes His saying: (to Him belongs judgment).

So, when you hear (alā), know that in it is an alert to a matter of great weight: ﴿Unquestionably, to Him belongs judgment.﴾

And (judgment) (hukm) is the separation between two matters, and the separation between two matters differs according to the judge. If the judge has a desire, the judgment inclines; but the separation between two matters must be without desire. Judgment by the balance requires that there be a pan here and a pan opposite it, and when we adjust the scale we try to balance the two pans in order to separate two intertwined matters. And since we want equality, we call that (insaf) (fairness), that is, standing at the midpoint without inclination or injustice.

﴿Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.﴾ When a person hears ﴿Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him﴾, each of us knows that He, glory be to Him, judges among creation from Adam until the world ends, and each one of us has affairs intertwined with others. Since judgment belongs to God, no other has judgment alongside Him. He judges among all creation, and His action requires no time. Here we recall Imam Ali, may Allah honour his face, when people said to him: How will our Lord reckon all people at one time, and in the time it takes to milk a sheep, as some of them said? Imam Ali said: (Just as He provides for them at one time, He reckons them at one time). This is an easy matter with no difficulty at all. In former times, when they lit the roads, they would light the lamps: here a lamp, there a lamp, and a third lamp at a distance, and the lamplighter would walk to light the lamps... etc. Then the human mind, which was created by God, advanced and was able to light the roads with electrical or solar energy at one time.

Thus the Almighty says next:

﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of land and sea, when you call upon Him humbly and in secret, [saying], 'If He rescues us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.'"﴾ (6:63)

It is exhausting for creation that darkness should come to fulfil the role of light, and that light should come to fulfil the role of darkness. Each of darkness and light has a function and a mission in life. For this reason, at the beginning of the surah, when the Almighty spoke saying:

﴿Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light...... (6:1)﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

Some have thought that it should have been said: "and made the light and the darknesses." But let us reflect upon the true word, and acknowledge that the mission of darkness is equal to the mission of light. Man must recognise the mission of darkness. We all know the mission of light, which helps us strive with the affairs of our lives, and striving requires energy. Energy cannot come except after stillness, calm, tranquillity and rest. Therefore rest needs darkness so that a person may sleep and be refreshed. Thus darkness is one of God's blessings. What exhausts a person is that he changes and substitutes, making light in place of darkness and darkness in place of light, and this is a departure from the function of each of two opposites. When the Truth creates opposites, He does not create them as contradictions or as mutual opposition, but He – glory be to Him – wills complementary things that help one another. Nothing destroys its opposite; rather, each complements and assists the other. For this reason the Almighty said:

﴿By the night when it covers, (1) and the day when it displays itself, (2)﴾ (Surat al-Layl)

He – glory be to Him – mentioned the night first and the day second, and each has its mission. The mission of the day cannot be fulfilled in its reality except when the mission of the night is fulfilled in its reality. Bring me a person who has not taken from the night rest, stillness and tranquillity, and who has suffered from the sting and bite of mosquitoes or fleas, or from noise and the like, and did not sleep; then in the morning you find him half asleep, half adolescent, unable to concentrate, or, as they say, "dazed."

Thus, for the sake of the movement of light, darkness must exist.

﴿By the night when it covers, (1) and the day when it displays itself, (2)﴾ (Surat al-Layl).

Night and day, then, are two blessings, and each blessing equals the other. Beware of saying that this is against that, or that they came to oppose each other. No! Each of them came to support the other.

In Surat al-Layl the Truth continues:

﴿And [by] He who created the male and the female. (3)﴾ (Surat al-Layl).

He – glory be to Him – has also brought opposites. Beware of supposing that they are mutually opposed, for God made them complementary so that life may succeed. If they oppose each other, life is corrupted. And since the night has a mission and the day has a mission, so the male has a mission and the female has a mission. If one mixes the two missions, corruption results.

﴿By the night when it covers, (1) and the day when it displays itself, (2), and He who created the male and the female, (3) indeed your effort is diverse. (4)﴾ (Surat al-Layl)

Here the Truth says:

﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of land and sea, when you call upon Him humbly and in secret, [saying], 'If He rescues us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.'"﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

Darkness, then, is the absence of light. The Truth did not say that the seeking of deliverance is from a single darkness, but from darknesses in the plural, which are accumulated darknesses; for when darkness is overlaid by a second darkness, then a third, then they become compound darknesses, one upon another.

The Almighty said: "the darknesses of land and sea." And so that we may know whether these are sensory darknesses or spiritual darknesses, we must know darkness in its sensory meaning: it is that which leads to failure to find the saving way. Thus every matter that leads to failure to find guidance – sensory or spiritual – is a darkness, because a person in such a state proceeds in his affairs without guidance. Events and calamities in which people find it difficult to know the way of escape are considered darkness, whether they are sensory or spiritual darkness.

The Almighty brings spiritual matters close to us through sensory things. The meaning of "darknesses" here is the events, calamities and disasters whose causes are too narrow for human beings to be saved from them. Man is always eager to benefit himself, and contradictions appear in the actions of one person compared with those of another, because each differs in evaluating and estimating what is beneficial. A clear example, which we always cite, is that of the pupil who goes early in the morning to his school, pays attention to his teachers, returns home to do his homework, and leaves the pleasant laziness to find pleasure in work. By doing so he loves himself and wants benefit for it. As for the pupil who sleeps and whose family wakes him, yet he does not wake up; when they wake him he leaves the house to loiter in the street – such a pupil loves himself with a foolish love, because he wants immediate pleasure which is followed by a chain of delayed pains. He awaits a future in which he has no dignity, unlike the diligent pupil who attains the rightful place befitting him.

A similarly clear example in the countryside is the farmer who spends his time in the café, stays up at night before the television, and leaves the land unploughed, unirrigated and unfertilised. The land he cultivates cannot yield a crop equal to the land of the farmer who takes the means ordained by God, ploughs the land, regularly irrigates it at the appointed times, and applies the fertiliser prescribed for it; for the one who takes the means of God and toils and exerts effort, the Truth must give him abundant provision. As for the one who is lazy in performing his work, he has loved himself with a foolish, short-term love; and the one who takes the means of God and devotes himself to his work with love and appreciation has loved himself with a deeper love, one that contains benefit for himself and for others.

Every movement that a person makes in life is intended to benefit himself, but there is difference in estimating what is beneficial between one person and another. The wise person is the one who sees the lasting, worthwhile benefit and works for it. Here is al-Mutanabbi, the Arab poet, saying:

I see that all people seek life for themselves,
eager for it, infatuated with it, ardently attached.
So the coward's love of self brings him to fear,
and the brave man's love of self brings him to war.

The brave man's love of himself, then, made him aspire to eternal life as a martyr in the way of God, while the coward's love of himself made him a captive of fear for transient life. When a person is struck by events, calamities and disasters, we see his self-interest moving him to seek means of deliverance, and he relies on his own means or the means of someone close to him. But if the means of human beings are scarce, and he was heedless of God, then events, misfortunes and calamities return him to remembrance of his Creator, so he says: "O Lord," and thereby he does not sell his soul cheaply. But if such a person deceived himself from the beginning, turned away from God, rebelled against his Lord, and then found himself before calamities, he surrenders his affair to God in time of hardship; but if it passes and the harm is lifted from him, he returns to disbelief and rebellion. For this reason the Almighty says:

﴿When harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him; but when He brings you safely to land, you turn away. Man is ever ungrateful. (67)﴾ (Surat al-Isra')

We find that those who face their desires and whose means come to an end do not lie to themselves; rather, they turn instinctively to the Truth, the One able to take them by the hand. At the moment a ship is shaken and waves and winds surround it, and its machinery fails, you find nothing but the word "O Lord, O Lord, O Lord" on the tongues of all its passengers, from the captain and commander down to the least passenger on board, and you find someone murmuring verses of the Qur'an seeking deliverance from God. Likewise, at the moment an aircraft is shaken in the air and its pilot knows no way of escape, nothing comes to the minds of the passengers and crew except the cry of humble supplication to God.

Therefore the Almighty tells us: ﴿Those whom you invoke vanish except Him﴾. The human being's calling upon his Lord and Master is the first of the means of certainty. We know that the events of life fluctuate between two matters: one that expands and makes a person happy, and one that constricts and oppresses a person and makes him wretched. What expands and makes happy is the perception of beauty, blessing, rest, happiness and the feeling of contentment. What constricts a person and makes him wretched is something from which he wishes to be freed and to be saved.

We have the complete lesson in the natural disposition (fitrah) with which God created man. By his nature, when a person sees what makes him happy, he finds no stronger expression than saying: "God" – the cry of appreciation and sanctification of God, who gave him the gift of perfecting work. The complete lesson is also manifest when danger overwhelms a person and he says by his nature: "O Lord." Thus there is no refuge except in God.

﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of land and sea?"﴾ The question contains a truth which the one hearing this question must affirm, namely: God is the Deliverer from the darknesses of land and sea. When the Truth commands His Messenger to put this question to the disbelievers, He – glory be to Him – knows that the answer of the natural disposition is what will prevail upon the tongues of the disbelievers, and they will acknowledge Him alone as the One who delivers from the darknesses of land and sea. The universe – as we know – is either land or sea. Someone may say: "But there are new calamities in our age, the calamities of the atmosphere?"

We say: you must understand that every atmosphere takes the ruling of its place. The atmosphere of land is from the land, and the atmosphere of sea is from the sea. An example of this is what we see when praying in the Sacred Mosque: we see worshippers performing prayer around the Ka'bah, or on the ground floor, the first floor, or the second or third floor of the buildings erected as a mosque around the Ka'bah. We notice that the height of the Ka'bah does not exceed the height of one storey of the buildings around it. The worshippers direct their prayers on those floors towards the atmosphere of the Ka'bah, because the atmosphere of a sacred place is also sacred, and the atmosphere of the Haram is from the Haram.

Another example is the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah: the Muslim performs the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah on the ground floor, and there is now a second floor built for the sa'y. Thus we see that the atmosphere of the place of sa'y is also a place of sa'y. In the past it was forbidden for aircraft to fly over the atmosphere of Makkah or Madinah. This happened in the days when the pilots were non-Muslims, so that a non-Muslim would not fly in the sacred atmosphere. Now, however, Muslim pilots have been permitted to fly their aircraft over the airspace of Makkah and the illuminated city of Madinah.

Thus the atmosphere has the ruling of the place, whether the place is land or sea.

﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of land and sea? You call upon Him humbly and in secret"﴾ Indeed, supplication by natural disposition is directed to God, and supplication is a request for something. A request necessitates a requester, a requested, and one from whom it is requested. The requester is the one who supplicates. The one from whom it is requested is the One we call upon and ask. The requested is the thing for which we humbly supplicate, hoping it will occur. A request is a kind of command, but when the request comes from the lower to the higher, do not call it a command; rather, it is supplication (du'a').

In grammar, when we ask the student to parse "rabbi-ghfir li" (My Lord, forgive me), you find the one who memorised his lessons without understanding saying: "ighfir is an imperative verb," whereas the student who comprehends his religion and excels in his studies says, with the courtesy of faith: "ighfir is a verb of supplication (fi'l du'a'), because a request which comes from the lower to the higher is supplication; if it comes from equal to equal it is an appeal (iltimas); and if it comes from the higher to the lower it is a command."

When we look at the psychological state of one whom calamities, events and disasters surround, and whom circumstances press, with no one to rescue him, does such a person command or supplicate? He supplicates, by natural necessity, and supplicates with humility, submission and abjection; and this is the meaning of du'a'... it is a request with humble supplication and submission. Humble supplication requires speech, and it requires action, and supplication takes the form of inner feelings and outward conduct.

Whoever supposes that there is supplication by speech alone, without linking it to action, is mistaken. When you are in a position of strength or influence and someone asks you to bestow something upon him, this is supplication by speech. But when you are in a position of strength or influence and someone asks you to do something for him, this is supplication by speech and action. In the moment of danger a person calls upon his Lord, and it is not possible that there should be in his heart...

Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿Say, "It is Allah who delivers you from it and from every distress; yet still you associate others with Him."﴾

Indeed, the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, delivers them from the material darknesses on land and sea. And He, glory be to Him, knows by His eternal knowledge that after deliverance they will return to what He forbade them: associating partners with Him. This is because a human being, by his nature, when he finds his life sufficient with what he possesses, may fall into what the Truth, blessed and exalted, has said:

﴿No! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient.﴾ (Surah al-'Alaq)

Man may go beyond his limits and act arrogantly toward those around him, and even toward his Lord, if he sees himself as a possessor of wealth. Nothing protects a person from such a stance except faith in Allah, because a person without the method of Allah swims in the sea of delusion and arrogance. But whoever lives in the light of Allah's method knows how to take care of Allah's blessing in every capacity or wealth that Allah grants him, and spreads his assistance so that the needy who lacks means may find shade in it. Therefore we find that the word "man" (al-insan), when used without qualification, is associated with loss.

﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ (Surah al-'Asr)

That is, man, taken absolutely, is in loss. But the Truth makes an exception of whom? ﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ (Surah al-'Asr)

Thus the person cut off from Allah's method is the one who lives in loss, while the one who lives within the sphere of the method is the one who never loses at all. And when a person lives without a method, there issues and occurs from him what the Truth, glory be to Him, has related:

﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was only given it because of knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.﴾ (Surah az-Zumar, 39:49)

Because man, living without a method, calls upon Allah when harm touches him; then when Allah delivers him, he claims that the deliverance was only by means he himself possessed. And when Allah bestows upon him some blessing, he increases in the claim and asserts that this blessing has its source in knowledge of his own, and does not attribute it to the true Originator, who is Allah. He has forgotten that every blessing is merely a test from Allah.

The Most High says next:

﴿Say, "He is capable of sending upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or of confusing you into sects and making you taste the violence of one another." Observe how We vary the signs, that they may understand.﴾ (6:65)

The word "capable" (qadir) means complete power, and that no one has any strength or stratagem against the power of God. For the Most High, glorified and exalted, gives respite to the wrongdoing people, extends the matter for them, and then seizes them suddenly with punishment. The punishment may come from above them, as it came to the people of Abraha who intended to demolish the Ka'bah: He sent against them birds in flocks, pelting them with stones of baked clay, and made them like chewed-up stalks (cf. 105:3–5). Others were seized by the Cry, and others were destroyed by a violent, roaring wind. All of these were punishments that came from above those peoples.

As for Qarun, God caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling. Likewise, the people of Pharaoh were drowned by the waters, and this is the "beneath" (punishment). So punishment may come from above or from beneath the feet in a physical sense, and it may also come from a higher or lower place in a moral sense. An example of this is the punishment that God sets upon great tyrants and despots, and punishment may also come from the poor groups who live at the bottom of the social ladder.

﴿or of confusing you into sects and making you taste the violence of one another﴾ (part of 6:65).

The meaning of "labs al-amr" (confusing a matter) is mixing it in such a way that the observer cannot distinguish it. "Shi'a" (sects) is the plural of "shi'ah." The shi'ah are those who cooperate in a matter, even if it is false, and who are united by one word, one movement, and one goal. The meaning of the Most High's words "or of confusing you into sects" is that each group among you splits apart, and each of them has a leader, and matters become mixed up among doctrinal disagreements that hide behind desires. In this way God makes people taste the violence of one another.

And why all this? Because when people have departed from the method of God, the Truth leaves some of them to others, and each people takes on the task of making others taste punishment. But is there any change in God's dominion and His fixed laws? Never. The sky is the sky, the earth with its elements is the earth, the sun is the sun, the moon is the moon, the stars are the stars, and the rain is the rain.

What happens is only that God makes people taste one another's violence, and each part of the people becomes a wrongdoer toward the other part. When we see people complaining, we know that all people are guilty. And as long as all have sinned and gone out from the method of God, the Truth must set some of us over others, so that everyone knows they have slipped away from the method of God; therefore they suffer hardships, and they will find no rest except by returning to the embrace of God's method. For God's method prevents a believer from being arrogant toward his believing brother, and everyone prostrates to one God. This is why the Truth has prescribed collective worship for us, so that the weak one in worldly authority sees the strong one in authority prostrating alongside him to the One God.

An example of this is what we see of people circumambulating the Ka'bah in the garments of ihram. Among those who circle it are some of the notables, people of high rank and lofty station, and among them too are those who hold only a modest position. The weak man sees himself as equal to the one in strong social standing. All stand before their Lord in humility, holding the curtains of the Ka'bah, weeping. By this He, glorified be He, intends to establish servanthood, and to humble the believer before God and before people, so that pride disappears among the believers and people stand together before God and in His House on equal footing.

﴿Say, "He is capable of sending upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or of confusing you into sects and making you taste the violence of one another. Observe how We vary the signs, that they may understand."﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

And here we are, seeing how the Truth confuses people into sects, and we see those who are attributed to Islam slaughtering one another for many years. If these and those are two believing groups fighting one another, where is the third group that separates the two, in fulfilment of the words of the Truth:

﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of God. And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, God loves those who act equitably.﴾ (Surat al-Hujurat, 49:9)

Behold, the blood attributed to Islam flows, and the number of victims increases, and strangely, others stand as spectators, or they supply each group with the tools of destruction. That indicates that the matter is a calamity and a general one.

The principle we stated before does not change: there is no conflict between two truths, because in a single matter there is only one truth. And conflict between truth and falsehood never lasts long, because falsehood is perishing and passing away. But conflict lasts only between two falsehoods, because neither of them is more deserving than the other of being helped by God.

Another example: we were in a country like Lebanon during the civil war, and the conflict raging there nearly made clear to us that every individual had become a sect by himself, each person had his own desire, and each person made others taste punishment and tasted punishment from others.

﴿Observe how We vary the signs, that they may understand.﴾ (part of 6:65)

The Most High diversifies the proofs and evidences; He brings them events and calamities, so that it becomes clear to everyone that there is never any rest in departing from the method of God, until they gain understanding. "Fiqh" (understanding) is intense comprehension. The meaning is that we should take and understand the lesson from all the signs that the Truth displays before us, perhaps we will return to the will of God.

And Allah says next: ﴿But your people denied it, though it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you.﴾ (6:66)

What did the people deny? The intended meaning is the Qur'an, or the religious method (al-manhaj) in general, because the faith-based method includes the Qur'an and includes what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought. The Qur'an is a miracle comprising the fundamentals (usul), and the Messenger (ﷺ) came with the Sunnah (the prophetic practice and teaching) to clarify and legislate. Therefore, we respond to those who seek every ruling from the Qur'an and say:

The Qur'an came as a miracle speaking of the fundamentals of belief, and the Messenger (ﷺ) came with the legislation that completes the method. An example of this is the number of prayers in each of the five obligatory prayers, the number of units (rak'ah) of each of the five daily prayers. The Qur'an did not mention them, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained them for us, for he said in a noble hadith: "Pray as you have seen me praying."(1)

The Messenger (ﷺ) is entrusted with legislation by the explicit text of the Noble Qur'an:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ (part of 59:7).

We pray as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed, we pay zakah at the nisab (threshold) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) specified, and we perform Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed Hajj. Allah, glory be to Him, sent down the Qur'an, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the first to apply the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them and that they might give thought﴾ (part of 16:44).

That is, there are doctrinal matters that the Truth revealed in summary in the Qur'an, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by commission from the Truth, explained them to the believers. Obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is obligatory by the explicit text of the Qur'an, and it falls within obedience to Allah, the Exalted. The Truth says once:

﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾ (part of 3:32).

Here the obedience to the Messenger is not repeated; it is included within obedience to Allah.

And He, glory be to Him, says another time:

﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ (part of 24:54).

That is, there is a command to obey Allah and a command to obey the Messenger.

And a third time He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.﴾

All of this is so that we comprehend the rulings in which the Sunnah coincided with the Book of Allah.

When the Truth said:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾ (part of 4:59).

He, glory be to Him, did not give independent obedience to those in authority; rather He made it part of the inner content of two obediences: obedience to Allah and obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ).

Returning to the meaning of the verse we are discussing:

﴿But your people denied it, though it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you.﴾ (6:66)

So whoever denies the existence of Allah and denies the Qur'an is also a denier of the method. The one denied here is the Truth, and the Truth is the established thing that does not change. In our daily life, an incident occurs and several eyewitnesses come forward, and we do not find them disagreeing in narrating the incident, because they draw from one reality. But if some of the witnesses did not actually see the incident they testify about, you find them confused in their statements. This is why we find the public prosecutor trying to extract all the facts from the mouths of the witnesses, because the truth may hide briefly behind some fog, but its concealment does not last long; it appears clear and bright.

And the Truth strikes examples for us, saying, glory be to Him:

﴿He sends down from the sky water, and valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a rising foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or utensil, is a foam like it. Thus does Allah present the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but that which benefits people remains on the earth. Thus does Allah set forth parables﴾ (13:17).

So water descends by the command of Allah from the sky, and by it the life of plants, animals and humans continues, and each valley takes according to its need. When the torrent comes down, it carries along some impurities that float on the water, and similar impurities also float up when gold or any metal is smelted, called dross (khabath). Thus falsehood floats like foam and goes away cast off and thrown far away, or settles on its banks, while the truth that benefits people remains in the earth. The denial of the Truth from Allah, of the Qur'an and of the faith-based method by the people is bewilderment (buhtan), and the Messenger (ﷺ) is not a guardian over the deniers, nor is he obliged to make them believe; the guardian is Allah, the Truth, who punishes every denier of Him, and the Messenger's task is only to convey.

﴿But your people denied it﴾. The phrase "your people" is a severe rebuke to them, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came from among them, and they knew him as truthful and trustworthy for forty years before the message, and they never found him lying. The length of his stay among them with this long history required that, immediately upon his proclamation of the message, they should have asked themselves: he has never lied to us, and we are creatures; would he lie against the Creator? But desire blinded their insight, and therefore the Truth says about this proclamation:

﴿Say: If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had remained among you a lifetime before it. Then will you not reason?﴾ (10:16).

That is, say to them, O Muhammad: If Allah had willed not to send down a Qur'an to me from Him, and not to have me convey it to you and inform you of it, He would not have sent it down, I would not have recited it to you; but He sent it down and sent me with it to you. When Allah bestows favor upon those to whom He sent His Messenger (ﷺ), He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; concerned over you; to the believers, kind and merciful﴾ (9:128).

Despite the arrogance, obstinacy and denial of the polytheists among the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) people, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated from Makkah to Madinah, he left Ali in Makkah to return the trusts (amanat) of the people. Is there any greater folly than the folly of those who denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He was trustworthy with them, yet they were not trustworthy with their Lord?

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, al-Bayhaqi, and al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 67:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says:

﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know.﴾ (6:67)

Al-naba' (news) is important information, so not every piece of information is a naba'. This is because there is much trivial information in which knowing it and being ignorant of it are equal, neither benefiting nor harming. An example of important information is His saying, the Truth:

﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news, about which they are in disagreement.﴾ (Surah al-Naba' 78:1-3)

So, "for every naba' there is a mustaqarr (fixed time/place)," and al-mustaqarr is that in which a matter is to settle. The naba' is contained (maẓrūf), and the mustaqarr is that which contains it (maẓrūf fīhi). Containment is of two kinds: temporal containment and spatial containment. That is, the Truth, glory be to Him, has assigned to every event a time and a place in which the news occurs. And a person will know the mustaqarr of every news when the Truth permits the birth of this mustaqarr in which the news is announced.

The naba', then, is the great and astonishing news, and there is nothing greater than the descent of heaven upon the earth with a new method that rescues it from the error it is in, a method that is general for every time and every place. So it is a great news, because it liberates the worldly life of people from the tyrants of the earth, and draws all people to a method that brings them out, all together, from their desires. Nothing harms society more than for every person to follow his own desire, because the desire of every soul serves its appetites, and appetites conflict. If every person rules by his own desire, the earth will not find a single matter agreed upon. Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, has taken upon Himself for mankind the matter of organizing the method, which is the very matter on which desires differ. As for the matter on which desires converge, namely extracting what is in the earth of treasures and discovering what is in the cosmos of secrets, He has left it to man to derive by the intellect that God created, from the cosmos that God created, and so that man may find happiness in those secrets that he discovers in the cosmos.

The reality of life confirms this matter for us. We find the ambition of the human intellect: when it reflected on the matter of the cosmos, it derived from it secrets and achieved many scientific discoveries. States and blocs have not differed in those fields; rather, all desires have converged at these discoveries. Thus there is not, as we have said, a "Russian electricity" and another "American" one, nor do we find "English chemistry" and another "French." Therefore you find political and social systems, however different, meeting in the fields of science, agreeing and not differing, to the point that some of them may steal from others what they have reached. And in the knowledge of matter, the laboratory and the experiment, we find differences between one political system and another; rather, desires meet at the discovered laws derived from the matter of the cosmos. This is the matter that God left to people so that they might be free in it: thinking, observing, reflecting, innovating, and arriving at secrets of the cosmos that lighten for them the burdens of life and deliver to them the ends of happiness in existence with the least effort.

But we find violent conflict on the other side, the side of principles and method, and it is a conflict that never ceases, because it is a conflict of desires, not governed by any material experiment. They differ in profound disagreements: capitalism differs from socialism, and the disagreements vary among all the doctrines that desires have produced: communism, existentialism, socialism, capitalism. All these matters were not governed by an experiment or a laboratory, and that is why disagreement arose. Unfortunately, people have exploited what they agreed upon, namely scientific innovations, to impose the systems on which they disagreed.

God, glory be to Him, made this matter clear to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: He left the minds of humanity free in everything subject to experiment, but He organized human life on earth in the light of the faith-based method, because Islam came after a religion whose custodians, the priests, sought to impose the domination of priestcraft over the human mind regarding the secrets of the cosmos.

The example of this is entirely clear in human history. In the age when Europe lagged behind and was called the "Age of Darkness," the Muslims in the East were living by following God's method, in an age of light, because Islam taught them the field of using the intellect and its capacities to derive God's secrets in the cosmos. He, glory be to Him, brought this religion, which is the great news, to clarify for us in the course of this religion every lesson, as if He were saying to us:

Indeed this religion began weak, and those who believed in it were a small group of oppressed people who could not protect themselves; rather, they sought protection and asked for it from a foreign king in Abyssinia. Despite that, they prevailed, because they held fast to this religion.

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, in what his Lord had said:

﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know.﴾ (Surah al-An'am 6:67)

The meaning of (mustaqarr) is: a birth in which it settles. That is, do not hasten the events, and do not abort them; for if God wills, this religion will have spread, and this spread has a birth in time and a birth in place. As for its time, it is until the Hour arrives; as for its place, it is the whole earth, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came as a messenger to all people and as the seal of the prophets and messengers.

The Truth, glory be to Him, confirms the matter ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾ by reality showing facts that confirm it. Like what happened in the recent period close to the birth of the Islamic call: when Islam came, a small group of the oppressed believed in it, and when His saying was revealed:

﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs.﴾ (Surah al-Qamar 54:45)

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "What multitude is this that will be routed and turn its back, when we cannot protect ourselves?" Then when the day of Badr came and he saw the slain of the enemy, just as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said, conveying a message from God, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "God has spoken the truth; the multitude has indeed been routed and turned its back." And we find every Qur'anic matter preserved and recorded in the lines (of history), which God preserves so that people will have no argument against God; for He, glory be to Him, is the One who says:

﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know.﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:67]

For if reality did not confirm that every news has a fixed time, but rather an event happened with a time and a place, what would the people who receive the Qur'an think? Therefore the Truth brought every Qur'anic matter together with its proof, and gave some of the truths documented by events in time and place, so that His saying, the Truth, would be confirmed:

﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know.﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:67]

The world has known, and Islam has prevailed. The Truth willed to train the first bearer of the call, peace be upon him, and with him his companions, may God be pleased with them all, teaching them a discourse by which they could keep pace with the events of the cosmos.

We know that the Truth, glory be to Him, used to send down messengers with religions at intervals, and when corruption spreads over the earth, the Truth sends down His method upon a messenger to guide people to the straight path; for the Truth, glory be to Him, placed in every human soul a self-balancing mechanism. When a person desires a desire that religion forbids, and he fulfills that desire, the intensity of the sin's heat subsides within him, and the person reproaches and rebukes his own soul. But the soul may grow accustomed to desires, and the restraint that holds a person back is lost.

If the restraint is lost in an individual, it will not be lost in society; we find among people someone who leads society to what is good and directs the soul that has grown accustomed to sin toward repentance and goodness. But if corruption spreads through the individual and through society, what then is the stance?

Heaven must intervene with a new messenger and a new method. The new messenger comes with the method necessary to reform the cosmos. Only the oppressed few follow the new messenger, along with people of insight from among the powerful, so that no one may suppose that the weak clung to religion and inclined to it out of their weakness. The Truth warns the believers, as if He were saying: you are facing a falsehood that has gripped people, oppressed them and burdened them; and when falsehood grips societies, the ones who benefit from that are the people of falsehood, and the ones who suffer from it are the people of truth. For every corruption there is a class that profits from it. When the class that profits from corruption exists, and when the word of truth exists, those who profit from corruption look at their influence, which will inevitably recede when the word of truth prevails.

When truth triumphs, corruption must vanish, along with all the influence of the people of corruption. Therefore those who profit from corruption stand against the new religion in order to preserve their position in society. The Truth says, refining the believers and disciplining the non-believers:

﴿When you see those who engage in vain talk about Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in a different discourse. And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.﴾ (Surah al-An'am 6:68)

By this statement God makes clear to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: know that what you have brought will be debated; they will say at one time that it is magic, at another that it is poetry, at a third that it is soothsaying, and at a fourth they will accuse you of lying. Only those who profit from the corruption of the cosmos say this, and when a reformer comes, they will make him their enemy. Therefore you must safeguard two matters. The first: those who followed you, who are weak, may not be able to confront the oppressive power; so do not burden them with what they cannot bear, but be patient, for every news has a fixed time. The second: when you see those who engage in vain talk about Our signs, turn away from them, show them the coldness, do not incline toward them, do not befriend them, do not listen to them, and do not let your companions listen to them, why? Because they are engaging in vain talk about the signs of God. But must this turning away continue at all times? No. Turning away from them is only during their vain talk and their denial of God's signs; at other times, know that their ears need to hear a cry of truth. So seize the opportunity when they are not engaging in vain talk about your religion and about you, and instruct them in what you bring good tidings of, and instruct them also in what you warn of; for if you leave them in their error, the matter of faith will become remote from them, and your task is only to convey the message, while God desires good for all His creatures.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 68:

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a different discourse.﴾ (part of verse 67, surah al-An'am)

The word (al-khawd) (wading, plunging into discourse) gives us a meaning of the utmost precision, because khawd in its origin is entering into abundant water. Abundant water covers what is beneath the feet of the one wading in it, and since it has covered what is beneath his feet, he does not know to what place his feet will fall, and perhaps they may fall into a pit. But one who walks where there is no water has a clear path before him; he places his foot where he sees firmness, stability and no harm. From this meaning they took the description of speech as false, because it is khawd without guidance. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Then leave them in their plunging, playing.﴾ (part of verse 91, surah al-An'am). And why did He describe their action as play (la'ib)?

That is because play (al-la'ib) is occupying the self with a thing that is not required, while it appears in the form of seriousness. But if this thing leads to excellence in some field of life, we train our children in it in the period before puberty. For example, training children in swimming, archery and horse-riding. As soon as a person reaches puberty, he acquires a task in life, and it becomes incumbent upon him to bear responsibility, so he does not waste his time in play or in what diverts him from performing his duty.

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a different discourse.﴾ (part of verse 67, surah al-An'am)

The human self has states of change, and these changes may cause it to forget through certain distractions. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is promised by his Lord that he will not forget.

﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget.﴾ (verse 6, surah al-A'la)

If this is the case for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), how do we understand the Truth's saying here:

﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.﴾ (part of verse 68, surah al-An'am)

We understand this statement on the basis that it is an instruction to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and when a command descends from heaven, the Messenger of Allah is the most entitled of people to apply it. So if the Messenger is addressed with: ﴿And if Satan causes you to forget﴾, then if a person forgets through some lapse of heedfulness, let him take God's remedy for forgetting, which is not to sit with these people who engage in vain talk concerning God's verses while they are plunging; rather he must leave them and turn away from them. Thus the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has honoured His creation; for He, being All-Knowing of them, created for every human a retentive faculty, a memorizing faculty, and an imaginative faculty, and each of these faculties performs a task: the retentive faculty preserves information, and the memory brings back the old preserved information to place it in the focus of awareness. Had there been no forgetting, no idea could have entered a person's mind, because the mind is occupied only with one matter at the focus of awareness. And for another matter to enter the focus of awareness, the first matter must shift from the focus of awareness to the margin of awareness.

Therefore it is necessary to forget one thought so that another thought may take its place. If a person remained recalling one matter in his self, it would be impossible for another new matter to enter. For this reason God created forgetting, that is, the movement of a matter from the focus of awareness to the margin of awareness. A person among us remembers something that happened twenty years ago, then this incident passes through his mind suddenly, and he wonders, how? And he knows that this incident was preserved and kept safe in distant circles of awareness. Therefore we find that when a person wants to recall some meaning, he leaves himself an opportunity to recall this thought or that meaning, and for this reason they call this matter (tadhakkur) (recollection).

﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.﴾ (part of verse 68, surah al-An'am)

And why does the Truth attribute forgetting to Satan? Because the realities of the Truth in His religion are sincere, and they should never be absent from the mind of the believer; and they are absent from the mind of the believer only through the action of Satan. Satan makes attractive to a person the matter he loves and occupies him from another matter. So when Satan prompts a person to forget, and the person recalls that this is from Satan's prompting, let him seek refuge in Allah from Satan and not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.

When you do this and withdraw from these wrongdoing people, you are drawing their attention to the fact that the certainty of faith you hold is dearer to you than the talk in their gatherings and whatever benefit they may have. Thereby you benefit from this reminder, and they too turn their attention to the importance of faith and its superiority in the believer's eyes over everything else.

Al-Sha'rawi's Tafsir (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), commentary on Surah 6, verse 69:

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, would not have imposed on the believers a boycott of the polytheists during the period of the believers' weakness at the beginning of the da'wah (the call to Islam). The believers used to meet in al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque), and the polytheists also used to go to the Ka'bah before the conquest of Makkah, for it was the place of their pilgrimage. So would the Muslims boycott al-Masjid al-Haram at the beginning of the Islamic da'wah and not meet there? Certainly not. Rather, the Muslims would go to meet in al-Masjid al-Haram, and when those who engage in vain discourse about the signs of Allah come, they turn away from them. The burden of those who engage in such discourse falls upon themselves. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And there is nothing upon those who fear Allah in respect of their account, but it is a reminder, that they may fear Allah.﴾

That is, if you are with them and they engage in talk [of this kind], and you rise from their gathering, or you forget and sit, then remember and rise, you are thereby making them aware that what has made you rise from their gathering is something far more important than that gathering. It is respect for the obligation of Allah in what He has commanded you and forbidden you. Neither you nor those who fear Allah bear any part of the sins of these wrongdoers, and nothing of their account falls upon you. Your mere rising from their gathering is a reminder to them, so that they may reflect upon the logic of truth, fear Allah, and distance themselves from falling into falsehood, so that they may be safe from the punishment and wrath of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 70:

Then the Truthful Lord says after that:

﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion, and whom the worldly life has deceived. And remind them, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it has earned. It will have, besides Allah, no protector and no intercessor. And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it. Those are the ones who have been given up to destruction for what they earned. For them is a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment because they used to deny.﴾ (70)

We said earlier that la'b (play) is occupation with what serves only to kill time, and we know that the domain of play is before accountability (taklif), that is, before the age of puberty. If play preoccupies you from something that is required of you, it becomes lahw (diversion), because you have been diverted from a duty incumbent upon you. So lahw, then, is the relaxing of the self with what wisdom does not require.

His saying, the Truthful: ﴿and the worldly life has deceived them﴾ is a depiction that cannot be surpassed in its eloquence, because they are among those with minds that are deceived by the worldly life, and such minds are bewildered. The mature mind understands the world to be of too little worth to be an end; rather, it is a means, or a field, a path, and a sown field for the Hereafter.

The mature mind must deal with it without forgetting its mission. The bane of people is that they have made means into ends, whereas the purpose of human existence on earth is to cultivate it through righteous deeds and the worship of the Truth. Whoever deviates from that will have his punishment on the Day of the Great End, which is the Day of Reckoning.

We know that the aim of a human being in the worldly life is not to live a long life, nor to attain positions, nor to acquire wealth, nor to gain power, for all of that is among the accidents (aghyar), and accidents differ from one person to another.

What we human beings differ about is not the end of our existence; the end of human existence must be one, and we must all agree upon it. This end is what we arrive at after death. The success of every work is in proportion to how much it brings one closer to the end. Therefore the true believer regards the way people receive the matter of death as foolish. When a youth of twenty dies, we find someone saying: "He did not enjoy his youth." The true believer responds to such a saying by asking: "Where do you want him to enjoy his youth?" And those of superficial understanding answer: "He died before he could enjoy his youth in this world."

The true believer says: Is this world the end? It is not the end; rather, the end is the other life. Whoever dies before accountability (taklif), Allah has saved him from reckoning and has settled him in Paradise, where he receives its everlasting bliss. So why, then, this excess of grief over any dead person? One who approaches the end loves that end. Suppose a person's aim is to go to Alexandria, and the means to it may be a horse, a carriage, or an airplane; whatever brings him closer to the goal is the best.

If Allah wills to take some of His creation while they are in their mothers' wombs, then this is His will, and the one who passed from the mother's womb to the grave has drawn near to the end, and has been freed from the stages that carry trials within them, and has entered Paradise.

Suppose the infant lived to the age of one hundred, became an elder, passed through every test of trial, and remained upright upon the method; then where is his destiny? It is Paradise.

So we must receive every decree of Allah with love: the decree of birth or the decree of departure from this world. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent. Who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed.﴾ (Surah al-Mulk)

He, glorified is He, did not say "He created life and death"; rather, He said: ﴿created death and life﴾, so that each of us receives life while the mind has already anticipated what terminates this life, which is death. Thus this is the end in which all of humankind agree, while whatever else is outside it is accidents about which we differ.

Therefore do not say that the aim for your son is that he be admitted to the preparatory school, then obtain the preparatory certificate, then obtain the general secondary certificate, then obtain a bachelor's degree from the faculty or a licence, or a master's degree or a doctorate, then become a person of standing in life. Do not say that, for all of that is not the end of life, because the end is that beyond which there is nothing further. Rather, we must work to cultivate the earth as Allah has commanded us, but we must not make it the end.

Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, said:

﴿Know that the worldly life is only play and diversion and adornment and boasting among you and rivalry in wealth and children, like a rain whose plant pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up and you see it turned yellow; then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness from Allah and approval; and the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ (Surah al-Hadid, 20)

This is the worldly life. Therefore one must always live in light of that which saves us from punishment, which is the remembrance of Allah. The Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And remind them, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it has earned, having besides Allah no protector and no intercessor.﴾ (part of verse 70, Surah al-An'am)

The remembrance here is intended as reminder by the Qur'an, which is the method sent down from heaven, and which the Messenger of Allah applied, and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is also among the remembrance. Or the remembrance here is intended as the punishment that awaits whoever opposes the method. His saying, the Truthful: ﴿And remind them﴾ indicates that the logic of the innate nature (fitrah) requires that we know that the Truth cannot treat the pious in this world as it treats the deviant. An example of this: a person who engages in disparaging people's honor and wronging them can never imagine that he will receive from the Truth, glorified is He, the treatment with which a person committed to the method of faith is treated. The innate nature tells us that the Truth recompenses every person according to his deeds, whether the recompense is in this world or in the Hereafter. It is reported from some Arabs that he said: "No oppressor dies until Allah takes vengeance upon him." Then a wicked man died, and people did not see in him the vengeance of heaven, so the Arab man said:

"By Allah, behind this abode there is another abode in which the doer of good is recompensed for his goodness and the doer of evil for his evil."

﴿And remind them, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it has earned.﴾ Al-basl means: prevention. Prevention has two forms. The first is preventing the movement of a living being's life... that is, confining it in a specific place in which it moves; and the second is preventing the very root of life... that is, destroying it and taking its soul. ﴿lest a soul be given up (tubsal) for what it has earned﴾ means: a soul is prevented because of what it earned, and the prevention is either by destruction or by confinement that perpetuates torment upon it. Confinement, in the customs of people, is placing a person in a place to restrain him from wronging others; that is, we restrain a person's evils from society by putting him in prison.

When Islam came, it did not confine an individual; rather, it confined society away from an individual. This is a greater and more severe punishment. Islam left the criminal free in society, but society was withheld from him; the criminal walks and finds no one who speaks to him, smiles at him, rejoices with him, or shares his sorrow.

This happened when the believers isolated themselves from three men who stayed behind from the expedition with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to the point that one of them came to approach his wife and she refused. Another tried to greet his cousin and he did not return the greeting, so he sat weeping. All the people shunned these three, and this is the greatness of Islam: it imprisoned society away from the criminal, so the criminal was tormented by society's estrangement from him.

﴿Remind with it, lest a soul be given up for what it has earned﴾: that is, remind with the Qur'an, or with the method, or with the consequence of a person's opposition to the method. Punishment is either confinement or destruction, and that is because of what the soul has earned. Kasb (earning), in linguistic usage, means an increase over capital. The word has a second derivation, iktasaba (to acquire). Sometimes the two words have the same meaning. Kasb occurs without artifice and without toil or hardship, whereas iktisab occurs with artifice, treatment, and strain, because the one who obtains what is forbidden takes more than his own capacity, and so he has acquired. As for one who takes what is lawful for him, he has earned. But some people take what they have acquired by trickery and deceit, and they think it is earning, and this is the evil, because he takes what is not lawful for him and makes it lawful to himself, considering it earning and not acquisition.

Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿It has what it earned, and it has what it acquired.﴾ (part of verse 286, Surah al-Baqarah)

Here (lahā) means in favor of the soul, because it has taken what is its right. And (ʿalayhā) means against the soul, because it has contrived in taking what is not its right. An example: a man's glance at his wife is a good glance at a lawful and good thing. But a man's glance at a strange woman may contain much artifice; he sneaks to see her, and does not want anyone to see him stealing a look at her, and all these are contrived emotions.

Another example: the lady of the house, when she enters her kitchen and takes something to eat, eats from her husband's lawful wealth. But the maid, when she wants to take a piece of meat from the kitchen without the knowledge of the household, sneaks about, tries to know the number of pieces of meat, and may ask herself: Has the housewife not counted the pieces of meat? So she takes a small piece from each piece of meat. This is contrivance that wearies the limbs, for such matters wear out a person's faculties; he tries to satisfy one faculty and exhausts all his other faculties.

﴿And remind them, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it has earned, having besides Allah no protector and no intercessor, and if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it.﴾ (part of verse 70, Surah al-An'am)

So this soul which is confined and delivers itself to ruin and punishment by the evil of its earning has, besides Allah, no protector and no intercessor, and no ransom is accepted from it. These are successive stages, beginning with the saying of the Truthful: ﴿has, besides Allah, no protector﴾. The protector (wali) is the one who supports you if you are in a predicament.

The predicament of the Hereafter is great, so what of the person who has no protector? He is the true punishment.

The second stage: ﴿nor intercessor﴾, that is, he has no one who will intercede with the One who possesses victory, who is Allah. The one who loves you, if he does not support you by his own essence, may intercede for you with one who can support you. This also does not exist for one who has not remembered and admonished himself and has not followed the method of faith.

The third stage: ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾, that is, no compensation (fidyah) will be accepted from him. These three outlets are closed, and there is no path to salvation for those of whom the Truthful said: ﴿Those are the ones who have been given up to destruction for what they earned﴾, that is, they have been destroyed or confined in the Hellfire in a confinement from which there is no release. And this is not all; the Truth also says: ﴿For them is a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment because they used to deny.﴾

When we hear the word (sharāb) (drink), we understand from it quenching. But here the Truth follows the word (sharāb) with specifying the source of this drink: it is ﴿of boiling water﴾ (ḥamīm), so that what is called (inbisāṭ) expansion and (inqibāḍ) contraction occurs. Something that pleases a person expands the soul toward it; something that grieves a person contracts the soul. Had the distressing matter come first in this noble statement, the soul would have contracted in its natural course; but the Truth willed to bring first a word that pleases the hearer, which is (sharāb), and then follow it with what contracts the soul, (ḥamīm), so that the pain becomes two pains: the pain of the cessation of joy, and the pain of the arrival of sorrow.

The Qur'an depicts this image in another place, saying:

﴿And if they seek relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces...﴾ (29) (Surah al-Kahf)

The soul expands when it hears the first part, which is: ﴿And if they seek relief they will be relieved﴾, but it contracts immediately upon hearing ﴿with water like molten brass that scalds the faces﴾.

Another image is when the Truth says:

﴿...so give them the good news of a painful punishment (34)﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah)

The soul expands, as we have known, when it hears news of glad tidings, because glad tidings come for a joyful matter, and it contracts when it learns that the glad tidings are of a painful punishment. Thus the Truth has brought expansion and brought contraction. This is one of the sunan (divine patterns) of Allah in discipline. An example of this: when a person commits many wrongs, his evil multiplies and grows, and Allah wills to take vengeance upon him; He, glorified is He, does not take vengeance upon him while he remains in his normal state, but rather the Truth, glorified is He, raises this wrongdoer to high ranks and then causes the earth to swallow him.

Therefore the Truth says:

{So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of...}

God says, after that:

﴿Say: "Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have enticed away in the earth, bewildered, though he has companions who call him to guidance, saying, 'Come to us.' Say: 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (only) guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'"﴾ (6:71)

This verse begins with a question about the worship of idols or other things. What did those idols, or others, do for those who worshipped them? And what did they do for those who did not worship them? This is the first argument against the divinity of anything other than Allah. For example, what did the sun give to one who worships it? And how did the sun punish one who disbelieves in it? It rises for those who worship it and for those who do not. As for the idol they worshipped, what did it do for them? Nothing. And this idol did not send punishment upon those who did not worship it. Rather, the one who benefited is the one who did not worship idols, because he exercised his mind to seek the Creator of this universe.

Thus we find that benefit and harm come only from the true God: ﴿and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us﴾. A person, whenever he walks, takes a step forward, which shortens the distance ahead of him. But one who turns back on his heels is one who reverses that step he has taken.

This is the speech about believers who refuse to return to worshipping other than Allah, because they have believed and walked on the path of guidance. It is not logical for them to turn back on their heels and become losers.

﴿like one whom the devils have enticed away in the earth﴾. The word "shaytan" (devil) here means the rebellious jinn. The jinn are a kind alongside mankind, and just as there are obedient and disobedient among mankind, so too there are obedient and disobedient among the jinn.

And Allah says:

﴿Say: "It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened, and said: 'Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an (1) that guides to righteousness, so we believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord (2)."﴾ (Surah al-Jinn)

So among the jinn there are believers, and among the jinn there are disobedient ones. The disobedient among the jinn are called shayatin. Beware, O Muslim, of denying the existence of the devil because you do not see him, for the devil is among the creatures Allah mentioned from the unseen world. The proof of his existence is your belief in the one who told you about him. There is a logical and philosophical difference between the existence of a thing and the perception of its existence. What troubles people is that they want to equate and link the existence of a thing with their perception of it. Here there is a distinction between existing and being perceived, for there are things that exist but are not perceived.

﴿Say: "Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us"﴾ (part of 6:71).

This image is presented in the form of a question. Allah ordered His Messenger to say it. It is as if the picture is: a people whom Allah guided to the truth were then called to worship other than Allah and to call upon what neither benefits nor harms, so they turn back on their heels, that is, after guidance. This is the picture of bewilderment and hesitation, because they were upon guidance and then were called to worship besides Allah what neither benefits nor harms. Allah, glorified and exalted, wanted to give us a picture of this bewilderment and this hesitation, so He said: ﴿like one whom the devils have enticed away﴾.

"Istahwathu" (ﻻ) is from the form "istaf'ala," which always indicates seeking, as in "istafhama" (he sought understanding) and "istakhraja" (he sought to extract something). "Fa-istahwathu" means they sought his desire, that is, they made him accept what they wanted and took possession of him without him having any evidence or proof for the truth of what they call him to, until he became dough that the devils shape as they wish. The root h-w-y carries meanings: if elongated, it is "hawa'," the air we breathe, by which life exists; if short, it is "hawa," inclination of the soul toward something; or it may be "hawiy," meaning falling.

So the root comes either for "air," if it is elongated, or, if short, it is from "hawa" or "hawy," as you say: "hawa, yahwi, hawiyan," meaning he fell from a height to a low place; and "hawiya, yahwa, hawan," meaning he loved. Thus we know that "istahwathu" means they sought his desire or his whim, that is, the inclination of his soul to follow whim. When the devils entice a person, they want to draw him toward his desire, and they stir up whim in the soul, and by this they call him to fall. Allah says:

﴿And whoever associates others with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him away, or the wind carried him off to a faraway place.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj 22:31)

When a servant falls from the sky, either the birds snatch him or the wind carries him to a distant place. When you come to "hawa" and "hawy," know that whim pulls you toward what harms you, and therefore you will not be safe from it unless your desire follows what the Truth has brought. But if you follow your desire, it must lead you to the fall:

﴿like one whom the devils have enticed away in the earth, bewildered﴾ (part of 6:71).

What is bewilderment? It is hesitation between a matter and its opposite. We have already known that the bewilderment in this verse applies to one who was guided and took a step on the path, then turned back on his heels and returned, yet has companions calling him to guidance. So he is between a devil who entices him and companions who call him to the path; therefore he is bewildered: between destruction and salvation. A thing that falls has no stability, and when we see, for example, a stone falling to the ground, we find it spinning with no direction. This is an expressive image. Then comes the decisive word: ﴿Say: "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (only) guidance"﴾ (part of 6:71).

So whom does one follow? He follows those who call him to the approach of the Truth, glorified and exalted, because guidance is the method and the path that leads to the goal. A made thing does not set a goal for itself; rather, the one who sets the goal is the one who made it. I have said before that the television does not tell us its purpose, nor does it know how to preserve itself; rather, its maker sets that. Likewise, man must take his purpose from the One who created him. What corrupts the world is that God created, but people wanted to set for themselves a law of preservation. Therefore we say: we must take the law of preservation from the One who created us, and the guidance of Allah is the guidance of the Truth.

The word "guidance" (al-huda) is used here to give us faith-based certainty in one God. When our belief in one God is established, our desires never differ, because He is the One who sets the law for us. When He sets the law for us and each of us is subject to that law, none of us humbles himself before another. You and I are servants of one God, and there is no disgrace upon you or upon me. When human beings want people to follow their own ideas, the holder of the idea wants others to be humbled before him and to take them onto his method and his principle, though in reality he is not better than them. Therefore you find true guidance when we all submit to one God, society supports and strengthens itself and does not contradict itself, and desire turns toward loving the method of God.

﴿But if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ (part of 23:71).

For this reason religion came, because the Sharia does not decree anything against the human being.

We all remember the story of the Queen of Sheba and Prophet Solomon, peace be upon him, when she said: ﴿And I have submitted with Solomon﴾. She did not say "I submitted to Solomon," but "I submitted with Solomon to Allah." There is no disgrace in her having submitted, for she was not a follower of Solomon but of Solomon's Lord. Therefore, when legislation comes from above, no one is disgraced by believing, and no one thinks he is a follower of another; rather we are all servants of Allah. When we are all servants of one, we are all masters.

Guidance is embodied in faith in one God, and we take this faith through our rational proofs. We enter upon it through the door of reason, and we submit our affair to Him, because He knows best what is good for us.

﴿And we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ (part of 6:71).

Wa-qawluhu ta'ala: ﴿And [We were commanded]: establish the prayer and be mindful of Him, and it is He to whom you will be gathered.﴾ (72)

Here you find a command concerning three things: we submit to the Lord of the worlds, we establish the prayer, and we guard ourselves against Him, subhanahu. Why? Because all the legislated acts that issue from the limbs must necessarily spring from doctrinal wellsprings in the heart.

And how do we submit to the Lord of the worlds? That is, we do what He wills and refrain from what He forbids. Then, we establish the prayer, which is a positive command, and we be mindful of God, that is, we guard against forbidden things, which is a negative command. Thus we find that guidance includes a doctrinal faith in a Lord to whom we surrender the reins of our affairs, so that our movement in existence conforms to what has been laid down for us in the light of (do) and (do not do). Our movement in existence is either doing or abstaining. Doing is to stand in the most excellent of deeds, which is the prayer, and abstaining is to guard against the prohibitions. All of this issues only from the doctrinal wellspring represented by His words: ﴿that we may submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, commands an act or forbids a thing, He knows that you are capable of both doing and not doing. So if He says to you: do such-and-such, then you are capable of not doing it; and if He says: (do not do such-and-such), then you are capable of doing it. Were you not capable of doing it, He would not say to you: do it, because you were created in a form that enables you to do and to not do. This is the choice created in man. As for the rest of the cosmos, it does not possess this choice.

An example of this: the sun is not free to rise or not to rise; the wind is not free to blow or not to blow; and the earth in its elements is not free to bring forth or not to bring forth. But man is distinguished by his capacity to choose between alternatives. Therefore he must be capable of both matters, and error arises only from transferring the domain of (do) into (do not do), or the domain of (do not do) into (do). The believer takes the logic of (do) within the sphere of action, and the logic of (do not do) within the sphere of abstention.
