When you look at man, you find that the divine obligation (taklif) suits the human constitution. You share with inanimate matter some things, with plants some things, and with animals some things, and you surpass them all through the faculty of choice that God has granted you.

To clarify this matter, I say: suppose someone took you to a high place and then left you in the air; you would then fall to the ground. Thus you find that the law of inanimate matter applies to you. You have no will to say: "I do not want to fall." Thus we see the inanimateness in you. Consider growth, over which you have no control, and you cannot say: "I will grow today by an increase in height of half a millimetre." Rather, you do not even know how you grow; you do not know how your heart beats, nor the secret of the peristaltic movements of the intestines, nor the movement of the stomach, nor the work of the liver, nor the movement of breathing by which life subsists. All of these are compelled matters, and it is by the mercy of God toward us that they are compelled. Had they been subject to choice, others would have controlled them.

So, by His mercy toward us, subhanahu, He made us compelled and subjected in these matters. Then He created for us choice in obligation: do, and do not do. Obligation from God, glorified and exalted is He, concerns the actions that proceed from man, not the actions that befall man, because the actions that proceed from man are those in which there is choice, and which the intellect first considers, so that man may then execute them. For this reason our Lord imposes obligation only upon the sane and mature, because no force compels them to act against what they choose. As for the insane, there is no obligation upon them, because they did not consider the matter in their minds before acting; likewise the one who has not matured, because he has not reached the perfection of full understanding; and likewise the one compelled to act by the force of another person or a power stronger than him.

Thus we know that obligation does not bind man in those states in which there is no intellect or the intellect is immature, or in which compulsion exists.

Then the Truth continues: ﴿And it is He to whom you will be gathered﴾. Had the matter, the matter of faith, been merely an appearance and not a substance, no consequence would follow from it. But let us note that there is an end-purpose. And I illustrate this—and to God belongs the highest similitude—: take the student, for example: whether he attends the lesson or does not attend, listens to the teacher or does not, studies or does not study—will not all of that appear in his end-of-year certificate?

Therefore, the reckoning is established upon every act, because you, O human being, enjoy the property of choice, that is, you are capable of doing or not doing. For this reason faith guides you to righteous deeds, because there is an end-purpose: you will arrive before the One who will call you to account for having transferred (do) into the domain of (do not do), or (do not do) into the domain of (do). And if you do not take the matters of faith for the soundness of your life, then take them out of fear of recompense and reckoning.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 73:

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the day He says "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. His is the dominion on the day the Horn is blown. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ (73)

Al-haqq (the truth) is the thing that is established and does not change. Since the truth is the thing that is established and does not change, let us look at the creation of the heavens and the earth. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease.﴾ (part of verse 41 of surah Fatir)

When we look at the horizon, we find the sky without pillars. This is a wondrous matter, and therefore He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Without pillars that you can see.﴾ (part of verse 2 of surah al-Ra'd)

Here the Truth says: ﴿the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, so that we know that the creation of the heavens and the earth is not an easy process, and He, glorified is He, is the Capable. He created you with a wondrous creation, and more wondrous than it is the creation of the heavens and the earth. He is the One who says:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind.﴾ (part of verse 57 of surah Ghafir)

When a person contemplates his own constitution, he finds wondrous things, and he verifies the words of Allah:

﴿And in yourselves. Will you not see?﴾ (21) (surah al-Dhariyat)

When you reflect on the heavens and the earth, you find precision of creation, as though He, glorified is He, has made yourself a measure. You will come to know their conditions in succession, and that you will be guided over the days to a new secret in this self. The earlier generations did not know this secret, but when you advance in scientific research and in instruments of probing and instruments of testing, you come to recognize and discover this new thing.

An example of this is what is called osmosis (al-istitrad). We have all seen the communicating vessels into which we put a liquid that flows through winding and straight tubes, so the liquid rises in them to one level. This is what we call the phenomenon of osmosis. There is water osmosis, and there is also thermal osmosis. Thermal osmosis is represented when we bring a heater in winter, sit in the room, and feel the heat radiating from the heater. You find yourself retaining your normal body temperature, which is thirty-seven degrees. What is wondrous is that it is equal among all people, even at the North Pole and the South Pole!! So why does your body temperature not equalize with the air? And why does the cold air not take from your heat so that the temperatures become equal?

This proves that you have an identity that makes you a unit independent of the universe in which you live, and your body temperature remains thirty-seven degrees at the equator and thirty-seven degrees at the poles. This is wondrous, and what is more wondrous is that the different parts of your body differ in temperature. If the temperature of the eye were thirty-seven degrees, it would melt; therefore we find that the temperature of the eye is only nine degrees. And there is the liver, whose temperature reaches forty degrees, and all the organs of your body, gathered in one form, yet the temperature does not equalize among them.

Therefore the Truth said: ﴿And in yourselves. Will you not see?﴾

Another example is from the process of breathing. When a particle of dust enters the passage of breath, you find that coughing has attacked the person to expel this particle, and you find that you have coughed forcibly until this particle is expelled. Did you cough by your own decision? No. Rather, it is an involuntary action subject to a precise system that could only be designed by a Creator of absolute wisdom. For example, we find the liver enveloped in successive coverings to retain its temperature, which reaches forty degrees, because it does not perform its function except at this degree. Likewise we find that the ear is the first organ to feel cold, because its temperature is low. Thus the Supreme Maker willed. As came in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth.﴾ (part of verse 73 of surah al-An'am)

The Truth created the heavens and the earth by fixed laws that do not change except by His will. He is the One who says:

﴿It is not for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, and each, in an orbit, is swimming.﴾ (40) (surah Ya-Sin)

So, O you who seek order as evidence of the wisdom of the Creator who originates, take it from the supreme order. And O you who seek anomaly as evidence of the dominance of the Truth above mechanism, take it from individuals; for if an anomaly occurred in the supreme universe, the heavens and the earth would be corrupted. But when there is one blind person among a thousand people, no disorder occurs in the universe. Therefore we find that anomaly comes only in what has a compensation, while order comes in what, if neglected, causes corruption. As He, glorified is He, says:

﴿The day He says "Be," and it is, His word is the truth.﴾ (part of verse 73 of surah al-An'am)

Thus we see the first origination is by the truth. Also, when He, glorified is He, demolishes the heavens and the earth, ends the world and removes it, the sky will tremble, and the stars will scatter and fall, this too happens by the truth. The creation and origination alone is not the only proof of the greatness of the Creator; rather the ending of creation, its annihilation and its removal are also proof of greatness, because He, glorified is He, said at the beginning: "Be," and there was the universe, and in the end He says: "Be," and it is, the ending of creation, to give the good-doer the reward of his goodness and to call the evil-doer to account. For the good-doer may suffer throughout his life despite his goodness, and he must have a reward; and the evil-doer will not take his ease but will receive punishment. So it is of goodness and greatness that life should end, so that the Day of Reckoning may come and each receive his recompense.

Therefore the creation of the heavens and the earth is truth, and the day He says "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. The truth lies in origination and the truth lies in annihilation; it is present at the beginning of creation and at its end.

﴿His is the dominion on the day the Horn is blown. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ (part of verse 73 of surah al-An'am). Was dominion ever for other than Allah?

On this point we must note that there is "mulk" (possession), and its possessor is called "malik" (owner); and there is "mulk" (sovereignty), and its possessor is called "malik" (king). Possession is what you own; you may own the robe you wear. Sovereignty, however, is that you rule over those who possess. This is called "mulk," and our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, in the world of causes made for each one of us a possession, and made for some of us sovereignty over others, so they remained kings. But in the Hereafter there is nothing of this, therefore the Truth says:

﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (part of verse 16 of surah Ghafir)

In the world, you may own, for example, that you employ me with you and give me a wage. You may own that you cook my food for me or give me food, or own that you sew my robe. But in the Hereafter no one owns for anyone any cause, because we live in this world by the causes which Allah has granted us, and in the Hereafter by the Causer alone, without causes.

﴿His is the dominion on the day the Horn is blown.﴾ If you trace it back before the Horn is blown, you will find the dominion is also Allah's, but through intermediaries; because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, made the earth a land of livelihood, and there is the Hereafter, that it is a land of return. Therefore He said:

﴿The day the earth will be changed to other than the earth.﴾ (part of verse 48 of surah Ibrahim)

The earth on which we live was created so that we may develop it, and we plow one part of it to sow, and build houses on another part. Thus the whole matter is causes that correspond with one another. I cannot plow except with a plow; likewise whoever wishes to extract iron ore from the earth sets up a mine, and whoever wishes to extract petroleum brings instruments that discover its locations. No one can own all the causes of his life; rather one corner is in his hand, and the remaining corners are in the hands of the rest of creation.

When you trace back the causes by which we live, we return to the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. When the hand of the creature and its causes become too narrow for him, the hand of the Creator, may His power be exalted, is always extended to him. Beware that causes should not deceive you, but trace the causes until they end at Allah.

If you trace every phenomenon of the universe, you would reach the logic of the Truth. A little child watches a phenomenon in the house: a switch on the wall; when they press it with one finger the lamp lights up, so he imitates them. When his brother, who studies in preparatory school, sees him, he says to him:

"Do not believe that the light comes from this switch. Rather, there is a wire coming from outside the house that links the electricity box to the homes." And when someone of greater knowledge than both of them hears them, he explains to them that the electricity inside this box comes from the great generator located somewhere in the city, which factories and minds have built, until the explanation ends and arrives at the idea of the electric current drawn from river waterfalls, for example.

So every phenomenon you see before you has unseen links behind it; if you traced them, you would reach the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. He, glorified is He, has respected our world and made us understand that some of us have possession, but we say to every possessor: this possession is not by your essence, for if it were by your essence no one could ever strip you of it. And He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty.﴾ (part of verse 26 of surah Al 'Imran)

Thus there is none who has sovereignty by essence except Allah.

And the Truth says here:

﴿His is the dominion on the day the Horn is blown. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ (part of verse 73 of surah al-An'am).

"Blown in the Horn" indicates the announcement of the coming of a matter: after the first blast, whoever was alive dies; after the second blast, the dead are revived and rise.

The phrase ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ explains to us that since He, glorified is He, knows the unseen, it is all the more certain that He knows the witnessed. This is a precise expression: He knows the unseen and He knows the witnessed, and His knowledge entails a recompense, not out of arbitrariness, but out of wisdom.

The Truth concludes the verse with His words, glorified is He: ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ The All-Wise is the One who places every matter in its place, and the All-Aware is the One who knows everything with complete encompassment. He, glorified is He, has no need to wrong anyone, because one who wrongs only wants to benefit from the thing in the possession of the wronged, whereas our Lord benefits from none of these things, but benefits all of us. Therefore, if you look at faith, you find it is all honour. You find people hate the word "slavery," and wars are fought to free mankind from the slavery of men. But the slavery of a human being to the Truth is a different matter; for in slavery to men, the master takes the best of his slave, whereas in slavery to Allah, the slave takes the best of his Master. Thus slavery to Allah is honour, while slavery to men is humiliation.

For this reason we find that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, bestowed favour upon His Prophet by the attribute of servanthood, saying:

﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque whose surroundings We have blessed.﴾ (part of verse 1 of surah al-Isra').

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, purified his servanthood to Allah, and so he received from the outpourings of the Truth in accordance with his servanthood.

And the Truth, glorified is He, makes clear to every servant: sleep your fill of your eyelids; for I am not seized by drowsiness or sleep, and I am the Self-Subsisting. And if you need anything from Me, call upon Me, and I will extend to you the help that suits you. Is there in this servanthood to Allah anything but honour?

The Almighty then says:

﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? Indeed, I see you and your people in clear error."﴾ (74)

The Almighty, glory be to Him, gives His Messenger (ﷺ) that which consoles him and makes him patient through the hardships of the call, because the call to Islam in its early days wore out the Messenger of Allah and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah. So He wills to give them an example of what happened to the Messengers, and here the Almighty brings an account about the father of the prophets, our master Abraham:

﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods"﴾ (part of verse 74, Surat al-An'am)

When you hear "idh" (when), understand that "idh" is an adverbial of time, meaning: remember well the time at which Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods?" And since you are reminding yourself of this, in this reminder there is consolation for you regarding what befalls you in the matter of the call. Here the scholars paused at length, and some of them asked: Is Azar the father of Abraham, or is his father Terah (Tarakh)?

I said earlier that "ubuwwa" (fatherhood) denotes that which is the origin of the individual: the father, the grandfather, and the grandfather's father are all fathers, and "fatherhood" has been applied to one who is equivalent to the father, such as the paternal uncle. Something like this comes in the Qur'an when the Almighty said:

﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers"﴾ (part of verse 133, Surat al-Baqara).

Here "aba'" (fathers) is plural, and if we count these fathers we find them to be: Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac, the speech being from Jacob, whose father was Isaac, and Isaac was the son of Abraham. Yet Ishmael came among these fathers. So if you distribute them, you would say: "Abraham is a father, and two remain: Ishmael and Isaac. And Ishmael is a brother of Isaac," as if the Qur'an declares that the paternal uncle is also called a father.

I say this to clarify a matter in which much confusion has occurred. Some of the scholars said: Was Azar the father of Abraham? And the noble hadith says:

("I came forth from marriage and not from fornication; from Adam until my father and mother bore me, nothing of the fornication of the Jahiliyya touched me.")(1)

So it is as if the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that he descends from a lineage of monotheism in which there can be no place for polytheism. Azar was a polytheist, and since the Almighty says in another verse: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, then had Azar been the true father of Abraham, Muhammad (ﷺ) would have been among his descendants. I see that he was his uncle, because the Messenger (ﷺ) said: ("I was continually transferred from the loins of the pure men to the wombs of the pure women"), a statement which indicates that his noble lineage is purified of polytheism from the side of the fathers and from the side of the mothers. Therefore it is not correct to believe that the father of Abraham was Azar, because he was in this state a polytheist. But how do you interpret the saying of the Almighty: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾?

We say: we take the language, and we take the Qur'an's usages of the meaning of fatherhood. The Qur'an is explicit that fatherhood, just as it is applied to the true father from whose loins the son descends, is also applied to the brother of the father or his uncle. The proof of this is that the Qur'an which said ﴿to his father Azar﴾ is the very same Qur'an which said:

﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers"﴾ (part of verse 133, Surat al-Baqara).

So "aba'" is the plural of "ab" (father), and the least plural is three: Abraham, then, and likewise the uncle Ishmael, each of them is called a father, and also Isaac, who is the father of Jacob; these are the fathers mentioned in this verse.

Here we understand that Ishmael's fatherhood to Jacob is in fact fatherhood of uncle-ness, because Jacob is the son of Isaac, and Isaac is the brother of Ishmael. Thus "ab" was applied and intended to mean the uncle, and the Messenger (ﷺ) shows us this when he took his uncle al-Abbas captive and said: "Return my father to me," meaning his uncle al-Abbas.

After that we come to say: when we use the word "ab" in our customary speech, we know that the language we speak is a language transmitted by hearing, fixed in our ears, our tongues speak it, and the colloquial, although it distorts the eloquent form, its roots are transmitted from our predecessors and our fathers. When they want the true father, they say "ab" to him and do not mention his personal name. If someone comes to you and says, "Is your father present?" without naming the father, he certainly means your father. But suppose you have an uncle, and the questioner says to you: "Is your father Muhammad present?"

Here he has specified the proper name so that the mind turns to asking about the uncle; for if he had meant the true father, he would not have mentioned his name and would have been content to ask about him by fatherhood alone. So if the Almighty had said, ﴿when Abraham said to his father﴾, without specifying the proper name, we would say that Azar is the father of Abraham and not his uncle, and thus he would be the grandfather of our Messenger. But the Qur'an specified the name and said ﴿to his father Azar﴾, that is, it distinguished the person's name to exclude the true father from the word "ab," and with this the dispute on this matter ends.

And why does the Almighty ask our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to mention ﴿when Abraham said to his father﴾? Because the Messenger of Allah came after a gap between the Messengers, and came at the crisis that faced the call at its first confrontation, namely the nation of the Arabs, headed by the Quraysh. And he (ﷺ), although he came after a gap between the Messengers, still Abraham lived within the beliefs of these people, because all of Abraham's ritual matters were in this place: for example, his resolve to sacrifice his son and the ransom from heaven for his son took place in this place, and his raising of the Ka'ba took place in this place, and the Ka'ba is the center of the Quraysh's dominance, and were it not for the Ka'ba, the Quraysh would have been like the rest of the tribes.

The Almighty wanted to clarify to the Quraysh that the dominance you have taken over all the Arabs came to you because of the Ka'ba and this House. Had this House and this Ka'ba not existed, you would be a tribe among the tribes, with no awe, no authority, and no standing. But you know that your trade goes to the north and to the south, and no one harms it at all, because those who would attack you, whether from the north or the south, will one day come to this Ka'ba to perform the rites of the Hajj, and you will be able to deal with them while they are in the House.

For this reason we said, when we treated the saying of the Almighty:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plan into misguidance? And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and He made them like eaten straw﴾ (Surat al-Fil).

Then He followed it with the saying:

﴿For the security of the Quraysh, their security in the caravan of winter and summer﴾ (Surat Quraysh).

So had the House been exposed to destruction by Abraha the Abyssinian, the awe of the Quraysh would have fallen, but God gave them victory so that the Quraysh would keep their caravans of winter and summer, and therefore He said:

﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them after hunger and made them secure after fear﴾.

The Lord of this House is He who honored them and protected them through the existence of this House which Abraham raised.

So although the people worshipped idols, they still had a doctrinal link with Abraham, so the Almighty wanted to enter into their hearts through the tenderness they know for Abraham, who is the cause of this honor, this cause of this standing and dominance. Also, because the doctrinal confrontation first came for the worship of idols, and the matter with our master Abraham was likewise about the worship of idols. So there are, therefore, multiple connections, and the Almighty brought here the story of our master Abraham to soften their hearts with it.

﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods"﴾. Idols (asnam) are things of stone fashioned in the likeness of a living form, whereas the wathan (idol/image) is a piece of raw stone that has not been shaped, treated or made, which they used to sanctify. Thus we know the difference between the sanam and the wathan. And how did the notion of idols enter people's minds? And from where did it come?

We know that people have direct causes in life: when a person seeks light, he sees the sun has risen; at night he sees the moon has come up; he sees mountains give him firmness and strength, and he builds homes in them.

So there are things in which a person sees apparent causality, and so he believes they are the doer. When he sees these things and supposes they are the doer, he supposes they have sanctity, whether it is the sun or the moon. So before idols came into being, the stars existed and they worshipped them, as the Almighty's saying proves:

﴿Do you take idols as gods....................... (74)﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

After that, in the argument, He does not mention the idols' story but says:

﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star...................... (76)﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

So there was a relation between the idols and the stars, and the root of it is that when a person sees something that benefits him, he ascribes to it every benefit he obtains and sees in it a power he respects, and man did not notice that the creator of these things is unseen, so he worshipped the thing that appeared to him. And when man found that the stars set and disappear, some people said: "Let us set up idols that remind us of them," and there was an idol representing the sun, an idol representing the moon, and another representing such-and-such a star. That is, the idols were made only to remind of the original stars. Therefore I always say: people must not neglect the Causer, for He, glory be to Him, is behind the causes, and as the intellect advances it traces causes back until it ends at a Causer that has no cause behind Him. When the creature's hand ends and falls short in causes, the Creator's hand begins; those who are seduced by causes are those who regard them as the doers in themselves.

So when the matter of religion was obscured and concealed in people's minds, they began to look at what is around them and what benefits them, and so they turned to worship it. Before the Message they used to make pilgrimage to the Ka'ba and love the Ka'ba, and when they were away on long journeys they would take a piece of stone of the kind of the Ka'ba's stones on the long trip, and when one of them saw it he would be reassured. But over the long passage of time these things came to be singled out with a special sanctity that isolated them from causes.

Thus we know that our master Abraham, the Friend of the Merciful, had this standing among the Arabs, and likewise among the People of the Book, to the extent that they claimed his affiliation to themselves: some of them said Abraham was a Jew, and others said he was a Christian. The Qur'an came addressing the disbelievers of Quraysh, and likewise the People of the Book, and God brings the story of our master Abraham to give us the matter of the creeds and clarify it in a way that makes them familiar with the one who has mention in their souls.

﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? Indeed, I see you and your people in clear error."﴾ (part of verse 74, Surat al-An'am).

Misguidance (dalal) is that you want a goal and miss the road to it. Among the people of that time, the goal was to sanctify and honor whoever bestows favors upon them. But they erred in the path and stopped at the cause, and did not mention or perceive what lies behind the cause, and from here came the manifest misguidance. It is in human nature to present allegiance, submission and gratitude to whoever is seen as the source of a blessing; but they lost the way, because they walked through the blessing in a chain of causes and did not reach the Causer through causes. This is manifest misguidance, because it is the seduction of a creature by a creature. The first human who came and turned to a world created for him, turned to the earth, turned to the sun, turned to the moon, turned to the stars, turned to clouds that rain water for him, turned to mountains that supply him with sustenance, was obligated to reflect on this matter, because he did not create these things and no one claimed to have created them. Was it not necessary for him to reflect a little on who created these things for him?

Even the most trivial things need a maker. For example, the cup from which we drink water does not become a cup before any one of us except after it passed through many stages, from the one who discovered the material, to the one who smelted it chemically, to the one who spent upon it, until it reached the cup. Likewise the lamp: if we look at the devices behind it that contributed to its existence, we find...

1 Narrated by Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil, and narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat from Ali (رضي الله عنه).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 75:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says:

﴿And thus did We show Abraham the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth, that he might be of the certain (al-muqinin).﴾

That is: just as Abraham was guided to the understanding that worshipping idols is clear error, Allah then showed him the malakut of the heavens and the earth, since he had been guided to the understanding that there is a true God. The true God makes clear to him the secrets of the cosmos.

Malakut is an intensive form (sighat al-mubalagha) from malk (dominion), like rahamut from rahma (mercy). The malakut gives us the understanding of realities that are not witnessed. The one who follows the visible causes attains the malk (the realm of dominion), because what he witnesses and senses is before him, while the malakut is what is hidden from him. So there is in it malk, and there is in it malakut: the malk is what you see before you, and the malakut is what lies behind this malk.

The example of this is what our master Abraham said when he spoke about the partners set up with God. He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Indeed they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds, who created me and so He guides me, and who feeds me and gives me drink, and when I am ill it is He who cures me, and who will cause me to die and then bring me to life.﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara')

Note here that the styles differ. He says ﴿Who created me﴾ and does not say "He who created me," then he says ﴿so He guides me﴾, because no one has ever claimed to have created the human being; it is a matter settled for God and needs no emphasis. As for guiding people, there are those who claim that they guide people. What is claimed by humans is emphasized with (huwa). What is not claimed by humans, such as creating, causing to die and bringing to life, is not introduced with the word huwa.

Our master Abraham continues: ﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink﴾. Here our master Abraham leapt from all the apparent causes and intermediate links to the reality, and recognized the unseen. ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾. In this he distinguishes between the means of healing, namely the treating physicians, and the Supreme Healer, who is Allah, blessed and exalted, because people are often seduced by causes and say that the physician is the one who cures. Therefore our master Abraham moves from the outward causes to the inner nature of matters, and from the outward appearances of dominion to the inner reality of the malakut, so that we know that the physician treats but does not cure. The evidence is that we have often seen someone go to a physician, who gives him an injection, and the patient dies; thus the physician in such a situation becomes one of the means of death.

Glory be to Him who inherits the physician and his medicine; He sees the patient, the ends of those who are ill.

So, ﴿it is He who cures me﴾: that is, healing is from God, and treatment is from the physician.

In this way our master Abraham brought forward the things in whose causes a person may be seduced, and he emphasized them with (huwa).

When we look at Abraham, peace be upon him, in the story of creed, we find that he attained a great authority which all the prophets acknowledge, because our Lord said of him: ﴿And Abraham who fulfilled (his trust)﴾.

Likewise He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed I will make you an imam (leader) for the people.﴾

(Part of verse 124, Surah al-Baqarah.)

That is: you, O Abraham, are trusted to be an imam for the people, by Abraham's humanity and by the outward dominion. He asked God that the imamate be in his offspring. He said: ﴿And from my offspring﴾, meaning: make some of my offspring imams. So the Truth says:

﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.﴾ (Part of verse 124, Surah al-Baqarah.)

Because the matter of imamate is not an inheritance of blood, and no one takes it except the one who deserves it. We have said that our master Abraham brought Hagar and his son Ishmael from her and settled them in a barren valley near the Sacred House, and the Qur'an says on his tongue:

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits, that perhaps they will be grateful.﴾ (Surah Ibrahim, 37)

That is: our master Abraham, peace be upon him, was aware of the matter of the Truth teaching him the secrets of the malakut, and it remained in the mind of our master Abraham that the Truth, glorified is He, does not give the imamate to one who has done wrong. Then He made clear to him that one must distinguish between the succession of prophethood and the bestowal of lordship in the matter of food. This is represented in the supplication of our master Abraham:

﴿And provide its people with fruits, those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.﴾ (Part of verse 126, Surah al-Baqarah)

So it is as if Abraham, when he asked for fruits for those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, did not distinguish in his supplication between the covenant of prophethood and imamate, and the necessities of life. Thus the Truth says to him: ﴿And whoever disbelieves...﴾

That is: He, glorified is He, will provide with food both the believer and the disbeliever, because food and the necessities of life are among the gifts of lordship (rububiyya), whereas the methods (manahij) are among the gifts of divinity (uluhiyya). Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is Lord of all people, because it is He who summoned them all: the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. And since it is He who brought them into existence, He does not withhold provision from them.

﴿And thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be of the certain.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

Everyone who walks in the footsteps of Abraham, peace be upon him, is bound and attached to the very essence of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. There is a difference between binding and attachment to the Essence, and binding and attachment to the Attributes. The one who worships Allah because He is the Provider, and because He is the Enricher, is one who is bound to the Attributes. But one who is bound to Allah simply because He is God, even if He makes him poor, is one who is bound to the Essence. When our master Abraham purified himself from all the earlier creeds, the Truth made clear to him: you are trusted with the secrets of My cosmos, and the Truth gave him much, just as He gives to everyone who is sincere in his bond with his Creator; our Lord gives him gifts from the secrets of His cosmos.

The Truth, glorified is He, strikes many examples for us in the Qur'an, and says:

﴿And fear Allah, and Allah teaches you.﴾ (Part of verse 282, Surah al-Baqarah)

That is: as long as you are trusted with what you have learned of the rulings of the Truth for the movement of your life and you carry them out, the Truth will consider you trustworthy with His secrets, and will give you more and more.

The meaning of (tattaqi, taqwa) is that you bind yourself to the method of the Truth; and if you bind yourself to the true method, you are within the continuous, unending outpourings of the Truth, because the one in whose company Allah is must be clothed by the Truth with inspirations and gifts of His attributes that reveal his connection to his Lord and reassure him. An example of this is what happened in the story of the Hijra: you find the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and our master Abu Bakr in the cave, and Abu Bakr says to the Messenger of Allah: If one of them looked down at his feet he would see us. This is a certain cosmic matter, and the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, answers him by lifting the matter from the apparent, clear cosmic realm to the pure realm of the malakut, and says: (O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is Allah?)(1).

That is: he says to him, be reassured, no one will see us, because we are in the company of Allah, and He, glorified is He, cannot be perceived by sight. When the weak is in the company of the strong, the law of the strong is what prevails, and the weak is no longer weak. For example, if there is a boy among children of his age who oppress him, hurt him and harm him, and they see him in his father's hand, none of them dares to approach his side. People cannot overpower one another except when they slip out of the company of Allah; and whoever is in the company of Allah is never dared against by anyone. Therefore our Lord sends us the matters of the malk and the matters of the malakut, and represents them in a messenger of the steadfast (ulu al-azm) among the messengers, together with a righteous servant to whom Allah gave something of His knowledge and overflow because he was mindful of Him.

The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So they found a servant of Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Our presence.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 65)

This servant took the method of the messenger who came with it and followed it, performed it in the fullest manner, and was thus connected to the Truth, receiving knowledge from His presence. When we look at this matter we are amazed, because we find our master Moses looking in the realm of the malk, while the one to whom Allah gave mercy from Himself and knowledge from His presence looks from the realm of the malakut. Moses is excused, because he looks within the circle of causes, and the righteous servant is also excused, because he looks within a second circle. Therefore the righteous servant will say: ﴿And I did not do it of my own accord﴾, that is, the matter does not come from himself, but he has been commanded in it. When we consider how each of them assessed the other's position, we find the righteous servant saying: ﴿Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me.﴾ That is, the righteous servant excuses Moses, and adds:

﴿And how can you have patience with what you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 68)

The Qur'an then says on the tongue of Moses:

﴿He said: You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 69)

Here then is the messenger who came to convey the method obeying a righteous servant who applied the method from an earlier messenger, carried it out as God loves, and was bound to the method. Our Lord brought us this story with a messenger of the steadfast. Moses, peace be upon him, receives the command from the righteous servant:

﴿He said: If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 70)

Why? Because the righteous servant knows that Moses will speak of the realm of the malk, while he speaks from the realm of the malakut.

When they boarded the ship and the servant damaged it, and damage is an apparent corruption in the realm of the malk, our master Moses explains to the righteous servant that this act is a violation of the law, and how can he attack the ship with corruption? The righteous servant replies: Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me? Such matters are beyond your capacity. Moses remembers, and then comes the account of the boy and the account of the wall.

When we look closely at these matters, we find that the knowledge of the malakut corrects what is anomalous in the realm of the malk. The damaging of the ship is an apparent corruption, but if Moses knew that there is a king who seizes sound, good ships by force, and this ship belongs to poor men who work at sea, and the righteous servant wants to preserve it for them, so he damages it so the usurper will not take it; for when the usurping king compares a sound ship with a damaged one, he will not take the undamaged one, and its owners can repair it.

So if Moses had known this matter, would it not be permissible that Moses himself was the one damaging the ship? He would have damaged it. Thus if the owner of the theory of the malk had known the secrets in the theory of the malakut, he would have done the very same act. And when we come to the killing of the boy, one must ask: what was the boy's fault? The righteous servant explains the matter:

﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would burden them with rebellion and disbelief.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 80)

The parents might indulge this son and feed him from unlawful wealth, and he would become a trial for them; so the boy was killed so that they would remain in faith, and our Lord hastened the boy directly to Paradise.

In the matter of the wall you find the difference between the view of the realm of the malk and the view of the realm of the malakut. In outward appearance, when they came to the people of the town, they asked for food, and asking for food is a testimony of genuine need, for it is not a request for money, since someone may ask for money to save it; but whoever says, "Give me a loaf to eat," this is the sign of the genuineness of need in requesting food. But the people of the town refused to host them; so they are miserly, not generous. The righteous servant sees a wall that wants to collapse, about to fall, and he set it upright. Moses became angry; the cause of his anger is apparent: he and the righteous servant asked these people for food and they did not feed them, so how can you build a wall for them? You could have taken a wage for it! Moses's anger has an apparent cause, but the righteous servant explains the matter:

He set up the wall because the people of the town are miserly and did not give us food; and if the wall had fallen and the treasure beneath it had appeared before such miserly people, they would have stolen it from its owners, who were children. The righteous servant built it with a faith-based engineering that God inspired in him, such that when the two boys reach maturity, the wall will fall. It is a timed structure, just as we set an alarm clock for a specific time: likewise the wall, so that when the two boys reach maturity, it falls and they take the treasure.

This clarifies for us the difference between the realm of the malk and the realm of the malakut: the realm of the malakut is what is hidden from us behind causes. Many people stop at causes and do not move from causes to the direct cause, until they reach the Causer with no cause beyond Him.

﴿And thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be of the certain.﴾ (Surah al-An'am) So has he become certain...

(1) Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 76:

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿So when the night covered him over, he saw a star. He said: "This is my lord." But when it set, he said: "I do not love those that set."﴾ (6:76)

The root (جن) indicates concealment and covering. From it comes (الجنون) (al-junun, madness), meaning the covering of the intellect, and (جن الليل) (jan al-layl), meaning the night grew dark and concealed things from you, so that you do not see others and others do not see you. The (الجنة) (al-jannah, garden) is likewise named for this, because it contains trees and things that conceal the one who walks within it. Thus the whole root carries the sense of concealment.

The word (كوكب) (kawkab, star) indicates that it takes its light from something else. We understand from the verse that Ibrahim was in darkness, then the star rose and he saw it, then the star set, meaning it passed from rising and appearing to setting. Long ago, people worshipped the stars and planets, so Ibrahim came to them from the same kind of thing they worshipped, and said: ﴿I do not love those that set.﴾

Sha'rawi continues, after this, with the Truth (Allah):

﴿So when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my lord guides me, I will surely be among the people who go astray." (77)﴾

Here Abraham, peace be upon him, said: "This is my lord." The scholars paused at this point and asked: how can Abraham say "This is my lord," which is a declarative statement from Abraham? How can Abraham attribute to himself a word of polytheism? The scholars wanted to clear Abraham of the issue. We say to these scholars: may Allah reward you well. But this matter should have been taken up from a very short perspective, because the One who said that Abraham said "This is my lord" is the One who said about Abraham:

﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾ (part of verse 124, Surat al-Baqarah).

So his saying "This is my lord" does not detract from his faith's loyalty, and it must have some explanation. We know that the people were worshipping the stars, and Abraham wanted to draw their attention to the corruption of this belief. If Abraham had, from the very beginning, said to them, "O liars, O people of misguidance," and kept hurling insults at them, they would not have paid attention to him nor listened to him. But Abraham used what is called in debate "matching the opponent" (mujaraat al-khasm), in order to win their ears and take their hearts with him, and so that they would know that he was not biased against them from the outset, and thus he would take them by the hand along with him.

An example of this in our lives: you find a man who has a daughter, and a suitor came to her, and this suitor is very short, while the daughter, may Allah protect her, is tall. When the suitor came to see her and she saw him, she says to her mother: "This is my suitor?!" This saying means that she denies that this short man is her suitor. When Abraham said "This is my lord," it meant a denial that such a star, or that moon, or that sun, could be the Lord.

We also note that he defines for them the fate of whoever worships those stars, saying: "Unless my lord guides me, I will surely be among the people who go astray." In this there is a recognition of who is upon guidance and who is upon misguidance. His saying "This is my lord" is a kind of mockery, because they had said, as the Qur'an conveyed on their tongues: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?"

It is as if he said: let us grant for the sake of argument that it is your lord, but it sets and disappears from you. And his saying "I do not love the setting ones" means that he is not fanatically opposed to them.

And likewise, when the Truth says:

﴿So when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord, this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, I am free from what you associate (with Allah)." (78)﴾

Thus it is established for him that every star, even the sun, is destined to set. It is as if he had led them, by way of logic, to the conclusion that worshipping the stars is not fitting, and to the use of a logic that achieves his intention of denying this lordship, and that the ears of those who hear it find pleasant. There are things that the Truth makes a justifiable cause for committing many things, except that we draw a comparison between some of them, just as the Truth says:

﴿But whoever opens his breast to disbelief﴾ (Qur'an 16:106), which came after His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Except one who has been forced while his heart is secure in faith﴾ (Qur'an 16:106).

So if Allah has permitted the utterance of a word of disbelief upon the tongue of a believer whose heart is at peace in faith, in order to save his own life, as an individual, is it not then permissible for Abraham to say to them: ﴿This is my lord﴾, with whatever possibilities of expression it may bear, so as to save an entire nation from worshipping idols?

Therefore, the statement of Abraham ﴿This is my lord﴾ is to be understood in two ways. Did not Allah, glorified and exalted is He, Himself say about Himself:

﴿And on the Day He calls to them, "Where are My partners?"﴾ (Qur'an 41:47)

And He, glorified is He, knows that He has no partners; but the partners are those whom the polytheists claimed.

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he would call out to some of the people, "O God of gods," because he knew that some people had deified natural phenomena in the universe because of the good they saw in them, wished to alert them that there is a true God.

The Qur'an clarifies the futility of association when it says:

﴿Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others﴾ (Qur'an 23:91).

And He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say, "If there were gods with Him, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne."﴾ (Qur'an 17:42)

And the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says to the disbeliever who used to take pride in his status in his worldly life:

﴿Taste, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ (Qur'an 44:49).

Is this statement an acknowledgment that the disbeliever is mighty and noble, or is it a sarcastic statement? It is sarcasm; for if the disbeliever were mighty and noble in his own estimation, he would not have disbelieved, nor would he have remained in Hellfire.

In the linguistic norm, it would have been expected to say: "When he saw the sun rising, he said, 'This is my lord'," because the sun is feminine; but he said ﴿This is my lord﴾ just as with the moon and the other stars, thus making the matter follow one context or one state. By this statement he intends to absolutely exempt the word "rabb" (lord) from being attached to a feminine marker, because the feminine marker is a branch of the masculine, and also because the sun is not truly feminine but is metaphorically feminine. For this reason, the scholars are attentive to this issue, and they say: when you give someone the attribute of knowledge and say, "So-and-so is 'ālim (knowing)," but when his knowledge becomes a settled faculty in him, we say, "So-and-so is 'alīm (all-knowing)." Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And above every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing﴾ (Qur'an 12:76).

And if a knowledgeable person has mastered his knowledge in an unprecedented way, we say of him: 'allām (exceedingly knowing). The Truth, glorified is He, describes Himself, saying:

﴿Knower of the unseen﴾ (Qur'an 5:116).

The scholars did not use the feminine marker in describing Allah, although this description is more eloquent, to avoid attaching the feminine marker to an attribute of Allah, glorified is He.

When the sun sets, Our master Abraham says:

﴿So when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate [with Allah]"﴾ (Qur'an 6:78).

The command came explicitly because he had preceded the matter with the dialectical arguments he had made; whenever any rational person hears them, he must declare his agreement with this matter, and therefore he said: "Indeed I am free from what you associate." And because, as a believing human being, he would not deceive himself, and consequently would not deceive his people, and this is what awakens the intellect when Allah grants it the gift of guidance.

Disavowal of association is the emptying (takhliyah) away from what corrupts, and emptying means that one disengages or ceases from the corrupting action, and after that one enters into the reforming action... the positive action.

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as one inclining away from all falsehood (ḥanīf), and I am not of those who associate partners with Allah.﴾ (6:79)

The heavens and the earth are the first manifestation of the universe into which man has entered, because man—the vicegerent on earth—came into the universe and found all its goods and subjugated things prepared for him. Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, makes clear: beware lest you say, "I have only been created," but rather, I created the universe for you.

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ (part of 40:57)

Our master Ibrahim presents his proof to his people: he worships Allah alone, who created the heavens and the earth, rejecting all corruption in the universe. This is embodied in his people by ﴿ḥanīf﴾. And "al-ḥanf" in the language is an inclination in the two feet, where we find the foot curved outward. This means that he does not walk on the path of corruption that exists in the universe, because the heaven intervenes with messages when corruption overspreads the earth, and when the Messenger comes inclining away from corruption, he walks upright, since inclining away from corruption is uprightness and straightness.

Then the Truth (Allah) says after that:

﴿And his people argued with him. He said: "Do you argue with me about Allah when He has guided me? I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills anything. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then take heed?" (80)﴾

"Wa-hājjahu" (and he argued with him): the word is "hājjahu," with the two jīms assimilated into one another. It means that each party puts forward a proof and the other party responds to it with a proof. When you are in a debate and each one presents his argument, this is called ḥijāj (argumentation), or mubṭil jadal (refuting disputation), meaning that you refute his speech and he refutes yours.

﴿And his people argued with him﴾ (part of verse 80, Surat al-An'am)

If Ibrahim had argued with them by engaging with their ideas and demonstrating their falsehood, then how do they argue with him? It is as if the aim of the argument was to turn Ibrahim away from his upright religion, which he had chosen, as expressed in His words, glorified is He:

﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah. (79)﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

And he responds to them: ﴿Do you argue with me about Allah when He has guided me?﴾ (part of verse 80, Surat al-An'am).

That is, the matter of faith has been settled. Ibrahim believed in Allah, and he declares to the people: (I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills anything), and this statement shows that they had threatened him, because the word "fear" was mentioned and he negated it from himself. Ibrahim declares it firmly: (I do not fear what you associate with Him), meaning I do not fear the stars that set, whether they are a star, a moon, or a sun, or those idols you worship, for they have no benefit or harm; harm and benefit are only the doing of Allah alone.

Therefore, precision in doctrinal expression is manifest, as the Truth says on the tongue of Ibrahim, peace be upon him:

﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills anything. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then take heed?﴾ (part of verse 80, Surat al-An'am).

If the Truth wills to send down upon a servant a star that strikes him or burns him, this is another matter, in which those who worship the stars have no part, and the stars have no part in it either, because the one who benefits and harms is Allah. When Allah wills harm, harm comes, and when He wills benefit, benefit comes.

﴿Unless my Lord wills anything﴾ (part of verse 80, Surat al-An'am)

That is, pay close attention and distinguish between an act that occurs from an agent, and an act that occurs from an instrument whose agent is other than that instrument. When Allah wills to make a star or a rock fall upon a person, the rock is not what made its falling happen, nor did the star drop itself; rather, the agent is Allah:

﴿My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not take heed?﴾ (part of verse 80, Surat al-An'am)

His words ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ indicate that matters of belief are received through innate nature (fitrah), and the soul's inclination toward desires is what obliterates the traces of this fitrah. What is required of you, O human, is not to originate a doctrinal idea, but only to remember, and remembrance is a natural, innate matter, because the human being, the vicegerent on earth, is the one who has descended from Adam until he reached us. Adam came to the earth with a heavenly method by which he organized the movement of life, and Adam taught the method to his children, and the children of Adam did likewise with their own children. But methods become obscured, because methods interfere with people's whims, restrain them from their desires, and turn them away from corruption, so they turn away from them or ignore them, and therefore they are liable to be forgotten. Messages are only recalled through the original method that we received from the Truth, glorified and exalted is He; for this reason Ibrahim declares it.

﴿And how should I fear what you have associated, while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority? So which of the two parties is more worthy of security, if you should know? (81)﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 81:

Our master Ibrahim says to them: "I do not fear except Allah, and I do not fear what you associate with Him, that which neither harms nor benefits." Here "how" (kayfa) comes for wonder, because the logical thing is that we fear Allah alone, the One who harms and benefits. When a debate takes place, the subjectivity of the debater awakens in every circumstance, and there are those who are too proud to accept the truth, not because it is not the truth, but because they fear being defeated before someone like themselves. Whoever wants to reach the truth without arrogance does not issue the judgment in a way that stirs up the subjectivity of the opposing debater. Therefore our master Ibrahim did not say: "Am I or are you more deserving of security?" Rather he said: ﴿Then which of the two parties is more deserving of security?﴾ (Q 6:81), just as our Lord taught His master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to say:

﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ (Q 34:24)

This is the peak of impartiality in debate, for he did not declare that their method is error and that his method is the upright correct path, out of confidence that when they review his method and their method, they will judge that he (ﷺ) is upon guidance and they are in error. This is progressive debate. Just as the Truth teaches His Messenger to say to his opponents:

﴿Say: "You will not be asked about what we committed of crime, and we will not be asked about what you do."﴾ (Q 34:25)

Does the Messenger commit crimes? Far be it from Allah that he should do so, for he is infallible.

It is as if the Messenger (ﷺ) is saying to them: "Ask about me if I have committed a crime." He did not say to them, describing their actions: "And we will not be asked about what you commit as crimes," but rather he said: "And we will not be asked about what you do." He did not bring up the matter of crime in relation to them; he brought it up in relation to himself, because he was certain that if they re-examined the matter intellectually, doctrinally and emotionally, they would end up believing in his method. This is the peak of gentleness in debate.

The gentleness in debate is manifest in His saying, the Truth:

﴿Then which of the two parties is more deserving of security, if you should know?﴾ (part of Q 6:81)

Knowledge is that you take a proposition you believe in, which has a reality, and which you can demonstrate. If a condition in it is lacking, then this is a departure from knowledge. An example of this is the words of language: every word is assigned to a meaning, and when you hear the word and you know the language, you understand the meaning. When I say "the sun," you picture the sun in your mind, and likewise the earth, the water and the mountain. You have known the reference of these words without there being any predication. We know that there is a difference between the meaning of a word in isolation and what the word gives and conveys when it comes in a predication.

When a word comes in a predication, there must be a proposition. If we say "the sun is hidden by clouds," this is a proposition; or if we say "the sun sets," this is another proposition, and here we have attributed something to something. But before we bring predicative propositions, the word must have a meaning in itself, and this is called the meanings of language. You join one word to another through it, so that a predication or proposition arises, on condition that we know the meanings of its individual terms. After that we know the predications, which is what you describe as subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar), topic and comment (mawdu' and mahmul), predicate and predicated subject (musnad and musnad ilayh), verb and agent, i.e. one matter attributed to another matter.

Knowledge, as we have said, is a real proposition that you believe and can demonstrate. If any part of this is lacking, it is not knowledge. If you believe in a proposition that is not real, this is falsehood. When I say: there are those who believe the earth is spherical, is the reality so or not? If you believe something and it is real, but you cannot demonstrate it, this is imitation (taqlid). If the matter is not certain and the two sides are equal regarding it, this is doubt (shakk). If one side is preponderant over the other, this is supposition (zann). The side that is outweighed is what is called delusion (wahm). All predicative propositions do not go beyond these.

Ibrahim's saying: "if you should know" means: if you are certain of a real predicative proposition, believed, which you are able to demonstrate.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 82:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Those who have believed and have not mixed their belief with wrongdoing – for them is security, and they are [rightly] guided.﴾ (82)

When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard this verse, they were fearful for themselves, because they reviewed the movement of their deeds and found that they were not free of wrongdoing (ظلم, ẓulm), and they feared that they would not be among those to whom "for them is security" applies. This troubled them, so they brought their matter to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he clarified to them, reassuring them: that wrongdoing is the one of which Allah said:

﴿Indeed, association [of others with Allah] is great injustice.﴾ (13) (Surah Luqman)

The verse, by its indications, shows that this wrongdoing is that which relates to belief (الإيمان, al-iman), not to action (العمل, al-'amal). This is because we know that a person's meeting with his Lord is first conditioned by the creed of the summit, which is that you testify that there is no god but Allah and that you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Its meaning: there is no one worshipped in truth except Allah; or, there is no command for anyone in the creation of Allah except that it is from Allah; and no action of anyone among the creatures of Allah except from Allah; and no one draws upon power, knowledge, wisdom, grasping and extending except from Allah. That is the circle of creedal belief.

The Truth says: ﴿and have not mixed their belief with wrongdoing﴾. So this matter is the domain of wrongdoing. As for action, He (subhanahu) has explained to us the distinction between a belief from which action gushes forth and an action from which energies burst forth, so He said:

﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds...﴾ (1-3) (Surah al-'Asr)

The conjunction in His saying ﴿except those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾ requires difference: belief is one thing and doing righteous deeds is another thing. So belief is a deed that springs forth in the heart, while action arises from the commitment that belief has legislated for it. The believer must note that Allah is one in His essence, one in His attributes, and one in His acts, having no equal and no partner with Him. If you find a quality like it in yourself, know that the quality of Allah is within the circle of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. So there is no power like His power, no essence like His essence, and no act like His act. If anything of that is disturbed in certainty, this is wrongdoing occurring within belief.

For example: you approach things with the energies created for you by the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala), and before you perform any act there must pass through your mind a mental relation, before it becomes a verbal or practical relation. This is the action entrusted to you and required of you. As for the action that does not pass through your mind, you are not responsible for it. An example of that: suppose you are walking along the road, then you find a pit into which you are about to fall; there is an instinctive matter for preserving the human being, so he moves his foot away, and in this matter he cannot make it pass through his mind. These are actions we call compulsory actions, or instinctive, or forced. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

("Every matter of importance that does not begin with 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate' is cut off.")(1) (noble hadith)

And he (ﷺ) said: ("Every matter of importance in which 'Praise be to Allah' is not [mentioned] is cut off.")(2) (noble hadith)

And "of importance" (ذي بال, dhu bal) means: every matter you do after it has passed through your mind that you will do, you must mention the name of Allah in it. Many people neglect this matter, so we say to them: logically, you must place this matter in your mind, because the act that does not pass through your mind is an act which Allah has given your instinct – without command – to do. An example of that: when a person eats and something other than air descends into his windpipe, you find him coughing without awareness until that thing comes out, because it is forced. As for the matter of importance, it is that whose mental relation passes through your mind, and then it passes into the act, whether it is a saying you say or an act you do; so it is required of you at the outset to name Allah, because the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) asks us not to let the means occupy us from the Causer of them.

For example, when you plough the land and till it, then you place the seed and cover it, then you water it, and after that the crop grows. Do you have any part in that? You have nothing but the gathering of an action; the seed is created by Allah, the soil in which the seed was placed is created by Allah, the elements present in the earth to nourish the plant are created by Allah, and the property in the seed by which it absorbs something that develops its root, then the grain splits – all these are means in which you have nothing at all. But Allah has honoured only your action, so He said:

﴿Have you seen what you plant?﴾ (63) (Surah al-Waqi'ah)

Then He said:

﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ (64) (Surah al-Waqi'ah)

Among the specifications of belief is that when you approach any matter of importance, you do not forget the One who subjected this to you. It is not within your power to do anything for yourself and by yourself except by the will of Allah, and if you do that and remember the One who subjected this to you, you have attributed the whole matter to Him (subhanahu).

In our man-made laws, when the judge sits to rule between people with a ruling, and there is an authority that enforces this ruling, he says: ("In the name of the people") or ("In the name of the law"). So the people or the law is what gave him the authority to issue this ruling. Therefore, what is the power that made things submit to you when you judge them? You must say then: "In the name of Allah who subjected this to me." If you approach an act other than that, you are an usurper, a fabricator, and a claimant to a matter you cannot achieve, because it is not in your authority or in your power to subject created beings to you.

Indeed the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) is the One who subjected created beings to you, so you must mention the name of the Truth so that those created beings submit to you; and whoever neglects that has mixed his belief with wrongdoing. When you see a fruit of yours, beware of saying as Qarun said: ("I was given it only on knowledge I have") (Quran 28:78); rather mention and say: ﴿What Allah willed﴾; for if you say "I was given it on knowledge," then the Truth said concerning Qarun:

﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ (part of verse 81 of Surah al-Qasas). Where did the knowledge of Qarun that he brought go?

So every matter must be attributed to Allah. If anything in you is disturbed in this matter, know that you have mixed your belief with wrongdoing. The Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) asks us for that so that the blessing will be blessed, whether in approaching it or benefiting from it. And nothing arises from the action you perform beginning with ﴿In the name of Allah﴾ except what helps you obey Him, helps you in righteousness, helps you in goodness, and you do not spend it except in well-being.

After that, the sum of these things in all your movements and actions qualifies you to receive another security, more comprehensive, complete and perfect than the security of this world: you receive the security of the Hereafter by entering Paradise.

So ﴿for them is security﴾ means those who have not mixed their belief with wrongdoing, and the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) wants us always to be connected to His method, because Allah's supplies are continuous, and His mercies and manifestations never cease from His creation; for He is al-Qayyum (the Self-Subsisting Sustainer), i.e., by the freedom of His power and the comprehensiveness of His sustaining, He (subhanahu) sustains all the causes of His creatures with capability and wisdom. So be always in the company of al-Qayyum, that He may manifest upon you with the attributes of His preservation, the attributes of His power, the attributes of His knowledge, and the attributes of His wisdom. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Bilal: ("O Bilal, tell me of the most hopeful deed you have done in Islam, for I heard the sound of your sandals before me in Paradise." He said: "I have done no deed more hopeful to me than that I never performed purification at any hour of night or day except that I prayed with that purification what was written for me to pray.")(4)

And he (ﷺ) said: ("When the Muslim servant or the believer performs ablution and washes his face, every sin that he looked at with his eyes goes out with the water or with the last drop of water; when he washes his hands, every sin that his hands seized goes out from his hands with the water or with the last drop of water; when he washes his feet, every sin his feet walked toward goes out with the water or with the last drop of water, until he comes out pure of sins.")(5)

So the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) wants us to be connected to His method by a close connection, so that He may give us, not take from us; for the difference between the servitude of humans to humans and pure servitude to Allah is that humans take the good of their servant, but our servitude to Allah gives us His good from treasuries that do not run out; we take from Him whenever we increase in servitude to Him. So the Truth always wants to join us to Himself.

﴿For them is security﴾: security in this world, and security combined with what was in this world along with security in the Hereafter.

Someone may say: there are people who do not name Allah's name, Allah does not occur to their minds, and they move through the energies and matter of the earth, enjoy them and are happy, and they may be made happy by the inventions of others. We say: yes, this is true; for there is a difference between the giving of the act and the blessing in the giving of the act. If a disbeliever plants, the earth yields to him, and whenever he does any work he takes its result, but he does not receive the blessing in the giving.

And what is the blessing in the giving? The blessing in the giving is that what you take from this giving does not help you in disobedience, but always helps you in obedience. We see many people to whom His saying applies: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾ (46:20). So beware of deluding yourself and saying: "They do not say ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾, yet they have taken the good things of worldly life." When you look at them you find all the peaks of their civilisation, and the ambitions of their research and discoveries, always tending toward evil; whenever an invention comes to them they use it for evil, until Allah permits and occupies them away from their things with what is poured upon them of punishment and calamities, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment for their association and disbelief.

So ﴿for them is security﴾ means: these who have not mixed their belief with shirk have security in the particulars of their actions, and the security gathered from the particulars of their actions gives them security in Paradise. ﴿And they are [rightly] guided﴾. Guidance is the path that leads to the goal. It is not said that you are stopped in your movement unless that movement has brought you to a goal drawn in your mind, such as success after study and striving. No created or manufactured thing determines its goal; so leave to Allah the determination of your task, for He is the One who created you. In human custom, no craft ever determines its task; rather, it is He who determines for it the goal of it; the goal exists first, before the craft. And since the goal exists before the craft, who then suffers through experiments?

In scientific, laboratory, material inventions that arise from interaction with matter, we find that the one who first suffers through experiment is the scientist, and you do not learn the experiment except after its medical results appear; and the theoretical problems that exhaust the scientist come from them because they are not first tied to fixed material things and to knowledge of the goal, nor to knowledge of the means to this goal. So who then is the guided one?

The guided one is he who knows the goal he strives for, and the means that qualify him for this goal. And if a defect occurs in the faculties of his soul, he seeks help in repairing the defect and turns to the One who made these faculties, Allah (subhanahu), just as a person returns a machine that breaks down to its maker. And we find many poets wandering in their imagination, one of them saying:

Will not someone show me my goal before my path?
And from where do goals come after the paths?

We say to him: the One who created you has clarified the goal for you.
