If the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, is the One who created the grain and created the stone in order to bring forth the living from the dead, and He is the One who brings forth the dead from the living, then He is more worthy that

The Lord says next:

﴿He it is who splits the daybreak, and has made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ (6:96)

He, glory be to Him, brings another of the miraculous signs, just as He brought the first sign in showing that it is He who created for us what sustains our lives.

﴿He it is who splits the daybreak, and has made the night for rest.﴾ The meaning of "fāliq" (splitting, cleaving) is that He made a thing into two parts, and these are two complementary blessings, neither of which can suffice without the other. For there must be daybreak, and there must be the night as rest, because daybreak is the time when things become clear to the sight of the eye. We know that darkness makes a person stumble among things: if you are stronger than these things, you smash them, and if they are stronger than you, they smash you. Walking in darkness, where there is no light to guide a person to his destination, may lead to the loss of things.

In the morning we work and strive upon the earth, and we fill the world with movement. When toil, fatigue and exhaustion from movement afflict us, the natural logic of a living creature is that it should rest, be still and settle, not only through its own motion ceasing but through the stillness of everything around it. For if you are at rest and light comes to you, it affects your constitution. This is why they now say that the "rays" by which they discover the secrets within the human body leave effects.

Thus the radiation emitted by the sun is withheld from you by God at night, so that the body may rest from every thing, from every movement arising within it and every movement coming upon it. In this way the blessing of the stillness and darkness of the night is like the blessing of the morning; each completes the other. This is why we have said that God, exalted be He, at the beginning of the surah placed the darknesses before the light:

﴿Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light.﴾ (part of 6:1)

Because you cannot benefit from your movement in the light unless you are energetic and refreshed during the night. If you do not rest, you will be exhausted and will not be able to work precisely in the activity of the day. Thus darkness is purposeful in existence. Therefore the advanced civilisation is the one that organises human life so that a person works by day and rests by night, so that he does not resume his work in the morning burdened. Whoever visits the countryside of Egypt these days will be startled to find that the villagers stay up all night with entertainment devices, and rise to work in the morning weary and exhausted.

We say: let us take civilisation from its summit, and not take civilisation from its base. When you go to Europe you find people sleeping and resting at night, and whoever walks in the street hears no sound and finds no one coming out of his house, nor do you hear the sound of the street loudspeakers, so that every person may obtain his share of calm. In our countries the matter is different: the streets are full of noise, the sick cannot rest, whoever studies does not find the necessary quiet, and whoever worships is driven out of the atmosphere of worship by the clamour; and we find someone describing this as a leap of civilisation!!

We say: let every blessing of God's blessings be taken in proportion to what it provides for you in beneficial existence, and when night comes upon you, you must put out the lamp so that you may sleep and your parts and your constitution are not thrown into disorder.

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He it is who splits the daybreak.﴾ And "fāliq", as we have said, means "cleaving", so does daybreak split? And by what? We say: "fāliq" is an active participle, just as we say "qātil al-ḍarbah" (the one whose blow kills), meaning that the blow from his hand is lethal.

And ﴿fāliq al-iṣbāḥ﴾ means that the morning splits away from the darkness, because the darkness is piled up, and when daybreak comes it is as if it cleaves and splits the darkness so that light may come forth. ﴿fāliq al-iṣbāḥ﴾ also means that the cleaving falls upon the daybreak, so that darkness comes after it. This is among the precision of the rhetorical expression of the Qur'an, because the One who speaks is God.

Imru' al-Qays said:

"Ah, O long night, will you not part,
with dawn? Yet the dawn is no better than you."

"Ṣubḥ" and "iṣbāḥ" have the same meaning.

Is "ṣubḥ" from the rising of the sun, or is "ṣubḥ" from the appearance of light before the sun rises? Daybreak (al-iṣbāḥ) comes first, as the calm light. We find eye doctors, after performing some operation on a person's eyes, unbinding the bandages that help the wound to heal, unbinding them gradually so that the light does not dazzle the sight at once. And among God's mercy is that He created the period of dawn with its gentle light before the sun rises with all its light at once. So it is as if the dawn came to cleave the darkness of the night with a gentle cleaving, and then the sun came and cleft the dawn.

Thus the daybreak is a cleaver once, because it split and cleft the darkness, and it is cleft once again, because the darkness came after it. So the active participle has discharged two tasks. The first task: "fāliq al-iṣbāḥ", that is, it entered with the light of the sun. And if we say its daybreak is a cleaver, that is, the first darkness of the night was split. So daybreak is a cleaver once, and cleft once again. And when He, glory be to Him, says ﴿He it is who splits the daybreak and has made the night for rest﴾, He wishes to give two parts, because He Himself is in His essence the splitter of the daybreak. He brings the noun to give it the quality of permanence, then He brings ﴿and has made the night for rest﴾, the quality of occurrence after the existence of the object. If He wishes the attribute necessary to it before the object exists, the noun comes; if He wishes the attribute after the object has come into existence, the verb comes.

This is why we find the Noble Qur'an depicting permanence in His saying, the Truth:

﴿And their dog stretched out its forelegs at the threshold.﴾ (part of 18:18)

The dog here is in this fixed image. And when the Qur'an wishes to bring a quality that changes, it brings the verb:

﴿Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ (part of 22:63)

The analogy would have been "fa-aṣbaḥat al-arḍu mukhḍarra," since He said "anzala" (He sent down), but He brings the renewal that occurs: ﴿fa-tuṣbiḥu al-arḍu mukhḍarra.﴾

The Truth continues: ﴿and the sun and the moon for reckoning (ḥusbān).﴾ We know the sun and the moon, and afterwards He brings the word "ḥusbānan," on the pattern "fa'lān," and this usually indicates intensification, just as you say: "So-and-so, God forbid, disbelieved intensely (kafara kufrānan)," and just as you supplicate: "May God forgive you abundantly (ghafara Allāhu laka ghufrānan)." So when you wish to intensify, you bring the form "fa'lān." The Qur'an uses the word ﴿ḥusbān⁠﴾ in two places concerning the sun and the moon: here, in the verse under our present reflection, ﴿and the sun and the moon for reckoning﴾, and in Surah al-Raḥmān the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿The sun and the moon are by a reckoning (bi-ḥusbān). (55:5)﴾

What is the difference between the two expressions? "Ḥusbān" here means that things are reckoned. We reckon the year by the sun's cycle of 365 days and a quarter of a day, as it passes through the zodiacal constellations during this period, and the moon begins its constellations each month in twenty-eight days and some of a day. We reckon the day by the sun, and we reckon the year by it, but we reckon the month by the moon, and you cannot reckon the month by the sun; rather you reckon the month by the moon, because it appears small, then grows and grows and grows. This is why Ramadan is established for us by the moon, not by the sun. And today we establish it by the sun.

Thus we have learned that the sun and the moon stand and operate in our reckoning of days and months, and both are "ḥusbān": the sun has a reckoning, and the moon has a reckoning. And if you look at the word "ḥusbān" you understand that the sun and the moon, both of them, are created so that something else may be reckoned by them, because they were created with reckoning, that is, the precise calculation is intended by them, because the sun is created with a calculation, and likewise the moon.

Come to the watch we use: does it not have a hand for the hours, another for the minutes, and a third for the seconds? This is the least we are able to achieve, though it is possible that we divide the second into parts, as we have learned in measurements: there is the metre, the centimetre, the millimetre, and then after that we spoke of the micrometre. So, the more we advance in scientific progress, the more precise the reckoning we make. And the sun and the moon would not have been a reckoning by which we reckon things unless they were created with reckoning.

When you look at your watch you perceive the leap of the second hand, but you do not perceive the movement of the minute hand, and likewise you do not perceive the movement of the hour hand, and each of the three hands turns by a spring and a particular gear. If the movement in a spring or a gear is disturbed, this defect is reflected on the other hands, and the second is reckoned against the minute, and the minute is reckoned against the hour.

Thus if the watch were not made with this precise reckoning, it would not work well. In this way we do not consider the watch a standard by which to reckon our times, except because in itself it was created with reckoning. And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The sun and the moon by a reckoning﴾, that is, that we may reckon by them because they are created with reckoning, that is, with precise calculation. And why did the Truth, glory be to Him, not say "ḥusbān" here and "bi-ḥusbān" in the verse of Surah al-Raḥmān? Because the matter requires intensification in precision: this is not merely "ḥisāb" (calculation), but "ḥusbān."

The Truth concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ The word "al-ʿazīz" (the All-Mighty) conveys dominance and subjugation, so that no one can rise above Him. These heavenly bodies that you see are stronger than you, and your hand cannot touch them, yet they perform their task for you without your coming near them. You do not approach the sun to adjust it, as you do with the watch invented by a man like you; and the sun has a power which God its Creator has granted it, and nothing in His making or His creation resists Him. This is the decree of the All-Mighty over it. And He, glory be to Him, gives us the grounds for confidence that its being a reckoning is for us to reckon by. He, may He be exalted, is its Creator by a decree of the All-Mighty who is not overcome, and He is the All-Mighty who knows with absolute knowledge that has no end and no limit.

Then Allah says:

﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.﴾

After He, glorified is He, explained that He created the sun and the moon with precise calculation, as a reckoning by His determination, and He is the Mighty, the All-Knowing, He – glorified is He – now describes for us the task of the stars, saying: ﴿that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea﴾. The stars are the shining bodies that we see in the sky, so that we may be guided by them in the darkness of land and sea. And from His mercy toward us and His knowledge is that some of His creatures will be compelled by the movement of life to travel the earth and to journey by night on land or sea, like those who keep watch and spread security in the world and cannot sleep at night. Rather, they must stay awake to guard us. All of this Allah willed with the determination of the Mighty, the Wise, the All-Knowing. For this reason He left us the stars, so that those who stay awake, or who travel the earth, or who sail the sea in their ships, may be guided by them, and they need a little light to guide them. This is why the Arabs used to be guided by the stars. One of them would say to another: "Put such-and-such star before your eyes and proceed above the tribe of so-and-so. And put such-and-such star on your left and walk and you will find such-and-such, or put such-and-such star behind you and walk and you will find such-and-such."

So if darkness were to cover everything, movement at night would be prevented, and that is a movement to which a living creature may be forced. Thus the Truth made the stars a guidance for those whom life compels to move at night.

Accordingly, the stars are not only for being guided by them in the darkness of land and sea, for if the purpose of them were only that we be guided by them in the darkness of land and sea, they would all be equal in size. We would see a large star and another small one, though the small star may appear larger than the large one but be farther from us. Therefore the wisdom of the stars is not confined to guidance in human movement by land and sea; this is not all the wisdom. This is the wisdom that the natural mind grasps first. Therefore the Truth, in the matter of the stars, brings another noble statement to make clear to us that the wisdom is not restricted to guidance by them at night, on land and sea, saying: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided.﴾ He – glorified is He – did not say "they are guided in the darkness of land and sea." So the stars have another task. He, may His power be exalted, says:

﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew.﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah 56:75–76)

And as science advances, the Truth shows us many things. Here is the comet about which they say much, and here are new stars being discovered, confirming the Truth's words:

﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are expanding it.﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat 51:47)

That is, He – glorified is He – has created a vast universe. And you, O human, have taken from it according to your perceptions and your range of natural sight, in which no instrument of vision is used, and you have taken from it by enhanced sight, in which you use the telescope and the microscope, and other things such as artificial satellites. Therefore the Truth – glorified is He – says: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars, and indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew.﴾ Some scholars say: every human being in existence has a star, and his life is linked to this star, and when the star sets, its counterpart on earth sets. There are shining stars whose flickering we perceive, and other stars that are not shining and are distant from us, and it is said that they belong to people whom no one knows, because of the small effect of their deeds on life. Science advances every day and links things to things for us, as if the Truth were clarifying: I created for you things, of which you, by your minds, can reach some of the wisdom in them; but do not say, "This is the ultimate of wisdom." Rather, behind it are higher wisdoms. He is the Wise, the Capable. You may grasp a small part of God's wisdom, but you must know that the perfection of God is infinite, and there remains in God's dominion what we cannot grasp of His wisdom until God brings to an end the earth and whoever is upon it.

The Truth – glorified is He – says in the concluding part of the verse: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who know.﴾ The word "ayah" (sign) means a wondrous thing, and it is applied to cosmic signs:

﴿And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon.﴾ (part of verse 37, Surah Fussilat 41)

And the word "ayah" is also applied to a section of the Qur'an that has an ending (fasilah). So there are Qur'anic signs and cosmic signs, and the cosmic signs serve as an explanation of the Qur'anic signs. The detailing of signs in the cosmos is what we see of their variety in forms, colors, wisdoms and purposes. And the detailing of signs in the Qur'an is what the Truth draws our attention to in His Qur'an, and to direct attention to the fact that this detailing in the signs of the cosmos, and that wondrous, wise creation, could only be from a capable, wise God who deserves to be the one unique God, and deserves to be the God who is worshipped.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 98:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿It is He who produced you from a single soul, and there is a place of lodging and a place of storing. We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.﴾

He, glorified be He, first spoke to us about the signs surrounding us, upon which the sustenance of our lives depends: the splitting of the grain and the date-stone. After that He spoke of the sun and the moon, then of the stars. All of these are signs around us. Then He speaks of something within our own selves, so that the proof may be stronger. He, glorified be He, brings you the proof from within your own being and your own soul, because this proof does not require you to stretch your eyes toward what is around you; rather, the proof is in your own self and soul. He, glorified be He, says:

﴿And in yourselves. Will you not see?﴾ (Surat adh-Dhariyat, 51:21).

That is, it is sufficient for you to make yourself a world. In this world there exists everything that establishes the power of the Truth and His right to be the one God and the one worshipped deity.

﴿It is He who produced you from a single soul﴾: this statement is consistent with being a report from God, and it is also an induction from existence, which we call "regression to the past" (al-tanazzul lil-madi). For if you look at the population of the world in this century, then look at the population of the world in the century that passed, you will find it is half this number; and if you look at it in the century before that, you will find it is a quarter of the present population. The further you go back into the past, moving away in time, the number decreases until it reaches "a single soul," and this is what God has mentioned to us. Someone might ask: how can it be a single soul when He says:

﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ (Surat adh-Dhariyat, 51:49).

We say: God, glorified and exalted be He, created the single soul, and He also made clear that from the single soul He created its mate, and then reproduction began. Therefore, the statistical induction into the past indicates the truth of the proposition. Likewise, everything that reproduces in existence, whether plant or animal, you find continuing to reproduce; and if you trace it back by counting into the past, you find the numbers decreasing and decreasing until they end at a origin from which reproduction came, which requires two:

﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs﴾ (from verse 36 of Surat Ya-Sin).

Why did the Truth here say "from a single soul" and not "two" (zawjayn)? The scholars explained that this is evidence of intense connectedness, because when we come from a single soul, every creature in it contains parts of the single soul. We said previously: if we took one cubic centimetre of a red-coloured substance, for example, and placed it in a flask, then shook the flask, we would find that the cubic centimetre of red substance has dissolved in the flask, and in every drop of the flask there is a portion of the coloured substance. Suppose we took the flask and placed it in a barrel, then shook the barrel well; we would likewise find that in every drop of the barrel there is a portion of the coloured substance. If we then took the barrels and threw them into the sea, the coloured substance would disperse so that in every drop of the sea there would be an infinitesimal particle of the coloured substance.

So, since Adam is the origin, and since we have arisen from Adam, and since the Truth took Eve from the living Adam so that she became living, her life is then connected to Adam and contains something of Adam. From Adam and Eve came children who contain a living part. In this way the Truth, glorified be He, returns us to a single origin, in order to stir and move within us the roots of mercy, affection and sympathy.

He, glorified be He, says: ﴿There is a place of lodging and a place of storing.﴾ The "place of lodging" (mustaqarr) has multiple meanings, which the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, explains to us in His Qur'an. In the story of the throne of Bilqis, we find Sayyidna Sulayman saying:

﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ (from verse 38 of Surat an-Naml).

An ifrit (demon) of the jinn answered Sayyidna Sulayman, and so did one who had knowledge of the Book. The Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿And when he saw it placed (mustaqarran) beside him﴾ (from verse 40 of Surat an-Naml).

Here "mustaqarr" therefore means "present," because the throne had not been in the assembly; rather it was brought to him. And in the matter of the vision that the Truth willed for Sayyidna Musa, peace be upon him:

﴿He said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look at You." He said: "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains (istaqarra) in its place, then you will see Me"﴾ (from verse 143 of Surat al-A'raf).

We know that the mountain had a state of stability (istiqrar) before the speech. So "istaqarra" comes to mean "was present," and comes at another time to mean "was firm."

And the Truth says:

﴿And for you on earth is a place of settlement (mustaqarr) and provision for a time﴾ (from verse 24 of Surat al-A'raf).

This is an announcement of the duration of our existence in this world. Likewise the Truth says:

﴿The companions of the Garden on that day are better in resting place (khayr mustaqarran)﴾ (from verse 24 of Surat al-Furqan).

So the Garden too is a "mustaqarr." Likewise the Fire is a "mustaqarr" for the disbelievers, and the Truth says of it:

﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement (mustaqarr) and station﴾ (Surat al-Furqan, 25:66).

So "mustaqarr" comes to mean "present," or "fixed," or an expression of the length and span of life in this world; the Garden is also a "mustaqarr," and so is the Fire. For this reason the scholars differed, and each of them looked at a different meaning. Some say: "mustaqarr" refers to the loins (al-aslab), where we were first placed, and then the Truth stored us in the wombs (al-arham). Others saw that "yastaqirr" is intended to mean remaining in this world, and then we are stored in the graves.

We say: stability (al-istiqrar) is based on "qarar," which is presence or firmness, and each thing according to its nature. There is a stability followed by a stability, followed by a stability, until the final stability is reached, which is what the believers hope for.

This is the stability after which there is no movement. As for the first stability in life, there may be a change from one state to another. We were settled in the loins; then afterwards the Truth stored us in the wombs. We were settled in this world, then we were stored in the graves, until we are settled in the Hereafter. Every scholar took one of these meanings. And the poet says:

Wealth and family are nothing but deposits,
and one day the deposits must be returned.

We notice that there is the word "mustaqarr" and the word "mustawda'," and "mustawda'" is something that another has caused to be deposited. But "mustaqarr" is evidence that the matter is not subject to human will; each one of us is "mustaqarr" in his own right.

The Truth says: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.﴾ "Detailing" (tafsil) means that He brought the signs sometimes in detail and sometimes in summary, because understandings differ, and the circumstances in which meanings are received differ. So the detailing of the signs is intended to meet every detail with a state of the human soul. For this reason the Truth left no room for anyone not to understand, and left no room for anyone not to learn. We notice that the concluding phrases of the two consecutive verses differ. There He says:

﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who know﴾ (from verse 97 of Surat al-An'am).

And here the Truth says:

﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾ (from verse 98 of Surat al-An'am).

"Fiqh" is to comprehend, that is, to have the faculty of understanding by which you grasp what is said to you as knowledge; understanding is the first stage and knowledge is the stage that follows.

The Truth intended by the first detailing, in His words "for a people who know," a call to contemplate signs external to the human being; here, in His words "for a people who understand," there is a drawing of attention to contemplation and reflection upon signs within the human being.

Allah says next:

﴿It is He who sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth with it the vegetation of every thing; then We bring forth from it green (stalks), from which We bring forth clustered grain; and from the palm-tree, from its spathe, clusters of dates hanging low, and gardens of grapes, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Look at their fruit when they bear fruit and (at) its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ (99)

The context required Him to say: "He sent down water from the sky, so (He) brought forth..."

Yet here He said: "So We brought forth" (fa-akhrajna), because everything in which there is no possibility of a partner with Allah is from His knowledge alone. Let no one say that he sent down the rain and brought forth the plants, because the earth is the earth of Allah, created by Him, and the seeds were created by Allah, and man thinks with a mind that Allah created and with energy that was created for him. When you attribute all needs to their first Maker, then He is the one who acts; yet He respects your effort, and He makes it clear to you: when He says "So We brought forth," (it means) "We and my means which I granted you": I created the means, and the means worked with you. So when you look to the Causer of causes, He is the Doer of everything. And if you look to the outward appearance of gathering and movement, the means which man has put to use are present; therefore He says: "So We brought forth."

Glorified and exalted is He, Who sometimes speaks in certain situations, affirming an action for man because he took up the means Allah granted him, but negating another action in which he has no part in any way whatsoever, such as His saying:

﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'a, 63–64)

Here He attributes the tilling to us, because we performed it, but by means from Him, glorified is He. He it is who sent down to us the iron from which we made the plough, and guided us to shaping it after He had made the fire for us, and the energy He gave us. As for growing, none of us has any part in it, and therefore He says:

﴿If We willed, We would make it into chaff, and you would be left wondering﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'a, 65)

Here—glorified is He—He used the lam in His saying "laja'alnahu" for emphasis, because man has a part in this matter: he tills and tends what he has sown with irrigation and toil until it grows and bears fruit. But a blight may strike it and destroy it. The means, though they have worked, do not guarantee the benefit of the crop, because the means do not rebel, do not refuse Allah, and do not oppose Him; they carry out what Allah wills of them, and He may nullify them. As for His saying:

﴿Have you considered the water which you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or are We the senders? If We willed, We would make it bitter﴾, He did not say "lajaʿalnahu" with the lam, because no one has any part in it, so He did not emphasise it with the lam.

And He says:

﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle? Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producers? We made it a reminder and a provision for the wayfarers﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'a, 71–73)

Every thing which the Truth mentions, He also mentions what annuls it, so that man will not be tempted by the existence of things, and he must receive things knowing that they may be destroyed. If man is the one who tills, the Truth, by the sweep of His power, has made the plant into chaff; and earlier He spoke of the foundations of life:

﴿Have you considered the semen which you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the creators?﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'a, 58–59)

Then He brought what annuls it, saying: ﴿We have decreed death among you﴾. As for the fire, He did not say that He will extinguish it, quench it or put it out; He—exalted is His majesty—left it to remind us of the fire of the Hereafter. ﴿We made it a reminder﴾, meaning: we must leave it before you so that the punishment of the Hereafter does not escape you. ﴿And a provision for the wayfarers﴾, meaning: and We leave it without annulling it, for another matter, which is the benefit in this world for those who alight in empty, barren places, or for those whose bellies, stomachs and provisions are empty of food, because the fire benefits them and helps them prepare their food to preserve their lives.

﴿So We brought forth with it the vegetation of every thing﴾ (from verse 99, Surat al-An'am).

"Thing" (shay') is that which is spoken of: a mote is a thing, an atom is a thing, and every need is called a thing. The meaning of "the vegetation of every thing" is that every need is exactly like vegetation. We see stones which the scholars call granite, and that marble, and that alabaster; and if you look at their origin you find them to be the lifespans of stones: one stone's lifespan lasted long and became coal, another's lasted long and became granite, and so on. Every need has a life, to establish for us the first matter, which is:

﴿Everything perishes except His Face﴾ (from verse 88, Surat al-Qasas).

Or "the vegetation of every thing" means that you see in them growth and life; the innate intellect takes it this way, but the comprehending intellect derives from it many matters, penetrates into the cosmos, and finds the sign swimming with it while it swims with the sign.

He continues: ﴿then We bring forth from it green (stalks), from which We bring forth clustered grain﴾. When you say the word (khuḍr, "green"), it may mean the colour known to us, which is green (akhḍar); but khuḍr contains a description slightly beyond akhḍar, because akhḍar informs only of a colour, and colour is related to the eye, whereas khuḍr gives the colour and also the tenderness (ghaḍāḍa), which we know by touch (al-jass). When you touch it you find softness.

So khuḍr contains many things: colour, related to the eye; and tenderness, known by touch, with a softness known by feeling. And this green may be so dark that its greenness is intense, even tending to blackness; therefore we hear someone say "sawād al-ʿIrāq" (the blackness of Iraq), meaning the fertile land in Iraq, which they call "the blackness of Iraq" because it is intensely green and so inclines to black. The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And beneath these two are two gardens, so which of the favours of your Lord will you deny? Dark green (mudhāmmatān)﴾ (Surat al-Rahman, 62–64).

And mudhāmmah means like the darkness of the night; as if, from the intensity of its greenness, it has become like the darkness of night. The Truth continues: ﴿green (stalks), from which We bring forth clustered grain (ḥabb mutarākiman)﴾. "Grain" (ḥabb) is that which has no stone, such as a grain of barley, a grain of wheat, a grain of lentil, a grain of beans. And "mutarākib" means grain that is tightly packed and mutually supporting.

﴿And from the palm-tree, from its spathe, clusters of dates hanging low﴾. The palm-tree has an elevated status among the Arabs, because it gives them lasting food, and so it reminds them of it: ﴿and from the palm-tree, from its spathe, clusters of dates hanging low﴾.

"Ṭalʿ" is the first thing that appears from the fruit of the palm, which we call in the countryside "the green cone." It is in the male palm, which is called "al-faḥl," and it is also found in the female; the first thing that appears of the palm's fruit is called ṭalʿ. Then the ṭalʿ splits and there emerges the qinw, or ʿidhq, or ʿarjūn, which is the part in which are the shamārīkh from which the dates hang.

So ṭalʿ is the first fruit of the palm before it splits and the qinwān emerge from it; and it is what we call in the countryside "al-sabāṭa."

﴿Clusters hanging low (qinwān dāniyah)﴾. The Truth describes them as "hanging low" because when you look at the palm's spathe as it first emerges, you find it splits and protects itself with the thorns of the frond so that insects do not eat it; then it grows heavy and bends, and nearly descends to the ground, so it is low and near. If there is a single spathe out of reach, whoever wishes to pick it must put his hand between the thorns to reach it. Glorified is He leaves for us some exceptions so that we recognise the blessing of Allah in making them hang down; for if they were all low, one might not pay attention to them. So He leaves one among the thorns so that man must exert himself to obtain it, so that you know that He has brought the rest near to you, and this is a blessing from Allah.

The ṭalʿ is sometimes applied to the sheaths (akmām), and the "kumm" is that in whose heart the fruits are; and sometimes it is applied to the fruit itself:

﴿And the palm-trees, tall, having ṭalʿ piled one upon another﴾ (Surat Qaf, 10).

You see the dates hanging from the shamārīkh, and each shammūkh has a number of dates; then you see the shammūkh attached to the mother (stem), and in that you see the greatness of the wondrous engineering in the arrangement of the fruits. Everything in this matter is calculated with wondrous engineering. When we consider what we have learned in our lives, when we design a water supply network and a sewage network: the water network that gives us the water we use, and the sewage network that takes away the surplus water and waste. When you look at this network or that, you find the engineering of each one precise, because any negligence in the design causes troubles. When you want to bring water to an alley, you use a pipe of such-and-such diameter in inches; in the alley there are branches, so for each branch you provide a pipe of smaller diameter than the first, then a smaller pipe for the houses, and a much smaller pipe for each flat. The engineers have made precise calculations for these matters.

If this is the engineering of men, what then of the engineering of the Creator? You find the ʿidhq, which bears the ripe dates, taken from the palm; each palm has such-and-such a sabāṭa, in each sabāṭa there are the shamārīkh, then there are the dates, and each date takes a hair for its nourishment. Thus we find everything calculated with extreme precision. It is a wondrous cosmic engineering made by the word of the Truth: "Be," and Allah has spoken truly:

﴿Who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided﴾ (Surat al-A'la, 2–3).

﴿And He it is who sends down water from the sky﴾. The words ﴿And He it is who sends down water from the sky﴾: we did not know what lies behind them; we knew only that the sky is everything above you that shades you, and the water comes from the clouds, and we all see the sky raining. We all know the innate expression that says: "The sky became overcast, then it rained," and there are those who say: "The earth laughs at the weeping of the sky, because it receives the water that irrigates the seeds within it." But what lies behind this process of sending down?

There is another process occurring in the cosmos without our awareness; we came to know of it only when science advanced and when we distilled water: we brought a stove and placed upon it a flask of water, and when it reached boiling point, vapour emerged, and the vapour travelled through the pipes, and the pipes passed through cool environments, so the water condensed and came down as distilled water. The same happens in rain. Consider how much a single cup of distilled water bought from the pharmacy costs us, and compare it with the sky that sends down water pouring forth, and we do not know how it was made. That is why the Truth says:

﴿Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or are We the senders?﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'a, 69).

Thus water descends from the sky, and we did not know how that happens. And here Allah says:

﴿And from the palm-tree, from its spathe, clusters of dates hanging low, and gardens of grapes, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar﴾ (from verse 99, Surat al-An'am).

When He says "similar and dissimilar" (mutashābihan wa-ghayra mutashābih), we affirm it. Take the example of the peach: there is a kind we call "the royal peach"; when you hold the single fruit it splits to reveal the seed clean, and another fruit we split ourselves and find the seed has some flesh of the fruit on it and also some fibres. This one has a colour, and the other has a colour; this one has a taste, and that one has a different taste.

﴿Watered with one water, yet We make some of them excel others in food﴾ (from verse 4, Surat al-Ra'd).

This is so that man knows that the perfect power accomplishes what the Creator wills; and afterwards you turn and find the virtues: this is an orange with a navel, and this is a local orange, and a blood orange, and then the tangerine. Therefore we will find in Paradise what He tells us of, when He says:

﴿Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom, they say: "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in similitude﴾ (from verse 25, Surat al-Baqara).

When an inhabitant of Paradise eats of it, he discovers that the fruit of Paradise has a different taste. And of the perfection of power: after the analyses carried out by the laboratory scientists—may Allah reward them on our behalf with good—of the grape, they found that the skin enveloping it has the nature of "cold" and "dry," the flesh of the grape has a different nature ("hot and moist"), and then the seed is "cold and dry." These are three natures in the one grape, and this is a wondrously constituted thing. Likewise the citron (utrujja), a fruit like the bitter orange: its peel is "hot and dry," the flesh in it is "cold and moist," the liquid in the flesh is "cold and dry," and the seed is "hot and dry": four natures in one thing. How? And by what power?

The scientists have toiled until they understood its composition, to make the matter clear to us; and you turn and find a fruit that you eat, its exterior and its interior

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 100:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And they attributed to God partners, the jinn, though He created them; and they fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.﴾

The root of the word jinn is (jīm) and (nūn), and all of its derivatives indicate concealment, covering and wrapping. From it comes junūn (madness), because the intellect is veiled in that state. We do not see the jinn, for they are hidden, and so are the angels. The whole root (jīm) (nūn) indicates wrapping and covering.

﴿And they attributed to God partners, the jinn﴾. The jinn (al-jinn) is that which is hidden of everything. The jinn, as you know, are a creation of God's creation. God, glory be to Him, created humankind and created the jinn. He created the jinn hidden, so that we would not believe that God's creation of a living being must take this material mold. Rather, He, glory be to Him, creates what He wills as He wills. Thus He creates things that are hidden and not seen, which have life, which have offspring, and He creates things that are hidden and have no offspring. All of this is by the unrestricted power of the Truth, glory be to Him, to bring this matter close to us, because our minds may stop short at some things that are not perceived and not seen, since we do not know the existence of a thing unless we sense it.

The Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies this. Beware lest you think that you can perceive everything God has created, for your senses are not the only means of perception, because your senses have laws that govern them. You see, but you see by a law, so that if the visible object recedes from you beyond the extent of your sight, you do not see it. Likewise your ear hears, but if the sound or its source is so far from you that the vibration does not reach you, you do not hear. Likewise your mind: it may understand some things and not understand others. Then He has struck for us, within our material existence, examples that bring close to us that hidden creation of the jinn and the angels.

We have found that the human intellect, which God guided — "who measured and then guided" — has been guided to discover something called the (microbe) (mīkrūb). The microbe is a living organism so minute that the naked eye does not perceive it, yet it was existing, and it did its deeds among people and entered their bodies without them feeling how it entered, and it worked in them and in their health, causing destruction and death, such as the diseases of plague and cholera and others. Nevertheless, the microbe existed, and it is of the same kind as our existence: that is, it is matter, it has life, it has action, and it has influence over the structure that perceives it, which is the human being.

Thus we have seen that something hidden, not perceived, threatens a huge being that is perceived. Does the discovery of the microbe mean that we created it? No. The existence of the microbe is one thing, and the perception of its existence is another. When we analyze the (microbe), we find that it is matter, but it is so minute that the bare eye does not see it. When the microscope was invented and we magnified it, we came to know it. And this living organism, if you do not see it, your not seeing it previously does not mean that it did not exist; rather it existed but you did not perceive it. Then you, O human, discovered an instrument that enabled you to perceive it. Let us know that the existence of a thing does not necessarily mean that you must perceive it. So if God says to you: "I have angels among My creation, and I have jinn among My creation, but you do not see them while they see you," we say: "You have spoken truly, O my Lord," because a thing of the kind of our matter was existing and we did not see it, and then afterward we saw it.

Therefore, the things we are now discovering are evidence for the truthfulness of the Qur'anic message in what it reports of unseen matters. The jinn are hidden, and all of the root, as we have explained, indicates concealment: junūn is the absence of intellect; janna (night) means it covered and concealed; and al-jannah (the garden) is so called because it has trees and other things, such that the one who walks in it is not visible, so it conceals whoever enters it.

Thus the whole root indicates concealment. And is what we marvel at that they made the jinn partners, or is the marvel not in making the jinn partners but in adopting the principle of partners, whether they were jinn or other than jinn? The marvel here is from the principle itself. We do not object only to the jinn being partners; we object to the principle itself, that God should have a partner, whether from the jinn or from the angels or from something else. For this reason the made (the partner) is mentioned before that from which it was made (the jinn), although the usual order is to mention the thing from which something is made first, as you say "I made the clay into a pitcher," meaning the clay existed and you took from it what did not exist, which is the pitcher.

Then, did the partners exist and the jinn occur to them, or did the jinn exist and the partners occur to them? In that case it would have been necessary to say: "They made the jinn partners to God." Therefore the marvel lies not in the jinn being partners; the marvel lies in the principle itself, and how the idea of partners came to their minds, whether the partners were from the jinn or from something else. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And they attributed to God partners﴾. When you hear it, say: "I seek refuge in God" — "they attributed partners to God!" And do not concern yourself with who the partners are, because the mere coming of a partner to God is the marvelous matter, whether he is from the jinn or from the angels. And how did they make the jinn partners? Did not the Truth say in His Book that Abraham said:

﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful﴾ (Surah Maryam).

And what is worship? Worship is that the worshipper obeys the one worshipped in what he commands him. As long as they obey the devils in their whisperings, it is as if they worshipped them. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the day He will gather them all and say to the angels, "Did these used to worship you?"﴾ (verse 40, Surah Saba).

The angels said: ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ (Surah Saba).

And how did they worship the jinn? They obeyed them in what they commanded them and forbade them from; for worship is obedience. And you, O worshipper, do not propose the worship; rather you look at what is asked of you to draw near to the one worshipped. Thus "do" and "do not" is the principle.

﴿And they attributed to God partners, the jinn﴾. And why did they bring partners to God? Why did they not worship them alone and exclude God from worship? Because the existence of a partner is evidence of acknowledging God as well. So why did they make partners for Him? Why did they not deny, reject and disbelieve in God and the matter would end? No. They did not do that, because they saw that the partners had no worship requirements, and when they worshipped them, for example, they were not told "do" and "do not," and there was no method to follow. But events beyond their causes, which they could not repel, might happen; to whom then do they cry out? To the gods they believe to be false, vain, and unable to benefit or harm? Therefore they kept their acknowledgment of God so that they might turn to Him in what they cannot repel, neither they nor those they took as partners. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us to remove a harm that touched him﴾ (part of verse 12, Surah Yunus).

It is as if he wants to worship God only for benefit.

﴿And they attributed to God partners, the jinn﴾. And it is strange, then, that they made partners for God, although God is the One who created the worshipper and the worshipped. The marvel concerns two matters: that they make partners for God from the jinn or from the angels; and the other marvel is that He "created them, and they fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge." And what is the meaning of "fabricated for Him"? It means they invented, because al-kharq (fabrication) is the creation of a gap in a thing that is sound according to the law of soundness. For this reason He said about the ship: ﴿I wanted to damage it, that its people might be drowned﴾ (part of verse 71, Surah al-Kahf).

"And they fabricated for Him": that is, they made a breach in a sound thing, which nature refuses to be.

﴿And He created them, and they fabricated for Him sons and daughters﴾ (part of verse 100, Surah al-An'am).

As for the category that claimed God has sons, they are the People of the Book; they said that:

﴿The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of God," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God"﴾ (part of verse 30, Surah al-Tawbah).

As for those who attributed daughters to God, they are some of the Arabs who believed the angels to be God's daughters:

﴿Has your Lord then preferred you with sons and taken for Himself daughters from the angels?﴾ (part of verse 40, Surah al-Isra').

And He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ (Surah al-Saffat).

And the One who said:

﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ (Surah al-Najm).

And among the Arabs there were those who established a kinship between God and the jinn, in confirmation of the Truth's saying:

﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾ (part of verse 158, Surah al-Saffat).

They slandered the Truth and claimed that a union took place between God and the jinn, so that the angels were born.

﴿And they attributed to God partners, the jinn, though He created them; and they fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

And why does the Truth say "without knowledge"? Because knowledge leads to the opposite. Knowledge is an inductive matter, a believed reality for which evidence is established, and this is something that has no reality and for which no evidence can exist. So it is a saying without knowledge; rather it is ignorance. It is thus ignorance to believe a need and that it is an actual event when it is not an actual event, and no evidence is established for it because it does not exist. Had the evidence been upright in their innate nature, receptive to the proofs of clear explanation and the proofs of the cosmos, they would have disavowed what they believed, and would have refused to take partners for God.

The Truth has presented a matter that occurred to confused thoughts, and they said "partners," so He said "glory be to Him," that is, exalting Him above partnership in His essence, in His attributes, and in His acts, because His essence is not like every essence, His acts are not like every act, and His attributes are not like every attribute. For this reason "glory be to Him" comes in every matter that contradicts the existing laws of the cosmos. Take every matter that relates to the true God within the frame of "glory be to Him." Therefore, when the Night Journey carried the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis and then he was ascended in a single night, and that was a marvelous matter, the Truth commanded us to accept it within the frame of His saying:

﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ (verse 1, Surah al-Isra').

Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, did not say: "I traveled from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis"; rather he said: "I was taken by night" (usriya bi). And since he was taken by night, the law of the Night Journey is the law of the Truth, glory be to Him. So take it within the frame of "glory be to Him," who said:

﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, from what the earth grows and from themselves, and from what they do not know﴾ (part of verse 36, Surah Ya-Sin). Then He comes with what is broader than perception and says: ﴿and from what they do not know﴾ (part of verse 36, Surah Ya-Sin).

As if we will later know things in which there is duality. Scientific discovery in the twentieth century has removed some of that, so we came to know the positive and negative in electricity and electrons. His saying "and from what they do not know" opens the field for the cosmic matters that occur through the activities of discovering minds.

﴿And they attributed to God partners, the jinn, though He created them; and they fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

So "glory be to Him" is for exalting Him and sanctifying Him from being measured against the existing creature. May His name be exalted, and His attributes and acts be exalted above what they describe, with descriptions unbefitting His essence.

Then the Truth says:

﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a child when He has no consort? He created everything, and He is Knowing of all things.﴾ (6:101)

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says in another verse:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind.﴾ (part of verse 57, Surah Ghafir, 40)

If you see within yourself many wonders, and every day anatomy or physiology gives you a new secret, do not be amazed at this matter. For the heavens and the earth are an origination from non-existence. Here He says: ﴿Badi'﴾ (Originator), meaning that He, glory be to Him, created them without any previous pattern. Some people make things according to past experiences or models, but the Truth, glory be to Him, is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. We have come to know through science that the earth we live on is a planet, one of the satellites of the sun. In former times they used to say that the satellites of the sun were seven, and therefore many scholars and thinkers were deceived and said that the seven satellites are the heavens. So the Truth wanted to nullify this notion after they had said "seven": scientists discovered an eighth satellite of the sun, then they discovered a ninth, then the satellites became ten, then the matter increased to satellites we do not know. And where is this solar system in relation to the heavens? All of it is merely an adornment of the lowest heaven. When the microscope and instruments that bring distant things near were invented, we saw the "Milky Way" (also called "Sikkat al-Tabbana", the Path of Straw) and found that it is a galaxy containing countless solar systems. We found a million systems like our solar system. This is one galaxy, and we have millions of galaxies. An astronomer says: if we possess new instruments, we will discover new galaxies.

Let us listen to the word of God:

﴿And the heaven We built with power, and indeed We are expanding it.﴾ (51:47, Surah al-Dhariyat)

Thus we must place the creation of the heavens and the earth at a higher rank of importance than the matter of the creation of mankind.

﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a child when He has no consort? He created everything, and He is Knowing of all things.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

Since He, glory be to Him, is the Originator of the heavens and the earth, and by His supreme essential power He created the heavens and the earth, which are greater than the creation of mankind, then if He wanted a child, that child would have to come into being by birth, and it could not be called a child unless it were born; and He is exalted above that. Furthermore, why would He want a child? The attributes of perfection would not increase by having a child, and the cosmos was not deficient before some claimed that the Truth, glory be to Him, has a child. The cosmos is created by the very essence of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, whereas people need children for the continuation of remembrance, and He, glory be to Him, does not die, confirming His word:

﴿Everything perishes except His Face.﴾ (part of verse 88, Surah al-Qasas, 28)

Human beings need to have offspring so that their children may assist them, whereas He, glory be to Him, is the Mighty who created and is Living and does not die. Therefore there is no sense in attributing this to Him, and this matter should not even be debated rationally; but God, in His kindness to His creation, has clarified and explained such matters.

He, majestic and exalted, says: ﴿Nor had He a consort.﴾ What does the Truth want with a consort? He wants nothing. Why this obstinacy about divinity? Neither a child nor a consort adds to Him any power to create, any wisdom to arrange, any knowledge to govern, or anything else. Merely this kind of imagining is futile. If partners are impossible, and the purpose of partners is to help Him in dominion, then there would be one god who takes the dominion of the heavens and another god who takes the dominion of the earth, and a god of darkness and a god of light, just as the ancient Greeks set up a god of evil and a god of good, and so on. The Truth is One, the Unique, who has no partners to help Him, so what is the point of a child or a consort?

I seek refuge in God! Will these people not refrain and desist from such a statement? ﴿And He is Knowing of all things.﴾ He is the Creator of the cosmos and the Knower of everything in it, and He needs no assistance from anyone.

He says, glory be to Him, after that:

﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god but He, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is over all things Disposer of affairs.(102)﴾

Note the precedence of the word "Lord" (rabb) before "there is no god but He." The word "Lord" here is the basis (haythiyya) for "there is no god but He." This is because "ilah" means "one worshipped" (ma'bud), and "one worshipped" means "one obeyed" (muta'), and "one obeyed" means one who has commands and prohibitions. And for what reason? The reason is that He is the Lord who undertakes creation and nurturing. It is obligatory and rational that we listen to His speech, because He is the Lord, the Creator, and the One who provides sustenance. The evidence is that when we ask the people of disbelief, in the heedlessness of their desires, "Who created the heavens and the earth?", their innate nature speaks and they say:

"Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth." But if the question is posed within a prior debate, you will find cunning and lying.

And when you want to extract from them a matter of truth, and to establish and nullify a matter of falsehood, take them by surprise and without preparation, and they will say that the One who created is Allah.

We have seen the machines they designed to detect lying, and to observe the mental process that strains the liar. As for the person of truth, he does not strain, because the person of truth reads off a reality that speaks for itself and does not suffer exertion. But the one who lies strains himself, wavers between matters, becomes agitated, does not know which to take, and gives contradictory answers on one and the same thing.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god but He, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is over all things Disposer of affairs.(102)﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

Since He is the Creator of all things and He is the Everlasting, He is most worthy of worship, because worship—as we have said—means obedience to command and obedience to prohibition. Since glory be to Him is the One who created, He is the One who sets the law of preservation for man and the universe. If you oppose the method, the universe and man are corrupted; and when the universe or man becomes corrupt, you turn to the method of the Creator to restore each of them to its soundness. Therefore He is the most deserving of worship. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god but He.﴾

This is a testimony which He bore to His own Essence before He created anything, and before He created the angels, and His angels bore witness to it, and those possessing knowledge bore witness to it.

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice.﴾ (part of verse 18, Surat Al 'Imran).

So Allah testified to His divinity from the beginning. Among His names is "Mu'min" (the Giver of Security), and we are believers in Allah; our Lord is the Mu'min in that He is one God. This faith of His is that He is one God, who addresses everything He wills, knowing that nothing can oppose Him. He addresses it saying: "Be, and it is." And because He is one God, He knows that no one or nothing has opposed Him; therefore He exercises His dominion, knowing that others are subject to His command and cannot fall short of His intentions. Or we may say: "Mu'min" (He who grants security) regarding what He created and to whom He created, that is, He grants them safety and security. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Who fed them against hunger and made them secure against fear.(4)﴾ (Surat Quraysh).

The Truth, glory be to Him, has made clear to us: You are My creation; if you take My method, I will feed you against hunger and secure you against fear. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god but He, the Creator of all things.﴾

Therefore logic compels us to worship Him, glory be to Him, and the matter that harmonizes with the premise is that there is no lord and no god but He; He is the Creator of all things. Therefore worship of Him is a necessity, and this is realized by obeying Him in what He commands and what He forbids.

﴿And He is over all things Disposer of affairs.﴾ (part of verse 102, Surat al-An'am).

This is the precision of expression in the Qur'an. In our customs we say, "So-and-so is the wakil (agent) of so-and-so," meaning he acts for his benefit in matters he wants. Glory be to Him is not a wakil for you; rather He is a wakil over you, because the agent for you carries out your orders. But He is a wakil over you, like the guardian over a minor: he is wakil over him, and says to the minor, "Do such-and-such," and he does it. Glory be to Him is wakil over us, and therefore we ask Him, and He is the One who responds to our supplication for good. So-and-so carries out our frivolous desires. And we find the fool who says, "I have prayed to Allah and He did not answer me." We say: you understand answering to mean that it fulfils your request, but glory be to Him knows what suits you, since He is wakil over you and corrects your conduct. When you ask for a need, if it contains good He gives it to you, and if you think it is good but it will bring evil, He does not give it to you.

And the one who supplicates should not hasten the answer. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: "Your supplication is answered so long as one of you does not become hasty, saying: I have prayed, but it has not been answered for me."(1)

﴿And He is over all things Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning whether that thing is chosen or not chosen; for the one who chooses may choose evil, and Allah, being wakil over him, says to him, "No." As for the non-accountable one with no choice, it is subjugated to the will of Allah, like fire: it is commanded to burn, but He commanded it not to burn our master Ibrahim and to keep him intact.

The next verse comes to affirm the reasons for His greatness, glory be to Him, saying:

﴿No vision perceives Him, but He perceives vision, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.(103)﴾

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from Abu Hurayra.

Why is He not perceived by sight? Because sight is an instrument of perception with its own law: a ray is reflected from the seen object and defines it. If sights perceived Him, they would define Him, and whoever saw Him would be able to encompass Him, and He would become something within the grasp of your sight. The one who is able (over something) never becomes something subject to that power, ever. So from His greatness is that He is not perceived. You may see the sun, but do you claim that you have perceived it? No, because perception (idrak) means encompassing, and when it is said "adrakahu" it means he did not escape from him. That is why, when the people of Pharaoh pursued and Moses and his people saw them, the companions of Moses said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken (mudrakun)﴾.

That is, there is no use; the sea is before us, if we advance we drown, and if we retreat they destroy and kill us. So "mudrak" means encompassed by it. If sights were to encompass God, sight would become the one able, and God would become the one subject to it. The One who is able by His essence, as we have said, never becomes something subject to His creation, ever.

﴿No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ (Surah al-An'am 6:103).

Everything other than God needs God for the continuation of its existence, and His existence is not with anyone; therefore ﴿No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision﴾, because if He has power over all sights, He is able by His essence, and the rest are subject to Him, since they are His creatures; and as long as they are His creatures they are subject to His power, and nothing new has befallen the creatures that would make them able by their own essences. ﴿No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision﴾.

The scholars have paused at length and differed: does a human being see his Lord or not, in this world or in the Hereafter? Some of them said: no one sees God, by the text of the verse ﴿No vision comprehends Him﴾. We say: but there are verses in the Qur'an that say:

﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah 56:22-23).

And "nazirah" (looking) includes seeing and conveys it. Also, God punishes those who disbelieve in Him by veiling Him from them, for He said:

﴿No! Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ (Surah al-Mutaffifin 83:15).

So the disbelievers are veiled from seeing God as a punishment for them. If we were to share with them and be veiled as they were veiled, what would be our distinction as believers? So the scholars did not notice that there is a difference between the Qur'anic expression and what they say. When one of them argues that seeing God is not possible because our Lord, glory be to Him, said to Moses:

﴿You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me﴾ (part of verse 143, Surah al-A'raf).

Why does this scholar not heed the saying of the Truth:

﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Moses fell down unconscious﴾ (part of verse 143, Surah al-A'raf).

So God manifests Himself to some of His creatures, but that the creation sees Him in this world, no; because our constitution is not qualified to see the Truth, as evidenced by the fact that the firmest and strongest of us, the mountain, when His Lord manifested Himself to it, crumbled. When the mountain crumbled, Moses fell down unconscious. If Moses fell unconscious at the manifestation upon the mountain, how would it be if he saw Him? So He is not prepared for it.

The scholars differed over this verse, and their disagreement reached its furthest extent: some permit seeing, and some deny it. I hold that their disagreement is not about a point of dispute, because they spoke about seeing, whereas the discussion here is about the negation of perception (idrak), and perception is encompassing, while seeing may occur without encompassing; encompassing is not possible. Even on the assumption that seeing and perceiving are identical in concept, we say: why is the disagreement about the Hereafter? If the disagreement were about seeing in this world, that would be a fine discussion, but you have made the disagreement concern the Hereafter.

The verses of the Qur'an are explicit that seeing the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, is one of God's blessings upon the believers, and an addition of goodness (husna) to them, and His being veiled from the disbelievers is a form of punishment for them. We also say: why do you not say that perception will exist in the Hereafter in a mode not present in our world? Because in this world we are prepared by causes, whereas in the Hereafter we will be prepared without causes.

Here, if you wish to drink, you ask for water or go to the water and drink; and when you want to eat a certain thing, you tell the household: prepare such-and-such for me, or you buy what you want. But there in the Hereafter, as soon as what you desire occurs to your mind, you find it before you. This is a new law unconnected to the law of this world. So why should there not also be in our constitution in the Hereafter a law by which we can see God, within a framework of "there is nothing like unto Him"?

In the Hereafter there are matters on which all agree that they contradict the laws of this world and the order of the world we now live in: in eating and drinking and the elimination of waste. But in the Hereafter we will eat and drink, yet there will be no waste, because you now cook and digest, and in digestion you take some food and what remains is waste that must be expelled. But cooking and digestion in the Hereafter are by ﴿Be!﴾ (kun), and there is no waste; it is food by the power of the Able. In Paradise you will obtain whatever you desire without it running out; in this world whatever is taken from something diminishes, but in the Hereafter nothing diminishes, because it has a supply from the quality of self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah).

After the two matters, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, follows with ﴿No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision﴾ and says ﴿and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾. "Subtle" (latif) corresponds to ﴿No vision comprehends Him﴾, and "All-Aware" (khabir) corresponds to ﴿but He comprehends vision﴾. "Subtle" has a particular meaning: a subtle thing is used of what is finely constructed, and to God belongs the highest likeness. The microbe was not known to us until recently, because it reached such subtlety and fineness that the eye cannot perceive it. But when we invented the microscope we saw it, and if it were finer than that we would not see it; we have discovered the virus and try to learn more of its properties. So the more a thing is fine, the more subtle it is and cannot be seen by us. A thing, when subtle, becomes noble and exalted. And to God belongs the highest likeness: so-and-so is of subtle manners (latif al-mu'ashar). God is Subtle in His essence and shows subtlety to His servants.

When you hear "latif" (the subtle one), it is an active participle, like "akil" (eater); when we say "Latif" it is an intensive form (mubalagha) of subtlety, because He is gentle toward every human being and every creature, and this requires intensification. Likewise we say "Rahim" (Merciful), an intensive form, because He lavishes His mercy upon His servants. The first manifestation of subtlety is the management of their fine affairs in a way that secures their interests in their existence. When we arrange a cup of water for each person we manage a great deal; how much more the management of the Subtle toward His servants?

He created the earth with three-quarters water and a quarter dry land, because He, may He be exalted, wants to widen the expanse of water; as the waters widen, evaporation becomes easier and greater. But if the waters were deep and their surface small, evaporation would occur only at the surface, and then the clouds would not bring enough water for creation. God widened the expanse of water so that the water evaporates, then gathers as clouds in the sky, and meets a cold region, so that He sends down sweet water for us to drink, for our livestock to drink, and to irrigate crops; all of that is from the subtlety of management.

Among the manifestations of subtlety in the Truth are matters that cannot be described, and so each of the scholars was moved by one aspect of God's subtlety toward His creatures. One said: it is "the abundance of blessings" (subugh al-ni'am). A second said: "the fineness of arrangement" (diqqat al-tadbir). A third said: among the manifestations of the Truth's subtlety is that He makes His blessings to His creatures seem few, for the blessings He has given His creatures are few, because His treasuries, glory be to Him, are full and His gifts do not run out or suffer diminution. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿If you are thankful, I will surely increase you﴾ (part of verse 7, Surah Ibrahim).

That is, His many blessings upon His servants are few, and in return He magnifies the little obedience of His creatures, that is, He regards it, out of His bounty, as much; for He is the One who repays a good deed tenfold.

So the manifestations of subtlety are without limit, and according to the fineness of the subtlety is the fineness of its arrival and its reckoning. He is the Subtle: when you call upon Him He answers; when you seek Him He shelters you; when you love Him He brings you near; when you obey Him He rewards you; when you give to Him and lend to Him from His bounty and the wealth He has granted you, He grants you well-being; and when you turn away from Him He calls you. He said: "O son of Adam, if you remember Me within yourself, I remember you within Myself; if you remember Me in an assembly, I remember you in an assembly better than them; if you draw near to Me a span, I draw near to you a cubit; if you draw near to Me a cubit, I draw near to you a fathom; and if you come to Me walking, I come to you running" (1). All these are manifestations of subtlety. He is the One who calls: "Turn in repentance to God" (2). And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than any one of you who, having lost his mount with its provisions in a barren wilderness, then finds it" (3). And when you draw near to God, He guides you.

Another scholar, moved by the attributes of subtlety, says: He who repays you if you fulfil, and pardons you if you fall short. Another adds to the meanings of subtlety, saying: whoever takes pride in Him, He honours; whoever is in need of Him, He enriches. Another, moved by a different aspect of the manifestations of subtlety, says: His giving is good, and His withholding is a store... That is, if He withholds something from His servant, He stores it for him in the Hereafter. All these are manifestations of subtlety, and this fits His words, the Truth: ﴿No vision comprehends Him﴾. His subtlety penetrates what we cannot perceive; and when you analyse any matter you may not reach an understanding of the blessing, and if you do reach it, you cannot render the praise due for that blessing.

His words, the Truth, ﴿but He comprehends vision﴾ fit the word "All-Aware" (khabir). In our life we hear the word "khabir": when we face any problem we find someone saying: we want to hear the opinion of the expert (khabir) on it; and in a judicial matter the judge summons an expert (khabir) to write a report on a matter that requires one specialised and knowledgeable in it. So the khabir in a field is one who knows the details of the matter. How much more so the Supreme Expert, to whom nothing in His dominion is inaccessible, and who comprehends vision. So His words ﴿No vision comprehends Him﴾ fit His words "Subtle," just as ﴿but He comprehends vision﴾ fits "All-Aware." This is what they call in the language "laff wa nashr" (folding and unfolding): he mentions two or three things and then mentions what corresponds to them. An example is His saying, the Truth:

﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day﴾ (part of verse 73, Surah al-Qasas).

So among the manifestations of His mercy toward us, glory be to Him, is that He made for us the night and the day; then He said:

﴿that you may rest therein, and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ (part of verse 73, Surah al-Qasas).

We rest at night, and seek His bounty in the day. This, as we have said, is called "laff wa nashr."

(1) Narrated by Ahmad from Anas.
(2) Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim from Anas.

The Most High says after that:

﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidences (baṣā'ir) from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own soul; and whoever is blind, it is against it. And I am not a guardian over you.﴾ (104)

Baṣā'ir is the plural of baṣīrah, and baṣīrah (insight) is for the immaterial matters and the illuminations that come into the hearts, just as sight (baṣar) is for the eye. The cosmos gives you the evidences of sight, and the Qur'an gives you the evidences of insight. Just as Allah guided man, warning him and forbidding him from sins, and granted him the light by which things become clear to him, so that he walks in guidance and does not stumble or collide, in the same way He made the immaterial matters a light. The first light, that of sight, is taken by the disbeliever and the believer alike, and we are all partners in it, just as with provision. But the second light, that of insight, is taken only by the believer. For this reason our Lord says:

﴿That He may bring you out from darkness into light﴾ (part of verse 9, Surat al-Ḥadīd).

This is the light of guidance in the insights of the immaterial matters. It clarifies: "I created you as creatures and set down for you laws for your preservation." The law of preservation in the material affairs of the world is for the believer and the disbeliever alike, while the law of preservation in the immaterial matters of life is specific to the believer.

And He is the One who said:

﴿And whoever Allah has not granted light, for him there is no light﴾ (part of verse 40, Surat al-Nūr).

We know that insights are immaterial, and "coming" is said of a sensible matter, as when we say "Zayd came" or "'Amr came." You may picture insights as they come. The Truth says:

﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light﴾ (part of verse 15, Surat al-Mā'idah).

He, glorified is He, has given us a sound, clear light, and it comes to us by His will.

"There has certainly come to you clear evidences from your Lord": that is, they have reached such a stage in their formation that they have become like sensible things that arrive. It is not valid for you to say that they have not reached you, for they come from the Lord who created us by His power and sustained us in everything by His self-subsistence. Among the requirements of lordship is that He give what guides. Allah has decreed that the insights have come to us, and has decreed that His Messenger has conveyed them. So He, glorified is He, gave to His Messenger, and the Messenger handed them to us. The Truth has legislated and His Messenger has conveyed; what remains is that you respond, and you have no excuse before the Supreme Legislator who created, who is the Lord, nor before the infallible conveyor, who is the Messenger.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿So whoever sees, it is for his own soul; and whoever is blind, it is against it﴾ (part of verse 104, Surat al-An'ām).

To Allah belongs the highest likeness. We find a child entering the house, finding his mother, and saying to her: "What have you prepared for us to eat?" She says: "Nothing." The son says: "My father has sent meat, rice and vegetables." It is as if he is saying to her: "Where is your work, mother?"

Our Lord, glorified is He, makes clear: "I created you, and I made for you a law of preservation, and I sent you a Messenger whom you know to be truthful in his conveyance, and he delivered this message. Therefore, what remains of the matter lies with you, and each one of you must perform what is incumbent upon him of action. If he sees, it is for his own soul; and if he is blind, it is against it.
