Beware lest you understand that I have charged you with something that returns to me in my essence, or that increases my authority in any way; for its benefit is for you, and I do not trust legislation from one who does not benefit from the legislation, because one who benefits from it may legislate for his own interest. But the Truth is trustworthy in legislation because He is not benefited by it."

He, glorified is He, says:

﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidences from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own soul; and whoever is blind, it is against it﴾ (part of verse 104, Surat al-An'ām).

Because the Messenger's duty is only conveyance, and the Truth has preserved and protected him from disbelief, and he conveys to you the method; and Allah created every human being with choice, and by this choice he either places himself within the judgment or removes himself from the judgment. Glorified is He, He did not send the Messenger as a tyrant, but sent him as merciful. Therefore Allah says concerning His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾. The Guardian (al-Ḥafīẓ) is one of the names of Allah, and He is the Guardian because He legislated and to preserve creation, and He wants to make them upon a good and conscious pattern. The Messenger is the conveyor, and the Truth says:

﴿And you are not over them a tyrant﴾ (part of verse 45, Surat Qāf).

So every person is free: he places himself within the judgment or removes himself from the judgment. The Messenger fought to protect choice, as evidenced by the fact that in the lands Islam conquered, some of their inhabitants remained upon their disbelief, and no one compelled them to believe.

And thus does the Truth (Allah) continue after that:

﴿Thus do We vary the verses, so that they may say, "You have studied," and that We may make it clear to a people who know.﴾ (6:105)

﴿Thus do We vary﴾.

That is, He brings to us situation after situation, repeating and renewing. An event occurs among the events, and legislation is revealed concerning it; He softens hearts, and brings examples of the messengers and the stances of their nations toward them, so that in every circumstance we find a heart receptive. For if He spoke once and then fell silent, and there were people whose hearts were turned away, then when He repeats the events and reveals within them legislation and admonitions, their hearts may be softened toward faith, and hearts take in guidance.

﴿Thus do We vary the verses, so that they may say, "You have studied"﴾ What is the meaning of: ﴿so that they may say, "You have studied"﴾? We know that heaven intervenes when corruption engulfs [the world]. But if there exists within human nature a self-reproaching soul (nafs lawwamah), it is a shield for the self and a protection for it: when a person commits a sin, his soul blames him and he returns. If the self-reproaching soul disappears and the soul becomes one that commands evil (nafs ammarah bi-l-su'), then enjoining good and forbidding evil cease within society, and this means that corruption has overwhelmed it. Here heaven intervenes and brings a new clarification and a new miracle.

Corruption arises only from the existence of classes that crush one another, and those who are crushed by corruption are the ones who welcome the method with longing, while the crusher who profits from corruption is the one who opposes the method. Therefore every community that fought the messengers was among the crushers of people, while the crushed only want someone who will rescue them.

Thus every bearer of a heavenly call has had from God an enemy among the criminals, because heaven does not intervene except when criminality has no resistance. And so God makes for every prophet and messenger an enemy among the criminals, and this enemy tempts people, and the weak in belief lean toward him. And the Truth varies the verses situation after situation, so that only the sincere believers remain steadfast with the true caller.

For this reason you find that Islam came and sifted matters. For example, the event of the Isra' (Night Journey): whoever's faith was shaky denied the Isra', so that the scum would depart and there would remain those who carry the call by the method of truth. As for whoever had weak faith, or worshipped God "on an edge" (Q. 22:11), Islam does not desire him.

﴿Had they gone out among you, they would have increased you only in corruption﴾ (part of 9:47)

Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted, has varied the verses so that the crushed would depart; and when the Messenger, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said that, they said, "You have studied," and they claimed that he had been sitting in the mountain and learned from a foreigner. Therefore we find the Truth saying:

﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him."﴾ (part of 16:103)

And the response comes from the Truth:

﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ (part of 16:103)

When our master 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, was performing the circumambulation, he came to the Black Stone and said: "By God, I know that you are a stone, that you neither harm nor benefit, and had I not seen the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, kiss you, I would not have kissed you." (1) 

'Umar did this so that he would teach us: if someone comes and asks, "What is the reason for kissing the Black Stone?" the answer is ready: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, did it, and this is legislation.

1. Narrated by Muslim.

The Exalted says, after that:

﴿Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. There is no god but Him, and turn away from the polytheists.﴾ (6:106)

When a speaker addresses someone regarding a matter in which he himself is involved, over which he has authority, and which he carries out, we must understand the true intent. Likewise, when the Exalted says:

﴿O you who have believed, believe﴾ (4:136).

And with what did God address His creatures, the believers, here? He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, so how can He say: "believe"? He addressed them because they had believed with a belief that made them worthy of being addressed with the obligations of the law, and man is a son of changing states. So it clarifies that the faith with which you received the obligations of My address, persist in it as well. The command here is for its continuation, meaning: just as you believed with a faith that made you fit for the obligations in My address to you, I say to you, O you who have believed: hold to this and persist in your faith. His saying, the Truthful: ﴿Follow what is revealed to you﴾ is a statement to a Messenger who follows; so it carries the command to persist in following. Do not be grieved by what they say, O Muhammad, for you are supported by your Lord, who undertakes your defence and gives you the proof.

﴿And they bring you no example but that We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾ (25:33).

Then the Exalted, addressing His speech to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), says: ﴿Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. There is no god but Him, and turn away from the polytheists.﴾

We know that revelation (wahy) is informing in concealment, and every revelation is informing in concealment. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) received revelation in various forms, but everything connected with and specific to the Qur'an came through Jibril. His saying, the Truthful: ﴿Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. There is no god but Him, and turn away from the polytheists.﴾

That is, there is no god but Him, glory be to Him, and you cannot alter the method sent down to you from Him. You must turn away from the polytheists: do not sit with them, do not mix with them, and do not show them affection. It is the turning away of discernment, guidance, and conveyance.

The Exalted says after that:

﴿And if God had willed, they would not have associated others with Him. We have not appointed you a guardian over them, nor are you a manager over them.﴾ (6:107)

Here God Almighty gives us a principle that we must keep in mind throughout our faith history, and the principle is this: no unbeliever disbelieves by compulsion from God. Rather, he disbelieves because God let the reins go slack for him by way of choice, that is, He created him as one who chooses. Therefore the unbeliever performs every act only by the choice that God has granted him, not against our Lord or by force. The evidence is that the universe in which we live is subjected to command: it cannot choose anything except what God wills for it, and everything in the universe proceeds toward God's will.

So whoever does not disbelieve by compulsion from God, because the nature of choice is granted by God. When God singled out man with choice, He set down the method upon which reward and punishment are based. For this reason the obligation (taklif) came down with "do" (if'al) and "do not" (la taf'al). And if God willed compulsion, He has indeed compelled all the kinds in the universe: He compelled them with the length of their lifespan, and [compelled them] to perform their task as God wills from them. He compelled the sun, He compelled the moon, He compelled the stars, He compelled the water, and every thing in the universe is subjected to Him, even the angels whom He created.

﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them﴾ (66:6).

So the attribute of compulsion has taken its object completely. But does God want from His creatures that they be compelled to what He wills? No. Rather, He wants them to be doers of what He loves, even though they are free to do what He does not love. It is as if the creation of compulsion in the kinds was to establish the absoluteness of power, and that no creature can deviate from God's will for it. And choice remained in man to show that some of His creatures come to Him, exalted is He, while they are able not to come to Him, and this establishes the attribute of love.

When the one who chooses chooses obedience, while he is able not to obey, and chooses faith while he is able to disbelieve, he has come to God out of love, not compulsion. For this reason our Lord says to the Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the sky, so that their necks would remain humbled before it.﴾ (26:3–4)

That is: "Have pity on yourself lest you destroy yourself in sorrow and grief over your people's failure to believe in what you brought from your Lord." Do you want, O Muhammad, that I compel them? Do you want necks or hearts? You, O Muhammad, know that the method sent down to you from your Lord seeks hearts, and hearts come by choice. So if We willed their faith, We would send down a miracle that seizes their hearts, and they would believe by compulsion upon them.

For this reason, if choice is damaged by the loss of any of its elements, the obligation ceases. The evidence is that there is no obligation upon one who lacks reason, because the instrument of choice in us is reason. Likewise there is no obligation for one who has not matured; the Truth leaves him until he matures, and becomes able to beget his like and to attain sound physiological development. He is protected from coercion by any force higher than himself that would compel him to do something against his will, and here the obligation comes.

So obligation requires three things: the existence of reason, so there is no obligation for the insane; and mature, sound reason, so before puberty there is no obligation and no compulsion until choice is secured. Why? The answer comes from the Exalted:

﴿That whoever perishes might perish by clear proof, and whoever lives might live by clear proof﴾ (8:42).

And the Exalted says:

﴿And do not revile those whom they call upon other than God, lest they revile God in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made attractive to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾ (6:108)

The passage is cut off mid-sentence at the end, so I translate it as it stands.

This verse contains an essential method of the call to God (da'wah), the call which the earlier messengers carried, and which God Almighty sealed with His Messenger, may God's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, making it the seal of the connection between heaven and earth. Therefore Islam had to encompass every matter related to the call to God, which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) carried as a trustee, and the Muhammadan community (ummah). God Almighty honored this community by placing in it those who bear the trust of calling people to God as extensions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Every Muslim who knows a ruling of God is required to convey it to others, for a conveyer may be more understanding than the one who hears him, even if God has not enabled him to act upon what he conveys. A bearer of knowledge may carry jurisprudence to one who is more learned than himself. If he fails to act, it is still necessary that he not forfeit, for anyone who knows a matter of his religion, the reward of conveying from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to people. But he must act, so that he becomes a behavioral model whom others emulate, lest he fall under the words of God Almighty: ﴿Greatly hateful in the sight of God is that you say what you do not do﴾.

Some poets insist on this matter, saying: "Take my knowledge and do not rely on my action; the fruits are to be consumed, and the wood is left for the fire."

Thus conveying from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is a necessary matter, and it is an extension of the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) testimony that he conveyed from the Truth what was intended for creation. It remains that those who followed this Messenger should bear witness that they conveyed to people what came to them from the Messenger of God (ﷺ):

﴿Thus We have made you a middle nation that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ (part of verse 143, Surah al-Baqarah).

So just as the Messenger will testify that he conveyed to us, it is from the core of the method that his followers testify that they conveyed to people. If there is shortcoming in conveying to people, the responsibility will fall on those who followed the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and they did not fully discharge the Messenger's trust (peace be upon him) to all people. The method of da'wah is a difficult method, because calling to God requires that the caller take by the hand those who deviate from the method of heaven following the desires of earth, and the desires of earth are always attractive to people, because they achieve the immediate pleasures of the self. They say that following the method of religion achieves a deferred benefit. In this statement there is injustice to religion, because religion, before achieving a deferred pleasure for people, also achieves an immediate pleasure; for if people adhere to God's method in (do and do not), they live a good life free of spite, exploitation, rancor, envy, domination, or tyranny, and so all people become secure.

Therefore do not say that the fruit of religion is in the Hereafter; rather say that the mission of religion is not the Hereafter alone, but the mission of religion is also this world, and the Hereafter is only a reward for success in this mission, because God recompenses in the Hereafter only those who did good in this world. Whoever follows God's method, as God said: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, and whoever turns away from God's method, for him is a constricted life. This happens before the Hereafter, then comes the Day of Resurrection to receive punishment from God:

﴿And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha).

When religion takes people from their base desires to the exalted method of God, the task of the caller becomes burdensome upon the self. Therefore they said: the one who advises good must be gentle, because he wants to remove people from what they love and have become accustomed to of evil; so the caller must not combine upon them the removal of what they are accustomed to with a manner they dislike, but must stir their hearts and desire to follow the method. For this reason this verse came:

﴿And do not revile those who call upon other than God, lest they revile God in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made appealing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do (108)﴾ (Surah al-An'am).

The wise have said: advice is heavy, so do not send it as a mountain nor make it a dispute; truths are bitter, so borrow for them the lightness of expression. Lightness in advice wins the heart of the one advised, and it is enough for you that you remove him from what he has become accustomed to and loved to what he has not been used to, so his removal from what he is accustomed to should not be done in a violent manner. Therefore the Truth teaches us this matter when we call our opponents to faith in Him, and these opponents take besides God rivals (andad); that is, they made God and with Him partners.

They therefore wanted immediate pleasure by distancing themselves from the method, yet they kept God alongside the partners, because difficult circumstances may come upon them that the causes of earth cannot repel, and it is in their interest to have a god able to rescue them from their situation. They do not deny themselves. The Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who says of such people if they persist in shirk:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship other than God are fuel for Hell; you will arrive at it (98)﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya').

Fuel of Hell, then, are the polytheists along with the idols they worshipped, and they will be fuel for the fire with which they are punished. Some superficial people think this is a punishment for the stones; no, rather it is zeal, vengeance, and anger from the stones at the polytheists' departure from God's method of affirming God's unity. The stones say: "You were infatuated with me, so I will be the instrument of your burning." We find those infatuated with gods, whether human, trees, planets, or stones, afflicted by God with punishment, and the stones they worshipped say, as one of them said in verse:

"They worshipped us, and we are more worthy of worship than those standing in the pre-dawn hours,
and they took our silence as proof against us, and made us for them fuel for the fire.
For the extremist is his recompense, and the extremist in it, [but] the mercy of the All-Forgiving saves him."

Therefore the command comes not to revile what those who associate partners with God worship, because the idols are not at fault, and the reality required that you be gentle toward the stones, for they bear no blame for those infatuated with them. God Almighty teaches us and makes clear to us not to wrong the one who takes a god, for he is excused; and reviling is mentioning what is ugly, insulting, blaming, and satirizing. If you revile and disparage what they worship besides God, the worshipper of it in his foolishness will revile your God, and you will have reviled a false god while they reviled the true God; and by this we gain nothing, so be mindful.

The Qur'an warns us against falling into this in the words of God, blessed and exalted:

﴿And do not revile those who call upon other than God, lest they revile God in enmity without knowledge﴾ (part of verse 108, Surah al-An'am).

They will do this in hostility, transgression, and arrogance, without knowledge of the value of the Truth and its sanctity, glory be to Him; therefore we must guard our tongues from reviling their gods, lest we embolden tongues that do not believe in God to revile God.

God Almighty wants to teach us gentleness in the method of da'wah, because you want to soften their hearts to win them to faith, and that will not happen except by good manner.

It is true that believers are excused in their zeal when they enter into debate with polytheists, but let the believer remember the ultimate value, which is the good of the da'wah. Let him ask God to grant him patience with the polytheists. The Truth teaches us how to proceed in the method of da'wah. For example, we find our master Noah, peace be upon him, who remained among his people nine hundred and fifty years, continuing to call and to be gentle in the call, until at the last they said to him: "You are fabricating this speech from yourself." So God taught him to say:

﴿Say: If I have fabricated it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit (35)﴾ (part of verse 35, Surah Hud).

The Truth, glory be to Him, says, instructing the Messenger of God (ﷺ): ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ (part of verse 24, Surah Saba').

That is: who gives you the sustenance of life? When you ask them a question that contradicts what they are upon, they stammer, and God helps His Messenger, so He makes it clear and commands him to say to them: ﴿Say: God. And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ (part of verse 24, Surah Saba').

"We" means the Messenger of God and those with him; "or you" refers to the disbelievers in God. He did not say to them, "I alone am upon guidance and you are in error," but said: our method and your method do not agree, and there must be a method upon guidance and a method upon error; and I will not say who is upon guidance and who is upon error, because Muhammad (ﷺ) is certain that if they applied the matter to their own minds and insight, they would find no answer but that the Messenger of God is upon guidance and they are upon error. So he left them to say it themselves.

Let us also reflect on the words of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed, and we will not be asked about what you do (25)﴾ (Surah Saba').

The Truth did not say they are the ones who commit crimes; rather He attributed the crime, if it applied to the believers, and the deed, even if corrupt, to the disbelievers. At the least, equality would have required "and we will not be asked about what you commit," but He did not say that. This is lofty manners and gentleness, because the Truth, glory be to Him, does not want to leave the Messenger to their instincts a place for refusal against him, nor to find a means to flee from the call. For this reason He teaches us this method, saying:

﴿And do not revile those who call upon other than God, lest they revile God in enmity without knowledge﴾ (part of verse 108, Surah al-An'am).

Thereby we achieve the gentleness of debate. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed, those you call upon other than God are servants like you﴾ (part of verse 194, Surah al-A'raf).

And if you want to uncover the reality of those idols, they too are created by God and worship Him. Ask them, and they will not answer; they have no feet to walk on, no hands to strike with, no eyes to see with, no ears to hear with. And beyond that:

﴿Indeed, those you call upon other than God will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ (part of verse 73, Surah al-Hajj).

Is there anything less than a fly in your estimation? Yes, the Truth says:

﴿And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not recover it from it﴾ (part of verse 73, Surah al-Hajj).

If a fly comes and lands on what you are eating, can you retrieve anything from it? You cannot. Even if you are a tyrant and a strongman, catch the fly and take back the food it took—you cannot. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought (part of verse 73, Surah al-Hajj).

This is the debate that makes the debater ashamed of himself. But if you rage in his face and become fanatical, you give him an excuse for resentment against you, anger at you, and attack upon you, and for turning away from God's method. We ask God to grant us patience, breadth of forbearance, and gentleness in gentle debate.

﴿And do not revile those who call upon other than God, lest they revile God in enmity without knowledge, thus We have made appealing to every community their deeds﴾ (part of verse 108, Surah al-An'am).

When the Truth teaches us gentle debate in the call, this is an adornment of the call, and the call in itself is beautiful, so its presentation must be beautiful.

An example from our lives: you go to a merchant who has goods that may be excellent, but he does not arrange them or present them well, so you may be repelled and go to another merchant whose goods may be of lesser quality, but he presents them well. This is adornment, that is, elevating what is good. For this reason the jewelry and what a woman beautifies herself with are called zeena (adornment), and a woman may possess beautiful femininity, yet with her beauty she adorns herself with jewelry, gems, and fine clothing. When an Arab wanted to praise a woman for supreme beauty, he would say: "This is a ghaniyah," that is, she has become independent of adorning herself through her beauty, because what she would conceal with a necklace is more beautiful than the necklace.

Adornment, then, is the beauty of presentation for attraction and inclination, and when we adorn a matter we give it dignity and goodness and add to its beauty: ﴿Thus We have made appealing to every community their deeds﴾. The ummah (community) is the group that has a affiliation uniting its members, like the Arab nation... meaning those who belong to it are Arabs, and the English nation, meaning those who belong to it are English; but the Islamic ummah includes the Arabs, and the…

And God says after that:

﴿They swear by God with their most solemn oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say: "Signs are only with God," and what will make you realise that when they come, they will not believe?﴾ (6:109)

The phrase ﴿They swear by God﴾ here involves an oath: there is the thing sworn by, the one swearing, and the thing sworn about. The thing sworn by is God; those who swear are the group opposing the Messenger of God. Why do they swear? When the argument overwhelmed them with the logic of truth, they swore, and it defeated them. They swore by God although the Messenger (ﷺ) had called them to worship Him. And ﴿with their most solemn oaths﴾ — from it you recognise the effort (jahd), which is hardship; that is, they exaggerated in the oath, to the extent that you find them making clear to those to whom they swear that they are keen to keep the oath. They poured out their effort and hardship into the oath, and this means they declared that they were swearing an oath dear to them, and what is dear to them they are more eager to fulfil. This apparently indicates their sincerity in the oath.

﴿They swear by God with their most solemn oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it﴾ (part of 6:109)

Did the Messenger (ﷺ) not bring a clear sign? He brought them the greatest sign, which is the Qur'an, and their failure to recognise this is their first calamity. Did he not say to you, "I am a Messenger," after announcing the sign, which is the descent of the Qur'an, while you know that he is truthful in conveying from God? ...And this was the peak of their contentiousness, and they continued in it when they themselves proposed signs to God. Did they not say:

﴿They said, "We will not believe you until you make a spring gush forth for us from the earth, (90) or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, (91) or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed, or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee.﴾ (17:90–92)

God wishes by this to show us that the oath they swore is a corrupted oath, for they said ﴿as you have claimed against us﴾, and claim — as we know — is the mount of falsehood, and this is the first flaw in the oath.

And God says: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or cause fragments of the sky to fall upon them﴾ (34:9).

They, then, do not believe in the original sign, which is the Qur'an, and they dispute it in that it descends by revelation. So God warns us not to accept their claim. He is the One who says:

﴿And even if We had sent down to you a Book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ (6:7)

And even if the sign came down, they would not believe, for God says:

﴿And if We opened for them a gate from the sky and they continued to ascend through it, (14) they would surely say, "Our eyes have only been intoxicated; rather, we are a people bewitched."﴾ (15:14–15)

If the Messenger (ﷺ) had bewitched you... then why did he not bewitch them so that they would believe in God?

Thus we see that God has told us in His Book that everything they say on this matter is evasion and flight from responding to the call, because there is no sign greater than the sign that was sent down to them, which is the Qur'an. All the signs they proposed do not rise above this sign, because they were a nation of grammar, morphology, eloquence, clarity and literature. So He brought them a miracle in which they excelled. They did not excel in the things they mentioned and proposed. We bring them a miracle of the kind in which they excelled, because miracles always come on this basis: every people who excelled in a field, God brings them something that surpasses them in the field of their excellence, to establish the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from Him.

We have said that miracles come as a breach of the fixed laws of the cosmos, because the laws of the cosmos have regularities that mankind has known and which have become familiar to them. When something comes that breaks the prevailing law recognised among them, they turn, asking how the law was broken, so that each of them knows that the One who created the law is the One who broke it, in order to establish the truthfulness of this message from Him. The miracle has come to you of the kind in which you excelled, and what indicates this is that they do not speak about the miracle but about the method and the person who brought the method. You find them saying:

﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him?﴾ (6:8)

The Qur'an clarifies that the angel, by the nature of his creation, is not seen by you; he sees you and you do not see him. If We sent an angel, how would you recognise him? Sending an angel would require that We clothe him in the condition of humans, and that God send him down in human form; and if he came down in human form, they would say: "He is not a human, and we are not obliged by what he brought." ﴿Had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they are confusing﴾ (6:9).

Our master Gabriel, for example, would sometimes come down to the Messenger of God in the form of a man arriving from a journey, and sit with our master the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Gabriel, peace be upon him, did not come by his nature of creation, but came in the nature of humans. There is another creation, like the jinn. We cannot see the jinn, and we cannot by our laws or the laws of the jinn see him; but if the jinn wish to show us themselves, they take a form that can be seen materially: they take the shape of an animal, of a cat, of a camel, of a man, and so on. Had this matter not been restricted by a regulation that preserves the balance between the two kinds, humans and jinn, people would have been exhausted; for the moment a jinn appears to a human, stands before him, then vanishes, terror would spread among people, although the jinn fears humans more than we fear them, because the jinn knows that its law permits it to take the form of a human or any material form, and then the law of humans governs it. If it met a person with a pistol, for example, he might strike it with a bullet and kill it. Therefore the jinn fear to appear to a human for a long time; rather it appears like a flash of lightning and vanishes, because, as we said, it fears the human. Thus the balance exists between jinn and humans.

That is why the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"A jinn of the ifrit kind came at me last night to cut off my prayer, and God gave me power over him, so I throttled him. I had intended to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque so that you could all look at him, every one of you. Then I remembered the words of my brother Solomon: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾, so God sent him back in disgrace." In another narration: "By God, had it not been for the supplication of my brother Solomon, he would have been tied up and the boys of Madinah would have played with him."¹

Thus we know that when a people proposes a sign, and then God brings the sign, if they deny it, He seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful, and does not postpone that until the Hereafter.

And God, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿But God would not punish them while you are among them﴾ (8:33). So even the disbelievers among them received some of His mercy.

﴿If a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say: "Signs are only with God," and what will make you realise that when they come, they will not believe?﴾ (6:109)

Here God instructs His Messenger to say to them: I do not bring signs from myself, nor do I bring them by the law of My power, because the law of My power is equal to yours; I am not superior to you, except that it is revealed to me and I convey to you what I have been sent with. It is God who gives me the verses of the Qur'an, and no creature may propose a sign to God. What preceded in earlier messages confirms that when God responds to a sign requested by creation and they still do not believe, He destroys and uproots them, or drowns them, or sends upon them a violent wind, or causes the earth to swallow them. And God says: ﴿Nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the earlier ones denied them﴾ (17:59). So some people of earlier messages proposed signs, God fulfilled them for them, and then they denied them. Thus denial is their original state.

It is supposed that a sign comes as God wills it, not that someone proposes it to Him. Therefore God commands His Messenger to tell them: ﴿Say: "Signs are only with God"﴾. Then comes a new address to people who differ from the polytheists: the believers. God says to them: ﴿And what will make you realise that when they come, they will not believe?﴾ It seems that when the people of polytheism said that, the believers wanted to ease their distress with the Messenger of God, so they said to him: "O Messenger of God, ask God to send down a sign for them so that we may be relieved of their obstinacy." God then turns to reply to the one who made this request, explaining: you are believers, your assumption is good, and your intention is kind, in that you wish to soften the severity of distress; but what will make you realise: that is, what will inform you that the sign they proposed, if I brought it, they would not believe. So it was as if the believers endorsed the words of these polytheists in asking for a sign, in order to prevent obstinacy.²

The Qur'anic text came with God's words "they will not believe," and the scholars differed on this point, and may God reward them all with good, for these are understandings contending to serve faith. We ask: what makes the style come in this form? We say: these are the intended meanings of the Divine, so that we live within the Qur'an, not pass over it quickly. The style in His words ﴿what will make you realise that when they come, they will not believe﴾ is evidence that you have no knowledge. We have said that awareness requires perception, experience and inclination; on what basis did you build this awareness? You took the apparent meaning of their words, but God knows and encompasses what they conceal and what they hide. It is as if He, glorified, clarifies that asking for a sign is only obstinate contention, and you do not know that if God brought them the sign, they would not believe.

Some exegetes said that "lā" (not) here is superfluous; others, more courteous, said that "lā" is a connective, because they feared to say that it is superfluous, since some might take this opinion and delete it. So they maintained good manners, because the One speaking is God, and there is no superfluous particle in His speech such that if you removed it the speech would still be correct. No. If you remove something, the speech is corrupted and does not convey its meaning, because God has purposes in His speech, and these purposes must be realised by His style. An example from our own lives: someone says to you, "I have no money" — or "I have no money at all?" Here "min mal" (of money) is partitive in a sense: "I have nothing from the beginning of what is called money." But one who says "mā ʿindī māl" means he does not have any money that has weight and value; rather he has coins, which would not be called money. In his pocket there are a few coins.

The "lā" in this verse comes because God wants to say to the believers: what informs you, O believers, that if I brought them a sign they would believe? So God rebukes the believers for supporting the demand of the unbelievers. Yet God treats the believers gently and honours their good assumption in supporting the request, because they do not support the demand out of love for the disbelievers, but out of love for the Prophet and the method. It is as if God says to them: I excuse you, because you take the apparent meaning of their solemn oath ﴿They swore by God with their most solemn oaths﴾ and their exaggeration in it. And I do not blame you for believing the apparent meaning of their words, because this is the extent of your knowledge; and what would inform you that if I brought the sign they too would not declare faith? Had you known what I know, you would have realised that they would not believe. So when the style came with ﴿they will not believe﴾, the "lā" is real and not superfluous.

¹ Narrated by Muslim, whose wording it is, in the Book of Mosques, in the chapter on prayer. Also narrated by al-Bukhari in the chapter on prayer, and by Ahmad. Meaning of (yaftik): he seizes in heedlessness and deception; in another narration (talfit). Meaning of (fa-dha'tahu), with a dotted dhal and a lightened unpointed ʿayn: I throttled him; in another narration (fa-da'tahu) with an unpointed dal: I pushed him forcefully. Meaning of (sariya): a pillar.
² Consult its original and its hadith takhrij by Dr. Ahmad ʿUmar Hashim, vice-president of al-Azhar University.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 110:

In order that the Truth might reassure the believers, He showed them that His vast knowledge encompasses the reality of their condition. He says: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾

When you say, "I am turning over the merchandise" (uqallibu al-silʿah), it means you are examining it. The Truth conveys to us here: "I have turned their hearts over in every way, and I will not take the outward appearance of the heart; rather, by My subtlety and My great experience, I know what is hidden within them. So be reassured that My judgment is the true judgment, resulting from a subtle and all-aware turning-over."

There may also be another meaning, namely that the turning (taqlib) is a kind of change. It is possible that when they swore by God with their most solemn oaths, they had at that time come close to faith, but their hearts did not remain fixed upon a belief; rather, they are always changing. And since their hearts do not remain steady, how can we trust their affirmation at the moment they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that they will declare faith if a sign comes? And is there among them one who can control himself after the sign comes, so that his condition remains the same or changes? For our Lord is the Turner of hearts (muqallib al-qulub), and what you approve of at first you may not approve of the second time, when ﴿We turn their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾.

Faith requires receiving the cosmic signs through sight, and after you receive the signs that point to the greatness of God, you believe in Him, and faith settles in your heart. Glory be to Him; He makes clear to us that He turns their hearts and their eyes. Do they see with reflection and conviction? Or is it a superficial sight in which they have no understanding and no ability to draw inferences? Have their hearts settled upon faith, or are their eyes deficient and their hearts deficient?

﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

So they do not believe and they proceed toward their misguidance. If a sign comes, they will not believe, and in this there is an excuse for the believers, who hope and wish that a sign will descend that would lead those who swore their most solemn oaths to believe.

Why? Because the Truth said: ﴿as they did not believe in it the first time﴾, meaning that they have not changed, and therefore the judgment is issued against them: ﴿and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ Transgression (tughyan) is exceeding the limit, and they have exceeded the limit here in receiving the signs. The verses of the Qur'an came to them and they were unable to produce its like, unable to produce ten surahs, unable to produce a single surah. They should not have transgressed, and should not have exceeded the limit in seeking conviction of the Messenger's truthfulness.

﴿And We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ "Al-ʿamah" (ʿamah, wandering blindly) is hesitation and confusion; they wander in their transgression because within them is a nature (fitrah) that awakens and a disbelief that persists. They say to themselves: "Shall we believe or not believe?" The natural disposition (fitrah) that awakens in them flashes like lightning, and they should not have hesitated. [Some of them are destined] for the Fire, because the sight did not perform its task of reflection, and the heart did not perform its task of understanding God; so God recompenses them in kind for what they did, by turning their sight and their hearts in the Fire.

The Most High then says, after that:

﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing face to face, they would not have believed unless God willed. But most of them are ignorant.﴾ [111]

Here God broadens the matter. He did not say, "They will believe," but rather said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels﴾, as they proposed, or even if the dead spoke to them, as they said before: ﴿Then bring us our fathers, if you are truthful﴾ [Surat al-Dukhan, 36].

Then comes the phrase ﴿and We gathered against them every thing﴾. "Hashr" (gathering) indicates driving with pressure, just as we place some books in a box of cardboard and are forced to squeeze in a book that has no room. So, "hashr" is driving that involves pressure. Here God clarifies: even if I brought them signs crowding one another, and My power were sufficient to bring all the signs they requested, their hearts, with this gathering and massing, would still withhold faith.

﴿And We gathered against them every thing qabalan﴾. "Qabalan" is the plural of "qabil" (a tribe or group), like "sarir" and "surar."

﴿And We gathered against them every thing qabalan﴾. This means that if God brought them every sign they asked for, as though each sign represented one tribe and the next sign represented a second tribe, and so on, they still would not believe. Or "qabalan" means direct observation, that they see them with their own eyes, because in everything there is a "dubur" (back) and a "qabal" (front). The "qabal" is what is before your eyes, and the "dubur" is what is behind you. So if We gathered against them every thing facing them, and visible to them, they would still not believe. And if you take it in the first sense, namely that He, glory be to Him, gathered the signs in abundance so that what was given exceeded what was requested, they still would not believe. And if you wish to make it "facing," meaning that if they saw with their own eyes what was in front of them face to face, they still would not believe.

﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing qabalan, they would not have believed unless God willed...﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 111].

God brings in His will here because He possesses absolute power, which, if He wished to compel them to believe, they could not resist. But compelling belief does not grant the choice that is the basis of moral responsibility (taklif). Therefore He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ [Surat al-Shu'ara', 3-4].

God does not desire necks that bow; He desires hearts that humble themselves. Thus God concludes the verse with His words: ﴿But most of them are ignorant.﴾ Ignorance (jahl) differs from lack of knowledge ('adam al-'ilm). Rather, ignorance is the knowledge of the one who opposes: there is a proposition, and the ignorant person knows what contradicts it. As for one who does not know the proposition at all, that is "ummiyya" (unlettered), and it suffices to state it for him to understand it immediately. But with the ignorant person there are two tasks: the first is to remove from his perception that false ignorance, and the second is to place in his perception the correct proposition. Since most of them are ignorant, this indicates that they have followed misguidance.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 112:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says:

﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy—devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorative speech as deception. And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and what they invent.﴾ ?

﴿Thus﴾ is a reference from the Truth, glorified and exalted, to the messengers and prophets, to give the Messenger an example from his brethren who preceded him in the procession of the messages. So, O Muhammad, you are no novelty in being a messenger who is confronted by enemies; every messenger among the messengers was opposed and met by these enemies.

Did the enemies of the messengers break the arm of those to whom they were sent, weaken their strength, enfeeble their resolve, and turn them away from their call? Or did the messengers also remain steadfast? ... They did remain steadfast, and God strengthened them and granted them victory. And if you are the Seal of the Messengers, the master of the messengers, the one who follows up on messages that preceded you, while there is no one who follows up on your message, then the enemies who confront you must necessarily be suited to the task you are performing. Beware lest you think the purpose of this enmity is that We left them as enemies merely for the sake of enmity. No, rather We wanted this enmity for the benefit of the call; because when a person is on a path of good and evil stirs him, he becomes enthusiastic for more good. Therefore you find the faith-based awakenings occur only when believers face a challenge from their opponents. Here you find the faith-based awakening has woken up because there are opponents challenging it; and if there were no opponents, the awakening would have remained lukewarm. This is what we see when there emerges, from the opponents of Islam in whatever form they take, someone who challenges some matter of religion. In such a case, you find even those who are not committed to the methodology of Islam become jealous for the religion. So enmity has a benefit. Beware lest you think that any manifestation in existence overcomes God's wills in His creation; and evil has a message, because were it not that evil exists and people are afflicted by its harm, people would not be stirred toward good. What makes us enthusiastic for good is the existence of evil. We explained earlier that falsehood is a soldier of the soldiers of truth; because when falsehood bites and rampages among people, people ask when the truth will come to rescue them. And when you see a sick person suffering, beware lest you think the pain came without cause; rather pain is a soldier of the soldiers of healing. It is as if the pain says to the one who experiences it: "O human, be alert that a defect exists in this place, so hasten to treat it." Therefore you find the most violent, fierce and malignant diseases are those that come without a preceding pain, and whose symptoms do not appear until their cure has become difficult. Thus we see that pain is a soldier of the soldiers of wellbeing.

When you have an enemy in the neighborhood or in the town, whose eyes are fixed upon you, you fear that some slip or fault may befall you, lest he disparage you; therefore you walk the straight path, because you do not want to give him victory over yourself.

The ancient poet, who liked poetry and split it (into hemistiches), says to you:

My enemies have a favor and a grace upon me,
So I have thanks for them for their benefit.
Their harshness is like medicine, and healing is in its bitterness.
May the Merciful never remove my enemies far from me.
They searched for my slips, so I avoided them,
Thus I became free of what stains honor.
They kindled my effort, but by their hatred,
They competed with me, so I acquired the lofty qualities.

Therefore you must look at everything with the wisdom of the All-Wise who created it; for the Truth willed to bring into being enemies for the Islamic call, so that it might triumph and grow strong.

﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy—devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorative speech as deception. And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and what they invent.﴾ (Surah al-An'am).

The Truth, glorified and exalted, appointed enemies for the prophets, provoking and stirring up the Prophet and his followers; because when a matter is met with opposition from one who disagrees, it kindles in the one opposing a strength, so that he is not defeated before it nor overcome by its argument. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿And thus We have appointed﴾, meaning they did not volunteer for enmity; rather it is a subjecting of enmity (to a purpose): ﴿We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾.

How does God appoint for every prophet an enemy? He does so by what He has deposited in people of choice; and as long as they are choosers, the one who chooses guidance becomes a helper to the Prophet, and the one who chooses misguidance becomes an enemy to the Prophet.

So they were not enemies by their nature, but by what God deposited in them of choice.

And if it is God who deposited choice, He wished to fulfil His will in His saying:

﴿That whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence...﴾ [Surah al-Anfal, 42].

Had God willed that there be no enemies to prophethood, He would have done so, for He has absolute power; but that would be by compulsion, and God does not desire compulsion for the rational; rather He wants them to come to Him by their own free choice, that is, while they are able not to come. The word "ʿadūw" (enemy), in its apparent form, is singular, but it is applied to one, to two, and to a group. You say: "This is an enemy to me" (hadha ʿadūw li); "This (feminine) is an enemy to me" (hadhihi ʿadūw li), and do not say "ʿadūwa"; and you say: "These two are an enemy to me" (wa-hadhan ʿadūw li), "These two (feminine) are an enemy to me" (wa-hatan ʿadūw li), "These are an enemy to me" (wa-haʾulaʾ ʿadūw li), because the word "ʿadūw" is applied to male and female, and is said of the singular, the dual, and the plural.

Read the Truth's saying:

﴿For indeed they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surah al-Shuʿara, 77].

﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha, 123].

He did not say "aʿdāʾ" (enemies, plural), so the word "ʿadūw" is applied to the singular masculine and feminine, the dual, and the plural masculine and plural feminine. But some people who like to be critics of God's speech say: "How does He say: 'For indeed they are an enemy to me,' or 'Go down, some of you enemies to others'?" And the Almighty says:

﴿Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf, 22].

Satan is an enemy, and he is an enemy. Then the Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And remember the favor of God upon you, when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, so you became by His favor brothers...﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran, 103].

We say to him: you have missed that the One speaking is the Most High Lord. Enmity has two kinds: when the enemy is plural, but a single interest unites them in opposing the one who opposes them, they become a unity in enmity, so they are one enemy because they are united on one cause of enmity. But when the causes of enmity are multiple, the matter differs: you may have an enemy because your appearance is better than his, another enemy because you are cleverer than him, and a third enemy because you are richer than him. Because the causes are multiple, each one of them becomes an enemy in his own right, and the plural "aʿdāʾ" is used for multiplicity of causes of enmity.

﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another...﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 112].

"Devils of mankind and jinn," as the grammarians say, is an apposition (badal) to "ʿadūw," and "shayatin" is the plural of "shaytan," meaning the accursed, expelled, hateful one, whether he be of mankind or of jinn.

﴿Inspiring one another with decorative speech as deception﴾. Inspiration, as we know, is informing in secret. Why do they inspire one another? Because: the dominance of truth does not enable them to make their stance openly; therefore they conspire with one another. But people who are right in a matter move openly, and do not hide from people.

﴿Inspiring one another﴾. And who inspires, and to whom? This is no concern of ours; inspiration is only informing in secret, whether it be a cast into the soul, or by gesture, or by insinuation, or by whispering, or through a messenger we do not see; all these are methods of inspiration, which encompass good and evil.

If the inspiration comes from the devils of the jinn, do they inspire only evil? Yes. And likewise there are devils from mankind who also inspire evil. In confirmation of the Truth's saying: ﴿inspiring one another with decorative speech﴾. "Decorative speech" means that they approach matters with embellishment, so they adorn desire for people; that is why our Lord called it "waswasa" (whispering), and we know that meanings are given names taken from sensible things, and "waswasa" is the sound of jewelry; God chose for what the devils of mankind and jinn do the word that conveys the intended meaning, because the whispering of ornaments entices with preciousness and great value, and the path of whispering is concealment.

﴿Inspiring one another﴾: they are devils of mankind and jinn; mankind inspires mankind to embellish for him disobedience and desire, and this happens often.

And a jinn inspires a jinn, since the jinn are also accountable. Likewise the jinn inspire mankind.

﴿Inspiring one another with decorative speech﴾. "Zukhruf" (ornament) is that which is adorned outwardly but whose inner part is corrupt; therefore the Mighty and Majestic said:

﴿And ornaments; and all of that is but the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf, 35].

That is, matters adorned outwardly, but having no depth, duration, or worth.

﴿Inspiring one another with decorative speech as deception﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 112].

That is so that they may delude and deceive them into acting and committing disobedience; and if they did not come to disobedience with words that embellish and adorn it, they would not be able to pass it off to people; therefore they present and display the attractions of disobedience on its surface; for example, you will not find anyone saying to another: "Drink wine so that you get cirrhosis of the liver, for instance!" But there is someone who says: "Sip wine to dispel your worry, energize your soul, and increase your joy."

﴿Decorative speech as deception﴾, that is, to delude you, by displaying a fancied benefit in it, while concealing from people its harm and its ruin.

The Almighty continues: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done so﴾. The Truth, glorified and exalted, is the One who gave His creatures choice in whether they would be believers or disbelievers, guided or misguided, in light or in darkness. There comes a time when He, exalted be He, rewards or punishes; therefore He, majestic is He, does not compel them to an act and then punish them for it, because He is Justice itself. That is why some say: "Why punishment, when nothing in existence occurs outside God's will?" We say: yes, everything is from God's doing; because the cause of choice is from God. And He, glorified be He, is the One who created choice.

So the disbeliever cannot believe except if God wills, but what is required of him is that he believe, because his nature is fit for disbelief and fit for belief.

Thus God created man as one who chooses to do or not to do in some matters. Whoever sees that every act is from God, that is, not by the power of a servant, we say to him: your view is correct. And whoever says that this matter is from the servants, we also say to him: your position is correct; because our Lord created man fit to have this from him and that from him. If you seek the truth, you will find every act comes from God; for example, you did not create the power in your hand to rise, nor did you create the power in your fingers to contract. And when you want to clench your hand, what are the muscles that move to produce the clenching? You do not know. You clench your hand by mere willing that you clench it, and He who created this power for you commands you not to use it to subdue others, but to use it for what benefits people. The hand is fit for striking and for good work, and you did not create the energy in the hand, nor did you create the responsiveness in it to your will.

﴿And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done so﴾, that is, had He willed their not doing it, they would not have done it; because He has absolute power, so no one can ever deviate from His will. We see the heavens, the earth, and all that is beneath man made subservient; so why do we take examples from the heavens, the earth, plants, inanimate things and animals?

Take the example from yourself. There are things in you over which you have no control and no choice. Do you have a choice to fall sick? No.

Do you have a choice that a stone falls on you while you walk? No.

Do you have a choice that a drunk driver strikes you? No.

Do you have a choice to die or not to die? No. God has placed in you two matters: compulsion in some things, and compulsion manifests His Power and its absoluteness, and He made you a chooser in other things, and choice establishes the validity of obligation.

The Truth continues, appending to the verse: ﴿So leave them and what they invent﴾, because their fabrication, their lying, and their false claims will not change the reality of the matter in the least. They think their fabrication obstructs the call; no, their fabrication, their scheming, and their enmity toward the Prophet have become a stirring fuel for the call, because it purifies the call of impurities, refines the believers in it, brings out of them the qualities of evil, and fills them with the qualities of good.

{ Then as for the foam

How would these people proceed?

﴿And the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.﴾ It is as if one who believes in the Hereafter would never draw near to adornment (zukhruf) nor incline towards it. And if a sin is made attractive to him, he asks himself: how long will the pleasure of this sin last? Two minutes, an hour, a month? And what will I do on the Day of Resurrection, when a person will be either entering Paradise or entering the Fire? Therefore, one who believes in the Hereafter does not let his ear or his heart accept this ornamented speech, and only one who does not believe in the Hereafter accepts it, for he knows only this world, and says to himself: let him enjoy only in this world. For this reason, if every believer kept the punishment for sin in mind, he would not commit it, and he only commits it when he forgets the punishment. If in this world we fear the punishment of one another, and our abilities to punish are limited, then what of the Lord's overpowering ability to punish?! Therefore we find that those who keep the Hereafter in remembrance of themselves and their concerns, whenever any sin presents itself to them, they compare it with the punishment, and so they do not approach it. ﴿And the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.﴾

Al-IṣghāʾĀ (iṣghā', listening attentively) is the inclining of the ear towards the speaker, because you may hear someone speaking without attentive listening. When a person walks along the road he hears much, but his ear does not stop at everything he hears; rather the ear may stop when a person thinks it is important speech. For this reason they call it tasammu' (eavesdropping, deliberate listening) rather than sam' (hearing), and this is iṣghā'. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever listens deliberately to a ghāniya" — that is, a woman who sings immodestly — and he did not say "whoever hears." A person among us may walk and go to any place while the radio broadcasts songs, and a person hears them; the faculty of hearing is a region and not an open one; he is not eavesdropping. The faculty of perception of closing or opening is like the eye; the eye does not see while closed, it sees while open, and the eye closes by the eyelids, but the ear has no eyelids to tell it: do not hear this, and hear that.

Therefore hearing is not something over which a person has choice, but eavesdropping is that in which he has choice.

﴿And the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.﴾ [Surah al-An'am]

It is as if there is something in it: the seeking of hearing springs from the heart, that is, it agrees with what is in the depths, and something else that a person passes over without paying attention to it. Al-af'idah (the hearts) are the hearts. It is true that the ears are what listen, but the hearts may listen to what is said, and it is as if the soul is prepared for this process, because it does not believe that there is a Hereafter and it is ready to take the pleasure of this world without regard to the Hereafter. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, transfers listening from the ear to the heart, and this is perception.

﴿And the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it..﴾ [Surah al-An'am]

Then come the second stage and the third stage:

﴿and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing﴾ [Surah al-An'am]

A person may listen, then his self-reproaching soul (nafs al-lawwamah) awakens, and he refrains from responding. But there are those who listen, satisfy their conscience, and find rest in what they hear, then they move towards action to commit sin.

These are three stages: the first is: ﴿and the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾. Then the second stage: ﴿and that they may be pleased with it﴾, then the final stage: ﴿and that they may commit﴾, i.e., commit sin. This matter has defined for us the conscious manifestations that the psychologists have studied: perception (﴿may incline﴾), emotion (﴿may be pleased﴾), and impulse (﴿may commit﴾).

Before psychology was born, the Qur'an came with a description of human nature in its different stages of perception, emotion and impulse; and the Law (sharʿ) does not intervene at any manifestation of a person's consciousness except at the impulse, except in one case where impulse cannot be separated from emotion and perception. Therefore the Law intervenes from the very beginning, and this is what happens in the process of a man looking at a woman; for when you look, you find in yourself: you love her, you desire her, you are enchanted by her, and impulse is forbidden to you; when you move towards her, the Law tells you: no. Because this is a matter that is difficult for the human soul, these processes cannot be separated, for if it perceives it feels, and if it feels it impels; so the Truth commanded abstention from the very beginning:

﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze..﴾ [Surah al-Nur, 30]

﴿And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze..﴾ [Surah al-Nur, 31]

Thus perception was prohibited from its beginning and did not wait until impulse; why? Because aesthetic perception of everything differs from aesthetic perception of a woman. Aesthetic perception of a woman causes a chemical process in the body that produces impulse, and they can never be separated.

﴿And the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing﴾

So when we say "mā" and vagueness comes, this is evidence that there are very many things.

For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Then there covered them of the sea that which covered them﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha, 78]

That is, it is a matter that words cannot define, like His saying: ﴿and that they may commit what they are committing﴾.

That is, each one commits, acquires, does and perpetrates what he is inclined to; there is one who backbites, envies, steals and other desires of the self that are not limited; therefore He brought for them a word that gives generality.

And since the matter concerns prophethood and following a prophet, and enemies of devils from mankind and jinn, and some of them inspire to others ornamented speech as deception, then this is a battle, and until it is decided there must be a judge who judges. So the Truth made clear: O Muhammad, I have sent you, and you have enemies who will plot against you in such and such ways and will exert their utmost effort to harm you and those who follow you; so beware of seeking a judge other than Me; for I am the Legislator and I am the Wise, and I am the One who will recompense.

Why? Because disagreement is about what God has legislated, and it is not right or valid for someone to say "the intent of the legislator is such," or "the French commentator said such," and "the English commentator said such." No, the one who judges is the one who established the law, and he knows its intentions best, and the clear truth is known best to Him, and He, glory be to Him, is the one who judges. The Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ("I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes to me; perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I judge for him according to what I hear. Whomever I give by judgment the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it.")(1).

That is, beware lest anyone say: the Prophet has judged; for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, judged by the apparent evidence, and one of the disputants may be strong in argument while the other does not express himself well.

So the judgment belongs to God, because He is the One who legislated, and since He is the One who legislated and the One who judges among you, let every person who disputes with another be reassured; for the matter is decided by the most just of the just and the wisest of judges.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, detailed? And those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be of the doubters.﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 114]

(1) Narrated by Malik, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 114:

﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, explained in detail? Those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters.﴾

So He, glory be to Him, is the One who judges, and He is the One who legislates. He is the One who knows the law, who knows who follows the law and who opposes the law. When you say: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God?﴾ this is evidence that you are certain that your question will only be answered: "Do not seek a judge other than God." For this reason the matter is put in the form of a question. The Prophet (ﷺ), conveying from his Lord, says: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book, explained in detail﴾. The Messenger of God did not say: "It is He who has sent down to me the Book," but rather he said, conveying from the Lord of Might: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book﴾, as if the enmity is not toward Muhammad alone, but is enmity toward the whole community of faith, and judgment belongs to the whole community of faith. Although the Qur'an was first sent down to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), its mission is delivery to the people, and its purpose is for all believers. Thus enmity toward the Prophet is enmity toward all believers. For this reason the Truth sent down upon him this question: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God?﴾ just as He had earlier sent down the true word:

﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn﴾ (part of verse 112, surah al-An'am)

Therefore, the enemy of the Prophet is an enemy of those who believe in him and follow him, but the peak of enmity is directed at the Prophet sent by the Truth:

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters﴾ (part of verse 114, surah al-An'am).

The phrase ﴿from your Lord in truth﴾ contains an encouragement to the believers that the whole matter returns to your benefit, because the purpose of the sending down of the Book is for you. The Book came with this method for your good, and it will not add a single attribute to God's attributes, nor add a single dominion to God's dominion. Rather, the purpose is you.

﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book﴾ (part of verse 114, surah al-An'am).

He, glory be to Him, did not send down the Book except with a detail in which one matter is not confused with another:

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters﴾ (part of verse 114, surah al-An'am).

What is meant here by "those to whom We gave the Book" is the Jews and the Christians, because they know your attributes, O Messenger of God, and know your description, and they know much of your Book. Everything related to you is present with them. But the calamity is that they have embraced two religions: a religion they declare and make manifest, and a religion they keep secret. What they keep secret they do not announce, and they forbid questioning about it and do not accept discussion about it. When you reach the truth and present it to them, they do not accept it. What made them twist like this? Because they have two states: the state of the days when they were opposed by those who do not believe in heaven and the method of heaven, such as idol-worshippers and polytheists. Concerning this the Truth said:

﴿And previously they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾ (part of verse 89, surah al-Baqarah)

Previously they were enemies of those who disbelieved and associated partners with God, so their concern and preoccupation was to triumph over these disbelievers, and they said: (The time of a prophet whom we will follow, and we will kill you with him, the killing of 'Ad and Iram).

When what they knew came to them, they disbelieved in it, because they: ﴿sold the signs of God for a small price﴾ (part of verse 9, surah al-Tawbah).

The price was the retention of authority in their hands. When prophethood comes, it strips them of authority, for there is no domination by clergy and no priesthood in Islam. They wanted their sovereignty to continue, so they sold the signs of God for a small price.

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters﴾ (part of verse 114, surah al-An'am).

They know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, and they know that what they propagate is falsehood. So there is a knowledge between them and their own souls, and another knowledge they tell to others. His saying, the Truth: ﴿so do not be among the doubters﴾, means: do not be among those who doubt that the People of the Book know that the Qur'an is sent down from your Lord in truth. This is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ), and we know that when a speaker asks the addressee to do something he is already doing, what is meant is persistence in it and increase; because there are matters that may shake faith, therefore the command to steadfastness comes. Or it is an incitement to him, or it is consolation to the believers, since he told them: do not doubt and do not be uncertain.

Then Allah says:

﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can alter His words. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (6:115)

The word "tammat" (was fulfilled) indicates that the matter has a beginning and an end. So what is meant by the word that was fulfilled? Is it the supreme word of Allah, the victory of Islam and the final outcome of the affair in its favour? Or is it the completion of the message itself, as when Allah says:

﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and approved Islam as your religion.﴾ (5:3)

Or is "the word of your Lord" meant as His Qur'an? We see that the meaning of "tammat" is that it has encompassed every matter of life until the Hour is established. Therefore no one may add to what has come in the Book of Allah a ruling of any kind, because the rulings have covered every matter.

The word "kalima" (word) is singular, yet it conveys the meaning of plurality. In everyday life you hear someone say: "So-and-so delivered a good word (kalima), which was met with approval and applause." He spoke many words, yet the expression came as "a word." Thus "the word of your Lord was fulfilled" means the method (manhaj) that encompasses all of life. Consider His saying:

﴿Terrible is the word that comes out of their mouths...﴾ (18:5)

Is it a word or words? It is a word, but it contains words. So the term "kalima" is used to mean a single word, and it is also used to mean speech. In origin, a kalima is a single lexical unit, that is, it is not accompanied by another word, but it indicates a meaning. If the meaning is not independent in understanding and needs something added to it in order to be understood, then it is a particle (harf). For example, you say "fi" (in), which is a word indicating location, but it is not independent in understanding, because a container requires something contained and a place in which it is contained. So you say "the water in the cup" to convey a meaning that is independent in understanding. Likewise, when you hear the particle "min" (from), you understand that there is a starting point, and when you hear "ila" (to), you know that there is an endpoint. If a word indicates a meaning in itself, and it is not tied to time, then it is a noun (ism). If time is part of its meaning, then it is a verb (fi'l). As for "kalam" (speech), it is the meaningful utterances.

When you hear "sama'" (sky), you understand the meaning, and likewise when you hear "ard" (earth), which is a meaning independent in understanding. When you hear the word "kataba" (he wrote), it indicates a meaning independent in understanding, and time is part of the verb: "kataba" indicates the past, "yaktubu" indicates the present, and "sayaktubu" indicates writing in the future. So the "kalima" is a word that indicates a meaning; if the meaning is not independent in understanding, it is a particle. And "kalima" may be intended to mean speech.

His saying: "The word of your Lord was fulfilled" means much. If by it you mean the Qur'an, then the intended meaning is the word of Allah. We call the speech of Allah a "kalima" because its signified content is one word: it has ended, and there is no contradiction in it. This is if we mean by it the Qur'an. You should understand that the Qur'an has encompassed everything and every matter in existence. Also, nothing has been forgotten in it, and no letter has been altered in it; rather, it has remained and will remain as it was revealed. This is because the flaw in the earlier books was that they concealed some of their contents, forgot some, and distorted some. Their preservation was entrusted to those who were obligated, and by the nature of a commanding matter, it may be obeyed at one time and disobeyed at another. If they obeyed, they preserved the books; if they disobeyed, they distorted them. The evidence is His saying:

﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, as did the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted to preserve of the Book of Allah...﴾ (5:44)

"Istuhfizu" means that they were asked to preserve it. This is a matter of obligation, liable to be obeyed and liable to be disobeyed. But the matter differs with regard to the Qur'an, for Allah says:

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian.﴾ (15:9)

So He, glorified is He, is the One who preserves the Qur'an, not humans, because the Qur'an is a miracle (mu'jiza), and for the obligated person there is never any action in a miracle.

Therefore, His saying: "The word of your Lord was fulfilled" means that you may be assured that the Qur'an in your hands, until the Hour is established, is the very same; not a single word in it will change. The evidence is that you find, in some passages of the Qur'an, a text that is parallel to another text, but the context differs. Allah says:

﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it.﴾ (74:54–55)

And again He, glorified is He, says:
