﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it.﴾ (80:11–12)

And again He says:

﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.﴾ (76:29)

This is a kind and type of similarity among the verses, so that the Real (al-Haqq) may say to us:

﴿So when We have recited it, follow its recitation.﴾ (75:18)

And the Real says:

﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded: those who are humble in their prayer, those who turn away from ill speech, those who are active in giving zakat, those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed they are not blameworthy, but whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are transgressors, and those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant, and those who guard their prayers.﴾ (23:1–9)

And in another verse:

﴿And those who guard their prayers.﴾ (70:34)

All of this shows you that every word has reached you as it was revealed, and thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled. Or the saying of Allah: "The word of your Lord was fulfilled" indicates that the word of Allah is the highest. Therefore you notice that "the word of Allah is the highest" was not made so by the Real as an act of making; rather it came as an established fact. Glorified is He who said:

﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest...﴾ (9:40)

This grammatical structure (i'rab, the grammatical analysis) contains a deliberate break. In other than the Qur'an, the expected construction would be: "and He made the word of Allah the highest." But He, glorified is He, says: "and He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, and the word of Allah is the highest." He, glorified is He, intended by this that we understand that the word of Allah is always the highest, and that it is not a matter of being made so. This is evidence that His word has been fulfilled.

We note that the saying of the Real, "The word of your Lord was fulfilled," comes after "Shall I seek other than Allah as a judge?" Trace the procession of the messages from Adam onward, and look at Allah's judgment between the falsifiers and the truthful, and between the guided and the misguided. He is the Real who says:

﴿So each We seized for his sin: among them were those upon whom We sent a violent wind (hasib)...﴾ (29:40)

The "hasib" is a wind that blows carrying pebbles, and it was the punishment of the people of 'Ad.

﴿And among them were those seized by the Cry...﴾ (29:40) These were the people of Thamud. He calls it at one time "the Cry," and at another time He calls it "the Overwhelming": ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming.﴾ (69:5)

And at another time He causes the earth to swallow them, just as He did with Qarun: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home.﴾

And likewise: ﴿And among them We drowned.﴾

Allah drowned the people of Pharaoh, and likewise He drowned those before them who denied Noah. So every people received Allah's judgment upon them. But you, O Muhammad, are different from them, and likewise the community of Muhammad, which has become trusted with the testament and with the method. Therefore the Real says:

﴿And We would not punish until We had sent a messenger.﴾ (17:15)

And after Allah sent His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, He said:

﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them.﴾ (8:33)

So, "the word of your Lord was fulfilled" is the final decision:

﴿And Our word had already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed they would be the ones given victory, and indeed Our army, they would be the predominant.﴾ (37:171–173)

You are the ones given victory, because you are attributed to a dominant method, and victory for a dominant method requires sincerity. If you support the method by following it, the One who sent down the method will support you. He is the One who says:

﴿I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.﴾ (58:21)

What He said is what occurred, and what occurred conformed to what was said.

﴿And the word of your Lord was fulfilled in truth and justice...﴾ (6:115)

That is, the cosmic reality conformed to what Allah had spoken. How can the reality be truthful and just at the same time? Suppose you brought a private tutor for your son, and it happened that he is the one who teaches at the school, and he is the one who teaches your son. Then you said to him: "I want the boy to pass the examination." The tutor promised that, then the examination came and the boy passed, so the tutor's word has been fulfilled. But is this just? The tutor may himself have written the questions and hinted to the boy at the questions, and the success would then be unjust. But the word of Allah comes in conformity with what He said; its outcome conforms with what He said, and it is also just, because He, glorified is He, has made clear the reward and the punishment:

﴿And the word of your Lord was fulfilled in truth and justice.﴾ For there is no alterer of the words of Allah, and no other god opposes Him; so He, glorified is He, has absolute power.

As for humans, Allah taught His servants the caution of truthfulness in their speech. So He instructed them:

﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed I will do that tomorrow," unless Allah wills...﴾ (18:23–24)

Because doing that, bringing it about and causing it to occur, is a matter connected to the future, which we do not control. So protect yourself and say: "If Allah wills." If it does not happen, you may say: "Our Lord did not will the occurrence of what I promised." In this way a person protects himself from being a liar, and makes himself truthful, so that he speaks only in accordance with what he possesses of the laws of doing and not doing. For when you say, "I will do that tomorrow," what will you do tomorrow, when you do not guarantee yourself, your life, or your circumstances? But when Allah says, "I will do," He has absolute power.

﴿And the word of your Lord was fulfilled in truth and justice. None can alter His words. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (6:115)

Since the words will be realised and the judgment will be issued, this is evidence that He, glorified is He, hears what they say in their enmity, and knows what they have plotted of their schemes. He is the One who said earlier:

﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you...﴾ (6:121)

That is, they inform them secretly. If their speech is open, it is heard; if it is in secret, it is known.

The Almighty then says:

﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah. They follow nothing but conjecture, and they do nothing but guess.﴾ (6:116)

"Those on earth" (man fi al-ard) refers to the mukallafun (those held accountable), because they are the ones distinguished by choice and to whom commands and prohibitions are directed. What is below the human being has no command addressed to it. "Most" (akthar) does not necessarily have as its counterpart the word "few" (qalil) or "fewer" (aqall). And since what is said is "most," the remainder may also be many. As for "kathir" (much/many), it gives its quantity in itself and is not related to anything else. That is why we used to hear someone say: written on the Egypt station, or on the "airport," or on the "port": "Ya dakhil Misr, minnak kathir" (O one who enters Egypt, there are many like you). That is, if you are a good man, you will find many like you, and if you are a wicked man, you will also find many like you.

The Almighty says:

﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures, and many of mankind? And many have deserved the punishment...﴾ (22:18)

All creatures are subjugated and made subservient, but among people the matter is divided, because they have choice: some go toward obedience and some toward disobedience. The Almighty did not say "and mankind" but said "and many of mankind," and He did not say "and few have deserved the punishment," but said: ﴿and many have deserved the punishment﴾. So these are many and those are many; if you look at them in themselves, they are many, and the others too, if you look at them, you find them many. Why then does the Almighty say: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾?

"Obedience" (ta'ah), as we know, is responding to a command in "do" and to a prohibition in "do not." When the Almighty tells a person "do such-and-such," the person is able both to do it and not to do it; and if He says "do not," the person is able both to do and not to do. If there is something you cannot do, He will not tell you to do it. A person, when commanded or forbidden, is usually commanded or forbidden for his own benefit. If there is no opposing interest arising from a divine method, then this too is in his interest, because Allah has permitted him freedom to act and to refrain. The Almighty makes this clear: it is by My mercy that I have given you legislation, because if we left people to their desires, each one who holds power over people would command what agrees with his desire, and each person would forbid what opposes his desire. Therefore we protect this command with a method, so that creation does not clash and your desire does not conflict with your brother's desire. It is in the interest that there be one obeyed authority with no desire of its own, and a method that says to all: "Do such-and-such" and "Do not do such-and-such," and thereby the path comes to benefit them all. That is why the Almighty says:

﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of...﴾ (6:116)

There are people who are believers, who are by nature people of sound disposition (fitrah), because goodness is the natural disposition of the human being. Legislation came to develop the fitrah of the one with sound disposition or to affirm it for him, and to correct the one with an evil inclination so as to return him to the good fitrah.

And those who lead you astray from the way of Allah, what do they follow? The Almighty says: ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture﴾.

Each one of them thinks that this misguidance benefits him now, and he is unaware of the calamity it will draw upon him afterward.

"Conjecture" (zann), as we know, is the apprehension of the more probable side, and its opposite is "wahm" (illusion), which is the apprehension of the less probable side. The conjecture here is what desire makes probable:

﴿They follow nothing but conjecture, and they do nothing but guess﴾ (6:116)

And "in" (inna), as we know, comes sometimes as a conditional particle: "in tafal kadhā tajid kadhā" (if you do such-and-such, you will find such-and-such), and sometimes as a negation, such as the Almighty's saying:

﴿Their mothers are not but those who bore them...﴾ (58:2)

That is: "ma ummahatuhum" (they are not their mothers); so "in" here is a negation. And the Almighty's saying ﴿in yattabi'una illa al-zann﴾ means: "ma yattabi'una illa al-zann" (they follow nothing but conjecture). They either follow conjecture or they guess. The "kharis" (guesser) is one who speaks without reality, rather he conjectures by guessing, as when a person looks at another in the grain market and asks him: "How much is this heap of wheat?" and he answers: "About ten ardabs or twelve ardabs," guessing without certain evidence or fixed measures, or saying something whose meaning is not precise.

So if you follow the people, they will lead you astray, because they possess no scientific proof and no certain knowledge; rather they follow conjecture if the matter seems probable, and they guess and speculate even if the matter is improbable.

Allah says after that:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.﴾ (117)

When you see this "Huwa" (He), know that it answers and responds to what might be said. There are those who say: "I will observe the conduct of so-and-so." And since you are a human being, however much you know about him, your perception is limited, because you will see only his actions and will not see the emotions of his heart or the fluctuations of his mind. But Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, is the most knowing, because the whole balance is in His hand; He perceives the outward and the inward. Here He says "a'lam" (most knowing), and elsewhere He says "'Alim" (All-Knowing). The "'Alim" is one who sees the outward aspect of a matter and encompasses it, not what is hidden of it, whereas one who sees both the outward and the hidden is "a'lam."

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) in many matters dealt with people according to their outward state and left their inner secrets to Allah. When a Muslim killed a man who had declared Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) asked him why, and he said: "Because he declared Islam only out of hypocrisy." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did you split open his heart?!"

And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is "a'lam" because He knows the outward and the inward, and He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 118:

The Truth says:

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.﴾ (118)

What brought this issue into this context? The Truth has spoken of how there are enemies to every prophet who seek a gap in his method in order to speak about it, and this is their task which Allah has prepared for them. When they raise objections, we find the method responds to them, and thereby the call benefits until the Hour comes.

An example of this: we find the group who opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding the Night Journey (isra') and the Ascension (mi'raj). When he said to them: "I was taken by night to the Farthest Mosque (al-Masjid al-Aqsa), and I was made to ascend to the heavens in a single night," they sought a gap through which to enter and mislead others, and they said to him: "Do you claim that you went there in one night, when we travel to it on the backs of camels for a month?!" But Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." This is the faith which receives a matter that contradicts the established laws well. They argued with Abu Bakr, and he said: "I believe him concerning the news of the heavens, so how could I deny him in this? As long as he has said it, he has spoken the truth." And this is logical speech.

However, the opponents of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you claim that you went there in one night, when we travel to it on the backs of camels for a month?!" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them the signs and described to them the caravan that was on the road, and other indications that make the matter a proof until the Day of Resurrection. Had the matter of the Night Journey and Ascension passed without any of the enemies objecting, we would not have found the fervour in affirming it.

Today we find someone who says: "Is it reasonable that he (ﷺ) went to Bayt al-Maqdis and came back in one night? It must have been a dream." Had they not said this, we would not have known the response; rather, they said it so that we would know the response, and the response remains a deterrent until the Hour comes. This is the task which Allah assigned to the enemies, because if he (ﷺ) had said to them: "I dreamt that I went to Bayt al-Maqdis," would anyone have objected that a prophet may dream, even if he said he went to the furthest part of the inhabited world? No one would dare deny him. But since they denied him and rejected accepting the Night Journey, this is evidence that they understood from "going" that it was not a going in a dream but a going in bodily form. They understood from him that he had moved bodily from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis, and for this reason they denied him. This denial by them benefits us now, that we may respond with it to the contemporary deniers.

Thus the presence of enemies stirs up the minds which can respond to any doubt raised by any person, whether of the past or of the present.

And the Truth says here:

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.﴾ (118) [Surah al-An'am]

This verse has a story which shows how enemies try to hunt for gaps to enter through. They said: "Muhammad says to you: what is carrion is not lawful for you to eat, but what you slaughter with your own hands, eat of it. Slaughter is a kind of death." This is the doubt they raised, and it is first a sophistry in its method, because carrion is not the same as what is slaughtered or killed. The slaughtered animal we have slaughtered in order to purify it from blood; therefore the juristic or scientific discussion defeats their claim, because there is a difference between dying and being killed. Death is the taking of life without the cutting off of the intention; killing, however, is first the cutting off of the body's [integrity], so the soul departs while the blood remains in the body. Moreover, does the Legislator, who is the Supreme Lord, take wisdom from us, or is wisdom His alone?

It has become clear to us in our age that unbelievers have begun to realise that carrion contains all harmful waste matter, and they have come to know the removal of harmful waste from the animals they wish to eat, because the constitution of an animal's body resembles the constitution of a human's body. It eats, digests, and absorbs nutritious elements so that blood and energy are formed, and in the body there are organs that filter and purify the body from harmful toxins. The kidney, for example, filters the blood of urea and other things, and the blood travels to pass through the lungs to take oxygen, and all of this is to free the body from harmful waste. The blood vessels in humans and animals contain good blood and corrupt blood, and corrupt blood is that which has not been purified. When the animal is slaughtered, corrupt blood and other things flow out of it; that is, we sacrifice good blood in order to protect ourselves from corrupt blood, but a dead animal that was not slaughtered retains the traces of both bloods. Likewise, the traces of waste that should have been expelled remain. This is what we do in this matter. But do we have any reasoning with the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, in anything other than confirming the ruling and being at peace that it came from Him, exalted in power?

Their argument was that they said: "You eat what you kill, and you do not eat what Allah kills; so you consider yourselves better than Allah." This is a fabrication on their part. Furthermore, when an animal dies, the name of Allah is not mentioned over it, but over the slaughtered animal that we slaughter we mention the name of Allah. So it is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted, is clarifying: "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned," that is, not carrion and not what is sacrificed to idols.

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.﴾ (118) [Surah al-An'am]

Receiving any ruling from the Truth is by no means correct by first seeking its reason and only then believing in it; rather, after we trust that it is from Allah in whom we have believed, we must take the ruling which Allah has commanded.

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to? And indeed, many lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.﴾ (116) [Surah al-An'am]. As we have known, the two verses have a cause of revelation: some of the opponents of the Messenger of Allah, who stand toward the call in a position of denial and work to nullify and eliminate it, were spreading rumours among the believers that could weaken their creed. So they presented this matter, which on its surface is doubt. They presented the issue in this inconsistent form, because who is the one who killed? They said: "Allah killed the carrion." Did Allah cut its neck? Did Allah strike it on its head and kill the root of the management of life, which is the brain? Did He aim something at its heart? Glorified and exalted is He above such human actions. How then do they call death "killing"? To name death "killing" is the error; so their saying, "How do you permit for yourselves what you have killed," that is, by slaughter, "and do not permit what Allah has killed," that is, caused to die, contains a sophistry in presenting the issue. Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to place in the believers an immunity from these anxieties they raise; so He said: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.﴾ (118). And what is the meaning of "remembrance" (dhikr)? The scholars' failure to define the intended meaning of "remembrance" is what created a great disagreement among them. Our master, the Imam Malik, holds that if you slaughter and do not mention the name of Allah, whether forgetting or deliberately, it is not valid for you to eat of the slaughtered animal. Imam Abu Hanifa holds: if you did not mention it out of forgetfulness, then eat what you slaughtered; but if you did it deliberately, do not eat. And Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, holds: as long as you are a believer and are approaching the slaughter while you are a believer, then eat what you did not mention the name of Allah over, whether forgetfully or deliberately, because your faith is the remembrance of Allah.

We say: what is remembrance? Is remembrance saying it with the tongue, or is remembrance a thing passing through the mind? If you say that remembrance is with the tongue, then let us examine the sacred hadith in which Allah the Exalted said: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs." (1)

Thus our Lord called a thought in the soul "remembrance," and thereby it becomes the right of Imam al-Shafi'i to say what he said.

Therefore I say: we must first define the meaning of remembrance so that the disagreement on this matter is ended. It is not acceptable to raise a battle over the meaning of "remembrance," because remembrance, which is a matter occurring to the mind, may be accompanied by the matter occurring to the tongue along with the occurrence to the mind, and it may remain occurring to the mind only, as is evident from the hadith mentioned above. The believer, when he finds many things before him, there may be a beautiful thing and another having no beauty at all; the buffalo is less beautiful than some of the animals that Allah has forbidden to eat, and believers have eagerly slaughtered the buffalo to eat from it, while we have never heard of a Muslim approaching an animal whose eating Allah has forbidden in order to slaughter it. Why? Because the believer turns to what Allah has made lawful, and this turning is evidence that he has remembered in his soul the lawful and the unlawful, which is Allah. So his choice of an animal for slaughter is evidence that he has remembered Allah in the soul or in speech, and by this we agree that the believer's remembrance is in his heart whether or not he speaks, and the disagreement on this matter ends. Imam al-Shafi'i acted on this matter because when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about a Muslim eating from an animal slaughtered by someone whom he does not know, and whether he mentioned the name or did not, he clarified to the questioner: "Mention it and eat."

Indeed, a person is not always present at the time of slaughter, and it suffices him to bring to mind the lawful and the unlawful at the hour of eating. The Truth, glorified and exalted, clarifies for us: "Remember the name of Allah," and He, glorified, knows that you approach things in order to do them. These things divide into two kinds: one kind passes through your mind before you do it, and another kind does not pass through your mind, but you do it spontaneously without anything passing through the mind. An example of this is all the reflexive actions that a person performs; they do not pass through his mind. If someone tried to put his finger in another's eye, that other person would close his eyes spontaneously. This differs from an act you think about before doing it. The act that a person does after it has passed through his mind is an act of consequence (dhu bal). For this reason the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, wished not to burden us with hardship or difficulty; so he said:

"Every matter of consequence that is not begun with 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate' is cut off" (2).

The matter of consequence (dhu bal) is the matter that has occurred to your mind, whether to do it or not to do it. Thus Allah, glorified and exalted, does not burden us except at the matter that passes across the mind; for when you approach any act and it comes out for you as you wish, this is from Allah's bounty to you. When you slaughter a calf or a sheep and reflect on how Allah has enabled you over this living creature, you have not done it to make all creatures subservient to you. Rather, you slaughter it in the name of Allah.

Thus there are many matters and acts of consequence that pass over you, and from good manners and faith is that you approach them in the name of Allah. For this reason some people err when they think that when a person slaughters an animal he is harming it. No, rather slaughtering this animal is the completion of its task in life, because it was created for this purpose and made subservient to him.

We have said previously that there is a wonder among the phenomena of physical acts: when you come to animals that Allah has not made lawful for humans, such as the donkey for example, if these animals are exposed to something that kills them, such as a rope wrapped around the neck so that it suffocates, it dies without stretching its neck forward. But an animal that Allah has made lawful for eating, such as a buffalo, a sheep, or a calf, if it suffocates, it stretches its head forward; the people of the countryside in Egypt say: "It is seeking the lawful," that is, slaughter. Thus the slaughter of the animal is not called aggression against it, because the animal was created for this task.

Thus the meaning of the phrase "in the name of Allah" is that I have not dared to do this act except within the scope of the name of Allah, who made this lawful to me.

After that, the Truth says to the believers: do not listen to the words of the disbelievers. Then comes the rhetorical question: "And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned?" The meaning: what reason prevents you from eating of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned? He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, so that which has the name of Allah mentioned over it is not among the prohibited things which Allah has specified; Allah is the One who makes lawful and forbids. And if it is said: since some of them have been forbidden to us...

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi.
(2) Narrated by Abd al-Qadir al-Rahawi in al-Arba'in from Abu Hurayra.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 119:**

A repeated passage, because it shares [its theme] with verse 118:

The Truth says:

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs (118)﴾

What brought this issue into this context? The Truth has spoken about how every prophet has enemies who seek a gap in his method to speak through. This is the task that Allah has prepared for them. When they raise objections, we find that the method responds to them, and thus the call benefits until the Hour comes.

An example of this is the group who opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding the Isra' and Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension). When he told them, "I was taken by night to al-Masjid al-Aqsa and ascended to the heavens in a single night," they sought a gap through which to enter and mislead others. They said to him, "Do you claim you went there in one night, when we take a month to travel there by riding camels?!" But Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said, "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." This is the faith that receives a matter contrary to the usual laws well. They argued with Abu Bakr, and he replied, "I believe him regarding the news of the heavens, so how could I call him a liar about this? As long as he said it, he has spoken the truth." This is logical speech.

But the opponents of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Do you claim you went there in one night, when we take a month to travel there by riding camels?!" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them signs and described to them the caravan that was on the road, and other indicators that make the matter a proof until the Day of Resurrection. Had the matter of the Isra' and Mi'raj passed without any objection from the enemies, we would not have found the same fervour in affirming it.

Today we find people who say, "Is it reasonable that he (ﷺ) went to Bayt al-Maqdis and returned in one night? It must have been a dream." Had they not said this, we would not have known the response. Rather, they said it so that we would know the response, and the response will remain a deterrent until the Hour comes. This is the task that Allah assigned to the enemies. For if he (ﷺ) had told them, "I dreamed that I went to Bayt al-Maqdis," would anyone have objected that a prophet may dream, even if he said he had gone to the farthest part of the inhabited world? No one would dare call him a liar. But since they called him a liar and rejected the affirmation of the Isra', this is evidence that they understood the "going" to be not a going in a dream but a going in reality. They understood from him that he had been transported bodily from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis, and that is why they denied him. This denial of theirs benefits us now, so that we may use it to respond to the contemporary deniers.

Thus the presence of enemies stirs up the minds that can answer any doubt raised by any person, whether from the past or the present.

And the Truth says here:

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs (118)﴾ [Surah al-An'am]

This verse has a story that shows how enemies hunt for gaps to enter through. They said: "The Prophet says to you that you may not eat of carrion, but what you slaughter with your own hands you may eat. Slaughter is a kind of death." This was the doubt they raised. First, it is a sophistry in the method, because carrion is not what is slaughtered or killed. We slaughter so as to cleanse the animal of blood. Therefore, jurisprudential or scientific discussion defeats their claim, because there is a difference between death and killing. Death is the taking of life without the removal of the intention, whereas killing is first the removal of the [animal's] structure, so the soul departs and the blood remains in the body. Moreover, does the Legislator, who is the Supreme Lord, take wisdom from us, or is the wisdom with Him alone?

It has become clear to us in our age that non-believers have begun to discover that carrion contains all the harmful waste, and they have discovered how to remove the harmful waste from the animals they wish to eat. This is because the structure of an animal's body resembles the structure of the human body. It eats, digests, and absorbs nutritious elements so that blood and energy are formed. In the body there are organs that filter and purify the body from harmful poisons. The kidney, for example, filters the blood of urea and other substances. The blood travels through the lungs to take in oxygen. All of this serves to free the body from harmful waste. The blood vessels of humans and animals contain good blood and bad blood, and the bad blood is that which has not been purified. When the animal is slaughtered, the bad blood and other [matter] flow out. That is to say, we sacrifice the good blood in order to protect ourselves from the bad blood. But if it dies without slaughter, the traces of both bloods remain, along with the traces of the waste that should have been expelled. This is what we do in this matter. But do we, before the Truth, the Glorified and Exalted, have any reasoning in anything other than confirming the ruling and being at peace that it came from Him, the Majestic in power?

Their argument was that they said: "You eat what you kill, and you do not eat what Allah kills. You consider yourselves better than Allah." This is a fabrication from them. Furthermore, when an animal dies, the name of Allah has not been mentioned over it, but over the slaughtered animal that we slaughter the name of Allah is mentioned. So it is as if the Truth, the Glorified and Exalted, is clarifying: "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned," that is, excluding carrion and what is slaughtered for idols.

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs (118)﴾ [Surah al-An'am]

Accepting any ruling from the Truth is never valid by first searching for its reason and only then believing in it. Rather, after we trust that it is from Allah, in whom we have believed, we must take the ruling that Allah has commanded.

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, when He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to? And indeed, many lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors (116)﴾ [Surah al-An'am]. As we have learned, the two verses have a occasion of revelation, namely that some of the opponents of the Messenger of Allah, who stood against the call with the stance of denial and worked to nullify and eliminate it, used to spread rumours among the believers that could weaken their creed. So they presented this issue, which in its outward form is a case of doubt-raising. They presented the matter in this inconsistent form, for who was the one who killed? They said: "The carrion was killed by Allah." Did Allah cut its neck? Did Allah strike it on the head and kill the basis of the administration of life, which is the brain? Did He aim something at its heart? Glorified and Exalted is He above such human acts. So how do they call death killing? To call death killing is the error. Their saying, "How do you permit for yourselves what you have killed," namely by slaughter, "and not permit what Allah has killed," namely caused to die, contains a sophistry in presenting the matter. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, wants to place in the believers an immunity against these anxieties that they raise. So He said: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs (118)﴾. And what is the meaning of mention (dhikr)? The scholars' failure to define the intended meaning of mention is what created a great dispute among them. Our master, Imam Malik, holds that if you slaughter and do not mention the name of Allah, whether you were forgetful or deliberate, it is not valid for you to eat of the animal. Imam Abu Hanifa holds: if you did not mention [the name] out of forgetfulness, then eat what you slaughtered; but if you were deliberate, then do not eat. And Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, holds: as long as you are a believer and facing the slaughter, and you are a believer, then eat of what you did not mention the name of Allah over, whether forgetfully or deliberately, because your faith is the mention of Allah.

And we say: what is mention? Is mention that you say it with the tongue? Or is mention that a thing passes through the mind? If you say that mention is with the tongue, then let us examine the sacred hadith in which Allah, the Exalted, said: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs."(1)

So our Lord has called the thought that passes through the self "mention," and by this it becomes the right of Imam al-Shafi'i to say what he said.

Therefore I say: we must first define the meaning of mention in order to end the dispute over this issue. It is not acceptable to wage a battle over the meaning of "mention," because mention, which is the matter coming to mind, may be accompanied by the matter coming to the tongue along with its coming to mind, and it may remain only coming to mind, as is evident from the hadith mentioned above. When the believer finds many things before him, there may be something beautiful and another that has no beauty at all. The buffalo is less beautiful than some of the animals that Allah has forbidden to eat, yet the believers turn to slaughtering the buffalo to eat from it, and we have never heard of a Muslim approaching an animal whose eating Allah has forbidden in order to slaughter it. Why? Because the believer turns to what Allah has made lawful, and this turning is evidence that he has remembered in his self, or in his speech, the One who makes lawful and forbids, which is Allah. So his choosing an animal for slaughter is evidence that he has remembered Allah in the self or in speech. By this we agree that the believer's mention is in his heart, whether he speaks or not, and the dispute on this matter ends. Thus Imam al-Shafi'i relied on this matter, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was asked about a Muslim's eating from an animal slaughtered by someone whom he does not know, and whether that person had said the name of Allah or had not, he clarified to the questioner: "Say the name and eat."

Now, a person does not always attend the moment of slaughter, and it is enough for him to bring to mind the lawful and the forbidden at the time of eating. The Truth, the Glorified and Exalted, clarifies to us: "Mention the name of Allah," and He, glorified, knows that you turn to things in order to do them. These things divide into two kinds: a kind that passes through your mind before you do it, and a kind that does not pass through your mind, but which you do automatically without anything passing through the mind. An example of this is all the reflexive acts that a person performs; they do not pass through his mind. If someone were to try to put his finger in another's eye, that other person would close his eyes automatically. This differs from the act that you think about before you do it. The act that a person performs after it has passed through his mind is an act of consequence (dhu bal). Therefore the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wished not to burden us with hardship or difficulty, so he said:

"Every matter of consequence that is not begun with the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, is cut off."(2)

The matter of consequence is the matter that has come to your mind, whether you should do it or not. So Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, only imposes on us [the mention] at the matter that passes through the thought, because when you turn to any act, it responds to you as you wish. This is from the bounty of Allah to you. When you slaughter a calf, or a sheep, and you reflect on how Allah has empowered you over this living creature, you did not do this to make all creatures subject to you by Allah's power. Therefore you slaughter it in the name of Allah.

So there are many matters and acts of consequence that pass over you, and it is from good manners and faith that you turn to them in the name of Allah. Therefore some people err when they think that when a person slaughters an animal he is harming it. No! Slaughtering this animal is the completion of its task in life, because it was created for this purpose and made submissive to it.

We said earlier: there is a marvel among the marvels of actual practices. This marvel is that when you come to animals that Allah has not made lawful for humans, such as the donkey for example, if these animals are subjected to something that kills them, such as a rope wrapped around their neck and they are strangled, they die without stretching their neck forward. But the animal that Allah has made lawful for eating, such as the buffalo, the sheep, or the calf, we find that such an animal, if it is strangled, stretches its head forward. The people of the countryside in Egypt say: "It is seeking what is lawful," that is, slaughter. So the slaughter of the animal is not called aggression against it, because the animal was created for this task.

Therefore the meaning of the phrase "in the name of Allah" is that I have not dared to do this act except within the scope of the name of Allah, who has made this lawful for me.

After that, the Truth says to the believers: do not listen to the words of the disbelievers. Then comes the rhetorical question: "And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned?" The meaning: what reason prevents you from eating of what the name of Allah has been mentioned over? He has detailed for you what has been forbidden to you, and that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned is not among the prohibited things that Allah has specified. Our Lord, glorified, is the One who makes lawful and forbids. And if it is said: since some [of the things] have been forbidden to us, …

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim; al-Tirmidhi.
2 Narrated by 'Abd al-Qadir al-Rahawi in al-Arba'in from Abu Hurayrah.

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit.﴾ (6:120)

These are the legislations of heaven that protect society from its own members, so that no one's eye falls upon another's transgression. When your eye falls upon a transgression by someone else, the transgression is something that can be perceived, but it is not all the corruption in society. The corruption of society comes from many things that do not fall within the scope of perception. There are things rooted in the wellsprings of the human soul from which the factors of inclination arise; so before an outward sin exists, an inward sin exists, and the inward sin precedes the outward sin. All human legislation protects us from outward sin, but the method of heaven protects us from the corruption of both outward sin and inward sin.

The Truth clarifies for us the difference between human legislation for humans and the legislation of God. He, glory be to Him, is watchful over your inner feelings, your conscience, and your secrets. So beware lest you commit the inward sin. It is not enough that you protect yourself from the law seeing you, because the most that law can do is prevent people from flaunting crime and committing it openly. The difference between the legislation of heaven and the legislation of earth is that earthly legislation protects people from outward sin, while the legislation of heaven protects people from both outward sin and inward sin, and inward sin is the most violent kind of sin on earth.

Some who are practiced in earning evil, through their training in evil, find it easy to do evil, as if they were doing a matter to which they have become accustomed without deliberation.

As we know, "kasaba" (to earn) is used in general usage for good, while "iktasaba" (to acquire, with effort) is used for evil, because in good the practical action proceeds smoothly along with all the faculties, with no contrivance in it. Whoever wants, for example, to buy something from a shop goes to the shop in broad daylight and buys. But whoever wants to steal arranges the theft in a different manner, and this is contrivance. Yet contrivance may, through much practice and habituation, come to require no agitation, because it has become a kind of earning. "Yaksibun" (they earn) indicates gain, because "kasaba" indicates that you took the principal and an increase over the principal. A person who does good gives his own soul the foundations of life and takes an increased reward in the Hereafter, and this is the peak of earning.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, desires from the servant in his movement that he achieve for himself a benefit for which he has need, but a person may achieve what benefits him at the time of need, and then harm arises from that act afterward. Therefore God protects the believing person through the method, so that he distinguishes between what achieves for him the present aim and achieves a lasting benefit without bringing him evil, and what achieves for him a quick benefit whose consequence is grievous and whose end is painful. We find that those who commit evil deeds and incline toward desires, for example, achieve for themselves a temporary benefit, like the student who pays no attention to his lessons, who sleeps and does not wake up, and who, if they wake him and take him out of the house, goes off to loiter in the streets. In the apparent matter, he achieves for his self a comfort, but its outcome is failure. Whereas we find that whoever strives, works hard, and toils has achieved for himself a lasting benefit that is not followed by regret.

﴿Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit.﴾ (6:120)

In this world we find that recompense comes from humans to humans, but what of the moment of being presented before God, who knows the outward sin and the inward sin?

So what protects society is the heavenly legislation, for the method does not only protect a person from those around him, but also legislates the movement of the person so that it is correct.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 121:

The discourse returns, after that, to the matter of food, and so He says:

﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiance. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you are then associating others with Allah.﴾ (121)

Here Allah calls what has not had the name of Allah mentioned over it "fisq" (defiance, transgression), and this is what another verse explains and makes manifest by a specific name:

﴿Say, "I do not find within that which has been revealed to me [anything] forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be dead meat or blood spilled out or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure; or it be deviance (fisqan) [slaughtered] for other than Allah."...﴾ (145) [Surah al-An'am]

So "fisqan" is conjoined to "dead meat," "spilled blood," and "the flesh of swine," but He, glory be to Him, separated the conjoined term, which is (fisqan), from the term it is conjoined to. A ruling that pertains to the term it is conjoined to applies to it, and this ruling is "rijs" (impurity). Thus the three prohibited items took on the ruling of "rijs." He then conjoined to them what is slaughtered with the name of other than Allah, such as idols, and it has combined both "rijs" and "fisq."

And Allah says: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies﴾. Glory be to Him wishes to show us that the sound innate nature, which is not inclined by desire, reaches the realities of good. That is why we find that those who urge and incite one another to evil, and who teach one another secretly, are in effect taking the station of the devil through whispering and inciting to disobedience and disbelief; for the innate matter rejects this. When a person commits one of the destructive sins, he only contrives and maneuvers to reach committing that sin, and he may inspire that to someone else, guiding him to corruption. He thereby stands in the station of the devils who inspire their allies with hidden information; for the sound innate nature rejects evil things and also stands against them, and it does not allow them to advance toward evil except for desire. So if a devil of mankind or a devil of the jinn wishes to make an action appealing to people, he does not announce it directly. Rather, he wraps and circles around with a wrapped, adorned speech.

﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you, and if you obey them, indeed you are then associating others with Allah.﴾ In this there is an allusion to the saying of the polytheists: "You eat what you have killed yourselves, and you do not eat what Allah has killed, and you are more entitled to eat what Allah has killed."

﴿...And if you obey them, indeed you are then associating others with Allah.(121)﴾ [Surah al-An'am]

It is as though mere obedience to these polytheists is a form of shirk, because the meaning of worship is the compliance and submission of a worshipper to a worshipped one in commands and prohibitions. So if you take a command from other than Allah, it removes you from the core and heart of His method, and by that you have associated others with Him.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-An'am (6), verse 122

Then the Truth (al-Haqq), exalted is He, says:

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness and cannot emerge from it? Thus the deeds of the disbelievers have been made attractive to them.﴾

Allah, exalted and glorified, as we have known, presents some matters not as a plain report from Him, but in the form of a question. This is because He, may He be exalted, knows that when a question comes to you and you turn your mind to answer it, you will find only one answer, which is the one the Truth wants. So the style is sometimes declarative, or it is a question whose expected answer is affirmative or a question whose expected answer is negative. When He, glory be to Him, presents the matter we are dealing with, He makes clear, and He is the All-Knowing, that if you wish to answer, you will find only the answer the Truth wants.

In this noble verse we find death and life, and darkness and light.

What is life? Life is the existence of a being in a state that enables it to carry out the task required of it. As long as a thing is in a state in which it performs its task, there is life in it. The highest level of life is that in which movement, sense perception and thought are combined, and all of these are found in the human being. As for the animal, it has sense perception and movement but no thought. Yet the animal has an instinct stronger than human thought; it is governed by instinct in some things and by choice in others. You have no role in instinct, but in the sphere of choice you have a role: you can do it or you can refrain from doing it.

So life is that a being be in a state by which it performs the task required of it. On this basis there is life in the human being, life in the animal, life in the plant, and life in the inanimate, and as science advances it establishes for us the "lives" of many things we used to think had no life in them. Although it appears to us in chemical reactions that some things transform into other things, for example, the animal has life; when we slaughter it, eat it, and throw away its bones, those bones had a kind of life, and then its parts became inanimate with a life of their own kind, as is proven by the fact that after some time the bone crumbles.

In former times in the countryside we used to milk the milk into clay vessels and place them in warm places, and the milk would remain for a week in the warm place, and it would be sweeter on its day than the day before. The milk would grow sweeter each day, and then the farmer's wife would take the last of the cream and make from it cheese of a pleasant taste, or butter. But after we boiled the milk, we find it spoils after several hours, because when you placed it in the warm place you kept it alive, so its life remained vigorous, but when you boiled it you killed the life in it. If you do not put it in a refrigerator, it must rot. The meaning of rotting is that it no longer performs its task as milk; rather it has passed into another life by the action of bacteria and others. Life is only taken away by destruction, and this is what the Truth said:

﴿Everything perishes except His Face.﴾ [Surah al-Qasas, 88]

So do not take the dead to be a thing with no life in it; rather it has passed into a second life.

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people...﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 122]

It is as though the human being has life in his own self, and then the Truth made for him a light by which he walks. It is as though life is transferred among things, and a human being needs life, and needs light by which the appearances of things become clear. In former times people believed that a person sees when a ray goes out from his eye to the object seen, until the Arab Muslim Ibn al-Haytham came. He said this was an opinion that missed the truth regarding the law of light, and he said: a person sees because a ray from the seen object reaches the eye of the one who sees. The proof is that if the object is in light a person perceives it, and if it is in darkness a person does not perceive it; had rays gone out from the human eye, he would see things equally whether they were in light or in darkness. All the theories of light were corrected at the hands of this Muslim scholar, and after that came photographic images and cinema. So light is the means to visible things.

In the sensory matters of the cosmos, the Truth leaves indications of non-sensory matters. The sensible light we see is either sunlight, or moonlight, or lamplight, or something else, and this is what enables a person to see things. To see things means to deal with them in a beneficial, non-harmful way. We light the lamp with electricity when natural light, the sunlight, is absent, and when we light our lamps we see things and interact with them, and we do not break them nor they us, and each of us takes from the light according to his capacity. So each person lights the dark place he is forced into by the absence of the natural source, according to his ability; when the sun rises we extinguish all our lamps. This is one of the sensible, tangible signs of the cosmos, from which we take a proof that if God gives us a light of values, we should not bring values from ourselves, as long as His values exist.

Allah shows us that a human being without values is a dead moving thing, and the method comes to him so that he may live a high life. He, glory be to Him, says to every person: be eager for the second, eternal life that does not end, and this is not attained except by following the method. Beware of thinking that life is only what you see in existence, for if this were the ultimate goal of life, a person would not feel happiness; for if this world were our goal, our share of this world would have to be one and the same, our lifespans one and the same, and our conditions one and the same. The difference in them, in length and in condition, is proof that it is not the goal, because the goal of what is equal must itself be equal.

So the word of God is the decisive word: ﴿Indeed, the Last Abode—that is the [true] life.﴾ [Surah al-'Ankabut, 64]

This is the life that is not lost from you, nor are you lost from it; its good does not escape you, nor do you escape it. So the one who lives the first, sensory life, which is movement through the breathing of the spirit into matter, is a moving dead thing.

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks﴾ (part of verse 122, Surah al-An'am)

That is, He, glory be to Him, has given such a servant an eternal life and a light by which he walks, which is not broken and does not break.

As for the one who says that worldly life, in its worldly meaning, does not differ from life in the light of faith, to such a one we say: No, there is no equality between them; they are different, as shown by the Truth's saying:

﴿Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life.﴾ [Surah al-Anfal, 24]

He, glory be to Him, addresses them, and since He addresses them, they are alive by ordinary law; but He, glory be to Him, sent down to His Messenger the method by which the believer lives a high life. Take note that the Truth, exalted is He, gave and bestowed the first spirit which He breathes into matter so that it moves and feels the life of this world; He gave it to both believer and disbeliever. Then He brings a second spirit that gives eternal life. For this reason the method of God for His creation was called a spirit:

﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command.﴾ [Surah al-Shura, 52]

So the method gives eternal life.

Thus the saying of the Truth, ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, means: or one who was astray and We guided him, or one who was a disbeliever and We made him a believer. Note that there is "mayyit" (with light stress) and "mayyit" (with shadda). The mayyit is one who is destined to die even if he is alive; each of us is mayyit even while alive. But the mayit is one who has actually died, whose soul has been taken and expelled. For this reason the Truth addresses His Prophet (ﷺ) saying to him: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die.﴾

That is, you are heading toward death, even if you are alive now, because each of us continues in life until he takes on the attribute of perishing. The Truth says: ﴿So We gave him life﴾, that is, through the method that gives him a second life; and for this reason the Qur'an was called a spirit, and the one to whom the Qur'an was revealed was also called a spirit.

﴿And made for him a light by which he walks among the people.﴾ Why does he walk among the people specifically, and not among all things? Because other things may be something you can encompass, but the word "people" expresses the difficult interaction, since they are people of changing states. The Truth continues: ﴿like one who is in darkness, not coming out of it.﴾ This is a question whose answer is: No. That is, the two are not equal to each other, just as we say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? The natural disposition here says: No, just as natural disposition affirms that darkness and light are not equal, or the shade and the scorching heat. Here God entrusts us with the answer, because He knows that if the matter is put forward as a question and an interrogation, we will find only one answer, which is what the Truth wants to state as a declaration.

The Truth concludes the verse: ﴿Thus the deeds of the disbelievers have been made attractive to them.﴾

The meaning here is that We left them exposed to being moved by the adornment, and the Truth did not protect them with infallibility in their choice, because He, glory be to Him, left choice free for the human being:

﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve.﴾ [Surah al-Kahf, 29]

Almighty Allah says next:

﴿And thus have We placed in every town its greatest criminals to plot within it. But they plot only against themselves, and they do not perceive. (123)﴾

His words, glorified is He, "And thus" indicate that one thing is likened to another. Just as there existed in Makkah those who take you as an enemy, oppose you, and stand against you in the matter of calling to Allah and turn away from the path of truth, this is a matter in which there is no novelty for the Messengers. This issue is a prevailing matter with every Messenger in the procession of faith. "Thus," meaning: just as We placed in Makkah criminals who plot, We placed in every town that preceded this matter with a Messenger who came before, so it was not a novelty among the Messengers. Since you were not a novelty among the Messengers, be patient in this as the Messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-azm) were patient. You are more deserving of patience than they, because the opposition you face is in proportion to the scope of your mission throughout the entire universe. Every Messenger came to a limited nation to treat a limited ailment in a limited time.

You, however, came with a universal matter in time and place until the Hour is established. Therefore the hardships that confront you must be commensurate with the comprehensiveness of your message, with which Allah has singled you out.

﴿And thus have We placed in every town its greatest criminals.. (123)﴾

The word "ijram" (criminality) derives from the root J-R-M: al-jarm, al-jurm, and al-jarimah. It carries the meaning of severing. "Mujrimiha" is the plural of mujrim, and mujrim is from ajrama, meaning he committed a crime or offense. The meaning is that he severs himself through the crime from the society in which he lives. He isolates himself for no benefit to anyone except his own benefit, as though he carried out an act of social isolation, making everything for himself and not making himself for anyone, because he wants to fulfill the desires of his own self without concern for the consequences that follow from that.

Thus criminality is the undertaking of abominations in a manner that makes a person isolate himself from the good of his society, because he wants everything for himself. As long as he wants everything for himself, the element of domination is present in him, and he commits vices. Because he commits vices, he wants vices of this kind to spread throughout the whole society, so that he does not feel that there is someone better than him.

﴿... to plot within it. But they plot only against themselves, and they do not perceive. (123)﴾

Plotting (makr), as we know, derives from the intertwining of branches with one another, so tightly that if you hold a leaf from the top you cannot say this leaf is from this branch, because the branches and twigs are wrapped, interlaced, and braided together. The schemer does this because he wants to wrap his scheme so that it is not uncovered. As long as he does this, know from the outset that he is weak in constitution, for if he did not know the weakness of his constitution he would not plot, since the strong never plot; rather they confront. That is why the poet says:

"A weak one, when it hits an opportunity, kills; thus is the power of the weak."

The weak, when he gains power, tells himself that this opportunity will not recur, so he finishes off his opponent for fear that another opportunity will not come. But the strong, when his opponent comes to him and he seizes him, may tell himself to let him go, and when this opponent commits a new folly, he punishes him. So only the weak plots. The Exalted Lord, in this matter, speaks of the criminals among the greatest people, that is, those who control the destinies of people, corrupt them, and no one can stand against them. There are many verses related to this matter, and some of them have been subject to dispute and disagreement; strangely, the disagreement has not been settled, and each group of scholars holds to its own opinion. This verse about which we are reflecting connects with the word of truth:

﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they defy therein; so the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it with complete destruction. (16)﴾ [Surat al-Isra']

This verse contains a difficulty, and a battle arose among scholars because of it. Some of them say: "How can Allah command people to defy?" They tried to find an interpretation for this, saying that the Truth compelled and forced the greatest people to defiance. The other side of the scholars said: No, the Truth does not compel humans to defiance; rather, when a person reads the word "command of Allah" in His method, he must know that this command is liable to be obeyed and liable to be disobeyed, because the one commanded, who is the responsible person, is capable of not doing it, and the commander has commanded something while the one commanded has the right of choice. Thus you find that the greatest of the people encountered Allah's command with disobedience, because the Truth is the one who says:

﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah.. (5)﴾ [Surat al-Bayyinah], and defiance is then consequent upon the choice of the one commanded.

When we reflect with insight on the meaning of "the command of Allah," we find that the command of Allah is manifested in the natural cosmic creations, and no one has the ability to oppose Allah in that. He is the one who says: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

The command of Allah is also manifested in legislation, and to the humans to whom these legislations were sent is the choice between obedience and disobedience. And He, glorified, says about the command of legislation: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah.﴾

When the Truth says: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they defy therein.﴾

He, glorified, does not destroy that town unjustly; rather He sends them the method. If they obey, then welcome and well-come; if they disobey, then punishment by destruction is inevitable for them.

Thus we see that the scholars who thought that defiance is consequent upon the command from Allah did not notice that the command in the Qur'an comes in two modes: first, the command of creation by compulsions, which the one commanded cannot fail to fulfill, and the compulsory command is represented by the word of the Truth:

﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin, 82)

So the command is ready in the realm of eternity to manifest when the Truth wills. The second command is the legislative command, which is suitable for the responsible person to choose between obeying or disobeying. In this framework we understand the word of the Truth:

﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they defy therein; so the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it with complete destruction. (16)﴾ (Surat al-Isra')

So do not say that Allah commands defiance; the Truth has commanded the believers with the method, for He, glorified, does not command abomination. Rather the command came to all of mankind to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, but the great ones of that town took the alternative to obedience, which is defiance and disobedience. So when He commanded them and they defied, what does He do with them? He, glorified, destroys them with destruction. As for the first command in the cosmic matters, no one among Allah's creation is responsible in cosmic matters; and as for His second command in following the method, we may understand that it is choice.

Thus we know and understand the meaning of this verse so that it connects with the verse about which we are reflecting: that is, "And when We intend to destroy a town, We sent it a method, and its greatest ones were a bad example, and they defied by not obeying the method of Allah, so the word became due against it, and We destroyed it with complete destruction." Likewise we also understand the word of the Truth: ﴿But they plot only against themselves, and they do not perceive﴾, because the schemer intends by plotting to achieve something by a crooked path, since he is weak and cannot face realities, and these realities are received by the sound nature, while he wants to falsify the matter to this nature, therefore he twists. To such a schemer we say: You want to achieve for yourself immediate good and a temporary desire, but if you were to bring to mind the punishment that arises from this matter for you, and likewise your punishment for having misled others, you would see how evil comes.

﴿But they plot only against themselves, and they do not perceive.﴾ (part of verse 123, Surat al-An'am)

That is, they do not know, because they do not weigh matters with the precision that leads to true benefit.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 124:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of God." God knows best where to place His message. Those who committed crime will suffer humiliation before God and a severe punishment for their scheming.﴾

It is as though the sign that God sent with His Messenger, namely the Qur'an, to establish for them the truthfulness of his conveying of the message from God, did not satisfy them, and they were not content with it. Rather, they demanded other signs, and they said:

﴿And they say: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee."﴾ [Surat al-Isra']

They do not want to believe; rather they engage in obstinate dispute and seek ways of escape from faith. Therefore you find that all the arguments they put forward against the call of the Messenger are falsehoods. They said that he is a sorcerer who separates a man from his wife and a son from his father, and who brings, with what he has brought, and claims that it is from God, discord into a single family.

But why did they not ask: since he has bewitched others, why has he not bewitched us? Did they themselves refuse sorcery? Does the one who is bewitched have any desire or choice with the sorcerer? In this they are liars.

Then they said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is a poet. Had anyone other than them said such words, it would have been acceptable, because he would be ignorant of the Messenger of God, and because he is not of a people who are the masters of eloquence, rhetoric and clear expression; they know poetry, prose, oratory and writing. If this matter had come from someone other than them, the statement would have been acceptable. Therefore you find among them one whose soul is pure who says: "By God, it is neither the speech of a soothsayer nor the speech of a poet." The Truth asks them not to speak with a crowd's opinion, for in crowd opinion truth becomes mixed and confused with falsehood. Rather, He asked them to make their speech precise, so that each word is attributed to its speaker, and so the Truth says:

﴿Say: "I exhort you to one thing: that you stand before God in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion."﴾ [Surat Saba', 46]

That is, do not come in the midst of people's agitation and accuse the Messenger (ﷺ) of madness, for your speech in collective frenzy is not reckoned as the judgement of any one of you. Rather, what is required is that you stand for God in pairs (mathna), that is two by two, and each two say: come, let us examine the affair of this Messenger and see his claims: is he a soothsayer? Is he a sorcerer? Is he a poet? Between two people the truth is never lost, because each argues with the other, and when two sit to debate, if one of them is defeated by the other he is not disgraced before others. But when three or four debate, each one fears being defeated before the rest, and each one defends himself. Therefore when two sit together to discuss and examine any matter, neither fears defeat; so the command comes from God that they stand for God in pairs or singly, and each of them recalls the matter of this Messenger: is he mad?

The actions of a madman are disjointed and not upright. Muhammad (ﷺ) possesses a tremendous character (khuluq 'azim), and would one say of a madman that he has a tremendous character? For a person does not know how the madman will confront him: will he strike him, insult him, or tear his clothes? As for the "tremendous character," its meaning is a character regulated and grounded in values, and the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was regulated by values until it became a habit (malaka) and not a contrived matter. When people say of a person that his character is generosity, meaning that the quality of generosity has become so deeply rooted in him that acts of giving issue from him with ease, then when a quality takes firm hold of the soul it becomes character, and acts issue from the soul with ease. In the works of meanings we call this a character (khuluq), and in the works of matter we call it mechanism (aliyya).

We all know that if a person wishes to learn to drive a car, he learns the actions that make the car move until he acquires the skill and performs them with ease and without difficulty. Likewise is the case with character, when actions issue from a person through practice and skill. For example, we find one who studies jurisprudence (fiqh), and when someone asks him about the ruling on a specific matter, he reviews the matter from every angle over a long time; but one who has trained makes jurisprudence a habit (malaka) for himself, so he does not tire in deriving the ruling. So it is with character.

The Truth clarifies for them: you say of the Messenger that he is mad, so sit in pairs or singly and study his conduct; you will find that his conduct is logical, built upon a complete and perfected character, and it is certainly a conduct different from that of a madman, for the madman has no control over his movements, nor over his stillness, nor over what he does or leaves undone. Likewise he cannot be a poet, for you yourselves are people of poetry; and likewise he is not a soothsayer, for soothsayers may sell the signs of God for a small price, whereas he is the one who announced to you his rejection of kingship, wealth and status. Yet they said:

﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of God..."﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 124]

Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira himself spoke of this, and he was older than the Messenger of God in years, rich in wealth, and had in his household the prestige and the son. He said: if prophethood were by all these things, I would be more worthy of it, because I am older, because I have more wealth, and because I have more children. He measured it by human standards, as though al-Walid did not know that the message is not leadership. If you alone among others possess wealth, children, and crops, and more, yet you are not of the character of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom God created with that nature and prepared and chose to be a messenger, then the matter is not in your favour. Nevertheless, some of them said:

﴿And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two cities?"﴾ [Surat al-Zukhruf, 31]

Let us hear the Qur'an's reply:

﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?...﴾ [Surat al-Zukhruf, 32]

The Truth clarifies for them: We apportion among them the matters of life, but you want to divide the mercy of God. There is a difference between mercy in the messages and the prolongation of life through sustenance and wealth, for these are gifts of lordship (rububiyya), whereas mercy is a gift of divinity (uluhiyya). You were distinguished in your worldly life by wealth, sons and gardens, not because of any special quality in you, but because the order of the whole universe needs complementary gifts, not repeated gifts. If all people possessed what you have, O al-Walid, of land and wealth, you would not find anyone to cultivate your land for you, nor anyone to saddle your horse for you. Therefore God made the matter of wealth to be in rotation (duwal), that is, He turns these matters so that they circulate among people; they belong to one at one time and to another at another time, and they remain for no one.

When people came to Abu Jahl to talk to him about the message, he said: "Banu 'Abd Manaf have competed with us in honour; they fed and we fed, they gave and we gave, they slaughtered and we slaughtered, until we became like two horses in a race. They said: 'Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes.' By God, we will never accept him or follow him unless revelation comes to us as it comes to him." The meaning of "like two horses in a race" is this: when horses set off in a race at one time, at the finish they used to drive a stick into the ground, and whoever pulled it from the ground was said to have won the prize (hāza qaṣab al-sabq), and the stick (qaṣaba) is the goal of the course, so that no one could say that he had beaten him by a step or otherwise.

Here the Truth says: (And when a sign comes to them).

Look at the phrase "a sign came to them": at one point He says: ﴿We have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾, and at another He says "a sign came to them", as though the sign has reached such clarity, such independence, such self-sufficiency and such distinction that it comes on its own.

﴿They say: "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of God..."﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 124]

God says to them in reply: do not propose this to God, for "God knows best where to place His message," because the message comes to spread good among all, but it keeps itself pure from the effects of benefiting from that good. The one who benefits wants good to come to him and then leaves some of it unclaimed except for delivering it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded, before his death, that his family should not take the zakat; what he left became charity for the people, meaning he did not benefit from it in this world. Therefore he was trusted with the message, and did not want to take the world so that his family might inherit it after him. God willed him to be so, so that his good would be for all people. The message is an obligation, and the reward of prophethood is not here; rather, part of the greatness of the reward is that it is in the Hereafter. Therefore when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to the pledge of 'Aqaba and they said: "Stipulate for yourself," he said: "That you protect me as you protect yourselves, and that you do such and such."

They said to him: "What is for us? You have stipulated for yourself; what is there for us if we fulfil it?" What did the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say? He said: "For you is Paradise." This is the price he had, so whoever wants Paradise comes to faith, and whoever wants what is less than Paradise does not belong among the people of faith. Although he told them later that you will ride ships and spread out cushions and carpets and sit upon them, and gave them glad tidings of abundance, he did not say that to them from the beginning, because some of them would not attain worldly good with Islam; rather they would die while Islam was weak and its followers few. So he gave them the guaranteed reward for all of them when they said: "What if we fulfil it?" He said: "For you is Paradise." It is as though the Messenger (ﷺ) was teaching them that the world is too small to be the reward of righteous deeds; the reward of righteous deeds is eternal, neither escaping you nor you escaping it.

﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe..."﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 124]
