When we reflect on their saying "We will not believe," we find in this saying an insistence on unbelief, that is, "we will not believe even in the future"; they have passed judgement on the future. Then God exposes them: some of them die in disbelief, and those who remain come to faith after the conquest. Strangely, the expression they utter is a shaky one that does not agree with the logic of their disbelief. They said: "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of God," as though they knew that there are messengers from God. The original point of the verse is that they should believe in the messengers of God, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is the seal of the messengers. This saying indicates mere opposition combined with stupidity, for since you know that God has messengers whom He chooses, how do you try to determine God's will in the choosing?

The messengers of God had cosmic signs, perceptible and visible; and although they had the compelling force of a visible spectacle, they had no permanence. Whoever saw Moses striking the sea so that it split would not deny this cosmic sign, but it became a report, and a report suits the limited scope of Moses' message. Likewise the message of Jesus, peace be upon him, in which he healed the blind and the leper by God's permission. These were messages for a limited time and limited people. But the Messenger (ﷺ) came with the enduring miracle-method that lasts until the Hour is established. If the miracle is perceptible, only specific people will see it, because a perceptible matter does not recur, but ends; whereas our master Muhammad is a messenger until the Hour comes. Therefore he must have a sign that remains until the Hour; so the sign was in the realm of meanings and intellects, in which nations do not differ and times do not differ. But they wanted a perceptible miracle and another intellectual one, so that when only one came they rejected the second. Thus the Truth settled the matter and said: ﴿God knows best where to place His message.﴾

If they had considered the words ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾, the word "knows best" indicates that God may enable some of His creation to learn why God chose Muhammad (ﷺ). For those whom the Prophet (ﷺ) confronted with the matter of the call, did they expect from him a sign or miracle, or did they believe simply upon being informed? They believed simply upon being informed, because their experience of him confirmed that he was truthful and trustworthy regarding the news of the earth; would he lie about a matter of the heavens?

We find that our master Abu Bakr, as soon as he learned of the matter of the message, said: "You have spoken the truth," and our mistress Khadija believed him from the moment he said

Then the Exalted comes to us with a matter over which the apologetic argument arises for some people who have transgressed against themselves, and who wish to make their excess in sins subject to the notion that God willed it of them. So He says, may He be glorified:

﴿So whomever God wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight, as if he were climbing up into the sky. Thus God places defilement upon those who do not believe.﴾ (6:125)

We find someone who says: when our Lord wills for a person to have his breast expanded to Islam, that is from the will of God, so what then is the fault of the one held accountable?

In answer to this we say: we have already known that guidance has two meanings. The first meaning: indication (al-dalalah), which is something that comes and is obligatory even for the disbeliever. For God's guidance to the disbeliever is that He indicates to him the path of good. But there is another kind of guidance, which is for the one who has believed, and who becomes worthy of God's assistance (ma'unah), by lightening for him the burdens of the obligations, making them easy for him, and causing him to love all the commands and to love aversion and withdrawal from all the prohibitions.

Some of the righteous said: "O God, I fear that You will not reward me for an act of obedience, because I have come to crave it." It is as if he had come to love obedience to the point that there was no longer any hardship or obligation in it. Therefore he is fearful, as if he had understood that hardship must exist. This righteous person, we say: you have lost the sense of the hardship of obligation because you loved it, so you became accustomed to worship as it became accustomed to you and loved you, and attraction arose between you and obedience. You made the Messenger of God (ﷺ) an example and a model for you. For he (ﷺ) would see that when the call to prayer was made, people would rise to it lazily, yet he (ﷺ) would say to Bilal when the time of prayer came: "Give us rest with it, O Bilal."

This is other than what some of those who perform prayer now say, where one of them says: "Come, let us pray to remove it from our backs." These perform it out of obligation, not out of love and passion. As for those who have become accustomed to finding rest in prayer, when a matter troubles them and grows hard upon them, a matter beyond the scope of their means, one of them says: "Since prayer brings rest to the heart, let me go to it and meet my Lord, beyond what He has obligated on me, drawing near to Him through supererogatory acts." For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when a matter distressed him, would rise to prayer. To be distressed (huzziba) means that human means cannot bear him up. So he rises to prayer, and this is a logical matter, and to God belongs the highest likeness.

When one of us was a child and something troubled him, he would go to his father. So what of us when something troubles us beyond the means given to us by God? To whom do we turn? We turn to our Lord, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would, when a matter distressed him, rise to prayer.

So love of obligation is a sign that you have tasted the sweetness of obedience, though it may be that it is hard upon you, because it first takes you out of what you have become accustomed to through habit. When a matter of hardship comes to you, you say: this hardship is only meant by Him to bring me a good reward. When you come to love prayer, it becomes love for you, and one of the righteous, as you have said, feared that he would not be rewarded for prayer because it had become a craving of the soul. The human being is obliged to fight his soul in its desires. But the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set us the example when he said: "None of you believes until his desire becomes subordinate to what I have brought." That is, what he desires comes to agree with the method of God. When the believer reaches and attains this station, he is indeed a good and upright servant.

Thus we have known that guidance is of two kinds: guidance in the sense of indication, and guidance in the sense of assistance.

So when you are convinced by the guidance of indication and believe in the truth, He lightens for you the matters of obligation and makes you a lover of them. For this reason the people of righteousness say: our Lord has enjoined upon us five prayers, and He deserves from us standing before Him more than five times; our Lord has enjoined upon us the zakat threshold, which is two and a half percent, and He deserves from us more than that, because He is the giver of everything. This is the love of obligation, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So whomever God wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam.﴾

﴿Whomever He wills to guide﴾ means He indicates to him, may He be glorified, as He indicates to all the servants the way. But the one who is convinced by the indication and believes finds the consequences of obligation easy, in confirmation of His saying, the Truth:

﴿And God increases those who are guided in guidance, and the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in return﴾ (19:76), Surah Maryam. This is the guidance of assistance. Here there is a difference between Islam and iman, because iman does not require only belief; rather it is the soul's bearing itself toward the requirements of faith. For this reason we find that the great men of Quraysh refused to say: "There is no god but God," because they knew it is not merely a word spoken, but has requirements that are wearisome in the obligations that result from it, in the form of "do" and "do not". Obligation says to you "do" concerning a thing that is hard for you, and says to you "do not" concerning a thing that is hard to leave. Therefore He says: ﴿So whomever God wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾ (part of 6:125), and He expands his breast to Islam after He knows that he has believed in the law of monotheism and is pleased with it and at peace with it. Then he comes to understand the obligations, because sound Islam requires submission to the matters of obligation. Whoever has taken the first guidance and believed in his Lord, God makes clear to him: "You have believed in Me and come to Me; therefore I lighten for you the consequences of action, and I expand his breast to Islam." Expansion of the breast may itself be a recompense. For He, may He be glorified, says: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ (94:1), Surah al-Sharh.

So our Lord has rewarded him with that, because he discharged what was upon him and persevered. It is as if God wants from the believer by faith that he turn toward the truth, and when he turns toward the truth, the servant seeks to know what is intended and required of him, and he learns that it is the obligations. So when God sees in you distinguished readiness to accept the obligations, He lightens them for you, not by reducing them, but by making you crave them. You may bind yourself to things beyond what God has obligated upon you, so that you become among the people of affection, and among the people of manifestations, and among those who enter into a mutual love with God. You consider yourself and say: God has obligated me with little, and He deserves much. So you increase your obedience, and before you is always the hadith qudsi:

"Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. And My servant continues to draw near to Me with supererogatory acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks." (1) That is, through matters that exceed what he was obligated to in prayer, zakat, fasting, and hajj.

So the meaning of "whomever God wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam" is that He makes the matters that some people think are tiring become, by his turning toward them and his love for them, restful, and he approaches them with longing and humility. Therefore the Exalted, may He be glorified, leaves among His creatures an example for people. We find wealth precious to the soul, and the soul is eager for it, because if wealth came by a way that God legislated and made lawful, it comes with toil and exertion; therefore a person clings to it. Yet God softens the servant's heart for giving and spending. We find the believer giving to the beggar, because the beggar is the bridge over which the Muslim travels to reward from God. The believing servant says to the beggar: "Welcome to one who has come to carry my provision to the Hereafter without a wage." For this reason, when a Muslim came to Imam Ali, may God be pleased with him and ennoble his face, the Muslim said: "I want to know whether I am of the people of this world or of the people of the Hereafter?"

Imam Ali chose a measure of faith in the soul of every believer, and said to him: "If someone who asks you comes, and someone who gives to you comes, and you are delighted by the one who gives you, you are of the people of this world; but if you are delighted by the one who takes from you, you are of the people of the Hereafter, because a person loves whoever builds up for him what he loves."

So "He expands his breast to Islam" means He lightens for him the hardships of obligation, to the point that there is no hardship, and then he rises to another elevation by loving it within obligation. God guides him to the path of Paradise, because there is guidance to the method and guidance to the reward for the method. For this reason we find the Qur'an saying, concerning those who went astray:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, God would never forgive them, nor guide them to a path, except the path of Hell.﴾ (4:168-169), Surah al-Nisa'.

It is as if there is guidance to action and guidance to reward. And we find the Truth saying:

﴿And those who are killed in the cause of God, He will not let their deeds be lost. He will guide them and set right their affairs, and admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them.﴾ (47:4-6), Surah Muhammad.

Someone may ask: how does God guide one who was killed, and is there obligation after killing? We say: look at the guidance; it is the guidance of reward: ﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs and admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them.﴾

Thus we know that there is guidance of reward: whoever does good, God rewards him with Paradise, while whoever does evil has punishment in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿And whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight, as if he were climbing up into the sky. Thus God places defilement upon those who do not believe.﴾ (6:125), Surah al-An'am.

Is this an injustice from God toward His creatures? No, because since He called them to faith, some believed and became worthy of manifestations, and some disbelieved and did not believe, so they became worthy of distress and constriction of the breast. The meaning of constriction (daiq) is that a thing is smaller in size than what it needs to perform its task. When one says, "The house became too narrow for me and my dependents," this means that the man and his wife had lived in two rooms, and the house was spacious. Then they had many children, and the house became too narrow for them. Thus we know that nothing happened to the walls or the area of the house, but when the number of its members increased, the head of the household felt the narrowness of the home. It is said: "his breast is constricted" (ḍayyiq or ḍayq), for the word ḍayq occurs in the Qur'an in two forms. The Truth says:

﴿...and do not be in distress over what they plot.﴾ (16:127), Surah al-Nahl.

And there, in the verse we are reflecting upon, the word ḍayyiq occurs. And the Truth says:

﴿So perhaps you will leave some of what is revealed to you, and your breast will be constricted by it...﴾ (11:12), Surah Hud.

So what is meant by ḍā'iq, ḍayq, and ḍayq? We know that the breast is the place of the two essential organs of the body: the heart and the lungs. The lungs are the organ without whose work life cannot continue. The intestines may slow, or stop working for a time, and a person feeds on his store of fat or flesh; therefore a person can endure hunger for a long period, and endure water for a shorter period, but he cannot endure lack of air for minutes, and no one can endure stopping inhalation and exhalation.

We have said before: God may possess some of the sustenance of some, and less than that, possess some of the water of some. But can anyone possess the air of another? No; because pleasure and anger are changes in the human soul. If a person becomes angry with another, and he possessed the air and withheld it, the person would die before the other was pleased with him. For this reason God has never given possession of air to any of His creatures.

So the whole matter related to His saying, "makes his breast constricted and tight," we know that the breast is the place of breathing, and the lungs take in oxygen and expel carbon dioxide. When a person suffers a bout of cold, you see him finding difficulty in breathing, as if the space of the chest has become narrow, so sufficient air does not enter to operate the lungs, and the person tries to compensate by movement for what he has lost, and he pants. Physicians describe this by saying that the patient wants to take in what he needs of air, and so pants, because the space has become narrow. Likewise, when a person climbs stairs, he also pants, because climbing requires effort, to resist the pull of earth's gravity; the earth has a gravity that draws a person down, and one who climbs needs strength to move upward and resist the gravity.

We find descending stairs comfortable, because in descending there is help from gravity, but ascent requires more effort. So when the breast is constricted, it means that the chest space is no longer able to take in air through breathing in a way that comfortes the body; therefore one says, "So-and-so's breast is constricted," meaning that breathing exhausts him to the point that he...

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari.

This is the Qur'anic verse 6:126 with al-Sha'rawi's commentary.

Then Allah says:

﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember. (126)﴾

"This" refers to what has preceded of verses from the Book of Islam, which is the Qur'an, and that is what expands the breast to receive faith. The Qur'an is the bearer of the method of Islam; so at times the reference returns to the Qur'an, and at other times to Islam. There is no contradiction between the Qur'an and Islam.

﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight.﴾ The "ṣirāṭ" (path) is the even, sound road. An even road may, despite being level, be crooked; but this road is both level and straight. We know that the straight road is the shortest of the roads leading to the goal. Thus, a ṣirāṭ does not suffice without being straight, and a straight course does not suffice without being a ṣirāṭ; rather, there must be a paved and straight ṣirāṭ so that it is the shortest path to the goal and without hardships. We humans see engineers measuring dimensions, distances, goals and beginnings and ends, and after that they connect the beginnings with the goals.

They bring certain instruments to observe the straightness of the road and how it is paved. Hard, severe obstacles may stand in the way of the road's straightness, such as a mountain for instance; so the engineers either carve a tunnel through the mountain to guarantee its straightness, or they bend the road to guarantee the quality of its paving. If the engineers come and say "we will go from here to guarantee the straightness of the road," then we do that. Otherwise they make the road winding or spiral; so that the traveler avoids the obstacles he has no capacity to face.

But if the ṣirāṭ has been paved by a Lord, is there an obstacle to it? Of course not; so it is a straight road. Let us note that He, glorified is He, said: ﴿the path of your Lord﴾, meaning that it came from the aspect of lordship, the gift of the Lord. He is the Master, the Nurturer, and the Creator of creation, and He guarantees for them what helps them in their mission in existence, an easy, facilitated assistance. Thus we know that the path of truth is the paved, straight ṣirāṭ, that is, the one that connects the beginning with the end. If the road we follow is straight, paved and easy, then why do we not follow it?

﴿And this is the path of your Lord.﴾ We note that He, glorified is He, attributed the lordship to Muhammad, meaning that for his sake He made the ṣirāṭ straight; for He, glorified is He, is the One who takes charge of your lordship, O Muhammad, and He, glorified is He, is the Lord of the whole universe, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the essence of the essences of the universe.

﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember. (126)﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

"We have detailed" means that everything in this universe is created for what suits it, and every matter of the universe was created by our Lord so that its benefit is achieved without hardship and without distress. The method that Allah has sent down only sets right the universe and makes everything in it suitable for its mission, because Allah is the God of all people, and they are equal in relation to Him, since He has not taken either a consort or a son. He does not give life to a creature and bring it into existence in the universe, then strip it of the weapons of movement in life; every person has a weapon of talent or capacity, and thus the weapons, talents and capacities are multiplied. If someone wants to build a house, do we say to him: go to the faculty of engineering so you learn how to draw and plan the house? Do we say to him: learn how to be a plumber, an electrician and a plasterer? An individual cannot learn all these specialisations, so Allah distributed talents among His creatures: this one has a talent to work for himself and to work for others. Then another comes to perform for him a work for which he has no talent, so that the whole society is complete and its members are not duplicated.

If we had all graduated as doctors or engineers, the world would not have benefited; and those whom we say have failed in education perform works in life without which we could not live; Allah created them with limited mental capacities in order to bestow on them other capacities that suit other missions. If the whole society were educated in the same way, the pyramid would be upside down. If the pyramid is inverted, this means that parts of it will be without foundations in the earth. Therefore we find that there is a mental preparation which the Truth willed for each one of creation, and we cannot say to every person: study, graduate from university, then sweep the street; and be a blacksmith tomorrow. Thus the Truth linked every work to the need for it, and whoever receives the decree of Allah well within himself, Allah gives him from work all good.

We now note that whoever works as a government employee lives on a limited salary, whereas you find the plumber assessing his work at a wage he himself determines, and woe and fatigue remain for the one whose assessment of his work is in another's hand.

﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.﴾

Look at every matter in the universe: where the son of Adam has not poked his nose, you will find it straight; corruption only comes in matters where the son of Adam has poked his nose without the method of Allah. If you enter into every question with the method of Allah, the universe will be perfectly straightened. For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, draws our attention to the highest order in His universe, into which we have no intrusion and over which we have no control: the heavens, the planets, the sun, the moon, and the motion of the earth; all these beings, we find their affairs proceeding in regularity. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And the heaven He raised and set the balance. (7) That you not transgress in the balance. (8)﴾ (Surat al-Rahman)

If you wish your affairs to be set straight in your matters and voluntary conditions, then enter into them with the method of Allah; for things that are run by the method of Allah, without humans interfering in them, perform their mission as they should.

It is incumbent upon the human, therefore, to remember how to take from the premises before him what leads to the conclusions, and he must take sound premises to reach the innate goals. The simplest of matters is that you ask yourself: whose handiwork are you? Your own handiwork? No; are you the handiwork of one like you? No. And has anyone in the universe of Allah claimed, and how often does one claim, that he created you or created himself? No. Rather, you and he and the whole universe are the handiwork of Allah; so let Allah determine the law of your maintenance, and people will remain weary until they hand the handiwork over to its Creator. ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.﴾ He did not say "We have detailed the verses for one person," but said "for a people," so that if one inclines or becomes heedless in thought, another corrects him. We are all mutually responsible for reminding one another, and this mutual reminding protects every believer from himself; if deficiency arises in me through forgetfulness, heedlessness or desire, another corrects me. This is a cosmic principle: if you were to survey all existence, you would find it never fails.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 127:

It is necessary to recall the end that He mentions in His saying, the Truth:

﴿For them is the abode of peace with their Lord, and He is their Protector because of what they used to do.﴾ (6:127). That is, for those who went before, who were patient, who endured steadfastly and stood guard, there is the abode of peace. This is a construction which, as is said, consists of a subject (mubtada') and a predicate (khabar), except that the subject has been placed last here and the predicate first. The expected logic would be to say, "The abode of peace is for them," but the Qur'anic style came to front the predicate, which consists of the preposition and its object (al-jar wa al-majrur) and what is attached to it, and to delay the subject, for a particularity that the Truth intended: that this abode is for them alone and to the exclusion of others, so it is exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection. The phrase "dar al-salam" (abode of peace) is made of two words. "Dar" means that in which a person settles, and this place gathers everything that human life requires. It is slightly broader than the word "bayt" (house), because "bayt" is a place prepared for spending the night, whereas "dar" is prepared for life and for what relates to life's essentials.

Here "dar" is idafa (construct) to "al-salam" (peace), which, as we know, is one of the names of Allah. So the Truth here clarifies: for them is an abode attributed to Peace, which is Allah, and they deserve it as a reward from Him. If the abode that Allah promised is the abode of peace, which is Allah, then it must contain enjoyments and provisions in proportion to the excellence of the one it is attributed to, who is Allah. Why did He not say, "the abode of Allah"? Because Allah wished to bring another of His attributes, to give them peace, security and tranquillity.

There is a difference between the abodes of this world and this abode. The abodes of this world contain enjoyments, but you are between two states: either you lose what you are in, or what is in them is lost to you. Therefore there is no security in this world, because another may oppose you in it and be hostile to you, and illnesses that cloud your life may come, and the troubles caused by enemies may come; all of this disturbs your security and peace in the world. Therefore the Truth wished that the Hereafter be for you an abode of peace, for as long as you have believed, and that you be secure in it from all the calamities that existed in the abode of this world.

﴿For them is the abode of peace with their Lord...﴾ (6:127)

It is as if the abode of peace is not merely a promise from Allah that it will be, but it is ready, prepared with Allah, kept safe in His keeping, awaiting the believers. Glory be to Him, He has created gardens sufficient for all His creation, on the supposition that they believe, and has made from the Fire the like of that in proportion to His creation, on the supposition and assumption that they disbelieve. The believers will take what has been prepared for them of the abodes of faith, and will inherit what has been prepared for the disbelievers of the abodes of faith, on the supposition that they believed in this world.

﴿Those are the inheritors (10). Who inherit the Paradise; they will abide therein forever (11).﴾ (23:10-11)

So the Truth has not created limited gardens; rather He has prepared and readied of the gardens what is sufficient for all creation if they believe, and of the fires what is sufficient for all creation if they disbelieve. And since the "nearness" (al-'indiyya) is attributed to Allah, it is a safeguarded nearness.

After this, would Allah abandon them and leave them to what He has prepared for them? No, rather He said:

﴿...and He is their Protector because of what they used to do.﴾ (6:127)

So there is preparation, then the guardianship (qayyumiyya wa wilaya) of Allah, and this guardianship belongs to Allah; it is for the believers in this world. But let us note that guardianship in this world may have causes created by Allah, but in the Hereafter there is a reward that Allah does not leave to causes, so the guardianship is direct from Him, because He will give you immediately, and whatever occurs to your mind you will find present. It is an enjoyment unlike what people are accustomed to, because people enjoy in this world through created causes that belong to Allah. But in the Hereafter no one has ownership even over causes, therefore He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Whose is the dominion today...?﴾ (40:16)

And you will find the answer in His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

The Truth is the Protector who is near to you, close enough that you benefit from Him, so you need not even call upon Him to bring you benefits and ward off harms, as He did for you in this world and enabled you to act; and He is your Protector in the Hereafter, by the goodness of the reward for you because of what you used to do. For work in this world is the sowing, and it is the tilling for the fruit of the Hereafter. But does Allah give us in proportion to our deeds? No, rather He gives us in proportion to our patience, because if the giving were in proportion to deeds, then even if we counted them we would not pay the price of a tenth of a tenth of Allah's blessings upon us in this world. It is as if we work in this world to render thanks for what He has bestowed upon us and given us of blessings; then when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, gives us reward after that, it is grace from Him. Therefore the Truth makes clear to us: when you are enabled to work, beware of being seduced by your deeds; rather you must remember that this is grace from Allah:

﴿Say: "By the grace of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ (10:58)

The Prophet (ﷺ) also explained this matter and said:

("None of you will enter Paradise by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His grace and mercy.")¹

So the whole matter is by grace from Allah, but the grace of Allah is conditioned upon righteous deeds: you do righteous deeds, and your Lord gives you multiples of them. Naturally, your deed will not benefit His majesty, beauty or perfection, nor add to Him any attribute or add to His dominion; but He gives you for what you have done, for your own benefit and the benefit of your kind.

Therefore we find Imam al-Razi, may Allah be pleased with him, saying: deeds in themselves produce in the self some purity in which it finds rest and happiness, so that you find the reward in comfort; and psychological comfort is the immaterial matter that exists in a material structure, which is your body. When something exists in the soul, it affects the body with changes; when a person becomes angry, that anger shows its effect on the structure itself, the face reddens and a person trembles with the agitation of anger. Anger is an immaterial matter, yet it has an effect on the structure; likewise, when something pleasing happens, that appears in the structure too, so your features brighten and beam. Thus deed affects the structure, and the structure affects deed.

1 Narrated by Muslim in the Book of the Hypocrites, and the wording is his; narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Softening of Hearts and the Sick, Ibn Majah in Asceticism, al-Darimi in Softening of Hearts; and Ahmad in al-Musnad 2/235, 256.

And the Truth (may He be exalted) says after that:

﴿On the Day when He gathers them all together, He will say: "O assembly of jinn, you have taken many of mankind." And their allies among mankind will say: "Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say: "The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide forever, except as God wills. Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing."﴾ (6:128)

When you hear "yawm" (day), know that it is a "zarf zaman" (adverb of time), meaning that there is an event. The Truth's words ﴿On the Day when He gathers them all together﴾ mean the day on which all of them stand and are assembled. When we look at what follows, we find that the event has not yet come, but there came ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾, which is a "call" (nida'). So the event is the calling itself. A calling requires a caller, who is the Truth (subhanahu), and those called, who are the assembly of jinn and mankind, and a speech that displays the form of the call. The sentence is thus: "On the Day when He gathers them together, He will say: O assembly of jinn and mankind." The "hashr" (gathering) is the bringing together, and the "ma'shar" (assembly) is a group mixed together in coexistence, meaning that all the elements and necessities of life are among them. The word ma'shar may be attached to people of a particular profession: "O assembly of merchants, O assembly of scholars, O assembly of ministers." But if you say "O assembly of Egyptians," it is a group mixed in coexistence and companionship.

﴿O assembly of jinn, you have taken many of mankind...﴾ (6:128)

"Istaktha'a" means he took a great deal of it, as one who acquires much wealth, or acquires many friends. The root "istakthara" indicates that he took an abundance. And what does their taking many of mankind mean? We know that among the jinn there are the obedient and there are the disobedient, and the foremost of the disobedient among the jinn is Iblis, who swore:

﴿He said: "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all."﴾ (38:82)

It is as if the Truth clarifies: you, O assembly of jinn, have strenuously tried to take mankind to your side and you have sought many of them. After the disobedient among the devil-jinn alone existed, disobedient people were also found, and you took many of them, because you thought you had dominance, abundance and might, for if they obeyed you in whispering, you became the masters. That is what used to happen: a person, when he descended into a valley for example, would say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the jinn," and he would ask it to protect him and his property, and whenever it whispered something to him, he would hasten to carry it out. This is "istikthar".

﴿And their allies among mankind will say: "Our Lord, we benefited from one another..."﴾ (6:128)

Likewise, it is not only that the jinn and mankind enjoyed one another; rather, there is also a mutual enjoyment of those who turned away from God's method. These have seduction and dominance, ordering them to do things contrary to God's method, and those [humans] enjoy them, fulfilling their desires in the form of religiosity. They say to them: "Worship the idols, worship the sun, worship the moon," and they do so. This satisfies in them the instinct of religious submission, because every soul is innately disposed to bind itself to a power higher than itself. For when a person looks at himself and at his companions, he finds them subject to changes: one of them is healthy today and sick tomorrow, rich today and poor tomorrow. So what guarantees for the human soul protection from these changes?

A person loves to take refuge in and be bound to the strong, so that when these changes come, it has support. However, there are those who ascend in religiosity: these are the ones who lean upon faith in God and rely on Him (subhanahu), and who devote themselves to faith in God with its requirements in "do" and "do not do." But the things they worship besides God have no requirements or obligations, except that they agree with the desires of the soul. This deceiving of the soul, that is, compelling the soul to lie, does not last long, because a person does not deceive himself. Faith protects the soul when a matter comes that is beyond your means. There is no one who says "O sun" or "O moon," "O devil" or "O rock!" That is impossible, because you will never lie to yourself. An example of this is the Truth's words:

﴿When harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us about a harm that touched him...﴾ (10:12)

And here the Truth speaks about mankind:

﴿And their allies among mankind will say: "Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us..."﴾ (6:128)

That is, this enjoyment lasts for a duration, the duration of the term, which is the hour when life ends. Then the reckoning begins, and they hear the Truth's words:

﴿"...He will say: The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide forever, except as God wills. Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing."﴾ (6:128)

"Al-thawa'" is dwelling, and "mathwakum" means your dwelling. "Illa ma sha'a Allah" (except as God wills): this exception was a subject of debate among the scholars, and a lengthy discussion occurred about it. Some said: the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) said ﴿except as God wills﴾, meaning that He has absolute power and will, so He does what He wants, but He settled the matter and specified "what He wills," saying:

﴿Indeed God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills...﴾ (4:48)

Here He specified "what He wills": what He wills is in other than associating partners with Him, for associating partners is not subject to His forgiveness. Or it may be that "except as God wills" is understood by some to mean that the Fire will be their abode immediately upon resurrection and gathering, but abiding in the Fire will only come after the reckoning, and this is an exception from the time of eternity, so entry into Paradise or the Fire will not occur except after the reckoning. Thus the time of reckoning and gathering is excepted and lies outside the time of eternal abiding in Paradise and the Fire. We also find ﴿except as your Lord wills﴾ in Surah Hud, where the Truth says:

﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, having therein groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends. And as for those who were made happy, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, a gift uninterrupted.﴾ (11:106–108)

So there is an exception concerning the Fire and an exception concerning Paradise. The Truth's words "abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills," where the exception comes after the description of eternity, indicate that eternity ends, although it has been established that the people of Paradise abide in Paradise and the people of the Fire abide in the Fire forever without exception. How is that so?

The answer to this is that the people of the Fire do not abide in the torment of the Fire alone, but they are tormented with the zamharir (extreme cold) and with kinds of torment other than the Fire, which are more severe than all of them, namely God's wrath upon them, His curse, His expulsion of them and His humiliating them. Likewise, the people of Paradise have, beyond Paradise, something greater and more exalted in station, which is God's good pleasure (ridwan), as He said:

﴿God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence, and good pleasure from God is greater...﴾ (9:72)

So for them there is what God bestows upon them beyond the reward of Paradise, which none knows the reality of except Him. This is the meaning of the exception, and the proof of it is His words ﴿a gift uninterrupted﴾. And the meaning of His words opposite it, ﴿Indeed your Lord is effecter of what He intends﴾, is that your Lord does to the people of the Fire what He wills of torment, just as He gives to the people of Paradise a gift that has no cessation.

The Truth concludes the verse with His words: ﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.﴾ He is All-Wise in punishing, All-Knowing of who deserves to be punished and the measure of his punishment, and All-Knowing of who deserves to be rewarded and blessed and the measure of his reward and blessing, and All-Wise in showing mercy.

And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn. (129)

"Wa-kadhalika" (and thus) points to what happened between the jinn and mankind of argument. So the Truth (al-Haqq) spoke on the tongue of mankind: ﴿Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others...﴾ (128) [Surat al-An'am].

He did not bring the speech of the jinn, because their speech came in other verses. So the Truth is the one who says:

﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it to you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me..."﴾ (22) [Surat Ibrahim]

Likewise, Allah mentioned what comes from the tongue of Satan in another surah:

﴿Like Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." And when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you..."﴾ (16) [Surat al-Hashr]

Likewise, the Truth in other verses brought the statements of mankind who went astray:

﴿...Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and mankind that we may put them under our feet so they will be among the lowest.﴾ (29) (from verse 29, Surat Fussilat)

And His saying here in Surat al-An'am:

﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾ (from verse 129, Surat al-An'am)

That is, just as We did with the jinn and mankind, through the jinn's multiplying of men and their enjoying one another in misguidance, seduction, obedience and submission, We make a wrongdoer to rule over a wrongdoer among them, and We do not appoint over them one of the people of goodness; for the hearts of the people of goodness are filled with mercy, and they are not able to discipline the wrongdoer. They inherited the Muhammadan prophethood in his saying on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "Go, for you are the freed ones" (al-Tulaqa'). Therefore, when Allah wants to discipline a wrongdoer, He does not bring one of the people of goodness to discipline him. Glorified is He: by honouring the people of goodness, He does not make any of them stand in the position of disciplining the wrongdoer. He makes the people of goodness stand in the position of spectators watching the wrongdoers discipline one another.

History shows us this. The wrongdoers have done much to one another, whereas if their true enemies had gained power over them, they would have shown them mercy, because their hearts are filled with mercy.

For this reason, we have received from our master Malik ibn Dinar, who was one of the people of goodness, that he said: I read in some narrations a sacred hadith in which the Truth says:

("I am the King of kings; the hearts of kings are in My hand").(1)

So beware lest the tyrant, the ruler or the despot think that he took power by his cleverness or by his strength; rather, the Truth brought him to discipline the oppressors with him. The proof is that when Allah wants this matter to end, in His majesty He strips awe from the hearts of his guards, and instead of repelling the rifle from him, the rifle is aimed at him.

So beware lest you think that a king takes kingship by force against Allah; rather, when the servants do wrong and transgress, the Truth sets over them one who oppresses them. For this reason it is said: "The wrongdoer is the sword of Allah on earth; through him He takes vengeance, and vengeance is taken upon him."

﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn.﴾ (129) [Surat al-An'am]

So the evil tyrants set over people are as if they were the outcome of their deeds. For this reason one of the righteous used to say: "I know my standing with my Lord from the temperament of my mount: if it bolts with me, I say, 'What have I done that the beast has bolted with me?'" As if the matter is being reckoned. This is the treatment of the good: when he commits a sin, he is held accountable for it immediately, so that his record is always clean. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: ("No affliction befalls a Muslim but that Allah expiates by it some of his sins, even the thorn that pricks him.")(2)

So when a servant of the people of goodness commits some misdeeds, the Truth repays him for them with illness in his body or loss in his wealth. Likewise the wrongdoer whom Allah does not want to be punished in the Hereafter. The Messenger (ﷺ) said: ("No Muslim is afflicted with harm, even a thorn or more than that, but that Allah, exalted is He, removes his sins for it, as a tree sheds its leaves.")(3)

﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn.﴾ They believed they had taken something beyond Allah and got away with it. We say: No; your Lord will call you to account, with reward or punishment, according to what your hands have sent forth and what evil or good deeds you have done.

1 Tadhkirat al-Mawdu'at of Ibn al-Qaysarani.
2 Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and Ahmad.
3 Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim from Ibn Mas'ud.

The Lord then says:

﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind! Did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this your day? They will say: "We bear witness against ourselves." It was the life of this world that deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers.﴾ (6:130)

We note that He said here: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind﴾, because He wishes to establish the proof that He, glory be to Him, did not penalize their deeds nor prescribe punishments for them except after the message reached them through the messengers. He gave them, through the messengers, a clear communication of what must be done and what must be left undone, so Allah, glory be to Him, did not seize them unjustly.

Here there is a pause. The address is to the jinn and humankind: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you﴾. Some scholars said: the jinn have messengers and humankind have messengers. Others said: the messengers are from humankind alone, because the Qur'an came in their own words: ﴿Indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses﴾.

So the jinn argued with a Book revealed after Moses, peace be upon him, and they had information about the Book that came after him. It is as if the jinn take their message from humankind; it is as if Allah sent messengers from humankind only, and they conveyed to the jinn what the Messenger said. And here He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind! Did there not come to you messengers from among you...﴾ (6:130) [Surat al-An'am]

When you come to two men, the first of whom has a hundred pounds with him and the second walks with him having nothing, and you say: "These two have a hundred pounds with them," this is a correct statement. So His saying ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you﴾ means from among your whole body. Or the messengers come to humankind, and afterwards some of the jinn take from the Messenger so as to become a messenger conveying to their fellow jinn:

﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an; and when they attended it they said: "Be silent." When it was concluded they went back to their people as warners﴾ (46:29) [Surat al-Ahqaf]

So it is as if the jinn warners take from the messengers from humankind, and afterwards they turn to the jinn.

﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses...﴾ (6:130) [Surat al-An'am]

The verses (ayat) are applied to the miracles that establish the truth of the messengers, and to the explanation of the cosmic proofs indicating the truth of the messengers. The phrase ﴿relating to you My verses﴾ means they recount to them the procession of messengers from Adam until it ended with Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. ﴿Relating to you My verses﴾ is a statement indicating precision in the historical account, because "qassa" is derived from tracing a track (qass al-athar), meaning following the footstep without deviating from such-and-such; thus we find that a story is supposed to be drawn from the reality of history. ﴿They relate to you My verses and warn you of the meeting of this your day﴾ (6:130) [Surat al-An'am]

This is the day of disgrace, when they will stand before Allah, and the Truth will remind them that He had alerted them, and that He had given a sufficient excuse to the one who was warned.

﴿...They will say: "We bear witness against ourselves." It was the life of this world that deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers.﴾ (6:130) [Surat al-An'am]

Their saying ﴿We bear witness against ourselves﴾ is an acknowledgment from them against themselves; they bore witness against themselves. But what prevented them from joining faith in the procession of prophethood? The answer comes from the Truth: ﴿and the life of this world deceived them﴾.

What deceives is the thing that has influence, and it is described as "dunya" (the lower, nearer world)! Therefore the delusion that comes from the world is a lack of insight. ﴿And they bear witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers﴾. Whoever surveys the verses of the Qur'an finds a verse saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ (6:23).

So at one time they deny for themselves that they disbelieved, and at another time they affirm that they were disbelievers; this is due to the inconsistency or variation of their positions. Or it means that ﴿they bore witness against themselves﴾, in the sense that their parts (ab'ad) bore witness against them. For a human in this world has a will, and this will dominates what he has of limbs and capacities created by Allah, because Allah gave the will in the human a authority over the parts that perform voluntary actions. But involuntary, compelled functions are not subject to the human's will: no one can tell the heart, "beat so many times a minute," and no one tells the intestines, "move in this peristaltic way." Yet he can walk on his feet to the mosque or walk to the tavern, and he can recite the Qur'an or read a book that harms and does not benefit.

So the human will dominates the parts to realize the choice that makes responsibility (taklif) valid. But on the Day of Resurrection the will that a human has over his parts is taken away, and all the parts remain free; and when the parts become free, the things that used to respond to you in this world under the law of their subjection to your will have ceased and ended. So in the Hereafter they bear witness against their owner: the skins, the hands and the feet bear witness:

﴿And they will say to their skins: "Why did you bear witness against us?" They will say: "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak"﴾ (41:21) [Surat Fussilat], and when they say to our Lord: "We were not polytheists," this is their own speech, but their limbs say to them: "O liars, you did such-and-such."

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware﴾.

"That" refers to what preceded it, which is the sending of messengers to convey the message from God, so that no one has an argument against God after the messengers. They had acknowledged that God had sent messengers to them, and they bore witness against themselves. Since they had acknowledged against themselves that God had sent messengers to them and had borne witness against themselves to that, this is a fresh affirmation that God would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware. This is because the Truth, glory be to Him, does not punish a crime, nor does He declare something forbidden, until the text has been sent down through the messengers. That is, God does not destroy them for an injustice committed by them except after that delivery of the message.

﴿While their people were unaware﴾. "Ghafla" (heedlessness) is the opposite of "yaqza" (alertness). Alertness is the constant awakening of the mind, while heedlessness is for some realities to be absent from the mind. The meaning of "our Lord does not destroy the towns unjustly while their people are unaware" is that they were not alert. Had they been alert and mindful, they would not have needed the messengers. This is because when God created creation, He sent Adam to his descendants, and it was expected that, just as parents instruct their children in the means of their livelihood, they would also instruct them in the values of their religion. Just as parents teach their descendants the means of their life, then transmit them and add to them through their innovations, it was obligatory upon the parents to carry out this task with regard to values, so that values would live among people just as the means of their life lived.

So why, then, did the means of their life survive, get inherited, and have things added to them? Because the aspect of religion is what people neglect, since it restricts their movement with "do" and "do not do," while they want luxury in the means of their life. Why, then, O human, are you eager to advance in the luxury of life and not eager to advance in values? For example, you used to drink water from a spring or with your hand, then you made a cup to drink from, purified the water of impurities, and transported it from the sources in tanks. You are beautifying your material and livelihood life, so where then is your concern for the values of religion?!!

Its original was reviewed and its hadiths were takhrij-ed (traced to their sources) by Dr. Ahmad Umar Hashim, Vice President of Al-Azhar University.

Had they been alert, every father would have taught his son the values he had inherited from his fathers. Despite that, the Truth, glory be to Him, showed mercy for this heedlessness and repeated the reminder through the messengers. Whenever the features of the values carried by the method are effaced, He, exalted is He, sends a messenger out of mercy, grace, and justice from Him, and He would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people are unaware, and heedlessness is the opposite of alertness.

So if they had been alert, there would have been no necessity for the messengers, because fathers would have transmitted values to their sons just as they transmit to them the means of their lives. This matter continues with us until now. For instance, if a son is absent from school for a day, the father blames the son; if he neglects his lessons or fails, the father punishes the son. This is the zeal for the material future of the son, but there is no zeal for his performance of the obligations of religion. Why? If people took care of the matters of their values as they always take care of the matters of their lives, the path of good among people would be upright and would become a routine matter.

We have learned that heedlessness is opposed by alertness, just as forgetfulness is opposed by remembrance, setting is opposed by rising, and absence is opposed by presence.

"And for each are degrees according to what they have done, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do." (6:132)

"Wa-li-kull" (And for each): it came with tanwin, meaning that for each of mankind and the jinn there are degrees according to what they have done. It is as if the deeds vary in their levels. Although they may appear to be identical in form, the variation arises from the abundance of the deed, or from the sincerity (ikhlas) of the one who performs it, the one who acquires it, and the one who does it. There is one who gives his deed his full energy, and there is one who performs his deed with half sincerity. This matter of sincerity is not defined by regulations or laws; rather, it is defined by God, glorified and exalted be He. For this reason, Muhammad (ﷺ), conveying from the Lord of Majesty, says this hadith qudsi: "Sincerity is one of My secrets, which I entrust to the heart of whomever I love among My servants." (1)

Thus, the measures of sincerity are known only to God, our Lord, glorified and exalted be He, and the degrees are according to the measure of that. The degrees are also according to what the servant adds of the same kind as what God has prescribed for him. God has prescribed five prayers, so the servant adds ten rak'ahs in the night, for example. God has prescribed fasting for a month, so the servant fasts on Mondays and Thursdays.

Whoever stops at what God has prescribed, God rewards him for his sincerity in performing what is incumbent upon him. When a Bedouin asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the situation of one who performs only the obligatory acts, he said to him: "He will prosper if he is truthful" (2). Thus, the one who adds to what God has prescribed, of the same kind as what God has prescribed, is more successful. A person does not reach the rank that is more successful except when he is at a higher degree. The word "darajat" (degrees) indicates elevation, and the word "darakat" (depths/lower degrees) indicates descent. And God does not overlook the outward and inward of every deed of any servant.

(1) Narrated by Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri in al-Risala, from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib.
(2) Narrated by al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 6, verse 133:

He, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can take you away and replace you with whomever He wills after you, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.﴾ (6:133)

Here Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, calls us to His worship and to His obligations; He calls us to the virtue of obedience. All of that is for our benefit, and this is the absolute of merciful lordship (rububiyyah), so He makes the reward good for us and magnifies it for us, so that we may work for our own good. For, as we have said, all our deeds do not add to the dominion of Allah the weight of a gnat's wing, and all our disobediences do not diminish from the dominion of Allah the weight of a gnat's wing. Allah created us with all the attributes of perfection, and we have added nothing to Him. He brought the world into existence from non-existence, and He distinguishes between the attribute that subsists in the essence of Allah and the bringing into existence of the object of the attribute. Allah is the Creator; Allah is the Merciful (al-Rahman), Allah is the Compassionate (al-Rahim), Allah is the Subduer (al-Qahhar), and He, glory be to Him, is the Merciful, the Compassionate, the Subduer and the Creator even before what He creates appears and becomes manifest; for He possesses the attribute of the Creator, so creation proceeds from Him. He is the Provider (al-Razzaq) before He creates the one provided for; the attribute exists in Him and subsists in Him, and by this attribute He provides. By the existence of these attributes in Him, He says to a thing "Be," and it is. To Him belongs this whole universe, and He is free of need of the servants, and to Him belongs all dominion. Likewise, He created repentance, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant than one of you who had his camel, which carried his food and drink, lost in a barren desert, and then found it." (1)

﴿And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can take you away and replace you with whomever He wills after you, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.﴾ [Surah al-An'am]

Thus creation is continuously bringing into being from non-existence, and this is evidence that the attribute of being the Creator exists. In the logic of reason, Adam is not one... but by analogy, or Adam [ ... ]. The whole universe from the first Adam exists, and the entire universe subjected to Adam as the vicegerent on earth is subservient to Allah; so if He wills, He removes the creation and brings a new creation.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Da'awat, Muslim in al-Tawba, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat.
"Saqata 'ala ba'irihi": meaning he encountered it and stumbled upon it without intention and so obtained it.

Almighty God says next:

﴿Indeed, what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape it.﴾

Since God, Glorified and Exalted, is the One Who has no god but Him, when He promises, His promise must come to pass, and when He threatens, His threat must come to pass. A promise, when stated without qualification, concerns good, while a threat concerns evil. And when a created being breaks a promise or a threat, this is an expected matter, because he is among the things that change: his opinion alters, so he is no longer fit for that promise, for he may have promised something that he thought was within his power, and then it went beyond his power. He has no control over things. But when the one who promises is All-Powerful, and there is no other god who could contradict Him in what He has promised or threatened, then the promise must be fulfilled or the threat must come. Therefore, when God decrees a judgment, the believer accepts that judgment as an established fact, because there is no god with God who would change the judgment, and He, Glorified be He, is not among the things that change. The example is that He said:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. He will burn in a flame of fire, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck is a rope of palm fiber.﴾ [Surah al-Masad]

This is a threat concerning a matter in which they had free choice, yet they did not embrace Islam. What follows confirms to every Muslim: beware of treating this matter with doubt, saying, "Perhaps Abu Lahab and his wife will repent and embrace Islam. Did Hind not repent? Did Abu Sufyan not embrace Islam?" But He, Glorified be He, knows what the choice of Abu Lahab and the choice of his wife will lead to, even though each of them is free to choose, and there is no other god to change the matter from what He has said.

﴿Say: He is God, the One.﴾ [Surah al-Ikhlas]

That is, there is no other god to alter this matter.

﴿Indeed, what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape it.﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 6:134]

Some people may think that God will bring about what He has promised, but that they may flee from it. The matter is not as they think: the promise is coming, and you are not able to escape it. No one has the power to prevent God from fulfilling what He has promised or threatened. You will not escape His promise or His threat, nor will you overcome God, outpace Him or render Him powerless; for God is dominant over His command.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 135:

He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your standing; indeed I am acting. So you will come to know to whom the ultimate abode will belong. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾:

The qawm (people, a group) are the gathering, and it is customarily applied to men, because they are the people who take on matters; for the woman, the original state and norm is covering, staying at home, and settling in the house to take charge of its affairs and look after it.

When you read the Qur'an you find the word "qawm" and understand that what is meant by it is the group bound together by a common tie, and that it is specifically for men. The example is the saying of the Truth:

﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule another people, perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule other women, perhaps they may be better than them﴾ (part of verse 11, Surat al-Hujurat)

Since "qawm" has been paired with "nisa'" (women) — "nor women" — this "qawm" refers to men, and from it are derived "al-qiyam lil-muhimmat" (taking charge of tasks) and "al-qawamah" (guardianship). For this reason the poet says:

"I do not know, and I do not think I know, whether the people of Hisn are men or women."

That is, are they men or women?

﴿Say: O my people, act according to your standing﴾ (part of verse 135, Surat al-An'am)

The "makan" (standing, place) is the space that a human body occupies. Every being has a place: if it stands, it has a place; if it sits, it has a place. The makan is the portion of the earth owned and allotted to you. When you stand in a place, no one else can stand there while you are standing; rather, he must move you away from it, and when you move someone who is standing, he goes to another place. Overlap between two in a space that accommodates only one is impossible, and this is a matter of nature. You will find a small child who has not yet understood anything and is only able to stand, then wants to sit on the chair on which his sister or brother is sitting; before he sits, he pushes the one sitting on it, because he knows by instinct that two cannot exist in one space.

You see this also in non-visible matter. When you bring a bottle and place it in water so that it fills, you hear the sound of air escaping from it as bubbling, because the water cannot enter unless the air leaves, and because water is denser it presses so that the air comes out. This confirms the impossibility of overlap, that is, that no two things exist in one space. Your makan is the position you occupy, and for this reason, even in armies and in war, plans are laid with different weapons so as to seize places.

"Act according to your standing" is a statement addressed to the group who opposed prophethood and took these positions. The Truth says to them, as a threat and as a way of despairing them that they will not reach the point of harming the Messenger of Allah: act according to the extent of your ability to establish yourselves, or remain firm in what you are upon of opposition and hostility. Why? Because he (ﷺ) is also acting: your firmness will not prevent me from acting. You act with your strength, and I act with my faith-based strength and the supply of my Lord, the Most High, of power.

﴿Say: O my people, act according to your standing; indeed I am acting. So you will come to know to whom the ultimate abode will belong. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

﴿So you will come to know to whom the ultimate abode will belong﴾: the "lam" in "lahu" indicates that the ultimate abode will be for the one who has faith, because for the others it will not be theirs but against them. Whenever you see the "lam", know that the matter is for them and not against them. So even if the wrongdoers obtain some outcome, it is not theirs; rather their outcome is against them, and the wrongdoers will not succeed.

"And He, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of tilth and livestock, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "This is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is their judgment.﴾ (6:136)

Here is a return to speech about those who oppose the method of Allah.

"Dhara'a" means created, scattered, and multiplied. "Al-harth" (tilth) refers to crops, and crops are called harth because they come from tilling. "Al-an'am" (livestock), which is represented in eight pairs in a verse that comes later, are the camels, the cattle, the sheep, and the goats.

﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of tilth and livestock﴾ means of what He created. They merely tilled, for the one who causes the crop to grow is Allah. Glory be to Him, it is He who gave the seed its strength so that it grows a root and draws nutrients from the earth. It is He who brought together all the elements of the earth, and He who made the seed turn toward the elements suitable for it and leave what is unsuitable, by the law of "the One who created and proportioned, and who decreed and guided" [87:2-3]. What Allah made into crops and livestock, you imagine that you dispose of as you please, despite the fact that it is He who scattered and created it. He, glory be to Him, is the One who disposes.

They assigned to Allah a share of what He created of tilth and livestock, and they said: "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "This is for our partners." That is, they brought the tilth and divided it into two parts. They said: "This is for Allah, and this is for the idols."

Likewise they divided the livestock, making one portion for Allah and one portion for themselves. Was it not just that the One who created should divide, instead of this claim from you, because you took what was not your right? Would that you had been fair, so that we might accept your division. Then the portion for Allah would go to the charities for the poor, and the portion for the partners would go to the idols, to the custodians who attend them, to the servants, and to those who cast lots for you with arrows. Would that you had known justice in division! Rather, what you have done is an unjust, oppressive, and wrongful division. Why? The answer comes from the Truth:

﴿But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their partners...﴾ (6:136)

You made the division and said: "This is for Allah and this is for our partners." So be honest with yourselves in this attribution. But they were stealing the right of Allah. In destruction they had one fixed division, and in increase they had another. When a blight came upon the crop and destroyed it, they took what they had set aside for Allah and gave it to the partners, saying: "Indeed our Lord is rich!" Although you divided, you did not keep the division you imposed and to which you agreed.

Likewise with livestock: they would estimate a number of animals and say: "This is for Allah, and that is for the partners." If an animal from what was vowed to Allah died, they did not replace it; but if an animal vowed to the idols died, they replaced it and took in exchange a substitute from the portion they had vowed to Allah. Also, suppose a flowing spring whose water ran to irrigate the crop assigned to Allah; they would take from it for the land planted for the idols. Thus the division was unjust from the start, and even then they did not keep to it. And so their judgment was evil and corrupt.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 137:

The Truth (Allah) then says:

﴿And thus have their associates made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to ruin them and to confuse them regarding their religion. And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so, so leave them and what they invent.﴾ (6:137)

Likewise, they transferred that unjust division to what concerns their own persons, in begetting and procreation. Their associates made the killing of their children attractive to them. "Tazyin" (making attractive) is the introduction of an element of beautification onto something that is an accidental, incidental matter. The aspect of the making-attractive is that they are either wealthy or poor. If they are poor, one of them says: "Why should I bring upon myself one worry upon another?" And if they are wealthy, one of them says: "The children will take from you and impoverish you." So there are two matters: either poverty that exists in fact, or poverty feared. For this reason you find that the verses which address this meaning come in two styles, and the wording differs according to the opening. Those who want to find fault with the styles of the Qur'an [say, since it says once]:

﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty; We provide for you and for them...﴾ (17:31) [Surat al-Isra']

and another time it says:

﴿We provide for you and for them...﴾ (6:151) [Surat al-An'am]. So what is the difference between the two expressions?

We say to this speaker: you are comparing the concluding phrase ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾ with ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾ [in the other verse]. These are the conclusion of one verse, and these are the conclusion of a second verse. Bring the conclusion of the verse together with its opening and you will find that the conclusion of each verse is suited to its opening. Since the opening differs, the closing must differ too. In the first verse the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, so poverty (al-imlaq) is an existing reality. Thus concern for a person's own provision takes precedence over concern for the provision of those he supports among his children. So the Truth says to these people:

﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty. We provide for you and for them...﴾ (6:151) [Surat al-An'am].

Poverty exists, and their preoccupation with their own provision fills their souls. Therefore He says to them: ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾, and Allah, glory be to Him, reassures them: We provide for you, then We provide for them. As for when poverty does not exist, the Truth says:

He says:

﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for you and for them...﴾ (17:31) [Surat al-Isra']

That is: do not kill your children out of fear of poverty, for you possess your provision, and when the children come, We provide for them and for you along with them. Thus we see that the opening differs in the two verses, and so does the closing. The associates used to make the killing of children attractive, and this is a matter that requires harsh beautification, because love of children is an instinct in the human soul, and the soul loves to have offspring, since a person understands that however long his life is, he will die, so his name must remain through successive generations. And you find a person, filled with happiness when a grandchild comes to him, saying: "I have secured my remembrance for two coming generations," and he forgets that true remembrance is what a person presents of deeds, not the memory of children and the love of extending the self. Killing children requires intense beautification, such as saying: "If you beget sons, they will impoverish and humiliate you, for you are a people of raids and a people of wars, and every day your sons will be drawn into fighting and combat, so you will be between losing your sons or having your wealth plundered; and if they are daughters, they will be taken captive after you." Thus there is exaggeration in the enticement toward an act that contradicts sound human nature in the extension of progeny.

﴿And thus have their associates made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to ruin them...﴾ (6:137)

The phrase ﴿to many of the polytheists﴾ indicates that some of them refused to kill children. "Yurdūhum" (to ruin them) derives from "al-radā", which means destruction and death.

﴿...and to confuse them regarding their religion﴾ (6:137).

That is, to mix up their religion for them. Did they have a religion? These people inherited from the matter of the upright religion what had been before, namely the religion of Isma'il (peace be upon him), until they turned aside and departed from it into polytheism. They made attractive to them deeds in order to bring them to the sources of ruin, and they tried to confuse them about what remained to them of religion.

﴿...And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so, so leave them and what they invent﴾ (6:137). Because burying children and killing them contradicts the idea of Allah's creation: would Allah create so that you kill?

It is as if they were opposing the will of the Truth, glory be to Him, to bring things into existence. But had He willed, they would not have done that. He has given them choice, and by means of choice they reach every aim they have. Had Allah not created choice in them, they would not have done this, for if He willed that they not go astray, they would not have done it. Allah willed to create a creation that does not disobey Allah in what He commands them and does what it is commanded, and these are the angels.

Thus this matter is not beyond Allah, and glory be to Him: when He compels with a will of His, that is for the benefit of the creature; and when He leaves him free to choose, that is from the Creator's enabling him with choice, and the one who chooses does nothing against Allah's will, because divinity requires two things: it requires a power that manifests in compelling matters which servants cannot withstand, and man is the only being that has the right to choose among alternatives in his aims, while the rest of the cosmos proceeds by the law of subjection and has no choice.

The subjected beings demonstrate the absoluteness of power, but they do not establish for Allah the beloved-ness of the creature, because beloved-ness arises from your being free to act, yet you prefer an act willed by Allah over your own will. ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so, so leave them and what they invent.﴾

"Al-iftira'" (inventing) is fabrication and deliberate lying, and they are fabricators, because they wanted to alter the truth of reality in begetting, for Allah created the pair, male and female, for the sake of procreation.

He says, glorified is He, after that:

﴿And they say, "These are cattle and tilth set apart; none may eat of them except whom we will," by their claim; and cattle whose backs are forbidden, and cattle over which they do not mention the name of Allah, fabricating against Him. He will recompense them for what they used to fabricate.﴾ (6:138)

This is a continuation in polytheism, for they divided the animals and the crops and set aside a portion for the idols. These animals designated for the idols are not to be disposed of by anyone: their milk is not taken, no one uses them as mounts, and their benefit does not extend to people. They did not realize that these animals are a blessing from Allah, and that benefiting from them is necessary, and that it is not sound reasoning to leave aside an animal whose subjugation to you could benefit you and not to make use of it. They did this, and the Truth related their statement when He said:

﴿And they say, "These are cattle and tilth set apart; none may eat of them except whom we will," by their claim..﴾ (6:138)

That is, these are cattle whose use is forbidden.

﴿And cattle whose backs are forbidden..﴾ (6:138) They also forbade riding them.
