Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 153:

That is, He concluded the nine precepts with this statement, because the Straight Path (al-sirat al-mustaqim) encompasses the nine precepts mentioned before it and encompasses everything not mentioned here. And I said: we notice that the first five were concluded by the Truth with His saying: ﴿so that you may understand﴾, and the four after them were concluded with His saying: ﴿so that you may remember﴾, and the one comprehensive precept that encompasses everything He concluded with: ﴿so that you may be God-conscious﴾. So what is the difference between understanding (ta'aqqul), remembrance (tadhakkur) and God-consciousness (taqwa)? As for the first five things, about which the Truth said:

﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him, and be good to your parents, and do not kill your children because of poverty — We provide for you and for them — and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. This He has enjoined upon you, that you may understand.﴾ [Surat al-An'am].

These things existed in the environment in which the Qur'an was revealed: they associated partners with God, disobeyed their parents, killed their children, approached indecencies, and killed the soul which God had forbidden to kill except by right. So He made it clear to them: understand them, for when you understand them you will find that God's command prevents you from these acts. It is a matter required by sound reason, which investigates things with sound premises and sound conclusions. But the other "four," they were doing them and boasting of them. Regarding those they used to practise — taking charge of the property of the orphan, fulfilling the measure and the balance, justice in speech, and fulfilling the covenant — He said: ﴿so that you may remember﴾, meaning: beware of neglecting them; for if you were doing them while in jahiliyya, then do them all the more while in Islam. Then He brought the comprehensive precept: ﴿And this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. This He has enjoined upon you that you may be God-conscious.﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 153].

Since this precept encompasses all rulings, positive and negative, prohibitions and commands, He made clear to them that you must follow the Straight Path, so that you protect yourselves from the effects of the attributes of wrath from the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and the first of its soldiers is the Fire.

As for the sirat: it is the paved road, and from it they derive the sirat of the Hereafter, which is, as it is said, "finer than a hair and sharper than a sword." What is the meaning of this saying? Its meaning is that one must walk upon it with complete alertness and balance, for if he veers to the right he falls into the Fire, and if he veers to the left he falls into it. It is a path made with precision, not a wide road. Rather, as we said, "finer than a hair and sharper than a sword." So walk upon God's path and His method in balance, do not deviate to the right or left, for deviation, as we said, distances you from the goal. If you begin from a place and your balance is upset in it by even a millimetre, then the more you proceed the more the deviation widens, and any slight deviation at the starting point leads to an increasing abyss and distance.

Likewise is religion: whenever we come together in it and draw close to one another, we walk the straight path, and whenever we move away from the legislation, the ways scatter us.

﴿And this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. This He has enjoined upon you that you may be God-conscious.﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 153]. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) made the verbal statement of the relation manifest through physical action, when he sat among his companions and drew a line. He said: "This is the way of God."

Then he drew lines to his right and lines to his left, and said: "These are ways, and upon each way there is a devil who calls to it." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way.﴾

Therefore, all the people of truth and goodness, whenever they draw near to the centre, meet together, and this meeting continues to draw closer and closer until it vanishes and all become one point.

And observe the majesty of the Truth when He makes the straight path to Him in His religion attributed to His Messenger: ﴿And this is My path, [being] straight﴾. So the Messenger walks upon this path, and he does not deceive himself; and the one who does it and walks in it commands you to walk in it, and he did not command you while he was distant from it and aloof. Even if he deceived you all, he would not deceive himself, and this is the path upon which he walks.

The way (sabil) here is known to be toward God, so it is as if the way of God is the path of Muhammad (ﷺ). He attributed the action and the event to God alone: at the beginning He said ﴿And this is My path, [being] straight﴾, then He said "His way." So the path was not made by Muhammad for himself, but God willed it for all the believers, and the Messenger of God is the one who takes them by the hand toward it.

When we look at all the disputes that arise between religions with one another, such as between Judaism and Christianity for example: ﴿The Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"...﴾ [Surat al-Baqara, 113].

And the polytheists said: neither of these is upon anything: ﴿Thus did those who do not know say the like of their words...﴾ [Surat al-Baqara, 113].

That is, we are before three statements: the Jews said: the Christians are not upon anything; the Christians said: the Jews are not upon anything; and those who do not know, namely the people of Makkah, said the like of their words. Then we find that each of these religions divides into multiple sects, and each sect has something it fanatically clings to. It sees that what it says is the truth and what others say is falsehood. And how does this arise when the source is one and the divine revelations to the messengers are one? The bane of all this arises from the lust for temporal authority, and every person wants to have status, influence and succession. This one wants to lead a group, and that one wants to lead a group; and if they had been gathered upon one path, they would not have become factions.

And we find him (ﷺ) saying: "The Jews split into seventy-one sects, the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and my community will split into seventy-three sects." (1)

In another narration: "All of them are in the Fire except one, and it is the Jama'a." The Jama'a are the People of the Sunna and the Jama'a. In another narration: "What I and my companions are upon." We notice the precision of this statement in a number of schools and sects, even if you do not hear of some of them, because they died with the death of those who fanatically clung to them and who wished to live in their glory.

So the bane comes, and we look at a ruling, where one person holds one opinion and another comes and holds a different opinion, for no reason other than difference. We say to them: pay attention to the difference between a decisive ruling (hukm muhkam), and a ruling which God left as a field for ijtihad (independent reasoning). The ruling which God willed to be decisive came with a text that admits of no disagreement, and this text settles every dispute. The ruling which God loves from those who are obligated, as a lightening upon them in some respect, comes with a text admitting of ijtihad, and the Lawgiver's coming with a text on a ruling for ijtihad is thus permission to exercise ijtihad in it; for had He willed it to be a ruling on which we do not differ, He would have brought it decisive.

The continuing example is what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) left us in his noble Sunna. When God, glorified and exalted is He, willed that he not lay down arms before disciplining the Banu Qurayza, who had supported the polytheists of Makkah in the war, he (ﷺ) said: "None of you should pray the 'asr except in the land of Banu Qurayza" (2).

The companions set out on their way to the Banu Qurayza, and the sun announced its setting while they were on the road, so the companions of the Messenger of God divided into two groups. One group said: we will pray the 'asr before the sun sets; and another group said: the Messenger of God said, "None of you should pray the 'asr except in the land of Banu Qurayza." So some people prayed the 'asr before the sun set, and the others did not pray until they reached the Banu Qurayza, and they referred their matter to the Lawgiver, who was the Messenger of God, and he approved this, and he approved that, because the text admitted of it.

Why? Because every event requires a circumstance that has a time and a place. Those who said the sun was nearly setting and we must pray the 'asr before it sets looked to the time. And those who said we will not pray except in the land of Banu Qurayza looked to the place. And when the matter was referred to the Lawgiver, the most knowing, he approved these and approved those.

So if a ruling has a decisive text, there is no room for disagreement about it. And if God has left it as a place for ijtihad, He brings us a text that is not decisive. Whoever goes to it, it is not correct for us to call him mistaken. Therefore there remains from the manners of the imams, whose schools have survived to this day, that one of them, along with another, says: what I have adopted is correct, admitting of error, and what my opponent adopted is wrong, admitting of being correct. Their good manners are what kept their schools alive until now, and the lack of manners in others caused their schools to crumble and vanish, so that you do not know of them, and praise be to God that you do not know of them.

1 Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from Abu Hurayra.
2 Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il and al-Sunan.

Then Allah says, after that: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete [in excellence] for him who would do good, and a detailed explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.﴾ (6:154)

When we hear the word "thumma" (ثم, "then"), we know it is one of the particles of conjunction (huruf al-'atf). There are many such particles, and each has a meaning it conveys. Here, ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾, and the giving of the Book to Moses happened before the statement ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ (6:151). The Torah came first, then the Gospel, then the Qur'an came as the final Book. So how has the expression come here with "thumma"? Given that the giving of the Book to Moses came before the coming of His statement, the True One: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you﴾?

To the proponents of this understanding we say: you have taken "thumma" to indicate the sequence of actions and events, and you have forgotten that "thumma" may also come to indicate the sequence of reports. For someone may say to you: "Why do you not ask about so-and-so and do not fulfil the right that is due to him, such as the right of kinship, for example?" So you say: "How? I have done such-and-such for him, then I did such-and-such for his father, then I did such-and-such for his grandfather."

So you are arranging reports, and ascending through them, and rising. For this reason the Arab poet said:
"Whoever became lord, then his father became lord,
then before that his grandfather had become lord."
So lordship came first to the grandfather, then to the father, then passed to the son. "Thumma" in this case is not for ordering events, but for the ordering of reports, meaning that the occurrence of the conjoined item after the item it is conjoined to is according to how they are spoken of, not according to the time at which the event occurred for one of them. So the intention is the ascent in the reporting of events.

Now look at the Qur'an in its perfect expression, it says: ﴿And We created you, then We fashioned you, then We said to the angels: prostrate to Adam﴾ (7:11).

We know that the command from God to the angels to prostrate to Adam was from the beginning. So in this noble statement He wishes to order our state: He created us after He fashioned us, and He fashioned us after He said to the angels, prostrate to Adam.

And to God belongs the highest description: you find someone saying to his son: "I took care of you in higher education, then do not forget that I took care of you in secondary education, then do not forget that I took care of you in preparatory school; then do not forget that I took care of you before all that in primary education." And by that you are ascending in reporting, not in events. The event may come later, but the ordering of the report places it earlier.

﴿Then We gave Moses the Book...﴾ (6:154). Certainly, since it comes with the story of Moses, the Book is the Torah. When "the Book" is mentioned without specification, it refers to the Qur'an, because it is the Book that gathers all that is in the books and that watches over all that is in the books. But if it were said, for example: "We sent down to Moses the Book," the Book would be the Torah; or "We sent down to Jesus the Book," the Book would be the Gospel.

﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete [in excellence] for him who would do good, and a detailed explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy...﴾ (6:154).

Completeness (tamam) is the comprehensiveness of the qualities of goodness, and for this reason the True One says: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favour upon you...﴾ (5:3).

"Perfected" means no deficiency, and "completed" means no supplement. Why did He bring completeness upon the one who did good in the matter of Moses, peace be upon him? That is because those who confronted the stubborn argument and dispute with him, may God bless him and grant him peace, were the Jews.

And you know that they filmed here in Egypt a cinematic film called "The Ten Commandments" about the story of our master Moses, peace be upon him. The Ten Commandments are what Ka'b al-Ahbar acknowledged to be present in the Torah, and they came in the preceding verses that we have recited and explained. So it is fitting that the mention of Moses, peace be upon him, come here.

When Moses, peace be upon him, brought the Torah as God sent it down to him, there were people who lived in his time who believed in what was in the Torah, and they were among the saved, and they died. As for those whose lives continued until the Messenger of God came, it was required of them to believe in him, because the Truth made clear to them in the Torah that there would be a coming Messenger, and you must believe so that the blessing of goodness may be completed upon you. For even if you are believers in Moses and act by his method, belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is necessary. Those before you did good in the time of the mission of Moses, peace be upon him, and Muhammad came with the final message. So if you wish that God complete for you goodness, honour and blessing, you must declare belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of you followed Moses, peace be upon him, well and believed in Muhammad, so goodness was completed for them: ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾.

﴿And a detailed explanation of all things﴾ means that it is suited to its time. And to God belongs the highest description: when you have a young child, you say, "I have tailored his clothes," meaning I have made for him the clothes that suit him. When he grows up, his old clothes will no longer be fit for him to wear. And ﴿a detailed explanation of all things﴾ means the values that suit the age in which they live. So if we bring a new detailing in the Qur'an, it is suited to its time. Someone may say: "Here is a detail, and here is a detail; what is the difference between one detail and another?" We say: every detail is suited to its time, and the verses of the Qur'an are detailed, ready and prepared for every age and for all people until the Hour arrives.

The affliction is always in those who are in charge of legislation. When a case arises involving a person of rank and authority, they try to prepare and tailor a ruling suited to him. We say to such a man: you are tailoring the ruling, although the rulings are ready, prepared and manifest. We find that bodily forms differ in their tailoring of clothes, while in moral forms we find equality among all people: truthfulness in a child is like truthfulness in a youth, like truthfulness in a man, like truthfulness in a woman, like truthfulness in a scholar, like truthfulness in a merchant. None of them has a special truthfulness of his own, and likewise trustworthiness. Islam has blessed us with the doctrinal matter and likewise with the ready legal matter, suitable for every human being; there is no verse cut to one measure applied to one person alone. No, the verses encompass everyone.

﴿And a detailed explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy...﴾ (6:154). Guidance is what indicates the ends, because the religion of fitrah has been obliterated by parents' failure to transmit to their children the method of heaven in the affairs of life, its concerns, and the values that ought to prevail. The affliction is that the father teaches his child how to eat and drink, and forgets to teach him matters of values. But the True One, glorified and exalted, has shown mercy for our heedlessness and our forgetfulness; so He legislated and sent for every age a new messenger and a new guidance to remind us. ﴿...that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾ (6:154).

Every affliction springs from turning away from God's legislations, and they forget to place in their minds the meeting with God. But if the meeting with God were clear in their minds, they would prepare for it, because ends are what make a person turn to means. The poet says:
"Would that someone show me my end before my way,
and from where, when ends come after the ways?"
We say to this poet: your saying "Would that someone show me my end before my way" is a correct statement; but your saying "and from where, when ends come after the ways" is an imprecise statement, for the end is what determines the way. Likewise, God's legislation set the end first, and after that made for it the path. God has legislated for everything what the life circumstances of humans require, and therefore there is no objection to it, for in it is a detailing of all things.

And God says after that: ﴿This is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and be mindful of God, that you may receive mercy.﴾

"Hadhā" (this) is a demonstrative, which usually comes to refer back to something previously mentioned. But if the demonstrative has no prior mention and no present object being pointed to, this is evidence that when you point, it refers only to that thing, because it is specific, and the mind turns to it without reflection, given its clarity. The word "kitāb" (Book) shows that it has reached such preciousness that it must be written and recorded, because a person does not record or write anything except what is beneficial; idle talk is not written down. Our Lord called the Qur'an "kitāb" and at another time called it "Qur'ān." So it is a "Qur'ān" recited from the chests, and a "kitāb" preserved in lines. For this reason, when they came to compile it, they brought the written pages to check them against what was in the chests.

﴿This is a Book which We have sent down, blessed﴾ [Surah al-An'ām]: "Anzalnāhu" means We ordered its sending down, and the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibrīl) brought it down. The word "mubārak" (blessed) is derived from "barakah" (blessing), meaning that it gives goodness and fruit beyond what is expected of it. You might say: "So-and-so's salary is two hundred pounds, and he raises his children well and feels content," and you will find someone telling you: "This is blessing." As if the salary could never cover these responsibilities. The word "barakah" indicates that God's hand is extended within the means. We know that people always look to the provision of what comes in (ījāb), and do not look to the wider provision than what comes in, which is the provision of what is taken away (salb). The provision of what comes in brings you two hundred pounds, while the provision of what is taken away removes from you expenses whose extent you do not know. You find someone whose salary reaches a thousand pounds, but one of his parents falls ill, and another child needs private lessons, so the thousand pounds is dissipated and he needs more than that.

Thus, when God takes away expenses, or spending money on disobedience or illness, this is the blessing of provision. And you find a man whose wealth comes from what is lawful and who toils for it, and God enables him to buy everything he needs and bestows upon his little money the quality of acceptance. And you find another whose wealth comes unlawfully, and God bestows upon his money the quality of anger, so he spends it on calamities and afflictions and needs more than it.

When you compare the Qur'an with the Torah in size, you find it smaller, but if you see the blessing within it, you will find a blessing that never ends. Each day the Qur'an gives its new gift, and its wonders never cease: one reads it and understands a meaning, and another reads it and understands a new meaning. This is evidence that its Speaker is wise, placing much benefit in a small thing, and this is the meaning of ﴿a Book which We have sent down, blessed﴾. Every book has a limited time, a limited era, and a limited nation, but the Qur'an, from the day God sent it down until the Hour arises, faces issues and a renewing nation, and provides solutions for them. The important point is that the Qur'an came in keeping with the aspirations of humanity and its civilization and its intellectual advancements; therefore it had to confront all these matters in a way that keeps it always ahead, and this is not possible except with blessing within it.

We all know that the Qur'an was revealed to an unlettered man (ummī), in an unlettered nation, and there is profound wisdom in this, because "ummī" means that he took no knowledge from humans; rather, he was as his mother bore him, and his culture and knowledge came from heaven.

So illiteracy in him is an honor and an elevation of the sources of his knowledge. The Qur'an was revealed to an unlettered nation because this religion and those legislations were sent down to a nomadic people moving from place to place, who had no law, but were governed only by the chief of the tribe. When these spiritual values and legal rulings descend upon them, this is evidence that the Book bearing these values and rulings comes from heaven. Had the Qur'an been revealed to a civilized nation, it would have been called a civilizational transition, but it was revealed to a nation that did not possess laws like those by which the Persians or the Romans were ruled.

Since the Book has these attributes, which relieve people of the burden of legislating for themselves and encompass all good, the command comes from God: ﴿So follow it and be mindful of God, that you may receive mercy﴾ [part of verse 155, Surah al-An'ām]. When you say "la'alla" (that perhaps), know that it carries hope. You may hope from someone, saying: "Perhaps so-and-so will give you such-and-such." The hope here is directed at one person, while the one who performs the hoped-for action is another, and the other may or may not perform it; he may become angry and not do it, because a human is subject to changing states, and who knows, at the moment he wants to act he may be unable. But if you say, "Perhaps I will do such-and-such for you," here you are both the one hoping and the one hoped for at once. Yet you too are subject to changing states: you expect your ability to act, but when you intend to act, such ability may not be available to you.

Why did the Truth (al-Haqq) send down this Book? Here the Truth specifies the community for whom the Qur'an was to be sent down, saying:

﴿Lest you should say: "The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of their studying."﴾

So the Book purifies the earlier beliefs that were revealed to the two groups, the Jews and the Christians. Had you been heedless of studying the Torah and the Gospel, because you are an unlettered community that cannot read or write, then We have sent down to you the complete Book, lest you find an excuse and say: "Our illiteracy prevented us from studying the Book that was sent down to two groups before us, the Jews and the Christians." It is as if God sent down that Book to cut off their excuses.

The polytheists may argue that if the Torah and the Gospel had been revealed to them, they would have been better guided than the Jews and Christians. This claim implies that their minds are prepared to accept faith. God has cut off every excuse from them by bringing them the Qur'an. The Truth says:

﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of God and turns away from them?﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 157].

"Sadafa" (ṣadafa, to turn away) is one of the verbs that are used both transitively and intransitively. "Intransitive" means that it is complete with its subject and does not require an object. For example, if you are told: "So-and-so sat down," you understand that so-and-so has sat, and the meaning is complete without needing anything else. But if you are told: "Zayd struck," you will necessarily wait for your speaker to tell you who was struck; that is, you have been given a verb that requires something after the subject on which the action falls. This is called a "transitive" verb (fi'l muta'addin), meaning that the action passes from the subject to a direct object.

"Sadafa" has both properties. The Truth used this form, which can be either intransitive or transitive, so that the expression serves two purposes. The first purpose: "sadafa" means "to turn away and avoid," and so it is intransitive, meaning that he has gone astray in himself. The second purpose: "sadafa" is transitive, indicating that he turns others away from faith, that is, he misguides others, and the burden of their misguidance falls upon him. He is first misguided himself, and then bears the burden of the one he misguided. For this reason, He, glory be to Him, used the word that is suitable for both: "sadafa 'anha" means he turned away, going astray himself, and "sadafa ghayrahu" means he caused others to turn away and avoid, thereby misguiding them. Thus God punishes him with two punishments, and He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿...We will repay those who turn away from Our signs with the worst punishment because of what they used to turn away.﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 157].

So it is as if the matter is this: those who turn away have turned themselves away from faith and turn away everyone who tries to believe. These are the people who have turned away from the path of guidance, or who have gone to extremes by turning others away from the path of guidance. If they had surveyed the existence they live in, they would find that death snatches away a people every day in no fixed pattern. Age does not govern or determine the time of the term's end, nor do causes govern it, nor does sickness or health govern it. Death is a common matter in existence. This means that every human must await his end, as if He is asking: why then do they turn away? And what do they expect from the universe? Have they seen anyone living among them who is granted eternal life in the universe?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 6, verse 158:

He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Are they waiting for anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come? The day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith. Say: Wait, we too are waiting.﴾

So, are they waiting for anything from the gifts of existence that surrounds them except that the angels come to them, the angels who seize the soul? The angels are mentioned here in general terms. In another verse He says: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, then they will offer submission...﴾ [Surah al-Nahl, 28]. No angel refuses, so they surrender to them and the matter ends.

He continues: ﴿Or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come. The day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith.﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 158].

The scholars paused at this noble statement because they wished to interpret the coming (ityan) from the Lord in light of the coming from us. Our coming entails leaving a place where a person was to a place where he is, and this does not suit God. We say: Have you interpreted every coming in light of the coming as it applies to you? By God, tell me: what is your view of His saying: ﴿And the agony of death came with truth﴾ (Qaf, 19)? How did the agony of death come, when it is a creation of God? We do not know how death comes, though it is created. So how do you want us to know how God comes?

You must interpret everything relating to God in a manner befitting the Essence of God, within the framework of "there is nothing like unto Him." Let us be courteous and give minds their measure of understanding, and let us attribute everything to God in a way that suits the Essence of God, because the coming differs according to the one who comes: the coming of a child is not the coming of a youth, nor the coming of an old man, nor the coming of a horseman. So what of the coming of God, glorified is He?! Beware, then, of understanding the coming in light of the coming of humans. I repeat it always: you must take everything as it relates to Him, glorified is He, not by your own law, but by the law of the Supreme Essence, and place everything that pertains to Him within the framework of "there is nothing like unto Him." Therefore say: He has a hearing unlike our hearing, a sight unlike our sight, a hand unlike our hands, within the framework of "there is nothing like unto Him." Beware of hearing any dispute over His saying: "Your Lord comes." Say that the coming and arrival of God is not like the action of humans; rather, He, glorified is He, "there is nothing like unto Him." ﴿Or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come, the day some of the signs of your Lord come.﴾

"Some of the signs of your Lord" are the indicators, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to good deeds before six: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the beast of the earth, the Dajjal, the particular affair of one of you (khuwaysat ahadikum), and the affair of the common people (amr al-'amma)" (1). "Khuwaysat ahadikum" is the diminutive of khassa (particular), and what is meant is the event of death that concerns the individual; it is diminished because it is considered small in comparison with the other great matters such as resurrection, reckoning and others. It is also said: it is what concerns the person of anxious preoccupations regarding his self, his wealth, and what he cares about.

"Amr al-'amma": that is, the Resurrection, because it encompasses all creatures; or the trial that blinds and deafens; or the matter that the common people take over and that comes from them rather than from the elite.

﴿Or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come, the day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before﴾ [part of verse 158, Surah al-An'am].

Because faith is only in an unseen matter; every matter that is witnessed and perceived by the senses is not called faith. For you do not say: "I believe that I am now reading the Khawatir of al-Sha'rawi on the verses of the Noble Qur'an," because in fact you are now reading these reflections. Nor do you say: "I believe that light illuminates the room," because this is a witnessed matter, not an unseen one. Faith is always in an unseen matter, but when the signs come, we move from faith in the unseen to belief in the perceptible, and at that point faith does not benefit the disbeliever, nor is obedience accepted, whether charity or other kinds of righteousness and goodness, after the soul has reached the throat and one says: "So-and-so is owed such-and-such, and so-and-so is owed such-and-such," when it was for so-and-so. This does not benefit, because the wealth is no longer one's own; it has become the wealth of the heirs. Likewise the one who did not believe and then saw the six signs about which the Lawgiver said: they will occur before the Hour or before the coming of the Hour. At the moment he sees these signs, it will not be accepted from you to say: "I have believed," because faith is only in the unseen, and the manifestation of the signs is a witnessed matter, so no declaration of faith will be accepted after it. The Truth is the One who says:

﴿Or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come, the day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith...﴾ [part of verse 158, Surah al-An'am].

That is, faith must precede the appearance of these signs, and there must not be an obstacle to acting upon it other than heedlessness, such as a person being insane, God forbid, and recovering only after the sign has come, or not reaching maturity until after the sign has come. This is the one whom faith benefits.

The Truth has presented to us these images of what happened in past history. He says:

﴿And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his hosts followed them in tyranny and enmity, until, when drowning overtook him, he said: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims." (90)﴾ [Surah Yunus].

And what was God's response to him? He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before. (91)﴾ [Surah Yunus].

So: when the soul reaches the throat, which are the preliminaries of death, then declaring your faith will not benefit you at that time.

The Truth concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿...Wait, we too are waiting﴾ [Surah al-An'am, 158]: they are awaiting failure, and we are awaiting success.

1 Narrated by Ahmad and Muslim from Abu Hurayrah.

The Almighty then says:

﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you (Muhammad) have no part in them at all. Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾ (6:159)

This verse explains the verse on which our reflections previously focused, namely His saying:
﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] paths, lest they separate you from His way. That is what He has instructed you with, that you may fear Him.﴾ [Surah al-An'am] (6:153)

Those who divided their religion forgot that religion came to unite, not to divide. Religion came to unify the source of command and prohibition in the fundamental acts, so that no disagreement arises between us and one another. Disagreement occurs only in matters that are permissible (mubahat) only: if you do them, welcome; if you do not do them, welcome; and whatever has not been subject to "do" or "do not do," it is permissible.

Therefore, those who create divisions in religion are in fact contradicting the approach of heaven, which came to gather people around one thing, so that the movements of life among people support one another and do not oppose one another. If you have a desire, and this one has a desire, and that one has a desire, then the energies will clash; what is sought and required is that the energies support and reinforce one another.

The shi'a (sects) are a group that follows a single matter; this matter unites them even if it is misguidance.

There is a following of a beneficial and good meaning, and there is a following of the opposite of that. Following in its absolute sense is that a group gathers around a matter, whether that matter is good or evil.

﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you (Muhammad) have no part in them at all..﴾ (6:159) [Surah al-An'am]: Thus they are far from your approach, O Muhammad, and it is not correct that they be attributed to your religion, because Islam came to establish values for existence, just as water establishes the life of existence. We know that water takes on no color, taste, or smell; if it takes on a color, a taste, or a smell, it loses its value as pure water. Likewise, if Islam takes on a color and the Muslims become factions, this is a matter that harms the religion, and we must know that Islam is one color.

﴿...Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾ (6:159) [Surah al-An'am]. If He, glorified is He, wills, He will hasten them with defeat or punishment, and if He wills, He will defer them until the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 6, verse 160:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like; and whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (6:160)

There is "hasan" and "hasanah." Do not say that "hasanah" is the feminine of "hasan" because it has a taa' (ة). Its taa' appears to be the taa' of feminization, but its name is "the taa' of intensiveness" (taa' al-mubalagha, the taa' of emphasis), which comes on the form used for the masculine, just as you say: "So-and-so is an 'allamah (a very learned person)," and "So-and-so is a rawiyah lil-shi'r (a great transmitter of poetry)," and "So-and-so (feminine) is a nassabah (a great genealogist)." This is the taa' of intensiveness.

The hasanah is the good that brings reward, and the more lasting and profound the reward, the more the hasanah is likewise. When the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like﴾, then "amthaluha" ("its likes") is the plural of "mithl," and "mithl" is masculine. The rule states: when the counted noun is masculine, we use the taa' with the number, and when it is feminine, we drop the taa', because the basis of numbers is built on the taa'. When you count, you say: wahid, ithnan, thalatha, up to ten ("one, two, three... up to ten"), so the basis of numbers is built on the taa'. When you use it with the feminine, you differ by dropping the taa' from it, and if you use the number with its origin, which is the masculine, you use it in its natural form, so you say: "thalathat rijal" (three men). If you want to speak about the female, you say: "thalath niswah" (three women). Here the Truth says: ﴿fa-lahu 'ashru amthaliha﴾ ("for him is ten of its likes"), and "mithl," as we said, is masculine. The Truth did not make the basic thing in giving "the like," but made the basic thing the hasanah: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ (part of 6:160). This is the absolute of mercy and grace. For this reason the sacred hadith came: on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He: "Indeed your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is Merciful. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; and if he does it, ten to seven hundred to many multiples are recorded for him. And whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; and if he does it, one evil deed is recorded for him, or Allah, Mighty and Majestic, erases it, and none perishes before Allah except the one who is doomed."(1)

We know that the Truth recompenses the good deed with ten times its like and multiplies that to seven hundred fold, because every act is accompanied by a measure of sincerity in its execution, so it is as if the Truth has established a system whereby the good deed is ten times its like, and then, with a sincere intention, the multiples reach whatever Allah wills. The Truth established this system because He, mighty and exalted, wants the good deed to be done and for others to benefit from it. If its doer is eager for the additional reward, he offers it with a sincere intention. The Truth says to us: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?﴾ (57:11).

And He also says: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him many times over? And Allah withholds and extends﴾ (part of 2:245).

Here He specifies the recompense of the good deed as ten times its like, and the intention of the giver of the good deed is what can multiply it to seven hundred or more. Glory be to Allah, the Exalted, gives an example of this in His saying:

﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾ (part of 2:261).

If the earth, which is created by Allah, gives you one grain and it gives you seven hundred, then what does the Creator of the earth give? His giving is unlimited and never runs out, and therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ (part of 2:261).

The Truth, glory be to Him, continues: ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged﴾ (part of 6:160). Since he is recompensed only with its like, they are never wronged.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) says after that: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a upright religion, the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists.﴾

And "dinan qiyaman" means that the affairs of life are established upon it, and it is its own sustainer. "Qiyaman" is derived from "al-qimah" (value) or from "al-qiyam" (standing over a matter); one "stands over" a matter when he attends to it directly, the way one who sets it right does. Likewise the religion came to set right the movement of people's lives, by giving them the standards (qiyam), and it stands over them as well: ﴿a upright religion, the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith﴾.

In every important matter that has its weight and rank, the Truth brings us a glimpse of the life of Abraham, peace be upon him, because he (may the blessings and peace of God be upon him and upon our Prophet) is the shared common ground that unites the disbelievers of Makkah and the People of the Book who dispute over him. The Jews said: "Abraham was a Christian," and our Lord says to them and to us: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a man of pure faith, a Muslim﴾ (part of verse 67, Surah Al 'Imran). Judaism and Christianity came after him. As for the other group, in their land, in all their life's movements, and in their trade and their benefits, there are clear and evident traces of Abraham, peace be upon him. The Truth says: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer; so make hearts among the people incline towards them﴾ (part of verse 37, Surah Ibrahim):

So it was our master Abraham who raised the foundations of the Sacred House, and he who made them a source of awe, and their trade went to the north and to the south with none daring to touch it, and it brought them abundant provision. And when the Truth says: ﴿a upright religion, the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ (part of verse 161, Surah Al-An'am).

What is meant is the religion in whose shelter you live through the bounties of its effects. "Al-hanif" is an inclination in the foot (a turning of the foot inward). Naturally, the religion of Abraham did not deviate from the truth and rightness; rather, it was turning away from deviation, constantly upright. We know that the messengers come when deviation has become rampant; so when Abraham came inclining away from the deviant, he was balanced.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 6, verse 162:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

By "my prayer" (ṣalātī) is meant the worship and the second pillar of Islam, which is repeated five times each day. It is the pillar that never drops at all. This is because the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, as we said earlier, suffices if you say it once in your life. The fast may be waived for you if you are unable; zakat may not apply because you have no wealth; you may be unable to perform Hajj. The prayer remains, which never drops from the servant at all. And, as we know, obligation (taklīf) has taken its share of being a pillar through it.

Every obligation among the obligations came through revelation (waḥy), except the prayer, which came directly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received it from his Lord without an intermediary. When the Truth says ﴿Indeed my prayer﴾, He is mentioning to us the mainstay of the pillars, which encompasses all the pillars, as we explained earlier. Even if a person is lying ill and cannot stand, he must move his head for the prayer, or bring the acts of prayer to mind in his heart. The Truth says: ﴿and my rites of sacrifice﴾. The word "nusuk" (rites, worship) is applied to mean every act of worship, and the Truth says: ﴿For every community We have appointed rites which they perform﴾ (from verse 67, surah al-Hajj).

"Nusuk," then, is worship, and it is applied especially to the many acts of the Hajj, such as the nusuk of circumambulation (ṭawāf), the nusuk of running between Ṣafā and Marwah (sa'y), the nusuk of standing at 'Arafah, the nusuk of stoning (ramy), and the nusuk of the pillars (jimār). All of these are called manāsik (rites). The origin of the term is that it derives from the word "nusayka," which is an ingot of silver that is smelted in a way that expels all the metals mixed with it until it becomes extremely pure. Thus worship was called nusk for this reason: that is, worship must be purified for Allah just as an ingot of silver is purified of all the metals that mix with it: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying﴾.

Here there are two matters that are optional and two matters over which man has no choice. The prayer and the rites both fall under the law of choice, but living and dying do not fall under the law of choice at all; they are in the hand of Allah. The prayer and the rites are also for Allah, but by your choice, and you do not pray except because you have believed in the One who commands prayer, or because the limbs did not do such-and-such except for Allah. So you have not done anything from yourself; rather, you have directed the created energies toward Allah in order to carry out the method that Allah has sent down. Therefore, if you wish to attribute any act, attribute it to Allah.

Why did He mention prayer and rites, both of which are optional? Because, although outwardly you have choice, all this choice springs from Allah's bringing you into existence as choosers. It is He who established the method, so that He made you pray. Or: ﴿Indeed my prayer and my rites are for Allah﴾, that is, that you be sincere in them, not associate anything with Him in them, not pray ostentatiously, not perform a rite ostentatiously, and not go to Hajj so that people will say of you, "the pilgrim so-and-so." Never! Rather, make them all for Allah, because if you make them for other than Him, then other than Him does not have the power to reward you with what Allah rewards you with. If you make them for another, you have chosen loss in the bargain. Therefore, make the prayer and the rites for the One who gives you the reward. ﴿Say: Indeed my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (162) [Surah al-An'am].

Life is a gift from Allah, and beware of spending the power of life and its manifestations on anything that does not please Allah. Your life should therefore be for Allah, not for your desires, and your death should be for Allah, not for your heirs. Remember this well, because the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿He has no partner. And of this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.﴾ [163]

This statement shows that a person may make a partner with Allah in worship: he makes his prayer an outward show for people to see, his rites an outward show, his life he dedicates to someone other than the Giver of life, he directs all his movements to other than the Giver of life, and he dedicates his death to his heirs and offspring. Therefore you must remember that Allah has no partner. ﴿...And of this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.﴾ [Surat al-An'am].

This is a command from Allah to His Messenger, and every command addressed to the Messenger is also a command to every believer in his message, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him. The commands that issue from the Lord are for your own benefit. Glory be to Him, Who is worthy of being loved, and every act of worship directed to Him contains good and benefit for us. I do not claim this for myself; rather it is a gift from your Lord and my Lord, who commanded it. Thus, when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, saw that His Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, was preoccupied with the affairs of his community, He informed us: ﴿It grieves him that you suffer; he is eager for you, and to the believers he is kind and merciful.﴾ [9:128].

At all times the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, would say: "My community, my community, my community, my community." Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wished to reassure His Messenger about his community's beloved status, so He said to him: "Indeed We will please you concerning your community and will not grieve you."(1) The full hadith is as follows: It was narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, recited the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning Abraham: ﴿My Lord, they have led many people astray; so whoever follows me, then he is of me﴾, up to the end of the verse.

And Jesus, peace be upon him, said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾.

Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my community, my community," and he wept. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad—and your Lord knows best—and ask him what makes him weep." Gabriel came to him, peace be upon him, and asked him; and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, informed him of what he had said, though He knows best. Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed We will please you concerning your community and will not grieve you."(2) And there was revealed His Word, the Truth: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [Surat al-Duha: 5].

It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Then I will not be satisfied while a single one of my community is in the Fire."(3)

The Truth concludes the verse with His words: ﴿And I am the first of the Muslims.﴾ When the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, says "I am the first of the Muslims" among his community, this is a true and correct statement, because before he commanded others to submit to Islam, he himself believed in Islam. Every messenger is the first of the Muslims among his community. However, there are people who say: let us take the phrase in this manner, and we say: the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, has a rank among all the messengers of Allah that is manifested in that he took the covenant from others, and no one took a covenant from him. So if he is the first of the Muslims in his community, he is also the first of the Muslims among the messengers. And if you do not take it as an explicit meaning, take it as a matter of rank. Let me give this example: suppose the Faculty of Law was established, for instance, in such-and-such year; every year has a first student. Then someone came and obtained 100% this year, and we say of him: he is the first at the Faculty of Law since its founding.

(1) Narrated by Muslim.
(2) Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Faith.
(3) Gharaib al-Qur'an wa Raghaib al-Furqan of al-Nisaburi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 6, verse 164:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of all things? And no soul earns [anything] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ."﴾:

The meaning of "Rabb" (lord) is that He is the One who has taken charge of nurturing and cultivating, and to Him belongs sovereignty. Everything in existence is nurtured by Allah. So how could one take any of the things of which He is the Lord and Creator as a partner to Him?! That is never valid. ﴿Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah"﴾: This is a denial that comes in the form of a question, addressed to every listener, as if the Truth were saying to each of us: "Present this to your mind without bias, and I will entrust you with the answer." You are only asked this when it is certain that the answer will be "No." Had the answer been open to this or that, He would not have entrusted you with the answer. It is as if He is saying: any sensible person who answers this question will agree with Me that one should not take other than Allah as a lord.

﴿Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of all things? And no soul earns [anything] except against itself"﴾ (part of verse 164, Surat al-An'am): "Abghi" means "I seek," and "taksib" derives from the root "kasb," and "iktasaba." "Kasaba" always comes with good, as we have learned before, while "iktasaba" comes with evil. But there are people who become accustomed to committing bad deeds, and they no longer find them burdensome; so, because they are easy for them, they regard them as earning (kasb). It is foolish to say "this is an earning" when it is against you and not for you, because when you look at the very name, you understand that it is not a credit to you but a debt upon you.

﴿And no soul earns [anything] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾ (part of verse 164, Surat al-An'am): "Wizr" is a heavy load, and whatever is derived from it carries hardship and difficulty with it, as in the word "wazir" (minister). The Truth says: ﴿And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother. Strengthen my back through him.﴾ (Surat Ta-Ha). It is as if Musa (peace be upon him) knew that carrying the message to the Children of Israel was a difficult task, so he said to Allah: give me my brother to help me with this hardship.

And the Truth says: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you? And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed down your back.﴾ (Surat al-Sharh). At the beginning of his receiving revelation, the Prophet (ﷺ) suffered from the impact of this process, and it was a difficult matter for him, because the matter required a meeting of an angelic with a human, and an interaction had to occur. This interaction would appear upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): his face would redden, sweat would pour from him, and afterwards he would say: "Cover me, cover me, and wrap me up." If he was sitting and his knee was upon the knee of someone beside him, his neighbour would feel the weight; and if he was on a mount, it would groan and moan from exhaustion. This is because the meeting of revelation with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) requires one of two things: either the revelation, being the bearer of the message, transforms into a humanity similar to the Messenger's humanity, or the Messenger moves into an angelic state suited to his receiving the angel. Thus his meeting with the angelic realm required emotion and interaction.

But when the Prophet (ﷺ) became accustomed to revelation and knew the sweetness of receiving it, he forgot the hardships. That is why, when revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he longed for it. Before that, revelation used to tire and exhaust him, so the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wanted the sweetness of what had been revealed to him to remain in his soul, and for his soul to be calmed and to long for revelation. When he receives revelation with longing, he will not remember the hardships.

﴿And no soul earns [anything] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.﴾ (part of verse 164, Surat al-An'am): Thus the root "wizr" is a weight carried with hardship; that is, no person bears another's heavy hardship. Responsibility is not transferred except when the act transgresses. We have already learned the difference between one who goes astray in himself and one who misleads others, so that he bears his own burdens along with their burdens, because of his transgression in misleading them. We will all return to our Lord, and He will inform us of that over which we used to differ.

And He, may He be exalted, says after that: ﴿It is He who has made you successors upon the earth, and has raised some of you above others in rank, that He may try you in what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (6:165)

There is another noble statement in another verse: ﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ (35:39). Here the Truth says: ﴿successors of the earth﴾. The meaning of "khalifah" (successor) is one who replaces another. He may replace him in time, or he may replace him in place. Succession in time is that one era comes after another, and one day after another. Succession in place is that one sits, then departs so that another comes and settles in his place. Look at all the stages of human life and you will find that in youth a person is strong, then youth leaves him and its end overtakes him, and he goes on to old age. Likewise, you find a person who owns a place, then leaves it and another comes and owns it.

Or, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, intended by succession not that some of us succeed others, but the succession of the human being to the Lord of the human being on earth. For everything is subject to Allah by compulsion, and the Truth, glory be to Him, has bestowed by the vastness of His giving that some things are subject to others as a gift from Him, may He be glorified. If you light a fire, for example, it submits to you; if you plough the earth and place seeds in it, it submits to you; if you drink, you are quenched; if you eat, you are satisfied. From where did you take all that?

You took it from the fact that the Truth subjected to you what is in the cosmos, and made causes and effects. So it is as if you are a successor of wills. In order that He, glory be to Him, may establish for us that He does what He wills, we must take this matter as an established fact. If you wish to test this, look at any person, even a disbeliever, who wants to stand up from his place, and his limbs submit to him and he stands. Which limb did he command to do that? He does not know anything except that by merely wanting to stand, he has stood. And lest you think that you took all that by your own cleverness, He makes some matters universal, such as death and life: these are two matters in which the English does not differ from the French or the Arab. Likewise laughing and crying. Is there any difference between an English laugh, a communist laugh, or a capitalist laugh? Of course not; all of them are laughter, and it is a universal language. Therefore He said: ﴿And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep﴾ (53:43). Glory be to Him, He has brought a common matter found in all people. You speak and act in the form and manner you wish, but at the moment you laugh, it is He, glory be to Him, who makes you laugh. When you wish to flatter someone and laugh at him, you are surprised to find that your laugh is artificial.

The Truth makes clear to you: the reins of My cosmos are in My hand. I make people free to choose in some things, and in other things I make them compelled and united despite their noses: I am the One who makes laugh and makes weep. There is no English weeping, French weeping, or German weeping; all of humanity shares in such matters.

﴿And He it is who has made you successors upon the earth…﴾ (6:165).

Your will over your parts and over your limbs, O human, is a gift bestowed upon you by the Supreme Giver and the Supreme Willer. He, glory be to Him, may withdraw that from some individuals, commanding the brain: beware of sending a signal to that limb so that it responds. Then that person is afflicted with paralysis.

If it were a matter of human cleverness, he would resist that. So you are the successors of the earth; things submit to you to the extent that Allah wills them to submit to you. If He withdraws their submission from you, it is in order to establish that you did not subjugate them by your own powers, but by Him. If He wills, He releases the succession; if He wills, He restricts the succession. ﴿And raised some of you above others in degrees﴾. It is as if from succession is that we are not alike or identical; rather, He, glory be to Him, wished us to be complementary in gifts and in perfections. For if people were a repeated image in talents, life would be corrupted. So our talents must differ, because the requirements of life are many: if we were all doctors, the matter would not work; if we were all judges, the matter would be corrupted; likewise if we were all engineers or farmers. Therefore the will of Allah must be realized in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ (6:165). That is, some have been raised, and others have been raised above them. Who is the raised one, and who is the one raised above? Each of you is raised in the aspect of his talents, and raised above in what he has no talent for, because the Truth wants created beings to support one another, and support does not arise as a favour, but arises from need. So the management of interests in the cosmos must be by necessity. This is the engineering of the Supreme Cosmic Maker, glory be to Him, which manifests in that you have drawn a chart of those who entered with you the stage of primary education, and of those who left study and of those who continued to enter preparatory study. You find them fewer; those who studied at secondary level are fewer; those who attained higher education are fewer; and those who obtained a doctorate are fewer.

Thus we find that some drop out of education because there are more tasks in the cosmos that require only a holder of a primary certificate, or a preparatory certificate, or a holder of a secondary school completion certificate. Had each of them remained in higher education, we would not find anyone for those tasks. Therefore Allah made mutual support in the cosmos a need, not a favour.

Notice well: when a person is gripped by the hunger of his belly or the hunger of his dependants, he accepts any work, and even if he is content with Allah's decree concerning what He placed him in, and does not harbour resentment toward others, he will perfect this work, excel in it, and Allah will provide him with lawful good provision. For this reason, the Imam ʿAli said: "The worth of every man is what he does well." So if a person performs his work well, he is a successful person in existence.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, willed not to make us repeated individuals, but made us differing and unequal, raising some above others; each of us is raised in what he excels at, and raised above in what he does not excel at, so that a person among us needs others to perform for him the work he does not excel at. In this way the world is bound by ties of interest and need, not ties of favour. ﴿And raised some of you above others in degrees, that He may try you in what He has given you…﴾ (6:165). It is as if this raising is a test for humans in what Allah has given them of talents, so that He may know with the knowledge of binding upon the servant. He knows eternally everything that proceeds from the servant, but He leaves the servant the opportunity to perform the deed, so that he is bound by what he did, and it becomes a proof against the servant. When the Truth says: ﴿that He may try you﴾, the intended meaning is to test you in order to establish acknowledgement against your own selves, not to inform Him.

﴿That He may try you in what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (6:165).

And He, glory be to Him, is "swift in punishment," so beware of thinking the Hereafter is slow; reward and punishment will come after we finish and die. Death has no cause that is known; every person is liable to die, and thus his resurrection has occurred, and once a person's resurrection has occurred, he cannot perform any other deed. So He, glory be to Him, is swift in punishment. But some people are deceived by the forbearance of Allah and consider the Hereafter slow. Therefore one of the knowers said: "Make your thanks to Him whose blessings never cease from you, make your obedience to Him whom you never can do without, and make your submission to Him whose dominion and authority you never leave." So every attribute of the Truth, whose effect is manifest in the created being, is a gift from Allah to him. For instance, if you want to stand up, you do not know which muscles you move to stand, but by merely willing it you stand, and that is a manifestation of the will of Allah: when He wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is.

Since we are successors, we must be complementary and not repeated; that is, each one has a talent that lacks in the other, and the other has a talent that lacks in someone else, so that every creature on earth is compelled to cooperate with another, taking the fruit of the talents of others and giving the fruit of his own talents. The Truth does not want us to give the fruits of talents as a favour; rather He wants to make them a need. You need the talent of someone you do not possess, and he likewise needs your work.

When Allah, blessed and exalted, makes us successors in this way, some of us outwardly stand above others. Therefore He, glory be to Him, makes clear: I have favoured some of you over others, but I have not favoured a group so as to make another group subordinate; rather each is favoured in something because he has talents in it, and is favoured over another in something else in which he has no talents. Thus people are all equal.

We are all the dependants of Allah, and none of us is more entitled to Allah than another, for He, glory be to Him, has not taken a consort nor a son. Therefore, if we try to count the talents among humans and distribute them among all creatures, we would find that each person's total is equal to every other person's total. You excel in one talent, but in another talent you find yourself unable, and in a third you may be able but do not like it. Add up the degrees in all talents and you will find that each person equals the other, and no one has superiority over anyone except by piety. ﴿And He it is who has made you successors upon the earth, and has raised some of you above others in degrees, that He may try you in what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment﴾ (part of 6:165).

So each of us may say: "I am raised," but he must not be deluded, for he is also raised above by others. Balance comes from this side: there is no arrogance in your elevation in one degree, nor humiliation in your lowering in one degree, because this is the will of Allah in one respect and His will in another, glory be to Him. Whoever respects the decree of Allah in distributing His talents among creation, Allah gives him the best of His gift, and no one with another talent will ever be distinguished over him.

But will all people succeed in this? No. There are people who fall short, and someone who sees another richer than himself while he is poor begins to feel rancour, envy and jealousy. We say to him: look at your strength; you may be stronger than him, and you may be happier than him in many matters. Take the talent Allah gave you and the talent He gave to others, and you will find that each person's total equals every other's. The one who succeeds in these comparative equations will have reward from Allah: He will overlook some of his misdeeds and forgive him. And whoever does not respect Allah's decree in His creation, Allah will punish him. Therefore He, glory be to Him, made clear: I test you and try you; whoever succeeds has forgiveness and mercy, and whoever does not succeed has punishment. Do not think My punishment is distant, for between a person and punishment is only death, and there is no known cause of death; a person may die at any moment, and then his punishment begins. ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (6:165).

Thus the Surah of al-An'am is concluded, which He began with His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿Praise be to Allah﴾, and concluded with His saying: ﴿and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. So praise is to Allah at the beginning, and praise is to Allah at the end.
